history.title: xXx: Return Of Xander Cage
history.text: The Return of Xander Cage(released Jan/17) stars,among others,Vin Diesel,Tony Collette,Donnie Yen,Deepika Padukone,Kris Wu,Ariadna Gutiérrez,Samuel Jackson and Ruby Rose.This newest in the Cage franchise does what the first one failed to do,and wins all around. The story finds the world being threatened with the bringing down of satellites,courtesy of a little device called Pandora's Box.The film begins with Jackson,the head of the triple X program, being snuffed out by a downed satellite.Then we are privy to a high level security meeting being interrupted by a fast moving and precise trio,who manage to abscond with the box.Cage is brought in to retrieve said box and save the world.Instead of a ready made team of top soldiers,he enlists the help of a known quantity, to band together a group he can trust. He heads to the Philippines to track down the thief who took the box.However it soon becomes apparent this guy and his associates also worked at one time for the triple X project.And farther along still Cage,his team and the the "bad" guys start working together as it is the Government agency that hired him that is the real threat.They track Pandora to Detroit where Cage and the head of the other group get captured and taken aboard a transport plane.They shoot Cage but of course the vest he wears saves his hide.A struggle ensues with Cage taking over the plane to crash it into the incoming satellite and escape to Earth unharmed. At Jackson's funeral who should show up, but Jackson himself....still alive and giving Cage his job,life and kick ass style back to him. This film,though cliched(the verbal banter,the corrupt government agency and official,the bullet proof vest,Pandora's Box,et al),it still is packaged just differently enough to give one a lot of kick ass moments.The stunts are spectacular, as are Donnie Yen's martial arts moves.This film has what the first one didn't,and that was solid action along with a decent and well paced plot.Vin Diesel fits right back into his character like a hand to a glove.In fact I think his character is more fully formed and fleshed out this time around. Technically speaking the film is in its w/s a/r of 2:35:1 and is clear and crisp.There are no extras...surprise! In conclusion,the film brings in a lot of new and fresh talent to spruce up the second go 'round of Xander Cage, and it all comes out in winning style.Yen's moves are particularly good and the scene of the plane smashing into an incoming satellite and Vin Diesel's subsequent escape have to be seen to be believed.Four stars.

history.title: Krampus [DVD]
history.review_title: A real stinker of a sinker!
history.text: Krampus(released Nov./15)stars,among others,Toni Collette,David Koechner,Allison Tolman and Adam Scott.It starts out nicely, but soon devolves into a cliche' ridden monster with terribly cheap S/FX,in the form of the Krampus and his crew. The film starts with Collette and Scott as the heads of the household who are having Xmas at their place.They live with Dad's German born mother,and have two kids,one pre-teen boy and his teen sister.Their son writes a letter to Santa but doesn't mail it.When Mom's sister and her hubby and brood of kids show up with their obnoxious Aunt, all hell breaks loose later at the diner table.Two of their girls have gotten a hold of the son's unposted letter and read it aloud.The son and sisters get into a scuffle, with the son retreating to his room.He rips up the letter and tosses it out his window,which rises mysteriously into the air. Shortly after the power goes out in the entire neighbourhood.With no power and a wicked storm whirling outside, the family hunkers down to weather the storm.The host familie's daughter decides,and gets permission to,go see if her boyfriend is alright, as she can't raise him on her phone.Outside the storm is fierce and after a short while the sky darkens even more.She sees some entity atop a roof top and runs back towards home.While hiding under an abandoned truck she is abducted by...something. Back home the Dad's decide to brave the elements and try to find the missing daughter.They have no luck and become besieged by some entity who almost gets the visiting brother in law.They hobble back home and tend his wounds.Later the old woman decides to tell a story of when she was a child and the town she lived in forgot the meaning of Xmas.That year her family was abducted by Krampus,who is an anti-St.Nicholaus who comes to punish and take those who have lost the Xmas spirit.Though initially poo-pooed,the entire family soon comes under siege as the two visiting sisters get taken, and a reconnoiter of the attic results in an all out assault.Back down stairs,while sleeping,one boy is lured to the fireplace by a ginger bread man attached to a chain.This quickly swirls about him and pulls him up the chimney.Collette awakens in time to try and pull him down ,and she herself is almost pulled all the way up the chimney until her hubby intervenes to prevent it.It is not long now until the entities outside start invading the family inside, and before long all are gone,except the young man who wrote the torn up letter.He ends up confronting Krampus and his crew near an opened portal ,presumably to Hell, in the ground.It's all to no avail as Krampus throws him into the hole also. Next thing he knows he is waking up in bed Xmas morning and falls out of it.He goes downstairs to see everything,including his family,back to normal.His wish to have a Xmas the way it used to be,seems to have come true after all.As they sit opening presents the boy gets an old bell,just as his grand mother had when her family was taken.Suddenly the memories of what happened the days leading up to that time come flooding into everyone's minds.The camera pulls back to reveal the house to be in a snow globe.Farther back still it sits among countless other snow globes. The film moves along quite well for about the first 40 minutes,until the two Dad's come back from being attacked outside.Then it falls into those cliched moments where folks start getting abducted and attacked when they shouldn't be,except for their own stupidity.Then comes our first looks at the monsters themselves.The attack in the attic with a big jack in the box,the screwy looking angel,then one by a sharp toothed bear are just too far fetched and phony looking to be believed.Then there are the ginger bread men in the kitchen with the nail gun.C'mon.Krampus himself,who looks like a decrepit anti-Santa Claus, always has his mouth open.The S/FX department couldn't have at least made a mouth that closed at some point?It made it obvious it was a cheap prop;along with the other mask wearing minions of Krampus's unholy crew,who for all intents and purposes looked like creatures from Labyrinth,but not as well done.When the attic attack comes they(the film makers) lose all believably.And by the time the boy confronts Krampus over the portal to Hell,well,it's all over but the laughter. Technically speaking the film is in its w/s a/r of 2:40:1 and is clear and crisp.There are a few extras like an alternate ending,a small featurette,a gallery and more. All in all a movie with potential, that soon implodes in on itself.It's cliched plot(been there,done this sooo many times) and less than effective S/FX(cheap!) doom this sinker stinker to the gloomy depths of Davy Jones locker in short order.A must to avoid.

history.title: Resident Evil: The Final Chapter
history.review_title: NOT the Final Chapter...you were thinking otherwise?
history.text: Resident Evil:The Final Chapter(released Dec/16)stars,among others,Milla Jovovich,Ali Larter,Shawn Roberts,and Ruby Rose.Don't go by the title, because there is lots more ahead for Alice and the RE franchise.This one brings it all full circle though, with impressive S/FX and action. We last saw Alice,Wesker and friends on the roof of the White House being attacked by mutated creatures on the ground and in the air.This film starts off in the rubble of where the last one left off.While searching for survivors the red queen appears telling Alice there is an airborne anti-virus available in the Hive.However if she doesn't reach it in under 48 hours the T-virus will have covered the entire Earth,and the Umbrella Corp.will have won. The race is on.Along the way she must battle thieves and Umbrella Corp. troops who are leading a massive horde of infected toward Raccoon City.In a stand off against the troops she reunites with her old friend Claire.The battle turns into a stall tactic,more or less,and the few survivors from that penetrate the Hive.Of course Wesker is there along with Isaacs and they don't let their party get crashed none to easily.When Alice finally reaches Isaacs she also meets with the woman she and the red queen were patterned after;Alicia Marcus.She is now old but she tells Alice what she must do,and that is to destroy the Hive an release the T-virus.She does both and afterwards the now dead Alicia uploads all of her childhood memories to Alice.As the film ends Alice makes her way to Manhattan telling us the anti virus is airborne and will take years to reach all corners of the globe.The mission continues. The acting is top notch all the way, as Jovovich continues her wonderful role as Alice.The stunts and S/Fx are also above and beyond and the story itself brings us full circle in the RE saga.However I found the deception in the title just a little bothersome.They had to lower themselves that much in order to grab not only the loyal fans but others also? This COULD be the final installment,but trust no one in Hollywood where money talks louder than words. Technically speaking the film is in its w/s a/r of 2:40:1 and is clear and crisp.There are a couple of featurettes.One of them talks of RE being the longest running action movie propelled by a leading female actor.That is true, but isn't this discussion of whether it is a woman or a man in the lead role now a moot point? When are we going to get over the man vs woman thing? The fact is Jovovich made this role her own from the start and the franchise has never looked back,so what's to debate or point out like a flashing neon sign?.....nothing. All in all yet another pleasing chapter in the RE franchise.The action and thrills are all taken to another level.This time around the story arc comes full circle and a lot of questions finally get answered.4-4 1/2 stars.

history.title: Aftermath
history.text: Aftermath(released April/17)stars,among others,Arnold Schwarzenegger, Scoot McNairy, Maggie Grace and Martin Donovan.This is a riveting portrayal of two distinct individuals and their grieving process and a tragedy that inextricably links both. Ahhnold/Roman is a supervisor for a construction company.It is near Christmas and he is expecting the return of his pregnant wife and daughter on a plane from Russia.He goes to the airport to find the flight delayed.Upon inquiring as to why, he is led into a private room and is given the news that his family has likely perished in a horrible accident.Switch to McNairy/Jacob who is an air traffic controller.He has just come on shift and everything is seemingly quiet.Trying to raise the Pittsburgh airport without success, he is distracted and misses repeated requests from an inbound flight for clearance to descend to the same altitude as the plane on which Roman's family is on.We now know the result. The film from here crisscrosses back and forth between the two men as both try to cope with their lives turned upside down,but both in two distinct ways.Roman is seemingly stuck and can't move.One day he volunteers at the crash site where the plane went down and finds his daughter's pearl necklace and his daughter(still in her seat,now in a tree).Farther on he often sleeps at the cemetery where his family is buried.Jacob is of course under investigation by the airlines and the NTSB.His marriage slowly falls apart and what little counseling he gets is doing nothing.His house is vandalized with hate graffiti on the outside.Eventually he is given the option of moving out of state,changing his name and taking a new job with a travel agency;which he takes. A year passes and based on the string of pearls found by Roman,a memorial is built in all the victims honours.His frustrations however are not over.The airline wants to financially settle with him,but no one wants to give him the simplest thing he really wants;an apology for the deaths of his family.Roman,through a reporter who is writing about the tragedy,learns of Jacobs new life and more importantly,his address.He heads off to get the apology from the man he holds responsible.It's a weekend and Jacob's estranged wife and son have come to stay,for the first time in a long time.Roman comes knocking asking for his apology and Jacob gets uppity, telling Roman it was just an accident and to get away before he calls the cops.In the exchange Jacob knocks Roman's family picture out of his hand.As he reaches down to get it he snaps amid Jacob's incessant chattering,pulls a knife and kills him.As Jacob lies bleeding to death on the floor, his wife and son sit cowering on the couch,and Roman comes and sits at the other side of it until the police come. 10 years pass by and Roman is released from prison.He heads back to the cemetery to visit his family.While standing there he is approached by a young man in a hoodie.Turns out,you guessed it,it's Jacobs now grown son.Under the pretense of being lost Roman escorts the young man out of the cemetery via a nearby bridge.Under there the youngster he pulls out a gun and reveals to Roman who he is.Roman tells him to pull the trigger as he"understands",but the boy can't.He backs away and sits down on a cement abutment,telling Roman to just leave.Roman,with head down,does as the boy asks. This is a taut and riveting film.The lives of both men,as the film goes back and forth,plays out nicely and succinctly.I must single out Ahhnold for,I believe,his best dramatic role yet.Who knew he had the acting chops he does? I saw it a little bit,in his first film back from being Governor in The Last Stand,then a little more in Maggie, and now more so in this film.McNairy also does a fine job as the fallen air traffic controller.Although we feel more for Ahhnold and his plight,McNairy manages to show us the compassion of a man who made a mistake,is totally torn inside out and is forced to give up everything as a result.He is not an unfeeling "murderer", but an ordinary flawed human being whose place none of us would enjoy being in for a nanosecond.I must at this point take exception to the blurb on the outside of the DVD case which says"revenge was all he had".Whatever pencil pusher came up with that drivel should be fired,as he never saw the film.This is NOT a revenge picture.Ahhnold didn't spend the majority of the film seeking revenge,he sought an apology from someone.If he wanted revenge,why wait a year or more to do it?Jacob was a sitting duck for months after the tragedy at his original home,which Ahhnold never went near. Technically speaking the film is in w/s and is clear and crisp.There is commentary,a featurette and the trailer in the extras department. All in all a fine film that Ahhnold should be proud of,as I think it is his best dramatic acting ever.The film is based on a true air tragedy and the direction and editing is spot on.4 solid stars.

history.title: The Wild Wild West Revisited / More Wild Wild West - Double Feature
history.review_title: A must have to complete your Wild Wild West collection!
history.text: This single DVD contains both made for TV movies The Wild Wild West Revisited and More Wild Wild West.Along with the films are both promo spots.Both were made for TV films, the former released in May/79 and the latter in Oct/80. Both films are good fun, but the best is the first one.In it we have the guy's old nemesis Michelito Lovelace,played originally by the fabulous Michael Dunn(he passed away in /73) rearing his ugly head once more.This time however it his son,played nicely by actor/songwriter Paul Williams,who does the threatening.Both men are brought out of retirement by the Secret Service head played by veteran actor Harry Morgan.They travel west only to discover Lovelace Jr.has created an atomic bomb and he has planted it in the several cities throughout the world.And each of those countries has sent their own Secret Service members to apprehend him Topping this is the fact that he also has robots posing as the heads of these nation states and the real ones are being held hostage at his lair.Of course it's up to Artie and Jim to save the day. The writers of More Wild Wild West seemed to run out of any original ideas whatsoever.This time around the bad guy is Jonathan Winters as Albert Paradine the 2nd. Like Lovelace Jr.,Winters has a rule-the-world complex as well and he also has created atomic bombs which are also planted in various cities.Concurrent with that is his plan to disrupt a peace conference in Washington,DC.He does, but the good guys discover his planted atomic bomb(which looks exactly like the one from the first film!),and Winter's ability to go invisible at his leisure also breaks down at the opportune time. "More" is really a wash out.Victor Buono plays a role as secretary of State, but he is wasted in it.I would much rather Buono had taken Winter's role and visa versa,as he could have added more depth to it. The plot is almost a clone of the first film and a running gag of Jim's Mexican girlfriend showing up with her family,all guns blazing for him,at the most awkward of times, falls flat. Both films are full screen and are decent prints,clear and crisp. All in all ,for those who want to complete their Wild Wild West collection,this is a must have.Just be warned that while the first film is a fun romp,the second falls flat throughout and is almost a clone,plot wise,of the first.But it was good to see Martin and Conrad back at it for couple of more kicks at the can.3 1/2-4 stars.

history.title: Logan
history.review_title: Not the final Wolverine which should have been far better.
history.text: Logan(released Feb/17)stars,among others,Hugh Jackman,Patrick Stewart,Boyd Holbrook,Stephen Merchant,Richard E. Grant and Dafne Keen.What is supposed to be the final chapter of the Wolverine off shoot of X-Men,turns out to be nothing of the sort and not the film it should have been. The story finds us at least 25 years into the future,where mutants are almost entirely wiped out.However at least three still survive in northern Mexico;Jackman,Stewart and Merchant ,as an albino by the name of Caliban.Logan drives a stretch limo to drum up money which he either socks away(to get he and Xavier far south) or buys drugs to keep an ailing Stewart's mind placid.This however is not the Logan of previous films.This is a disheveled,sick and older version whose life is spinning in the water,just ready to go down that proverbial drain.His condition and attitude permeate this film and give it it's heavy layers of grief,sorrow and regret. One day a Mexican woman,with a young girl, comes into his life and things instantly change.She pleads for Logan to take her to a location in Northern Dakota where there are also other mutants who are waiting to cross the border to freedom.He refuses and returns to Mexico,but with the offer weighing on his mind.Eventually the $20,000 she offered him becomes too much of a temptation, and he returns to the hotel where the woman and young girl are staying.He finds the woman dead and leaves.Once back in Mexico,Merchant asks Logan where the duffle bag in the trunk came from.They soon have their answer as the young girl stands directly behind them.In an instant the black ops arrive to take her back. Suddenly Logan,Xavier and the girl are on the run. During their journey we learn,as does Logan,that the girl is a mutant and is his daughter! The girl's guardian had left a video phone entry which also tells them she was part of a secret black operation(Transigen Corp.) that wanted to develop mutants and control them from children on up.She helped them escape,but most scattered and she was only able to keep the girl,Laura,by her side.We also find out that this location in North Dakota has been taken directly from X-Men comic books;"pablum for bet wetters",Logan calls it. Along their path they bed down one night with a local family.The black ops catch up and this results in the death of the entire family that puts them up, and of Xavier also.The bad guys have also developed /cloned a new and much fiercer Logan.It's a sad moment when Logan buries Xavier.Exhausted he and Laura head back out on the road, but Logan soon collapses from exhaustion and Laura drives.When he re awakens he is being hoisted up a mountain face on a winch.It's the rest of the mutants....all children.They stay overnight and the next day Laura and the rest are off to freedom.But the black ops aren't giving up so easily and have of course been tracking them all the way.They intercept the rag tag group and hunt them down,capturing them all.A very sick Logan has seen this and attempts a rescue.He is not gaining much ground and decides to take a chemical enhancement at its strongest dose.This gives him enough temporary strength to catch up and battle with the black ops.However by the time they unleash Logan's double he is almost out of juice.The children mutants by now are all free and they finally join in to help defeat the bad guys.The film comes to an end as Logan dies beside his daughter.They bury him and leave to a better future....(?). This film has been publicized as the last Stewart/Jackman collaboration.However for those following the film closely,they will know that this cannot be anything of the sort.In Mexico in Stewart's confinement,he asks Logan what he had done to get them there,to which Logan is silent.Then just before Xavier dies he tells Logan(actually the clone,but he doesn't know it) he finally remembers what he(Xavier) had done and now understands Logan.So what exactly are they talking about? Well,we definitely need another film to find that out don't we? This follows another recent film Resident Evil:The Final Chapter,which was also publicized as the last,but was nothing of the sort. This film establishes itself as totally different from the outset from any other X-Men/Wolverine film you have seen.It has an unprecedented heaviness and darkness to it in its feel and look.This is a sick Wolverine that has gotten himself,by whatever means,to a dead end existence.He is looking after an equally sick Xavier,who we learn later has Alzheimer's.The problem with a film like this is keeping the pace flowing throughout,otherwise it is likely to bog down easier than not.And this is what unfortunately I found happens much too often.The director/editor seemed to think we needed a rest after each action sequence,and this slows the film up terribly.It loses its punch.The entire side trip to the families house for a temporary stay,while resulting in Xavier's death,goes on far too long to the detriment of the pacing.We also have the stay at the casino in Oklahoma city,the burying of Xavier and Laura's subsequent taking over of the driving chores and the final destination of Eden where their stay is far too prolonged.These are all in-between sequences and either contribute nothing or very little to the overall narrative and/or could have been paired down and edited much tighter for a smoother flow.The nicest touch of the film is when Logan is buried near the end and has a cross at his grave.As Laura leaves she turns it on its side to make an "X". Technically speaking the film is in a 2:35:1 a/r and is clear and crisp.There are no extras. All in all a disappointing "final" film for the Wolverine;which in reality is nothing of the kind.It has its moments, but is broken up far too much with side trips that slow the film's pacing to a crawl.This stop and start thing is anathema to a picture like this,which is already dark and gloomy to begin with.As much as I am a big fan of the X-Men and Wolverine,I can only,in good conscience,give it a 3-3 1/2 stars.

history.title: Comic Book: The Movie
history.review_title: A dedication to those who`get it`.
history.text: Comic Book the movie(released Jan/04)stars Mark Hamill and an incredible gaggle of voice actors, which include such shows as the Animaniacs,Ren and Stimpy,Inspector Gadget,The Tick,Pinky and the Brain and so many more. The story here is about one Don Swan(Hamill) a high school teacher who runs a comic book store on the side(his real passion),in Wisconsin.He comes to Hollywood as an advisor to the filming of an updated version of the the comic book hero/series Commander Courage,which debuted during WW2.Hamill wants the version to be shot closer to the original,whereas the film company wants it updated and"improved".He brings along his own small film camera to document his journey, but the studio gives him a more proper cameraman.Together they roam the confines of the San Diego Comic-Con where the film company will first announce the new project.Along the way Don also discovers the original creator of the comic strip has a living relative(his grandson)who also trips along with Don.The more he is exposed to this new world,the more the grandson becomes a problem(future revenues)for the film company.We are a fly on the wall as Don Swan endures the travails of keeping true to a comic book while trying to gently manipulate the producers.In the end Don is tied up in his room,escapes and confronts a comic con crowd and the film company, and exposes what they are trying to really do to Commander Courage. The story itself is solid until the second half where it tends to drift.In the finale Mark ends up tying the pieces all together and brings it home.There are some Easter Eggs in this film.One has them describing an animated series in the 70s,from which they show a clip.It clearly has the date in Roman numerals at the bottom and it is 1966. This is a fun film and Hamill,who is also a comic"nerd",looks like he had a ball making it.It really is a tip of the hat to both the unsung voice actors who are SO talented, and to us the fans.This is the first disc.The second disc is fully loaded with endless extras.I went through this entire DVD two disc set and it must have taken me at least 3-4 hours to do it.On that second disc you get an introduction to the entire cast.Who they are and who they have voiced will blow you away.It was like actually being there without having to pay the exorbitant entrance fee.To top this veteran Gary Owens is there to moderate and share some of his own experiences in his long career.In addition there are the extended interviews with various celebs who appear in the film.Folks like Bruce Campbell,Kevin Smith,Hugh Hefner,Jonathan Winters and Sid Caesar,the perennial Stan Lee,and others.While the interviews are done within the context of the film,many such as Hugh Hefner`s drift away and we learn many amazing real details on Hugh`s life,career,the creation of his Playboy empire and his connection with various writers and producers.An amazing individual. All in all this is a homage to everyone who has ever collected a comic book in their life, and to the many fans who go to conventions and who `get it`.It also celebrates the tireless voice acting talent that has entertained us for decades.If the story itself had been a little stronger this set would have gotten a 5 star rating.Still,a worthy buy.

history.title: Phantasm 5 Movie DVD Collection
history.text: The Phantasm series started with the first film in /79 and ended in 2016 with Phantasm Ravager.When I think of this series of films I first think of three things:the flying sphere,The Tall Man(Angus Scrimm) and Reggie(Reggie Bannister).The most disappointing of the series was #2 when they replaced Baldwin(Mike) with Michael LeGros.It seems Universal(now cutting the paycheques)wanted to recast both the Reg and Mike roles! A typical example of how the big guys sometimes just don't get it.However Coscarelli managed to get Reg back at least to keep some of the conformity going.He was able to bring Baldwin back for the rest along with the rest of the originals. Here we are presented with all five films,all remastered excellently which look fresh and clean in their original a/r's.Most of the five discs here have some kind of extras,some more than others.Be warned as these discs are pancaked/piled one on top of the other, over an extra high spindle! So check those discs thoroughly for scuffs and scratches. The biggest form of disgust Reggie used in the films 1-3 was sh$t.In 4 his language becomes a little saltier,and tones down a little for the last.I recall at the time of their release that these were terrifying films.That first with the flying sphere really captured people's imagination.The ending to the first though was strange.Suddenly Jody disappeared and Mike was left with Reggie looking after him, with no explanation as to why.It was if Coscarelli ran out ideas/film and stopped it.As it also appears, as the films progress, that he kept expanding on the Phantasm universe as he went.By the end of the series everything roughly comes to a close and we find there is a dimensional threat here rather than an occult one as we all first assumed.But the films themselves did say"Nothing is as it seems". In conclusion a wonderful re-release of the Phantasm series all remastered and clear and crisp.There are extras with many of the titles.Though they look rather quaint now,they were the cutting edge horror films of their time.

history.title: The Betty Grable Collection, Vol. 1 (My Blue Heaven / The Dolly Sisters / Moon Over Miami / Down Argentine Way)
history.text: This four film BG collection contains Moon over Miami,(released June/41),Down Argentine Way(released Oct/40),My Blue Heaven(released Dec/50) and The Dolly Sisters(released Nov/45).All four films are in glorious colour and generally crisp and clean,as opposed to the "vault"series which goes under different names by different studios,and which are generally average to poor prints and are not worth the money to buy them. First off is Moon over Miami.This is about two sisters(Grable and Carol Landis) and their Aunt( Charlotte Greenwood) who go down to Florida in search of a husband for Grable.Two male friends down there are Bob Cummings and Don Ameche.Grable falls for Ameche first,but when she finds out he's broke she reluctantly gives him up for Cummings.But Grable's sister loves Cummings,so in the end Grable goes back to Ameche and Cummings lands Landis, and all is happiness and roses.Jack Haley is also on hand to provide some much needed laughs and inter play with Greenwood.This is a typical plot for the time and is alright fair for what it is.Typical escapism entertainment, and just what was called for during this period.3 1/2 stars. Secondly is Down Argentine Way.This finds Grable as a society gal who loves her horses.Ameche is from Argentina and he and his dad sail to New York to sell some.However his father has a grudge against Grable's father.So when Betty almost is set to buy one of their horses the cat comes out of the bag and Ameche refuses to sell.The two get close and when Ameche returns to Argentina,Grable follows.In the end Grable and Ameche get together as his father finally puts away the feud.This is not a film that hold up in the least.The plot is a plodding one, with almost nothing noteworthy about it.The only saving graces(only just) are Carmen Miranda's two brief appearances(and even she was filmed separately in New York-and you can tell there's a disconnect there), the Nikolas Brothers and Charlotte Greenwood.2 1/2 stars. My Blue Heaven stars Betty and Dan Dailey as a song and dance couple who have been stars on the radio and who eventually move their act into the growing medium of television.The plot has the couple wanting a baby.Betty loses one,they adopt one,she gets pregnant,then they adopt another.In the end it's all happiness and roses.Another terribly long and plodding plot.Grable isn't at her best in this one(she doesn't seem that interested), and Daily steals their scenes.They did four pics together and this is one of the worst they did.On hand are David Wayne and Jane Wyman who would go on to have careers in TV and a very young Mitzi Gaynor also appears.2 1/2 stars. Finally The Dolly Sisters,with June Haver and Grable playing the titular roles.Grable ends up falling big for John Payne,whom she later marries.However Payne goes off to war(WW1) and when it ends the two cannot get back together fast enough,due to commitments on the sister's parts,and Payne and Grable divorce.Grable ends up in a car accident ,but eventually returns to the New York stage for a benefit with her sister.In the end,while still divorced, Payne and the two sisters reunite on stage in the final number,and it looks like there might be hope for the future for the pair. This film was the one I was least expecting to like and it turned out to be the best of all of them.I have seen very few pictures with Payne I didn't like,and this is no exception.He sings here, and always had a pleasing voice.Also on hand was one of my favourite character actors of all time S.Z.Sakall.This film is also elevated by the wonderful musical score which gets you singing along to some old classic hits like"Always Chasing Rainbows" and"I Can't Begin to Tell You".I liked it and it gets 4 solid stars. All in all not some of Grable's better films.The best to me is The Dolly Sisters,followed by "Miami" and all the way down to "Argentine" and "Heaven".If you are a Grable compleatist, then there is no stopping your purchase.But for those who are a little more discerning,I would buy The Dolly Sisters on its own and forgo this rather costly set.By the way,some of these films not only come with explanatory inserts, but small repro lobby cards.

history.title: The Thing [Collector's Edition] [Blu-ray]
history.text: I purchased this on on another site but I have no doubt Amazon will have this as a lightning buy this 2016 holiday season. Buy It. The transfer is Criterion quality, if not better. The DP and gaffers did a great job on this film especially considering what film stock they were shooting on at the time. The telecine on this version is light years ahead of the original and worth every cent.

history.title: Bob's Burger's Season 3
history.review_title: Great Show Lousy On Demand DVD Presentation
history.text: Love the show, the show is worthy of 5 stars. Fox is cheap though and does not put out quality blu ray or dvd products as this is made on demand. With such a large fan base for this show it is ridiculous that they don't put out a quality Blu Ray of this season and the others. If you are going to buy it wait until December when Amazon puts it on sale for $12.99, don't be fooled by lightning buys, it was on sale for an entire week last year during December.

history.review_title: Not a Cookie Cutter Hollywood Film Easily One Of The Best of 2016
history.text: This was even better than Sicario and Sicario was very good. There is a tension and edge underlying throughout the whole film right to the end, and it is not predictable in anyway. One of Jeff Bridges best roles. Not a fan of Chris Pine at all but damn he was good, especially the scene with his son. Ben Foster was solid, it was the perfect role from him. Taylor Sheridan has become a first rate writer, ironic it took him getting the boot off of the over the top melodrama Sons of Anarchy and the fear of having to audition for bit parts the rest of his life to pick up a pen and start writing, he's got some skills, look forward to his next film.

history.title: Garfunkel & Oates
history.review_title: Solid Funny Comedians Very Poor DVD Release
history.text: I have seen several of their live shows at UCB and in the early days Largo. But this DVD does not do them justice, it's sad and clearly not the fault of these 2 talented artists do not have a better quality blu ray or dvd set that shows their talents.
Solid acting. Albert Finney

Sad a great American actor like Robert DeNiro did this film. I'm in my early 40's and grew up (or down) on raunchy films, "Van Wilder", the "Harold and Kumar" "Pineapple Express" these films are not stellar by any means but entertaining and have funny moments and you know what to expect that you are not going to be viewing "Citizen Kane" or "M" but this film was just plain beyond bad. Worse than the sequel for "Dumb and Dumber" They must have driven a truck load of untraceable money and gold up to one of DeNiro's Tribeca lofts and threatened his wife and family to get him to do this. Don't waste your time.

history.review_title: Better Than Expected and Worth The 99 Cents
history.text: Was better than I expected from the viewing of the previews. It's a one and done film, you'll only want to view it once but it's worth the .99 cent rental price and worth the $5 blu ray price that it will of course be for this years black friday/holidays. It's not anywhere near a classic nor worth repeated viewings or comparable to the original or "The Searchers" or a modern classic like "Unforgiven" or even "Pale Rider" but it good for what it is, Denzel is solid as always. The first part is a little distracting and unrealistic with Haley Bennett's breasts hanging out in every scene but it gets better and has a satisfying conclusion.

history.review_title: Subpar Production Values With A Terrible Team and Un Engaging Story Line
history.text: Poor story line with uninteresting players and personalities, of course I understand that any worth while team that is in Super Bowl contention would never allow a film crew to follow them around during pre-season/ season due to the distraction but the production values are horrible. Even the most casual fan knows the Rams are a horrible team but I tried watching because I thought maybe there would be something of redeeming value like the team dynamic and the inner workings of a professional team but the editing is so poorly done there is no story line. Looks like it was shot and edited by 1st year film students from a 3rd rate school like ASU or Cal State Northridge, proving an Emmy nomination for reality TV means absolutely nothing. It is far from usual high standard that you expect NFL film productions to be. If you are a football fan do yourself a favor and don't waste your time.

history.review_title: Nothing New Or Unique/ MJ Jumped The Shark Your Time Is Literally Better Spent Watching Plants Grow
history.text: Boring, been done, nothing new, terrible production values. This show is a a decade plus late. Weed aka MMJ jumped the shark 10 years ago, it hasn't been cool since the influx of dispensaries hit California in the mid 2000's and the Russians and Armenians took over the business, even Doug Benson has rebranded and stepped back his association. There is absolutely nothing new or original here, the "niche" interest and uniqueness of the MJ industry is over and done.

Formulaic, poor acting, not funny. Not an Oscar or FYC worthy film by any means. A poor Woody Allenesque imitation. Amazon needs to revise and police their feedback, most of the positive 4 and 5 star reviews for this film appear to be from people who worked on the film or work at the studio.

One of the worst films I have ever suffered through. The actors are great at their jobs, but without some sense of realism we lose touch with them. I could not believe in the chemistry between the two main characters other than to believe they had a strong sexual connection. We are meant to think, however, that they have a real marriage. I found it impossible to relate to that idea, not because they were so at odds with each other -- as that often happens in marriages. But that there was nothing to make me believe in them as human beings. Both are enormously selfish people, difficult to like as individuals, and grating as a pair. The policewoman, and the twin sister, were the only characters in the movie who seemed motivated by recognizable impulses. There is a lot of gratuitous sex and violence on top of the main flaw that prevents any sort of empathy toward the central characters. Finally, it is way too long. I couldn't wait for it to be over.

history.title: Charles & Camilla - Whatever Love Means
history.text: A sad effort. Lawrence Fox is excellent as Charles. The problem is, Charles is something of a stick: hates his father but is a total wimp in his presence; is socially inept despite years of training; and feels sorry for himself. With so little to recommend him personally, the efforts to pair him off with a suitable mate feel like an uphill battle. Camilla's affection seem to be stoked mostly by the rejection of her own husband. There is little in their relationship to arouse our admiration or concern: two rich snobs who believe they have every right to cheat those who trust them. But the main problem is that when the central character in a movie is dull as dishwater it is impossible to get interested in what happens to them.

A strange movie dominated by an apartment. The place in which most of the movie takes place is like another character -- the central motif and motivation of all the action that takes place within it and because of it. The acting is excellent but the story itself lacks verisimilitude. We are asked to believe that a 57 year old man, seemingly normal though not especially happy with his life and circumstances, will become unglued when he learns his Dad had an affair. His reaction, even when it appears he also lost his mother decades earlier because of the infidelity, feels extreme. Meanwhile, as the result of a casual comment, the Kristin Scott Thomas character ends an affair she has been having with a married man. This decision also seems unrealistic and arbitrary. Finally, two relative strangers become romantically involved way too quickly, given the back story and the repressed and furtive natures they express. Given the excellence of the production and the quality of the acting it would not be possible to dislike the overall experience. But the ability to believe in the characters and the changes that take place in their relationships seems forced upon them rather than an unfoldment to which the viewer can comfortably relate.

A bit slow going at first, with tension between a mother and son, the mother oddly jealous for his interest in the old man, and between the mother and Holmes over who is running the household. There is a focus on an old case, complicated by the failing memory of Holmes. But the real story is in the relationships of the three people in the house and how Holmes, after a life marked by a strict hold on his emotions and adherence to fact over fiction, finds some use in the latter and the value of allowing compassion to rule the day. A touching, heartfelt, and quietly satisfying picture.

history.title: The Age of Adaline [DVD]
history.text: First half of movie is slow going; hard to relate much to Adaline other than her scenes with her dog. But need to hang in as the entrance of a persistent and engaging man seems to wake her up. Also, movie gets another jolt [there are several others from genuine electrical sources] when Harrison Ford enters the situation. I have rarely enjoyed this actor as much as I did in this movie. Instead of coasting on his stardom and familiar moves and phrasing, he finds a center of the character he is playing and injects emotional sense into a bizarre and barely believable plotline. Ford adds gravitas to the situation. Romantically, the movie works because despite an absurd premise, the emotional interactions are quietly developed and gradually resonate with reality as we know it. Again, the earlier scenes have a distancing 'Ground Hog Day' quality that requires some patience. But the end result is affecting and worth the journey.

history.title: A Place to Call Home
history.text: Totally engrossing drama with two brilliantly played and written staring roles for women. There is balance between the negative energy of the matriarch, Elizabeth and the invading alien Sarah, and the positive relationship unfolding between George, Elizabeth's son, and Sarah. Because of her power-playing MO, Elizabeth recognizes her match in Sara -- instinctively at first -- and takes an instant dislike to her. That said, there are a few less compelling relationships -- Anna and her Italian lover, for example. The idea that a carefully bred beauty of her class and time would be reading 'Lady Chatterley.." and that her catholic-bred farm boy beau would, after reading a few pages of same, dismiss years of catholic indoctrination, feels contrived. The chemistry between the two is enough without this motivating prop. Other oddities that struck an off note: Sara's physical domination of a the local bully felt off. Women can be successful fighting off men, in certain circumstances. But what works dramatically fails to resonate humanly. No matter how violent their backstory, women don't borrow trouble by taking on men in open combat [unless armed], to the extent of pursuing them into their man-caves to humiliate them further. Doesn't scan. Yet, on the whole, this story, playing out in a grand family homestead set in magnificent Australian countryside, is a visual and emotional treat. The main characters are well written, believable, complex, and nicely played. It makes for great adult entertainment, assuming one has the hours to spend watching it.

This series thrives on the believability of its main character, Sidney Chambers. In the beginning I found him a bit much -- too handsome, too nice, too charming by half. But the writing is great and what brings us close to him is his relationship to two other main characters: the spoilt and difficult Amanda, who makes us understand -- by breaking his heart -- that his affections are not as superficial as we might imagine. The other is Georgie, a more edgy personality t, who challenges the young vicar with his good humored cynicism. There are many mysteries to solve in the series, but they seem more about bringing out moral and ethical choices than about solving crimes. Not having read the book I cannot say how well the filming of it reflects its ideas, but this series stands on its own as a worthwhile study of fully realized and dimensional people, working through relationships with each other. Absorbing and satisfying in myriad ways. Highly recommended.

history.review_title: ... the antics and improprieties of Sylvia [Rebecca Hall in fine form], that our sympathies lie with her long-suffering ...
history.text: The script telegraphs that we are supposed to be so offended by the antics and improprieties of Sylvia [Rebecca Hall in fine form], that our sympathies lie with her long-suffering husband Christopher Teigiens [Cumberbatch] and his suffragette sweetie [Clemens]. The problem with this is that in their few bedroom scenes together the chemistry between Tiegiens and Hall feels more real than what takes place between him and Clemens. The extra-marital romance simply fails to convince. Clemens character is so pure in her love for Christopher that it feels airbrushed, more articulated than felt. And his love for her seems feckless, though we are supposed to think it is his high-mindedness that keeps him from acting on it. To his credit, Cumberbatch lends substance to a character that might seem absurdly academic and repressed, and we grow to like him. But it is Hall who walks off with the movie. She displays more sensuality in a single turn of her head than her young rival can convey naked in bed with Silvia's husband. Bottom line: if you don't buy the affair, the series is without much to offer aside from the blood bath in the trenches and some great period piece costumes.

history.review_title: McAdams does a superb job of making it possible to believe she could go either way with a choice between a baffling husband or o
history.text: A disarming and surprising film. All characters thoughtfully cast. McAdams does a superb job of making it possible to believe she could go either way with a choice between a baffling husband or old love. Her children are drawn with more care than kids usually are, and we find ourselves paying more attention to what they are thinking. The privatized space aspect of the drama is sketchy, but believable enough. What makes it all work, however, is the artfully directed communications between the characters. The flirtation between Cooper and Stone is offbeat, quirky, sometimes hard to follow, and ultimately convincing. More than usual is asked of the audience to figure out what these two protagonists are thinking and saying. Communications between people are not scripted in the usual way. There is much conveyed with tone and body language. Much of this resonates with the backstory of the Hawaiian culture and its haunting music and story-telling dance movements. The silent husband has an eloquence of his own. But the scene in which the daughter discovers the truth about her real father is the most effective and demonstrates how much can be conveyed to another without words. This is not a movie for those who want the obvious. It forces the viewer to partake of a more subtle, more compassionate, version of human life and love.

Lovely acting but script doesn't quite scan. The idea that a paralyzed man would want to go to the wedding of his ex to best friend doesn't fit emotionally. This choice does, however, foreshadow his final solution to his problem. What William cares about most is his right to choose his destiny and, in his case, to martyr himself. Much of his reasoning is capsulated in a scene in which he reveals how much he loved his former life. This life, seen in bits of flashback, consisted largely of high risk sports activity and daring-do, at which he excelled when not busy with his career, not to mention a cushy role as son and heir of a castle owning dripping with money doting family. That such a lifestyle might make a man feel life in a wheelchair didn't quite 'cut it' is not surprising, nor an attitude confusing high achievement with self-knowledge. Despite being given every advantage money can offer in trying circumstances, not to mention the devotion of a bouncy Pollyanna from the other side of the tracks, he chooses to end his existence. One get the sense that he believes he has a right to make this decision the way he has a right to stay in five star hotels and select the best wine for dinner. For all his attractions -- and he is an attractive character despite his condition -- he fails to see that life is not something to toss aside, simply because there are others involved. What makes the film moving -- ironically -- is not the fate of the invalid but the deep love his parents have for him and the wonderful performance of the young woman who falls in love with him. The emotional struggles of these three characters ring true and clear, and restore a bit of the faith that the central character seems so unable to muster. What the film lacks is a moral message that is, in any way, inspired [though clearly the writer assumed we would respond differently]. William's gift to Ms. Clark -- in the form of some sort of trust fund -- falls terribly short of what she gives to him.

history.title: The Battle of Algiers: The Criterion Collection [Blu-ray]
history.text: Looking at this film from a purely artistic standpoint, there's no doubt this is truly a fine artwork. What is so hard to grasp is that it was done so realistically, so believably, that it's like watching real documentary or newsreel footage. No wonder the director had to include a statement that no such footage was used in his work. How could he achieve such incredible effects, with such large crowds of extras and nonprofessionals in supporting and leading roles? From this standpoint, this film is truly breathtaking--indeed, jaw dropping. He tried to make his work well balanced and was quite successful; it's fair to both sides and there's no particular political statement to be had. Only the tragedy and futility of war.

history.title: Rope [Blu-ray]
history.text: The amazing thing here is that Mr. Hitchcock actually created an experimental work, released to the public disguised as a standard film. It's not a whodunit--we see who the culprits are in the first scene. The only mystery is, are they going to get caught. More interestingly, breaking of the fourth wall is a genuine technical tour de force, with the camera(s) gliding past the seeming narrow doors gliding from living room to foyer to dining area in one smooth take. I also was aware of the ceilings that may have had to be swung away to provide for the technical crew. The drama kept the viewer's attention throughout, even with the limited "one room" set, with the close ups carefully placed for maximum impact. The cast was uniformly fine, working in perfect synch with one another. Hume Cronyn's adaptation of Arthur Laurent's script was smooth and balanced. Mr. Hitchcock had total control of the production, with everything from set to costuming worked to perfection. Finally, the technicolor lent a air of east side penthouse glamor to the otherwise sordid action of committing the perfect murder of "an 'inferior.'" A true classic worthy of multiple viewings.

history.title: Southside With You [Blu-ray + Digital HD]
history.review_title: This is a very sweet vignette of two young lovers before the they blossomed ...
history.text: This is a very sweet vignette of two young lovers before the they blossomed in real life into an internationally famous couple. Having the drama confined to a single evening's date on Chicago's south side nicely gives perspective and credibility to the enactment.. The fact that this is a work of art and not a documentary is to the production's credit, and creates an even more interesting film. The actors are all very capable and the writer did a careful job of researching his subject. Interest is maintained throughout and provides as fine a footnote to a U.S. President and his wife as can be expected.

history.title: The Hobbit Deluxe Edition (DVD)
history.review_title: A well done 2014 DVD release of a great old animation classic!
history.text: This review is for the Hobbit Remastered Deluxe Edition (2014). I point this out first, as it is annoying that Amazon chooses to mix in customer reviews for an older unrelated product versions with a new product release. This often quite unfairly drags down the ratings for the new product and is confusing to customers. Such is the case here, which explains so many of the negative reviews you will run across. The original made for TV film was released in 1978 using the animation standards of that time. If you have seen it on TV, VHS or older DVD releases since that time most likely you have seen rather fuzzy imagery of an aging animation classic film. This 2014 DVD release however has done a wonderful job of restoring the animation artwork and it looks much better then I remember viewing it many years ago. The colors are pretty vibrant. The voice, singing and sound effect quality is also fairly good as well. Some people have said that there are missing sound effects. I, or my wife who also viewed this release, cannot in all honestly say if that is the case here. We simply don’t remember the original TV release well enough to be able to say for sure. In any case, we didn’t feel that the lack of such sounds detracted from this film in any way when we viewed it. For a made for TV film the voice acting and casting was top notch and really added to the quality of the film. As an example, Richard Boone as the voice of Smaug was a stroke of genius! I believe that this is still IMHO the best film version of The Hobbit done to date and the closest to the original book – and yes, even taking in the abysmal Peter Jackson live action version films, which butcher the original book. My wife also feels that way as well. This is a fine old animation film that makes for wonderful family viewing. Until a better Blu-Ray version comes along I highly recommended this 2104 DVD version for the serious animation collector!

history.title: Shogun [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A great Blu-Ray release but no longer in episodic format
history.text: I previously had purchased the DVD version of this TV mini-series a few years ago and in comparison this 3 Disc Blu-Ray release version has much better sound and video. The video is very sharp and much more detailed. One drawback to this release however is that this 3 Disc version has been done as a single three part movie rather than in the original episodic format in previous DVD releases. As an example Disc 1 ends rather abruptly when Lord Toranaga walks into a room where Blackthorn is showing three ladies his sea chanty dance. Disc 2 ends in a similar manner. No fade out in either case at all. I much preferred the way it was done in the original DVD release, which was set up in a manner to how the episodes aired on TV rather than as a continuous movie broken into three parts. Another thing I noted is that the much sharper video tends to show some of the bad make-up used on many of the series background actors. As an example, you see on many of the Japanese actors the color difference between the real head skin and where they covered the hair with a skin applique rather than shave it to make them look like Samurai warriors. This difference is very glaring in some cases. The infamous helicopter shadow you see at the very beginning is surprisingly still there and you can also see the wall beams on the special effects tank where they filmed the Galley being swamped by a storm and Blackthorn rescuing Rodriguez. You have to wonder why they didn’t take care of these glitches during the restoration process, which would be a fairly simple matter to do. Apparently, they decided to preserve the original, warts and all, for this blue-ray release. Other than that, this is a very good Blu-Ray release of this grand old mini-series!

history.title: Red Dawn [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: An extremely well done film no matter what your politics may be!
history.text: This is without a doubt the finest film that John Milius has directed as of 2015. While most reviews to date fall in the ”love it or hate it” category, usually due to the politics of the reviewer, it is still an extremely well done film no matter what your politics may be. Being a retired senior U.S. Soldier myself, I have seen many war films over the years and have been critical of many of them due to their lack of authenticity and attention to detail. Even the famous film “Patton” suffers from this. When it comes to ground war films this film, and Kelly’s Heroes, are two that get it right for the most part. The Russian equipment and uniforms used in this film are very realistic and appropriate to the forces you see. As an example; the Russian tanks really do look and feel like the real thing and the three Hinds in the film look pretty darn close and have real impact on the screen, as you would expect from attack helicopter gunships. This film does not attempt to sugar coat in any way the reality of guerilla warfare, nor makes the characters on either side two-dimensional. War is a very human and personal thing and you feel that here. This film displays insurgency in all its ugliness and with all the consequences that come with it - for all sides. The main and supporting cast members in this film are top notch and the area around the city of Las Vegas New Mexico is highly scenic and a beautiful backdrop for the film, shown to great effect in this Blu-Ray version of the film. I highly recommended this film to you! BTW if you like this film, you will probably also like “Flight of the Intruder”, also done by Milius.

history.title: The Zero Theorem [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Not one of Terry's Gilliam's finer efforts - in fact downright disappointing!
history.text: I am a fan of Terry Gilliam’s films and have seen and owned many of them. His film work tends to be very inventive and original, albeit in an often quirky kind of way. I went into this film wanting to like it and found I just could not do so. This film went way beyond strange to almost bizarre at times. My wife’s reaction was even more negative. She flat didn’t like it nor could develop any interest in it at all. For my part, I kept waiting to make a connection and become engaged with the plot, and just couldn’t get there. This major problem is that this film reminds me more of interpretive art then a film at times. I saw this same problem with his other film “The Imaginarium of Doctor Parnassus” as well. The performance of the actors, especially Dave Thewlis, is way over the top and rather disappointing, even embarrassing at times. David’s scene in the cat suit is particularly memorable in this context. The only acting bright spot in this film was the performance of Melanie Thierry. It is unfortunate that Terry seems to have lost the ability to maintain a tight focus for his film plots and tends to let the plot wander all over the place, and the actors to improvise all they want, often to the detriment of the film. I hope Terry isn’t going to keep on in this style. If so, I probably will not continue viewing and purchasing his films. I am rating this film as a 2 star film and we are donating this film, as we did with the “Imaginarium of Doctor Parnassus” to our local library, since neither my wife nor I feel we will ever want to watch it again. Bottom line: not recommended.

history.text: Both my wife and I found it hard to like this rather depressing film. There is nothing likeable or engaging about the main characters at all. They are all rather shallow, narcissistic and as always, for a Woody Allen film, neurotic. If you are looking for honesty, gentleness, fidelity, loyalty and the other positive human traits you won’t find them here in this film. These type characters seem to be a trend in Woody’s movies lately, unfortunately. I remember when Woody Allen films were funny as well as neurotic. Now they are just depressing and neurotic. Now having said that, the actor’s performances in general were all rather good, especially from Cate Blanchett. There is some language but it is fairly constrained compared to many recent films I have seen and the sexuality stuff is kept to a minimum. There is no drug use in this film, which was nice to see for a change.

history.title: Alien [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Timeless classic blending sci-fi and the fear of 'The Other' that hides in the dark. Or in this case, the dark of space.
history.text: Fantastic film that has held up over time. Wonderfully shot with beautiful use of camera angles to propell the viewer into the story and get a real feel for not only the human element cast so far out into space, but the vastness of the space and the loneliness that surely must have enveloped the characters and that will envelop future space travelers. As the film evolves, this gives the viewer a real sense the isolation of the crew adrift on the sea of stars with a (at the time of the original film) mysterious and murderous intruder in their midst; a genuine alien in all respects. Yes, the tech depicted is dated, but this is really minimal and limited to some flashing lights on control panels and monochromatic screen displays which are quickly lost in the atmosphereic and cinimatic treat that the film provides (and in some ways adds to the feeling of being alone and detached from warm, earthly things). Also, compared to other sci-fi films of the same era there are no glaring fashion and hair style gaffs of the 70's (Battle Beyond the Stars or Star Wars, anyone?) which is just as important in allowing the film to stand the test of time. The commentary by the cast and by the director Ridley Scott add fantastic insight into how and why the flim was shot the way it was and how a film from 1979 can outshine many (dare I say most?) sci-fi films and stories of this modern era. All-in-all a true Masterpiece that has its haunting beauty brought into the 21st century with Blu-ray remastering.

history.review_title: More than just a clever title?
history.text: A very nice suprise as I had low expectations having been burned since the original in this franchise. A (mostly) tight plot, clever twists, well cast movie with a return of the 'original' terminator embracing more of the original depiction: i.e. no deliberate clever lines, no trying to be cute or clever. Exciting action sequences, of course, but more importantly character development. A must see if you are a fan of the Terminator series and perhaps the seed for a new 'genesis' of terminator movies?
Good intellectual bit of sci-fi.

The title says it all. Sort of. Women are funny, but female comics are not. The 'documentary' spends a lot of time with interviews and stand up footage, none of which is in the least bit humorous or funny (to me, at least). There is not very much investigative journalism, but to be fair I didn't expect it to be a serious documentary. Sadly, any film focused on comics and the world of stand up should at least make me laugh once, which this one failed to do.

So, I liked the cast. I also laughed out loud at some scenes. But the story has a meandering plot and different story lines that never weave together but travel near and far from each other. It opens with a wonderful and whimsical murder scene but devolves into the interaction of the principle characters that, again, never really mesh well. history.title: Piche Entre Ciel Et Terre

Justesse de ton, magnifique interprétation de Michel Coté et Maxime Leflaguais, très belles scènes d'avion... Un grand film québecois. Il serait bon que pour nous autres "Français de France" et sans doute les Canadiens anglophones qui veulent parfaire leur français, les films québecois soient systématiquement sous-titrés en français. Ces grands films québecois sont étonnamment méconnus en France et jamais ou presque disponibles en DVD Zone 2. la faute en est certainement à la France qui ne s'intéresse pas suffisamment à ces Américains pourtant cousins mais n'y a t il pas aussi une autre politique plus dynamique à l'export des responsables du film québecois. Un film comme Piché n'est nullement un film "régionaliste", il résume les aléas de l'ame humaine et devrait plaire à des spectateurs du monde entier.

And now this Season 4 Volume 2 is a big let down. It drags interminably before the death of Ragnar that occurs during the 5th episode and many characters come inexplicably from nowhere, adding nothing to the very dragging plot. Moreover, with the exception of Bjorn, Ragnar's sons seem to come directly from the fountain soda of a teenager party and actors are really poor, particularly Ivar the Boneless who perpetually winces to make sure he is a very very mean man. Lagherta makes her revenge but becomes unexpectedly a lesbian (?) while Floki seems fascinated by Algesiras'Mosque in a particularly grotesque scene. The final battles are way better and bring at last some driving action to the series. As the authors of those Vikings (Seasons 1-3 are very good) are for a 5th and 6th Season, let's hope it will be much better than this mostly poor 4th Season.

(Remember the maid who became a concubine of the prince was trying to get pregnant with a son because his wife couldn't seem to get pregnant so obviously a son born out of wedlock could inherit) 3- The prince looked old enough to rule, why was his mother regent? 4- Upon the death of the prince, why did the concubine's son automatically become Emperor? 5- Why did the concubine get away with killing the Emperor? 6- Why did the concubine kill the Emperor? He would have ensured her son's safety and was easily led. When she talked about doing anything for her son, I thought she meant she'd work the king. Instead she kills him with a zillion witnesses at the palace and zero of her family (remember the old queen had them all killed) to back her. I realize that due to the subtitles, much may have been lost. If anyone understood Korean and got the answers to these questions, I'd like to know; perhaps then I'd give it a better rating. As I said it was interesting.
