history.title: Planet of the Apes [Blu-ray]
history.text: My review title is in reference to the fact that the kind of self-pandering thought process that produced this film was exactly what the original movie was lampooning. Let me get right to the point. The Original: Heston plays a cynic whose eyes are perfect through which to view the Ape's world. His splendid outbursts reflects the audience's outrage at a world(our own) seemingly gone mad. The Remake: Wahlburg plays a generic action/adventure hero who reacts to his situation with all the emotion of someone who missed the "blue-light" special at Wal-mart. The Original: Features a bizarre but convincing Ape City built to scale. The Remake: Claustrophobic Ape City looks like a bad set from the old "Buck Rogers" TV show. Obvious CGI shots. The Original: Constant social commentary through-out as we view our own hollow social conventions, reliance on uninformed scientific conclusions, and unfounded notions of supremacy based on religious conceit. A plot as nihilistic as the theme. The Remake: More Hollywood political commentary about why guns are so evil that - stranded on a hostile world with pursuing hostile creatures - we are better off getting rid of any we have(!). A plot that "cleverly" tries to wrap up centuries of story set-up with a trite, time-loop cause and resolution. The Original: Moody directing with an epic feel topped off with a final scene that truly shocked audiences of the time. The Remake: Typical "summer-blockbuster" style direction with a finale that attempts to blend the ending of the original with the ending in the novel, and only serves to confuse the audience. Now, if you are truly a POTA fan, then you will watch this regardless (I would, and did). Just don't expect to like it very much. The emphasis is clearly on the sci-fi story rather than what made the original great, and the sad part is, this movie had an excellent cast that delivered excellent performances; the story just didn't allow most of them to shine. I say "most" because there is one reason to watch this: Tim Roth as General Ursus. His make-up as a chimp is absolutely phenomenal, for one, but his ability to emote through it and create a distinctive and convincing personality is just as astonishing. This movie is worth one viewing for that alone. If you are unfamiliar with the franchise, the only one you need to see is the original, as this one will give you the wrong impression that it is yet another shallow sci-fi potboiler. Not recommended, unless it pops up in some future incarnation of "MSK3000".

Over-the-top supposed "horror-comedy" that tries to make up for its lack of good material by throwing lots of 3-yr old level toilet humor at the viewer in the hopes that he won't notice that there is very little here. The various installments (shown as fictional drive-in features) have their moments, but each of them, about 20 minutes long apiece, go on about 15 minutes too long, like a good joke that goes stale fast. As a child, I loved watching the old Adam West "Batman" show, but when I saw it again as an adult, I quickly became annoyed at its unsubtle, in-your-face campiness. This movie reminds me of that experience, with its initial shock-value wearing off far too quickly, while oblivious film-makers carry on laboring under the delusion that what they are doing is "comedic" when, in actuality, it devolved into obnoxiousness long ago. The best one, I thought, was the B@W "Diary of Anne Frankenstein", with its mixture of truly bad taste and Hogan's Hero-esque humor. The '60-ish film look in the initial "Wadzilla" feature was well done (better than the actual story). The cast did a good job, so don't blame them, they aren't script-writers or directors. For fans of movies like "Evil Dead 2" or "Feast", don't expect anything here as there is absolutely no attempt to make an actual horror movie, just a miserably failed attempt at comedy.

history.title: Creature from the Hillbilly Lagoon
history.review_title: as there are so many butthurt fanboys trying to sound intelligent when they clearly have A) closed minds and B) ...
history.text: I've found that when it comes to B Horror flicks, one simply can't go by the reviews here on Amazon, as there are so many butthurt fanboys trying to sound intelligent when they clearly have A) closed minds and B) no conception of good film making. I just finished watching this movie on YouTube. It appears to have been videoed using someone's cell-phone while the makers saved their lunch money for a month to reach the budget. Nevertheless, it was a fun little romp. The script is fast moving and actually humorous at times (my favorite line is when they're trying to escape the monster and the truck won't start: "Deader than a whore's ass on Sunday!") while the monster suit is surprisingly well done. The performances are rather good for a grade C movie like this; I suspect that the cast members were mainly playing themselves. I also suspect that the actors were locals as, at times, a couple of them seem to forget that they are on camera and not on a stage before a live audience. But it's the casting that really makes the movie fun. Nothing great, but if you like monster flicks and want to have a smile from some people having fun making a cute little flick, I recommend this along with some beer and chips. More than worthy of 3 and a half stars, I give it a 5 just to counter some of the butthurt fan boys.

history.title: The Witch
history.text: After reading the various reviews where people call each other idiots depending on whether or not they liked this film, I just had to see it. I have to say, now that I've watched it, that the "idiots" are (mostly) on the side of the detractors of this movie. Now, don't get me wrong; obviously, no movie is for everyone. I can understand if someone who just doesn't like horror movies in general avoided this. Also, I ignore the "reviews" that are obviously written by 14 year old under-achievers ("this sucks/ it's boring/ I wasn't scared", etc.). What struck me was some comments made by people who were quite capable of meticulously expressing themselves. One reviewer said that the movie lacked any "visceral scenes". Really??! Did this reviewer see a highly edited version or something? There were several "visceral scenes" in the movie that, unlike, say a "Saw" movie, actually had a realistically mature context to them that made them truly disturbing, unlike "Saw" where it's just some throw-away splatter to make the 12 year olds go "ooohh!". No, this movie was not a gore-fest, not because it shied away from that sort of thing, but because it was actually telling a story, which brings me to my next comment. Another reviewer thought that the movie lacked any real plot. I don't understand this one, as there is always something going on in this film, just not explosions and car chases. Every scene either adds to the mounting fear or shows the dissolution of the family as things go from bad to worse. It's just that that sort of plot has an entirely different focus than some juvenile super-hero movie. I think that particular reviewer was more jaded that he/she realized. Yes, it is slow at times, but creep-outs can't be rushed. It's only action or suspense movies that should have a break-neck pace. It DOES require some imagination on the part of the viewer to place themselves in the protagonists' shoes. Sadly, I think too many in our society can't empathize with anyone who doesn't look, talk or think like a typical mall shopper, no matter how well acted, and the performances in this film are truly excellent. While it's true that the real idiots are in Hollywood for advertising this as if it were some air-headed "Jason" or "Chucky"-type trash (see "the Hunter" with Willem Defoe, a graceful outdoor drama falsely advertised as a conspiracy thriller; it does involve a conspiracy, but that is not the focus, or "the Tall Man" with Jessica Biel, a very good suspense twister that was panned by 14 year olds because it was advertised like a horror film, or the excellent "Ravenous", a quirky and unique thriller about cannibals that was described to seem like a "Hills Have Eyes" type B flick, but I could go on....), I don't feel that it absolves the viewer of the responsibility to be open-minded when viewing a film. We've all been disappointed by movies that weren't as advertised, so why do we insist on casting our minds into the frame that the advertisers tell us we should? In fact, the above mentioned "the Tall Man" turned out not being what I was hoping it was, but it was so well done that I chose to be pleasantly surprised and enjoy it rather than sulk in groundless disappointment. Now, it's almost impossible to give examples of the previous points without spoiling it. Other reviews here will have given the reader the general idea of the movie. It is far more character driven than filled with cheap plot devices. My only criticism is that the ending seemed to me more akin to what one might see in one of the B films this movie tries to rise above. Other than that, I highly recommend this to lovers of something different, artistic or moody. Also to those who have some imagination and can let themselves be creeped out for entertainment's sake. If you're looking for non-stop action or mind-twisting mysteries, look elsewhere.

history.title: Rift, The (1990) aka Endless Descent
history.text: I'm actually giving it one (or two) more stars than it really deserves just for the cool cast. Nonsensical plot (what little there is) and really, really cheap FX is what sinks (haha) what could have been a fun little flick. Reminded me of a bad episode of the old "Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea" TV show, but at least "Voyage" had cool visuals. These monsters look really rinky dink, like little hand puppets. I don't think it was even filmed in actual water. Maybe it would have worked better if they had kept the setting in outer space as originally scripted. Oddly, though, I want to see it again for some reason.

history.title: Iron Man 3 [Blu-ray]
history.text: This is perhaps the second best Marvel superhero film after "the Winter Soldier", though I actually have yet to see "Civil War" so that rating could change. It is, however, the best of the three Ironman films by far. Now, some reviewers have expressed anger because of a plot twist about halfway through. Why? I thought it was pretty clever. I fail to understand why this would be angering to anyone. Aside from a few fanboy grumblings over some detail being different from the comic or whatever, this film is filled with heart as well as spectacle, and is a terrific culmination of the trilogy. No denying that it is a Robert Downey, Jr. vehicle through and through, so if you're a fan, you will be in hog heaven (as they say). Also, I didn't find the little kid annoying at all. In fact, he didn't play nearly as big a role as some reviewers seem to indicate.

history.title: Batman v Superman: DOJ 2-Disc (DVD)
history.text: Upon my first viewing, I thought this movie was "good enough". Just having watched it a second time, I found it MUCH better. In fact, it is probably the best superhero movie made so far. But, be warned: this one is very heavy unlike almost all of the rather lighter Marvel Comics fare, so if simple adventure is your thing, this may not be for you. I'll forego the synopsis as the title says it all. What surprised me was the absolute dark nature of the story. Despite pointless comparisons to the Christopher Nolan Batman films, Affleck does a great job playing Batman/Bruce Wayne derived directly from Frank Miller's "the Dark Knight Returns"; they even do a phenomenal job of making the Batman look like he jumped from the pages of that graphic novel, though the way he was depicted in it was never my favorite. Anyway, Affleck's Batman is an aging, cynical and angry one, disillusioned with a corrupt world and feeling he must accept that, for all his efforts, nothing is better and he will leave behind no legacy. Cavill is excellent as Superman/Clark Kent once again, but, this time, as opportunistic politicians and the media-incited masses protest his interventions on their behalf, his character starts to doubt himself. Their enmity towards each other (sparked and fueled by Lex Luthor's manipulations) is motivated by flip sides of the same coin that represent the basic nature of each character: Superman's because Batman doesn't "play by the rules", and Batman's because his cynical nature makes him believe that if Superman CAN destroy the world, he eventually WILL as the inevitable corruption sets in. This is further expressed by Luthor when he states, "....if God is all powerful, then he can't be all good." Although many have compared the theme of this movie to Marvel's "Captain America: Civil War", here, it goes deeper than the politics, touching on the battle between Man's duel nature, each side represented by the antagonistic heroes (Superman as the light and Batman as the dark). In the end, the two must co-exist in order to survive. This film even hints that the battle is representative of our aspirations to the divine vs our human vulnerabilities (Lex at one point describes the impending fight as "God vs Man"). This might seem pretty heavy stuff for a comic book story, but comics have been compared to the ancient Greek myths, so maybe it's actually fitting; only symbolism and allegory can do such lofty themes justice. The editing is relentless and the script tightly written. Special mention must go to Hans Zimmer's outstanding musical score. Aptly brooding to match the tone of the film, it soars to apocalyptic heights with, occasionally, a quiet dollop of his "Man of Steel" theme as a sad echo of a once hopeful past. The first time I watched it, I thought that, rather than a movie about both characters, it was more like a Batman movie in which Superman just guest-starred. The dark nature of the film further highlighted this impression, as Superman seemed rather lost and almost helpless in this grim view of the World. Upon a second viewing, I realized that, although we see primarily from Bruce Wayne's perspective, everything revolves around Superman, and not just through his actions, but because of his very existence. And, in the end, it is Superman's final sacrifice that rekindles the dying embers of hope, not only in Bruce Wayne, who finds a new mission, but in the populace as well. Although the movie was a financial success (though not attaining quite what the makers had hoped), many critics panned it, and legions of fanboys, outraged that it didn't slavishly follow some comic book story line or their limited perceptions of characters who were published long before they were born, trashed the film in a butt-hurt frenzy. As for the general audience looking for the typical feel-good but ultiimately shallow fare, they enjoyed the spectacle, then shrugged their shoulders and moved on. I guess nobody expected a movie based off of comic book characters to have this much depth. Also, it could be a little confusing unless one was very familiar with the characters (for instance, how many general movie goers know that Superman derives his strength from our yellow sun?). This is sad, as it will probably result in Warner Brothers not taking a risk to attempt anything that doesn't toe the party line when it comes to their comic book franchises. But, the film stands as a testament to Zack Snyder's talent at bringing his vision successfully to the screen. Highly recommended, just remember to set your sights above where they normally go for this genre if you want to truly "get" it.

history.title: Last Supper [DVD + BLU-RAY COMBO]
history.text: Just had to write a review after reading some of the brain-dead ones on this page. No, this is not some cheap, stupid chop-socky flick. In fact, the only time any "Kung Fu" is used is in a scene where some villagers briefly get the drop on some soldiers, but are quickly subdued by the armed and armored troops as, in reality, Shaolin martial arts are a myth, most kung fu styles were civil boxing styles used by peasants and we don't really know what martial arts were used by Chinese soldiers as they died out from lack of use with the advent of firearms No, this is a serious drama, well acted, beautifully filmed and interestingly directed; Jackie Chan fans need not apply. Told from different points of view, it did become a little confusing to me at one point. Also, a westerner might find him or herself a little aloof to the goings ons due to subject matter, but when the movie wraps itself up at the end, I found it unexpectedly emotional. Better directed than scripted, the movie ends greater than the sum of its parts. Recommended for lovers of good foreign films and realistic historical movies.

history.title: Hammerhead
history.review_title: it wasn't quite as stupid as most of the others
history.text: Although this seems to be a Syfy original, it wasn't quite as stupid as most of the others. Now, it IS an attempt to make a "B" monster flick in the late '50s-early '60s style, but this one actually tries to recreate that atmosphere rather than just moronically spoof them like most of their others. Jeffery Combs does his usual hamming as a mad scientist who's created a half-man/half-shark creature that runs amok on an island on which is trapped a boatload of victims. The monster is CGI in underwater scenes, but practical FX on land (though sparingly shown). Like any good drive-in movie, it has momentary lapses in logic and formulaic dialogue but has the saving grace of being done with a straight face. If you like Roger Corman films, or movies like "the Killer Shrews" and "Humanoids from the Deep", you'll find this one's ok, though not great. If you're expecting Ridley Scott, go elsewhere. It was good enough to add to my collection along with "Attack of the Killer Crabs" and "Mad Doctor of Blood Island". Recommended with a six pack and a burger with fries, to go.

history.title: Interstellar
history.text: OK, overall, this movie was enjoyable and definitely worth seeing. So, why only 3 stars? One star detracted for: a story with so much hard, realistic science, the plot device that everything depends on to happen falls into the category of "alien magic". Another star detracted for: this film strives mightily to be original, yet, I saw a season 6 episode of "Star Trek - Voyager" made years earlier that was based on almost the exact same premise and was, in some ways, more poignant. I hate it when someone comes up with a good, original idea that gets credited to some bid budget feature that came along later with a lot more hoopla. Keeping these 2 points in mind, this movie IS recommended.

history.title: Chimes at Midnight (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.text: I used to think the Criterion company could do no wrong when it came to their releases; they nearly always offer the very best quality when it comes to the video/audio of the films themselves, and their bonus goodies are a plus that gives the title of being the cream-of-the-crop when it comes to home video releases. Lately (within the past couple of years), however, instead of always including a standard booklet of notes about the films--one that you read like an ordinary book by turning the pages--the CC has began to put their notes on the back of a poster that requires completely opening up to its full size and makes you read it like it some kind old-timey proclamation. This is beyond annoying. And what's even worse is the "art" for these posters is done by whatever in-house "artists" are employed by Criterion, and to call these scrawlings "art" is an insult to all the real artists in the world who actually produce works worthy of hanging on a wall. And that's another thing...even if these poster-booklets DID have something on the poster side that people thought was good enough to "hang" on their wall or otherwise display (for me personally, it would be the theatrical one-sheet used for the original release of the film), how many film purists who buy Criterions are going to devalue the collectability of their item by tacking a poster to their walls? Yes, maybe some, but I think they'd be in the minortiy as I would bet most Criterion collectors keep their cherised titles in pristine condition. Criterion--STOP with these stupid posters on the back of the notes immediately! And, yes, I am reviewing the PRODUCT not the film itself (which I consider great, btw). I'm not one of these AMZ dime-store Eberts who needs to blather about how much I loved or hated a film. That information can be found elsewhere on countless sites on the net. AMZ is a marketplace where people come to purchase PRODUCTS, and the quality of said products deserve mention, not the subjective worth of the item itself. That's what I read reviews on here for...if you can't appreciate that, then suck it.

history.review_title: Universal's cheapness omits Kansas song at climax of film
history.text: Universal Studios are some of the biggest tightwads on the planet when it comes to production of their films and subsequent video releases of their titles...and they certainly prove that true in the case of this film where they were too cheap to pony up for the music licensing fee to be able to include Kansas' song "Carry On Wayward Son" at the very conclusion of the film. I can understand and even concede that sometimes when an existing song merely appears as background music during a scene the decision to exclude it can be justified...but when a song is an integral part of a film and makes a statement or provides the mood for an entire story, then it has to--no--it MUST be included. I think TV showings of this film still use the original edit of the film...I'll have to look around on the "grey market" to find a copy. history.text: This is a review of the blu-ray On the plus side, I don't think I've ever seen a 1915 film look this good. For the age, the quality is staggering. history.title: Sting of Death [DVD]
history.review_title: Mediocre Program, Poor Quality Picture, Burned DVD-R
history.text: This appears to be a British TV show (though it may be an American Broadcast as the box states; all the actors & the style are British). I don't "get it", & also am having trouble with the accents. While this is not stated, based on the acting styles & the often painted fake backgrounds, I believe it is a TV film of a British play. The histrionic acting style of the play does not fit Karloff at all well (& I do enjoy both his horror roles & his his non-horror roles such as Colonel March & Mr Wong). As the Thriller episode is available on the Image box set, I am not going to comment on that. The picture Quality is fair; it's obviously from a worn Kinescope that has likely seen 1 or 2 VHS generations & appears to me to have also once been an avi (some pixelation). The aspect ratio is also slightly off; bodies appear a bit tall & thin in some places, & a bit short & fat in others. Most importantly, it was burned on extremely low quality media. While they used Verbatim dye, it is bottom of the barrel Verbatim. Using a Nero software error scan, I got a score of 84, with 9900 PI failures. I consider the minimum acceptable score to be 95, with less than 400 PI Failures. I strongly suggest if you buy this, make a back up. I consider this a defective dvd-r (due to Alpha's bad choice of media), & it will only get worse over time. Only for Karloff completests.

history.title: The Old Dark House [Blu-ray]
history.text: I am reviewing the Cohen blu-ray. Absolutely stunning restoration. Completely blows the old Kino/Image dvd out of the water. Iconic pre-code film with Boris Karloff's first named starring role (his 1st film after Frankenstein) & a very young & somewhat slim Charles Laughton. The drastically improved picture quality makes it much creepier than the Kino. For those who are Rocky Horror fans, while that film paid tribute to numerous classic horror & sci-fi; I've always felt that ODH had the biggest influence on Rocky Horror of any of them. Very highly recommended. This is my 4th Cohen; & quality wise may very well have the best quality of the bunch. If you are a fan of Karloff, classic horror or pre-code films; buy this. It's that simple. Even if you have the Kino already, this is so much better it's almost like watching a different film.

First season i was able to put aside my knowledge of the actual history and enjoy the fun. But second season! They are so horrifyingly far away from the actual characters... Madame de Montespan was a splendid beauty, a vivacious bon vivant, sponsor and patron of the Arts, who kept a menagerie of exotic and mundane animals (including a bear) in her extensive quarters, and was very much loved by many... & very much hated by others! NOT the depressed dimwit of the show who apparently only has one room- a bedroom, and one dress In real life, the Queen never learned to speak French well, she was shy and retiring and considered to be somewhat retarded due to inbreeding. Louis himself was quite affable & genial, an extroverted exhibitionist and another bon vivant. The paranoid, frightened dork they've made him into... almost unbearable. And another thing! The women wear the same dress all the time. One always wears pink, another blue, another (Queen) wears red and Madame de Montespan wears bile green.

On the other hand, the leading lady is gorgeous, sexy, and vulnerable. The villain, also, is perfectly evil. These three actors do a very good job of driving the plot to its inevitable conclusion. history.title: Be Yourself
history.review_title: The real Fannie in an okay movie with several musical highglights
history.text: Early in "Be Yourself," which was made in 1930, someone tells Fannie Brice, "You know, you're a funny girl." That she is, playing a nightclub entertainer in love with a boxer. The songs are so-so, except for "I'm Cookin' Breakfast for the One I Love," the film's comic highlight. But you get to see the original Funny Girl mugging, singing songs both dramatic and antic and wearing period clothes elegantly. This was a lady who had style, who knew how to use every talent she had at her disposal and brother, she had plenty. She almost never walks out of frame without a funny look, as if she doesn't want a dull frame in the picture. A bit hokey-poky, but who cares when you're watching one of the great entertainers of the twentieth century?

history.title: Marlowe
history.review_title: Cool Updating of Raymond Chandler's "Marlowe" character
history.text: This under-appreciated 1969 update of Raymond Chandler's "The Little Sister" should have been more successful than it was. James Garner isn't an intense Philip Marlowe, he's more a cool, laidback private eye, in his "Rockford Files" style. But the story is solid, the screenplay is by the excellent Stirling Silliphant and there are three great leading ladies: beautiful Gayle Hunnicutt, bitchy young Sharon Farrell (whatever happened to her?) and Rita Moreno as a stripper in a blonde wig. Also, a parade of great character actors: Carroll O'Connor, William Daniels, Jackie Coogan and -- surprise, surprise -- Bruce Lee in a knock-out two scenes. In the last one, he makes the most dramatic exit from a movie since Agnes Moorehead in "Dark Passage." Directed by a major TV talent -- Paul Bogart -- who should have had the same kind of movie success that one-time TV director Norman Jewison did.

history.title: Lady of Burlesque
history.review_title: Backstage Burlesque comedy-mystery with Barbara Stanwyck and lots of great character actors
history.text: Burlesque, not the way it really was, but the backstage atmosphere, wisecracks and mystery from Gypsy Rose Lee's novel "The G-String Murders" make it worth your time. (The book is more complicated, with several twists at the end that aren't here, but isn't that always the case with books turned into movies?) Star Barbara Stanwyck began as a dancer on Broadway and her challenge dance with Pinky Lee to cover up a backstage brawl is astonishingly good. This babe could could do it all! The cast is wonderful: Michael O'Shea as Rags Ragland-type comic,the hilariously sublime Iris Adrian as Stanwyck's gal pal, Stephanie Bachelor as "The Princess Nirvina," J. Edward Bromberg as the cop investigating the crimes, Gerald Mohr as a gangster and glorious, lisping blonde Marian Martin as the danseuse Pinky Lee fancies. Stanwyck gets a funny, gritty song: "Take it Off the E-string, Play it on the G-String." This is a movie I can -- and do -- watch again and again.

history.review_title: Boogey Man Burlesque Great family fun
history.text: A classic horror spoof, in which Bud and Lou tangle with the Frankenstein Monster (Glenn Strange), Dracula (Bela Lugosi, playing the vampire for the last time on film) and The Wolf Man (Lon Chaney Jr.). Costello sitting in the Monster's lap, the plot calling for Lou's brain to be transplanted into the Monster's skull and the Wolf Man's travails when the moon is full, delight fans no matter how many times they see this Boogey Man burlesque. Some cool, if rudimentary special effects involving Dracula, are both hokey and spookey. Great for both adults and kids. Get the popcorn popping and gather the whole family around for this one.

Stanwyck has played the Lady-in-Jeopardy well in other films, but never one as nutty and lame as what we have here.

Rather unpleasant unless you get into the nasty spirit of the piece. A good double feature would pair "The Two Mrs. Carrolls" with "Conflict." In both, Bogie's lusting after Alexis Smith at her freshest and most alluring.

history.title: Sailor Moon S:S3Pt1 LtdEd (BD Combo)
history.text: So by now we all know that Viz Media's remastering of the show is quite controversial. They saturate colors and use a technique called DNR (digital noise reduction) to help make the show look cleaner and smoother, but as a result, take away from image detail, as well as create new digital imperfections that weren't present in the masters. To see what the show SHOULD look like, watch the clean opening bonus feature, as it was not put through their remastering process, and the image is the most honest representation of the show's originally-intended esthetic. But at this point I didn't purchase this set expecting anything new, as it's our fifth time at the rodeo. I will say that the ghosting issues present in the first three releases are gone - it's just a shame it was ever there to begin with. As for the color saturation, it seems to have been done to a less jarring degree. The show originally had a very soft palette, but in an attempt to make it look more vibrant, the colors have been saturated a bit - and even though I know it wasn't the original intention, the colors don't look bad this time around. Unfortunately I can't say the same for image detail. Many lines are quite jagged as a result of their remastering process, and the new digital imperfections that came about as a result of trying to rid the image of film/video tape grain, are very obvious. I watch TV on both a 55" 4K Ultra HD TV and a 42" 1080p HD TV, both have been calibrated with the Spears and Munsil Benchmark disc so that colors, contrast, sharpness, etc are as close to possible as the professional industry standard used by filmmakers and movie theaters. The general consumer uses a TV right out of the box, which means that the settings are FAR from industry standards, resulting in oversaturated colors, sharpness and the dreaded 'soap opera' effect that makes the content you're watching look like a low-budget adult film. So anyone without a calibrated television that is over 32" is going to probably be appalled at the picture quality on these Blu-ray discs. I for one don't like watching these discs on our 4K TV. The size and added resolution do nothing but highlight the faults of Viz's remastering process, and I find myself so distracted that I can't enjoy the show. I decide to watch them on my smaller, 1080p TV instead. And even though I can still pick out the boogers, they are much less noticeable. It's unfortunate because I have watched both the Ranma 1/2 Blu-ray sets as well as Dragon Ball Z Dragon Box DVD's on my 4K TV, and they are GORGEOUS. The problem with this show is that Viz was given videotape masters instead of film masters, so I get that it won't look as good as the two aforementioned programs. But having digitized VHS tapes by upverting to 1080p at home, I know for a fact that Viz could have done a better job using less money and tampering - they just don't have the right minds handling the process. And while there's the small issue of seeing the tape marks at the top/bottom of the screen during scene transitions on the original Sailor Moon S DVD's, they still had a more detailed image with more accurate color representation. The real reason I buy these sets is for the dub. While the old voices will always hold a place in my heart, I've really enjoyed the new cast and always wanted a consistent dub for the entire series. So at the end of the day this set isn't without its merits, but I'm not going to lie and say the image is "perfect" or "the best it's ever looked/could look" because that's just not the truth, and I know so from personal experience of digitizing videotape masters myself. My advice? Calibrate your TV('s) using the Spears and Munsil Benchmark Blu-ray or the Disney World of Wonder Blu-ray, and you will get the best image from not only these discs, but from any source you are watching on your TV.

history.title: Fantastic Beasts (Blu-ray 3D+BD)
history.text: I'm an avid collector of films on the Blu-ray 3D format, and watch them on our LG OLED 4K TV with passive 3D technology. Having seen so many films in the format, I can confidently say that this is EASILY one of the best presentations out of my entire collection. Warner Brothers has really used the format to immerse you in the Wizarding World and make you feel like you're a part of all the action and adventure. If you've been looking for a great 3D disc to add to your collection, or have a 3D TV that you haven't quite enjoyed yet, this is a fantastic addition to your collection. My only complaint is that aside from some quick-moving newspaper headlines in the opening sequence, Grindelwald is never properly introduced - leaving anyone who hasn't read the books either recently or at all, in the dust. It's nothing a quick Google search can't fix, but I can see a lot of people feeling a bit lost by the end of the film and skipping any future sequels as a result.

history.title: Miss Hokusai [Blu-ray]
history.text: If you have knowledge of the manga or titular artist and knowledge of Japanese religious and superstitious culture, then this is for you. But as one can imagine, that won't be most people. The film is episodic to a fault and feels disjointed from the get-go. This plays out like a bunch of short films strung together, never having an overall plot or even bothering to utilize many of the characters and plot elements it introduces. The trailer, good reviews and synopsis on the back on the case really had me confident that this was going to be awesome, and it was a bit of a snooze. It's pretty to look at and the sound design is fantastic, but the script is a boring mess that never delivers.

history.title: Prometheus [Blu-ray]
history.text: I have a VERY large collection of films on Blu-ray 3D and this is hands-down my favorite (I watch them on an LG 4K TV with passive 3D technology). Not only does it supplement the original "Alien" films VERY well (I just binged them all), but the production value and amazing use of 3D really make this movie the benchmark for modern sci-fi films. Many fans of the original films were disappointed, and I really can't imagine why. This film was obviously a labor of love and if nothing else, is stunning to look at from beginning to end. Top that off with a great cast and tons of suspense, action and gruesome aliens - you're in for one heck of a ride. If you're a fan of 3D, this is a must-own - and if you're a fan of the original "Alien" films, even more-so.

history.title: The Boss Baby [Blu-ray]
history.text: I have a diverse Blu-ray 3D library, and while DreamWorks films aren't always my priority when it comes to beefing up my collection - I have yet to be disappointed. It's hard to think of a DreamWorks 3D presentation that is sub-par, so I'm never shy about skipping a film in theaters, but picking it up to watch at home instead. The Boss Baby is no exception to that rule - it uses 3D in a beautiful, fun way that really immerses you into the imaginative world of the movie. I had fairly low expectations going in, and I'm happy to say that I was very pleasantly surprised. I recommend this title for anyone who wants to add a silly animated film with a stellar 3D presentation to their library. It's certainly not a Disney film, but that doesn't mean it isn't a lot fun. 👶🏼

history.title: Red Sonja
history.text: Picked this up at the request of my husband, but was concerned that the imported disc may not play in the U.S. Thankfully that wasn't an issue and the movie played just fine. We watched it on a calibrated 4K LG OLED TV and it looked quite good considering the film's age and probably man-handled masters. It's a campy fantasy adventure with a bit of silly violence, and some shirtless Arnold - with a bit of She-Ra & He-Man sensibility thrown in for good measure. If that sounds like you're kind of thing, I say check it out. ;D

history.title: IMAX: Flight of the Butterflies [4K UHD]
history.text: I watched this film on Netflix, but I was really excited to see it in 3D - and wow, what an upgrade! It's the definitive version of the movie and even though it's not feature-length, it really does impress. It's a great way to show off a nice 3D display without committing to a long Hollywood Blockbuster - and it's also a very interesting story to boot. Definitely pick this up if you're looking to add a beautiful nature documentary to your Blu-ray 3D collection. Kudos to Shout Factory for packaging the 4K UHD and 3D discs in one package - major studios should follow that example. I definitely plan to pick up the other 3D films in this collection.

history.title: 300: Rise of an Empire (Blu-ray 3D + Blu-ray + DVD)
history.text: The 3D presentation isn't terrible, but if you hold no nostalgia for the first film, this will be hard to sit through. I guess I'll tackle each topic one at a time. The 3D presentation is fun and helps makes this photorealistic, special-effects fantasy come to life. One gimmick that happens a bit too much is the splattering of precipitation and/or blood on the fourth wall. Used sparingly it could have been fun, but after a while it's a bit too expected and worn out. But there are plenty of great scenes with beaming streams of light, ambient dust and underwater action that look gorgeous. It's not the kind of movie you'd pop on to show off your TV to house guests (find a good bunch of nature documentaries for that), but for an enthusiast of the format, it's among the better presentations in the genre. The movie itself is absurd, and takes full advantage of its R rating in tasteless ways. If you didn't like the first movie, you won't like this one - and if you did, you still might be disappointed. This one is strictly for those who want more backstory to the original film and a ridiculous conclusion to the story. Casual viewers won't find much here, but die-hard fans with have a good chuckle watching this all unfold. Be warned, it starts out with a solid thirty minutes of exposition.

history.title: Roger & Me (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: How to catch a LIAR in the act
history.text: This flick provides insight as to why Flint, Michigan is the failure it is today. Yes, Michael Moore is a sloppy, overweight, trickster. But, similar to TV detective "Columbo" - he uses that disguise to cause the bad guys to dismiss him, without consideration of his potential skill, at their own peril. You see, in order to catch a bad guy (Corporate America, in this case), you need camouflage. Admit it, everybody takes their foot of the throttle, when they see a cop car with a rack, right? Even if they're not speeding. It's simply human nature. So the best way to hunt the speeders, is with an unmarked car. Wouldn't you agree? In his debut successful film, Michael Moore must resort to concealed 8mm cameras hidden in a briefcase. That's why the look of his films appear "unprofessional". But it is how he catches the "liars" at their game; spitting out 75mph lies in a 25mph zone.

history.title: The Dead Room [Blu-ray]
history.text: There are ultimately no surprises here - we've seen the paranormal investigators gig before, and none of the plot developments are new - but this is nonetheless a reasonably decent haunted house story. Highlights include a cast of competent actors, and the unusual element of their being only three characters in the entire movie. use of sound effects is also effective, and the fact that the filmmakers made the very intelligent choice to NOT go with the found footage/first person recording format, which the first Blair Witch did well and none of those who have since turned it into a cliche have done effectively. Note: some web reviews have complained that Dead Room leaves too much unexplained. No. This would only be true for those who are really unfamiliar with ghost stories or ghost flicks. Dead Room doesn't explain or show everything precisely because the filmmakers knew that most viewers would be familiar with ghost story tropes. Their bothering to offer all kinds of exposition would be like a new vampire movie wasting time explaining that vampires don't like crucifixes and the way to kill one is putting a stake through its heart. Why both when everyone watching already knows? The movie shows the viewer everything they need to know. Expecting further explanations is missing the point. So: if you like ghost flicks, you might want to rent this (I don't think it's worth buying). It does not compare to the original version of The Haunting, or other more contemporary ones like Darkness Falls, but it's worth a look.

history.title: The Great Wall [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Best action fantasy movie since Lord of the Rings
history.text: Above-average action movie dialogue, even a bit of character development, and very solid chemistry among all of the actors. Others have commented on the special effects. Some of the CG is a little soft, but the effects are indeed very, very good, and coupled with the production design and cinematography, they contribute to a rich, beautiful tapestry, exploding with colors. The film obviously owes a lot to the Lord of the Rings trilogy, and yet even though a lot of the action and battle sequences seem familiar, the creative team none-the-less manages to distinguish them from LOTR's. In addition, while the score certainly cannot hold a candle to the LOTR's, it is nonetheless a wonderfully effective epic score, and adds an important element to the film. One final note: it is really nice to see an action movie that does not waste time on a two-dimensional romantic subplot. Men and women are complete equals in this film, and to the extent that there is a gender plot, it emphasizes men and women working alongside each other for a common goal, with mutual trust and respect.

A fun, suspenseful ride. The acting is sometimes over the top, characters make dumb choices on a few occasions, some of the action toward the end is too by the numbers, and some of the stylistics, makeup FX, and set pieces toward the end too derivative of Hellraiser and Jacob's Ladder. That said, still a solid 3 star movie for fans of Lovecraft and Clive Barker. One final point: some have complained that the very ending is too oblique, or asked "What the heck is 'the void' anyway"? The answers to these questions will be readily apparent to anyone paying attention, and certainly to anyone who understands the worlds Lovecraft, Barker, and Carpenter (a la In the Mouth of Madness). The final shot of the movie is a superb coda to what comes before.

I generally dislike faux documentaries, and, with the exception of the original Blair Witch, I despise found footage or similar movies; but this one is simply superb. Savageland is cleverly written, masterfully edited, and if you didn't know better it would be a while into it before you'd realize it wasn't a real documentary. It uses genuine documentary techniques, and key roles are played by people who actually function in the given capacity in real life (e.g., a real life reporter plays the reporter, a professional photographer plays a photographer consulted for the purposes of discussing the role of photos that are at the heart of the "documentary," and so on. The tone of Savageland is creepiness, more than straight out horror, per se, which is a good thing. There's also a compelling but not overpowering social commentary dimension that is so cleverly woven into the form and content of the movie that it does not detract from the creepiness or horror. On the contrary, this aspect enhances the creep factor because it is so true to life. Horror is perfectly fine as horror, and I do not believe films that don't convey some kind of "message" are somehow less valuable than other movies. However, this film does provide an excellent example of how horror cinema can be filled with meaning or used to convey a message, and do so while still fulfilling the other imperatives of the genre; that is to say, providing creepy, compelling entertainment.

history.title: Jigoku (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.review_title: Worth watching at least once for fans of Japanese horror
history.text: While acknowledging the historical importance of this film, and it's apparent impact on subsequent, modern Japanese horror directors, it does not stand up as well as the Ghost of Yatsuya and Kwaidan. In the first half we see the sins and debauchery, and the second half we see various depictions of hell. It all seems more symbolic and allegorical than anything. It is horrific, but not scary or creepy, so don't go into it expecting the latter. Nonetheless, it's an interesting movie, even if not as interesting, entertaining, are beautiful to look at as the other two I've mentioned above. It's most redeeming quality consists of the wonderful sets and use of color in the second half or so. That alone makes it worth a look, not to mention the interesting aspect of seeing what many consider to be the precursor of modern Japanese horror cinema. Any aficionado of J-horror or Asian horror in general really should check Jigoku out at least once.

history.title: The Plague of the Zombies [DVD]
history.text: This movie is not only plagued with zombies, but lifeless production values and an anemic script. I do not say this lightly, as I am a fan of many Hammer horror movies. The Mummy, (The Horror of) Dracula, Brides of Dracula, Quatermass and the Pit: these are great horror and Sci-Fi movies. Plague of the Zombies simply doesn't measure up. Here are some reasons: Much of the film is supposed to take place at night, but the cinematography is truly abysmal; it's filmed day for night, and it shows. It is perfectly obvious the characters are walking around in slightly filtered sunshine instead of under "the full moon," as one of them claims. In some scenes blue, daylight sky is seen behind characters when it is supposed to be the middle of the night. Not only does this simply look cheap, but it utterly saps the scenes of any creepiness. An inexpensive filter over the lens would have improved things greatly, so even the low budget isn't an excuse. The makeup is cheap-looking, too. In a number of shots you can see that the zombie makeup essentially ends at the bottom of the jaw line, when it would have cost mere tuppence to bring it below the collarbone so the entire person would look zombified, not just the head. Even the Bernard Herrmann score is uninspired. The movie's only redeeming quality is Andre Morrell, who is very good, except in the climactic scenes, in which poor scriptimg has him acting like kind of an imbecile. The final nail in the coffin is the actor who plays his protege, whose name I will not even bother looking up for the sake of this review, who has absolutely no screen presence, and, it would seem, little capacity for acting. If you're familiar with Hammer movies, generally like them, and haven't seen this one, you're probably going to watch this anyway. If you're new to Hammer, start with the other ones I've listed above and introduce yourself to the studio by way of some of its greatest moments.

history.title: Ghost Train [DVD]
history.text: Friendship melodrama is not uncommon to J-horror, but is more tedious than usual in this movie. There is also little internal logic, as the movie seems to establish certain rules for itself, but then tosses them out toward the end. The climactic moments are kind of cool, but ultimately make no sense because they occur at the height of said breakdown of narrative logic. Additionally, and as an extension of the problems with the friendship melodrama, the movie frequently comes to a grinding halt with additionally tedious scenes that are extended well beyond what is necessary for providing information about the story, or what is effective for building suspense. I've seen worse, but Ghost Train is at the bottom of the heap insofar as J- and other Asian horror.

history.title: Blade Runner 2049 (Blu-ray) (BD)
history.text: A few editing missteps toward the end don't prevent BR49 from being a solid 5 star movie. I've also checked with some who weren't enamoured of the first film but who ended up enjoying the sequel. As you can tell from the fan reviews, most who love BR19 also love BR49. Now we just have to hope they don't go minimalist on Blue-ray bonus features. Update: Well, they went minimalist on bonus features. This movie deserved so much more in its Blu-ray release. What is here is very good {comma} insofar as some brief documentaries and the web shorts released prior to the film itself. They're just is not much of it.

history.title: Sicario
history.review_title: how not to write a whistle blower story (spoilers)...
history.text: Emily Blunt's character works as an anti-drug officer for a government agency (FBI?, don't remember which one). She's highly successful and apparently in charge of her unit. We enter the story as her team executes a drug bust which goes horribly wrong when, after the agents discover decaying corpses, and are in the beginning of their investigation, a bomb booby trap goes off when officers (not wearing gloves in an investigation) attempt to open a locked floor door, killing two officers. After this Emily Blunt's character is manipulated into volunteering on another team, being told the absolute minimum about her new team but meeting her supervisor who instructs her to watch, listen and learn. She is treated the opposite of how you'd treat a valued member of a team and basically ignored by the guy in charge. She accepts this though is clearly not happy with it. In going after a drug warlord she observes that her new team breaks all kinds of laws. This is not apparent to the audience because the film fails to show what the new team is supposed to be doing and it's only because Emily Blunt behaves as if there is a problem that we're told there is one, but we're not shown what the problems are. Time and again when she sees a problem she protests, only to be told basically to sit down and shut up, which she refuses to do. She is an employee and she volunteers for this duty but it apparently never occurs to her to not go to work, to resign, even though she disobeys direct orders from her supervisor and goes against the guidelines her new team lays down in the middle of an operation. I disliked this film because I didn't believe an officer would behave the way the Emily Blunt character behaves. For example, her new team does a bust of a character who is depositing drug money. Her supervisor tells her not to enter the bank and the Emily Blunt character disobeys his direct order, and the reason she gave was that they could get the drug dealer legally by building a case and she felt that instead of asking her supervisor why she was not to enter the bank, she just did as she wished. The writer did a very poor set up here, with her being filmed by the bank's video and then a hit being put out on her with a corrupt officer joining her and her friend for a drink at a bar. The hit would've worked if the Emily Blunt character had behaved believably but I just didn't find her character's willingness to disobey a direct order from a supervisor believable with an officer used to a military chain of command system. In real life just don't think she would've done what she did. In another instance, another character did something she apparently thought was illegal (still not sure what he did), and she raised her gun to him and he shot her though her vest protected her. The thing is, this character barely knew anything about what her new team was doing, they told her next to nothing and when she believed they were breaking the law she tried to stop them, but the story itself didn't show us what her team was doing that was so wrong. Unless you know drug law and drug enforcement policy law you won't be able to follow what she disapproved of, and that was a real problem in my opinion. Also, her new team screwed her over, something you could clearly see that was going to happen, but when the story actually revealed it, it was a surprise to the Emily Blunt character, but any audience would've seen that coming, they were obviously using her and by their treatment showed her her lack of value to them. I think the story held some interesting truths about the drug war, but it was so ineffectively told that I never got to emotionally enter the story. I also disliked the aerial shots and the music. The acting was great. My take on this story is, just as an ordinary citizen, if I were a drug enforcement officer and had been offered a job the way the Emily Blunt character was offered one, and had I been treated as the Emily Blunt character was treated as a non-member of her team, I would've resigned. She kept going back even though she kept protesting their procedures. The character was not bright enough. She smelled a set up but didn't want to believe it and so failed to protect herself. At the story's end, when they put a gun to her head to make her sign a piece of paper saying that they followed correct procedure, I was not at all surprised as they were pretty consistent throughout the movie. Very poorly told story. I'd give it one star except the acting was solid and the film was in focus so it deserves 2, but it really destroyed it's impact by being so poorly told. P.S. How to fix this story: (1) Show in the story why Emily Blunt's character is upset with the way her new crew does things. They were breaking the law. Show us what they should've been doing; (2) Completely change her character's behavior with regard to her new crew. Have her join the crew against her will. Have her not jeopardize the mission and potentially the lives of her crew by taking action in the middle of a mission. Do not have her entering the bank after her boss tells her not to. If she must enter the bank and be photographed, have her do so before her boss can tell her not to. This is important because her decision to enter the bank makes absolutely no sense to the audience, as written; the writer doesn't show the audience what she sees or the advantages of pursing the villains the way she wants to. We get she wants to follow the letter of the law but if you're not sure what the law is, and how the new crew is breaking it, then the audience is left out; (3) Have her insist on more information from her supervisor, don't have her subordinate do it, have her do it; (4) Since her new team screws her over, have her anticipate it. Do not have her discovering that in Act 3, long after the audience knows it. It makes her look dumb. These changes would change the entire way the story is told but she's the main character and the audience is not properly attached to her and we do not trust the storyteller. The storyteller had no idea how to get us to enter his story. He needed to provide alot more information and he needed to get us to trust him. The story was really great, the way it was told ruined it, I'm sorry to say. I simply do not believe that any officer would've behaved as the Emily Blunt character did, especially in the middle of a mission. I had no problem with her reporting the problems to her old boss, that was believable. After she was shown he would be no help, she should've quit her new team and returned to her old squad. There are many plot holes here where the story fails to adequately communicate the problem. I just don't think the writer had a clue in the way to tell his story, though he had a truly great and important story to tell. Final Thoughts: Errors in storytelling: (1) when Emily Blunt's team is investigating the crime scene in the opening sequences, right before the explosion, we see an investigator working the crime scene without gloves. We know it is a crime scene because of the many corpses in the house. His bare hand reaches for the floor door that's locked and cut away to explosion. Based on what I see in crime type film stories, what I've seen for years, crime scene employees always wear gloves to protect the evidence. Why this is important is because, especially in the beginning of a story, the director needs to convince us that his fake world operates similarly to our real world. When characters in his fake world don't follow widely known investigative procedures in our real world, we're out of the story, and he wants us in his story, i.e., accepting that his story reality matches our reality. If he fails to do that, we never enter his story. The film fails from that point on, about 10 minutes into the film. It was believable that the Emily Blunt team executed a warrant by driving a vehicle through a home, that was believable. But bare hands by an investigator pushed us right back out of the story. A story is a proof. If you're not trying to convince me, then you don't understand what your job is as a writer/director. (2) In the sequence where the officers are caught in traffic after they'd collected their guy in Mexico, after they've just past the check point, totally unbelievable that officers could not have made their way through the traffic jam. Roads have room on the side to allow for emergency vehicles, and an agent or two could've easily gotten out and had room made for the cars. With the blocking the director tried to show that the agents were trapped in those lanes, but I wasn't persuaded, as I know there are almost always emergency lanes for emergency vehicles, and by directing drivers to scoot closer to the next lane, room could've been made. I thought the director wanted to have a hit attempt go down at that location and I just thought the soldiers, who already saw that as a potential problem area, would've not just sat there like fish in a barrel. Poor writing and poor directing. It wouldn't have happened like that. Even I as an innocent civilian know officers can make a way through the most dense congested traffic, so that sequence just didn't fly. (3) When the Emily Blunt character is assaulted by the crooked officer and almost strangled to death, after her attack I saw no marks on her neck nor did she sound hoarse, though she was strangled to near unconsciousness. At the very least she should've sounded hoarse and/or cleared her throat more when talking to her rescuers. That attack was poorly set up, it was supposed to be a pay off from the bank scene but the bank sequence where she disobeyed orders in the most unbelievable way, meant that any payoff from it wouldn't work. If a character behaves bizarrely for reasons not clearly explained to the audience, a pay off from that won't work, unless it's a payoff that's a spinoff of more bizarre behavior. The writer and director didn't know how to do a proper set up and pay off. They know such a thing exists, they just didn't know how to execute it. What the film has going for it is the actors, and the story. It strongly implies that America is a major player in the Mexican cartel drug scene and I would've loved to understand that or at least understand the story's position on their argument more clearly, but that story pretty much got lost in the poor story structure. A lead character basically running around screaming, no you're doing it wrong, you're doing it wrong, distracted from the story's major argument, that America is in the Mexican drug trade. It's said, by Emily Blunt's new boss, but it's not shown. Instead of this story, where the soldiers basically carry the Emily Blunt character because they need her to sign off on something, which by the way is totally unbelievable (can't imagine a spy/guerilla agency needing to behave in this way to do their job: they can kidnap a Mexican citizen and extradite him outside the law but need a signature by a lower ranking officer? Not.) Story would've been much more interesting if we'd seen and learned about the guys who did the mission, who they were, who they reported to, why they did their work the way they did it. Emily Blunt's character was an irritating distraction, in my opinion, and the exact opposite of how a vehicle for a star should be written. If an officer behaved the way that she did in a real world situation, by disobeying a direct order from her immediate supervisor (not to go into the bank), and in another instance lifting her weapon against her team member (when he took possession of the crooked cop in Mexico), I think at minimum she would've been arrested at the scene, if not outright killed. The entire story was a mess and poorly told. If guys high up in Washington could okay this type of operation, why couldn't they okay the sign off that was apparently needed by the low level officer Emily Blunt represents. Why take along someone who you refuse to inform of your mission and have to try to wrangle her, while simultaneously completing your mission. This movie is an Emily Blunt vehicle so I get the director was trying to sell her as a heroine, but to do that the writer and the director needed to have her back, needed to show the audience what the problems were, as she saw them. What I saw was a character throwing tantrums at the worse possible moments, which could have easily lead to the deaths of some of her team. An officer would absolutely not have behaved this way, nor would her supervisor have continued to allow her participation in the mission when he saw she could not handle it. When they first went out, and after she saw how they extricated the guy from Mexico, right then is where she should've gotten out, if she found what they did unacceptable. Instead she went on to the bank, and the tunnel, where her behavior could've jeopardized the mission. Let's say, just for argument, that a character like the Emily Blunt character needed to tag along to witness and sign off on questionable behavior. When her new supervisor saw that she wasn't comfortable with it, why didn't he fire her. Get another somebody to sign off on whatever they needed signed off on. Her behavior could've jeopardized their mission and gotten some of them killed. Now the thing is she's supposed to be promoting what's right, the right thing to do in the right way, but the story itself failed to back her up by failing to provide the audience with basic information as to what the problems were. We saw that she believed they were doing it wrong, but we didn't understand, we weren't shown what they should've been doing. Just a really poorly told story and certainly not an effective vehicle for Emily Blunt, who is a really good actress. She should've passed on this one. P.S.S. Kate, the character Emily Blunt plays, should've been protected by her own story, after all she was fighting the good fight (law and order). Instead, somebody made the decision to fail to explain to the audience her point of view, something usually not done for lead roles. Additionally, I noticed someone made the choice to have a mexican actor be the hands-on heavy (instead of a caucasian male - someone who'd be more likely to be in charge in the events depicted in this film). In my opinion, the story is set up to fail. In other movies, take a Tom Cruise film for example, the audience is shown what's at stake and why Tom Cruise is fighting the good fight. No such support is provided in this film for Emily Blunt's character. I find generally, though not always, when stories which feature America's alleged wrongdoing are made into film, the story is told particularly poorly. In Kill The Messenger, a film which alleges American involvement in the South American coke trade where an American agency allegedly was involved in facilitating the movement of cocaine to American markets, particularly into poor African American neighborhoods, that film was also particularly poorly told. So, in my opinion, our government can say freedom of speech is allowed in this country, and that even the most serious allegations are allowed to be made in this country, but when you actually look at the theatrical films, the ones I've noticed are written so poorly that they don't really function as a believable story. In my opinion.

history.title: Westworld: The Complete First Season (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I love the original Westworld movie. So I was anxious to watch this ridiculously short series (Only 10 episodes). This show is BORING. I have found a consistent cure for insomnia. This series tries to be cerebral, but ends up being inane. Ed Harris’ character is ridiculously SADISTIC. The writers of this series only seem to have ever seen two movies... “Groundhog Day” and “Eyes Wide Shut”. The single saving grace of this movie, is Thandie Newton. Always liked her ever since “Flirting”. And Anthony Hopkins would be wise to get a new agent. Looking back, maybe creating only 10 episodes was merciful.

history.title: Days Of Thunder [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Days of Thunder on blu ray….They thundered past a remaster
history.text: This review is about and based solely upon the transfer of the film to Blu Ray and does not provide the 100th summary of the plot or my opinions on the movie's quality, acting or storyline. VIDEO…. I watched on a Panasonic ZT 65" plasma and an Oppo 103 Blu Ray player. Do not think that this film has been remastered in any way. It is rare that I actually see artifacts on a blu ray, even a bad one, but Days of Thunder does have them in the form of white dropouts. Granted, I saw them only once around the 20th chapter and went back and confirmed them as well. The imaging is not terrible but not great either. The film has a relatively soft focus with a smoothing out of small details. It's not that you don't get used to seeing what your watching but this film was probably transcoded to Blu Ray from an old mother copy and was not cleaned up at all. Deep blacks are not deep and the warm color grading is pretty lifeless. Despite the dated soundtrack, I like the film but this transfer doesn't cut it. Glad I bought it cheap at BB. 2 stars for the video. AUDIO…. You'd expect the audio on a film about car racing would be incredible but it isn't. While the lossless Dolby True HD 5.1 soundtrack provided clean and transparent dialogue they could have done so much more for those who's home theaters are just waiting for a film like this. Some good panning from and across the front and rear stages but no where near what the action in the film dictates. While better than the video imaging, a disappointment for me in the holding back of what should have been much discreet directionality from the surrounds. Bottom end for the LFE channel gets some use but is not anywhere near as deep as it should be for those who have ever been around a race track. 3.5 stars on the audio Extras…. There are none, not even a commentary. They do include the movie trailer but I hardly call that an extra. All my reviews focus solely upon the quality of the transfer to blu ray and I do hope that this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

history.title: Starship Troopers: Invasion [Blu-ray]
history.text: I enjoyed the original Paul Verhoeven's live-action version of Starship Troopers for its thrill ride action, outright humor and satire. This sequel, Starship Troopers: Invasion, was a huge disappointment to me in almost every way. Usually, for my reviews of films on Blu Ray, I focus only upon the actual quality of the video and audio elements of the BR disc and leave the plot summaries and opinions on acting et al to the many other reviewers but this review will deviate somewhat from my past reviews. Please do keep in mind that what you see and hear at home is dependent upon the TV monitor and home theater equipment you are using. My system is a fairly high end esoteric(and costly) system. VIDEO QUALITY..... I felt as if I were watching a video game throughout the entire film. The whole movie is CGI animation and not very realistic at that. Desaturated color palate, smoothed out faces with no details really at all. Since it is all CGI, there were obviously no dropouts or grain, no artifacts or aliasing but just plain Japanese style animation. The so called nude scenes served no purpose at all in this confusing cast of characters. I have no issues with nude sex scenes in films but these were absurdly placed in the film. Dialogue was entirely cliché and syncing of lines to the characters mouths often seemed very off...like the old Godzilla movies of the 50's. Much of the battle action scenes were confusing as you couldn't tell what characters were doing what as there was little distinguishing who was in what 'power suit'. Video Stars....Zero AUDIO QUALITY.... The audio quality was an uncompressed (actually it is all compressed but this lossless audio codec is much less so) DTS HD MA 5.1 which I listened to on a 7.1 system. The dialogue, though poorly synched to the character's mouths, was clear and transparent. The audio is not bad at all and fairly immersed you within the film utilizing your entire audio system. There was not a whole lot of front to back or visa versa panning, nor left to right(and visa versa) panning of the sound stages and almost no discreet directionality of audio foley effects, but the overall audio came through strongly through all speakers with the LFE channel getting a decent workout. EXTRAS... There were a few blooper scenes with the voice actors ad libbing some dialogue, a couple of deleted/extended scenes and the director's commentary which, while somewhat interesting, seemed too much to me as if he was patting himself on the back for his excellent (in his opinion) job of staying true to both the real movie and Robert Heinlein's novel. One thing I truly hate on either DVDs or Blu Rays are the extras called ' previews'. This disc had an ad telling us how wonderful Blu Ray discs are and about 5 or 6 different previews of other films. Basically, you are paying for advertisements that take up some of the very limited room on these Blu Ray discs causing for more compression and reduced resolution of the movie you are actually paying for. This was one Blu Ray disc I wish I had not gotten. Just terrible for me but it might suit the tastes of a 12 year old. I do hope that this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. All my movie reviews are of this nature and focus only on the quality of the transfer to BluRay so check them and see if they are of help as well. Thank you for reading.

history.title: The Legend of Tarzan
history.review_title: The Legend of Tarzan (Blu-ray + DVD + Digital...
history.text: All of my many Blue Ray reviews focus solely upon the actual quality of the film from Standard Def DVD quality to the higher standard set for Blu Ray. Summaries of the plot and opinions of the story line and acting can be found in the majority of the other reviews so I do not want to be redundant. My rating is based solely upon the Blue Ray disc's video and audio quality and not the quality of the movie itself. Keep in mind, however, that the quality of what you see and hear is also dependent upon the quality of the TV monitor you are watching on as well as the home theater set up you are using. The monitor I use is a fairly new Panasonic ZT 65" plasma and the amps, speakers, cables, OPPO 103 BluRay player and AVM-60 7.1 Atmos enabled Surround Processor I use are hi end esoteric gear to provide me with a more realistic and objective perspective. The Oppo player is not enabled to transcode Atmos audio so it will default to the next best audio coded, in this case, DTS HD MA 7.1 I am not trying to be a snob here, but just pointing out that what you see and hear is very dependent upon the quality of the gear you are using. VIDEO QUALITY..... I had not seen this film in the theaters nor read about it so I bought it on a blind gamble and won. Very well done film in most respects with a very credible storyline. The film's video quality rates a 4 in my mind. Colors are deeply saturated without over popping colors as you might find in a Transformers movie. Skin tones are normal and natural with clarity to small details even in the darkest of scenes. No artifacting anywhere was noticed, which having been shot in video rather than on film would be expected. A great many of the scenes were done in CGI and, to my eyes, some of the CGI was less than perfect. The CGI apes, while appearing to be well done were nowhere near as natural looking as the apes of the recent Planet of the Apes films were. You could see the CGI of them pretty clearly. I wouldn't call them poorly done, just not as good as other CGI I have seen. The CGI of Tarzan and the natives running along the tree branches was dizzying but not as obvious. Mbps rate appeared to average in the mid 30's. This could easily have been increased if it weren't for the several ads for other films that the company calls 'extras'. They just take up room on the disc calling for more compression of the film you are paying for. AUDIO QUALITY...... The Atmos 7.1 lossless codec is the default audio but since I do not have an Atmos player, it defaults to the lossless 7.1 codec and does a good job with that. All audio levels were properly set so even quiet dialogue was clean and discernible. The surrounds are used primarily for an immersive ambient experience and does so respectfully. There was not a whole lot of discreet directionality from various front, side or rear channels for various foley fx but the overall audio experience was a good one. Left and right pans across the front stage are few but effective. While the audio quality is good, why the audio editors do not put effort into utilizing the 7.1 codec is disappointing but is due probably to budget reasons. Audio gets cut first. EXTRAS.... No deleted scenes or gag reels but some good docs on creating the many CGI effects as well as the training the actors needed to go through and the development of a excellent story line that easily could have gone awry and turned into a cheapo storyline. As it is, the story was very well done. The Standard Def disc is included as well as your ability to download it from UltraViolet but not iTunes which I prefer. I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

history.title: Everest [Blu-ray]
history.text: All of my many Blue Ray reviews focus solely upon the actual quality of the film from Standard Def DVD quality to the higher standard set for Blu Ray. The monitor I use is a fairly new Panasonic ZT 65" plasma and the amps, speakers, cables, OPPO 103 BluRay player and AVM-60 7.1 Atmos enabled Surround Processor I use are hi end esoteric gear to provide me with a more realistic and objective perspective. The Oppo player is not enabled to transcode Atmos audio so it will default to the next best audio coded, in this case, DTS HD MA 7.1 I am not trying to be a snob here, but just pointing out that what you see and hear is very dependent upon the quality of the gear you are using. VIDEO QUALITY..... The Video quality of this Blu Ray disc is exceptional. Colors are treated respectfully with a cool grading apropos of the snowy environment. Details even when snow storms would normally mush them out, are clearly and precisely defined and easily denoted. Skin and hair textures are extremely detailed and contrast is exceptional throughout the film. Even clothing creases are clearly defined without any flattening to their appearances. Opening scene colors where the actors are not in snowy conditions are as natural appearing as one could expect. A truly brilliant job of cinematography. AUDIO QUALITY.... Utilizing an Atmos lossless 7.1 which will default to a 7.1 DTS HD MA codec if you are not Atmos enabled, the audio is also superb throughout the entirety of the movie. This audio editing fully immerses you into the film, especially during the blizzard scenes where the wind is all around you with different wind noise coming from the surrounds so that the audio is not the same, for example, in the left rear as it is in the right rear. There is a great deal of discreet directionality utilizing the surrounds as individual audio channels. This is a film where the audio engineers really put some thought and effort into creating a seamless audio soundtrack with breathtaking use of both pounding and subtle foley fx. EXTRAS..... In addition to the UV download which, surprisingly went pretty smoothly for me, and in addition to the typical 'Making of' documentary, there are extras pertaining to the real story of what occurred that year on Everest as well as an extra pertaining to the training the actors had to go through. All in all, this film will be a great addition to your collection. I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

history.review_title: Olympus Has Fallen (Two Disc Combo: Blu-ray /...
history.text: All of my many Blue Ray reviews focus solely upon the actual quality of the film from Standard Def DVD quality to the higher standard set for Blu Ray. Summaries of the plot and opinions of the story line and acting can be found in the majority of the other reviews so I do not want to be redundant.
