Keep in mind, however, that the quality of what you see and hear is also dependent upon the quality of the TV monitor you are watching on as well as the home theater set up you are using. The monitor I use is a fairly new Panasonic ZT 65" plasma and the amps, speakers, cables, OPPO 103 BluRay player and AVM-60 7.1 Atmos enabled Surround Processor I use are hi end esoteric gear to provide me with a more realistic and objective perspective. The Oppo player is not enabled to transcode Atmos audio so it will default to the next best audio coded, in this case, DTS HD MA 7.1 I am not trying to be a snob here, but just pointing out that what you see and hear is very dependent upon the quality of the gear you are using. VIDEO QUALITY.....I find it interesting that the company is now packaging this film as a two for one package along with the movie 'White House Down' as both movies are very similar in appearance and plot. That said, the video quality of Olympus Has Fallen on blue ray is pretty decent but not without some faults. For a film shot on video the colors definitely appear somewhat muted and skin tones tend to be a bit pasty. While sharpness is good, overall contrast and focus is a touch soft. While there was no edging or other artifacts anywhere during my viewing the overall softness might be partially to blame on the company includes several previews of other films which amount to no more than ads. These ads, which they have the nerve to call 'extras' take up room on the disc necessitating for greater compression of the actual film you are paying for. Colors do not pop and brightness is a touch dimmed unlike its cousin film 'Whilte House Down'. Dark scenes also appear to be crushed too much contributing to the lack of small details to be seen. Never the less, you don't buy a film like this for the smallest of visual details. It is definitely a pop corn movie and one I enjoyed despite the less than perfect video transparency. AUDIO QUALITY..... The DTS HD MA 5.1 lossless audio code is the star of the disc. Too bad it does not arrive with the current standard of a 7.1 audio as this is the type of film that would and could make great use of the enlarged audio sound stages. Despite that, the lossless 5.1 audio editing is really quite good. The audio editors make great use of the surrounds for more than just the musical immersiveness. Audio fx from pans back and across the front and rear sound stages are put to the test with a great number of foley fx for both the front sides and rear speakers. My buddy who is hearing impaired did ask me whether I could up the volume of the center channel's dialogue and, in truth, sometimes the dialogue is overshadowed by other audio input. However, most dialogue felt clear and transparent to me if not a touch lower in the balance of aircraft and explosions. EXTRAS... As I said before, previews of other films I do not consider extras. However, there are several other decent extras included. Bloopers, a making of documentary, the bit on the cast ensemble, training for the film and one on the special fx add a touch of spice. Finally, there is the UV digital download disc as well. I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

history.title: Independence Day Resurgence(Bluray+DVD+Digital HD)
history.text: All of my many Blue Ray reviews focus solely upon the actual quality of the film from Standard Def DVD quality to the higher standard set for Blu Ray. Summaries of the plot and opinions of the story line and acting can be found in the majority of the other reviews so I do not want to be redundant. My rating is based solely upon the Blue Ray disc's video and audio quality and not the quality of the movie itself. Keep in mind, however, that the quality of what you see and hear is also dependent upon the quality of the TV monitor you are watching on as well as the home theater set up you are using. The monitor I use is a fairly new Panasonic ZT 65" plasma and the amps, speakers, cables, OPPO 103 BluRay player and AVM-60 7.1 Atmos enabled Surround Processor I use are hi end esoteric gear to provide me with a more realistic and objective perspective. The Oppo player is not enabled to transcode Atmos audio so it will default to the next best audio coded, in this case, DTS HD MA 7.1 I am not trying to be a snob here, but just pointing out that what you see and hear is very dependent upon the quality of the gear you are using. This film was roundly criticized for its weak rehashing of the original Independence Day and in my opinion, deservedly so. Many hole plots, some weak and obvious CGI along with the good CGI as well. Never the less, the Blue Ray deserves its 5 stars strictly for the excellent quality of the discs video and audio which could easily be used as a demo disc to show off the quality of your own home theater set up. VIDEO QUALITY.... Independence Day Resurgence displays some of the finest video quality you will find anywhere. Colors are true and bright with color correction doing nothing to take away of the imaging. Skin tones are very natural and contrast is excellent throughout the film. Small details such as hair and skin pores are easily seen and are not blurred into mushiness. While several 'previews' ,which add up to nothing more than advertisements for other movies and take up room on the disc's limited room causing for greater compression of the film you are paying for, the video quality remains superb. Average bit rate appeared to be 30 Mbps which is not very high but better than those with those low 20 rates. AUDIO QUALITY.... While there is no Atmos 7.1 format on this disc, the lossless DTS HD MA 7.1 codec is utilized to its full potential. Not only is the audio totally immersive, the audio engineers use the surround channels for a lot more than simply spreading the musical score around. There is a ton of discreet audio foley fx spread across and around the different sound stages. These fx come from all directions so you are in the battles from all angles. Your LFE channel will also get a great workout throughout the film's many action sequences. 10 stars on the audio for sure. EXTRAS.... Aside from the completely unnecessary ads for Blu Ray and other movies, the disc has several decent extras. The bloopers, which I usually enjoy when they are included, are not the funniest and are often redundant. They are all shown with the blue screen in the rear as almost all the CGI was done with blue screen rather than green screen. You are also provided with the typical directors commentary which I never listen to. Additionally, there is a typical 'making of' documentary. One extra, 'It's Early, ABQ" is a hilarious spoof that is not to be missed and a wonderful addition. Still another extra is entitled 'The War of 1996' which could have been a part of the film serving as a prologue but would have made the theatrical release far too long. Never the less, it takes on the appearance of a news report going back to the original Independence Day. There is also a concept art gallery which I didn't look at and the Standard Def disc. The UV download process for this Fox movie is horrible. The redemption code has far too many letters and numbers that could be interpreted as something else. I tried every possible alternative for S that could be a 5 and B that could be an 8, G that could be a 6 but I still cannot have the code verified. There is no way to contact customer support other than by email which I have sent. I have no idea how long it may take for them to get back to me on my inability to redeem the download and there is no phone number to call on their website. A real pain in the butt and inconvenience. So far, I have heard nothing back. The movie deserves the negative reviews it received on many levels, however if you can get past the holes in the storyline it remained an enjoyable evening with popcorn at hand. The real value of the film on blue ray is the excellent transfer for both the audio and video. I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

history.title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
history.text: All of my many Blue Ray reviews focus solely upon the actual quality of the film from Standard Def DVD quality to the higher standard set for Blu Ray. Summaries of the plot and opinions of the story line and acting can be found in the majority of the other reviews so I do not want to be redundant. My rating is based solely upon the Blue Ray disc's video and audio quality and not the quality of the movie itself. Keep in mind, however, that the quality of what you see and hear is also dependent upon the quality of the TV monitor you are watching on as well as the home theater set up you are using. The monitor I use is a fairly new Panasonic ZT 65" plasma and the amps, speakers, cables, OPPO 103 BluRay player and AVM-60 7.1 Atmos enabled Surround Processor I use are hi end esoteric gear to provide me with a more realistic and objective perspective. The Oppo player is not enabled to transcode Atmos audio so it will default to the next best audio coded, in this case, DTS HD MA 7.1 I am not trying to be a snob here, but just pointing out that what you see and hear is very dependent upon the quality of the gear you are using. VIDEO QUALITY..... Whether you are a Star Wars fanatic or not, the video quality found on this disc is absolutely demo worthy. Color resolution is spot on no matter what environment any specific scene is in. From the very beginning with the iconic yellow lettering introduction you can tell that contrast will be superb. The darkness of space easily passes pluge and displays a nicely deep black while a very fine grain throughout the film adds depth and dimension to both the landscapes and the characters. Fine and small details are easily deduced without overly crushed blacks. Color grading leaves all colors from the brightness of the light sabers to the sandy desert scenes to colors of clothing are all stunningly displayed without unnatural popping colors as you might find in some super hero films. Nasty artifacts are no where to be seen anywhere on this blu ray as the transfer is as clean as you could ask for. AUDIO QUALITY..... This film on Blu Ray comes with DTS-HD Master Audio 7.1 lossless soundtrack though I am perplexed as to why an Atmos 7.1 audio option is not included. Never the less, the soundtrack and all audio remains topnotch. The music soundtrack is fully immersive though all channels and discreet directionality from individual channels both front and back, left and right are put to great use for foley effects of ships panning all ways and action taking place off center screen. Dialogue is brisk and transparent and audio levels for both soundtrack, foley fx and dialogue are correctly balanced so playing roller coaster with your remote should not be an issue or concern. With all the space ships roaring by, you can expect your LFE sub channel to get an excellent workout with some pretty deep bass in several scenes. Also, demo worthy so bookmark those scenes you want to show off your home theater to. EXTRAS..... Some very interesting extras are included in the disc though I have not watched them all. An initial table reading with cast members is unique as an extra as was a doc on the building of the BB-8 robot. Other docs include docs on the John Williams symphonic score, crafting of the creatures seen in the film and some fairly good deleted scenes that would not have been important to an extended version. Unfortunately, the code to download the streamed film was no good. You should be able to download it to either iTunes or to VUDU and I always prefer to download via iTunes. After many times trying I contact iTunes who simply passed the buck and suggested I contact the production company. I wound up downloading it to VUDU, not my first choice. The attitude of iTunes regarding this was simply unacceptable in every way. I did find this release superior as a movie to some of the other Star Wars films but my opinion on that does not count. My 5 stars only reflects the quality of the transfer of the film to Blu Ray. I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

VIDEO QUALITY..... The video resolution is really quite decent for this shorter than expected film which runs for 1.5 hours. Color grading is fairly neutral and real life. Excellent contrast throughout with only the slightest hint of grain in just a few areas. Small details such as skin pores and hair separation are easy to discern. Bit rate averages about 31 Mbps. Sky scenes show no banding at all. AUDIO QUALITY.... While there is no Atmos 7.1 soundtrack, the default to Dolby Tru HD 7.1 does a very commendable job when immersion into the sound field is called for. Much of the film is center speaker, dialogue based with a few audio pans across the front stage. There is not a whole lot of foley fx coming from the surrounds during these scenes. That said, during the sky and water landing scenes, your LFE channel as well as your surrounds will all come into play with aggressive use and immersive ambience drawing you into the scene. Audio pans from rear to front are several and foley fx from the surrounds are fitting and at proper, if subdued levels. Dialogue is clear and transparent throughout. EXTRAS....I hate ads for other movies of which there are many on here. That said, there are 3 very good extras including interviews with the real characters, extraordinary footage of an actual crash that didn't have the good fortune to have Sully as captain and a making of doc. All in all, I can't quite say I'd pull this disc for use as a demo disc, not only is the film well made but the entire storyline plays out in totally realistic tone. Look out for director Clint pulling an Alfred Hitchcock move in one of the scenes....I won't tell you which. I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

history.title: The Finest Hours
history.text: All of my many Blu-ray reviews focus solely upon the actual quality of the film from Standard Def DVD quality to the higher standard set for Blu-ray. Summaries of the plot and opinions of the story line and acting can be found in the majority of the other reviews so I do not want to be redundant. My rating is based solely upon the Blu-ray disc's video and audio quality and not the quality of the movie itself. Keep in mind, however, that the quality of what you see and hear is also dependent upon the quality of the TV monitor you are watching on as well as the home theater set up you are using. The monitor I use is a fairly new Panasonic ZT 65" plasma , a new McIntosh 7 channel amp, Aerial Acoustic Speakers for center and surround speakers, Velodyne Sub, hi end cables and XLRs, OPPO 103 BluRay player and a new AVM-60 7.1 Atmos enabled Surround Processor I use are hi end esoteric gear to provide me with a more realistic and objective perspective. The Oppo player is not enabled to transcode Atmos audio so it will default to the next best audio coded, in this case, DTS HD MA 7.1 I am not trying to be a snob here, but just pointing out that what you see and hear is very dependent upon the quality of the gear you are using. VIDEO QUALITY..... Video quality is completely free of any artifactting or visual defects. Color grading has been deliberately colorized to be on the warm and slightly desaturated side. I would not call this color grading to be completely normal or natural as things colors did not look any different in 1952 when this real life story takes place than it does today. That said, the color grading does provided that feeling of age and naivety that permeated the 50's, Mbps rate appeared to average at about 32; not too shabby. Black levels are decent but do not get too deep and small detail visuals rate about the same, a 4. Nothing bad at all but nothing terribly great either. Details of rain and snow drops towards the film's end are pretty discernible and that is always a good thing. AUDIO QUALITY.... No new Atmos soundtrack but we are provided a very decent lossless 7.1 DTS HD MA soundtrack that brings with it very transparent dialogue even with a cacophony of storm noise behind it. The audio is really quite immersive throughout the entire film and this aggressive surround approach does put you front and in the very center of what is going on, especially so during the scenes when you are on either the stricken vessel or rescue boat. Unfortunately, this very immersive audio does not provide much in the way of discreet channel directionality. You won't hear too many waves hit you on the left while your right is quiet or doors slam behind you, pans across left and right, front and rear sound stages. You are in a storm and it is all around you. Bass reproduction is solidly handled and very natural sounding, so that when a wave hits a bar, it sounds as it should. I have spent enough time at sea to know reality when I hear it. Good job here. EXTRAS....I really liked that Disney used real photos of the actual characters and placed them side by side with the actors. I love historical events and took pleasure in seeing these real life survivors and heros. Bonus Features: Against All Odds: The Bernie Webber Story – 14 minute featurette 2 Deleted Scenes Two Crews – 2 minute featurette What is Your Finest Hour? – featurette The Finest Inspiration: The U.S. Coast Guard – 2 minute featurette Digital HD Copy I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

history.title: Hacksaw Ridge [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital]
history.text: All of my many Blu-ray reviews focus solely upon the actual quality of the film from Standard Def DVD quality to the higher standard set for Blu-ray. Summaries of the plot and opinions of the story line and acting can be found in the majority of the other reviews so I do not want to be redundant. My rating is based solely upon the Blu-ray disc's video and audio quality and not the quality of the movie itself. This disc was bought from Amazon by a friend as a birthday present for me. Keep in mind, however, that the quality of what you see and hear is also dependent upon the quality of the TV monitor you are watching on as well as the home theater set up you are using. The monitor I use is a fairly new Panasonic ZT 65" plasma , a new McIntosh 7 channel amp, Aerial Acoustic Speakers for center and surround speakers, Velodyne Sub, hi end cables and XLRs, OPPO 103 BluRay player and a new AVM-60 7.1 Atmos enabled Surround Processor I use are hi end esoteric gear to provide me with a more realistic and objective perspective. The Oppo player is not enabled to transcode Atmos audio so it will default to the next best audio coded, in this case, Dolby Tru HD 7.1 I am not trying to be a snob here, but just pointing out that what you see and hear is very dependent upon the quality of the gear you are using. VIDEO QUALITY..... Video quality is completely free of any artifacting or visual defects. Color grading is warmly devised reflective of the 70 years ago that this real life hero and events took place. Skin tones are smooth but do not deny details in skin, hair or other small detailed considerations. Mbps rate seemed to average around 34 even in the first hour's slow paced scenes. Action scenes are hand held but not so blurry as to get you dizzy or leave you uncomprehending of what is going on. Dark scenes went deep and clearly pass pluge on my monitor. AUDIO QUALITY... I believe this film won an Academy Award for Audio mixing and it is well deserved. While the first half of the film leaves the sound stages in a very passive mode, relying upon dialogue that always comes through with wonderful tonality and clear, transparent dialogue, the second half of the film which focuses upon the actually battle of Hacksaw Ridge produces an aggressive mix of audio foley fx that both and immerses you. There is plentiful use of your individual surrounds as discreet audio sources as well as some nicely deep LFE channel workout for your subwoofer. Ship cannon blasts have just the right amount of resonance and cut the air like a knife, deep and profound. There is much is in the second half of this film that, for your audio system, is clearly demo worthy. EXTRAS.... Aside from the digital download, which, when choosing my preferred iTunes, has become increasingly problematic, I had no issues downloading it to VUDU instead. However, since I use Safari, I find it hard to watch a VUDU film on Safari and have to go to FireFox. A bit of a pain. There are a couple of deleted scenes that were interesting but no big deal, a documentary of over an hour on the making of the film, and a short doc on the real character this film is based upon. As a history buff, I enjoyed this part a great deal. Whether you liked the film or not, my rating is based upon the actual quality of the Blu-ray transfer and it is excellent. I do hope this review has been of some help to you in deciding upon your purchase. Thanks for reading.

history.title: All That Heaven Allows (Blu-ray + DVD)
history.text: This review is for the Criterion Blu-ray. I'm so disappointed. After reading a "professional" review of the Blu-ray version on another website, I was excited. This is one of my favorite movies, and the reviewer spoke of the brilliant colors and how they pop. I already owned the Criterion DVD, and after reading the review of how much better the Blu-ray was, I couldn't wait to see it. But when I received it and watched it, I was so disappointed. I can't tell any difference from the DVD version. I was hoping that the very grainy picture would be clearer, but it is ever so grainy still. Ugh! The facial tones are yellowish, not any different from the DVD. Has anyone else compared the two versions? What do you think? I wish I had my money back. If you want to see a huge difference and wonderfully brilliant upgrade from the DVD to the Blu-ray version, watch and enjoy "How the West Was Won." Incredible and mesmerizing.

history.title: Remember the Day
history.text: The 20th Century Fox Cinema Archives has produced several wonderful films, otherwise unobtainable on home video. This is a great film, very nostalgic and sentimental, but a disappointing transfer from the folks at 20th Century. The picture is very dark, even in the outdoor daytime scenes, which look as though they were filmed as day-for-night. Many scratches and dust specks are visible, as well as a constant graininess. At the 5:34 mark, there is a skip in the film, obliterating the third line of "(Back Home Again in) Indiana." The movie is watchable, however, a cut above the many public domain films available on home video, and the audio is clear. Given the production company of this transfer, I had higher expectations; my low rating is for the transfer, not the film itself.

history.title: Home Before Dark [Remaster]
history.text: Warner Archives did a great transfer of this movie---not a restoration, but the audio and video are more than adequate to enjoy the movie. But personally, I didn't enjoy this movie as much as I thought I would. Given the premise of a mental patient returning home after a year in a hospital to the very situation that caused her breakdown, and having Jean Simmons as that patient (she's a terrific actress), and with a great supporting cast (including Rhonda Fleming and Efrem Zimbalist, Jr.), I was expecting much more. I love film noir, suspense and gothic tales, but this movie didn't register as great in any of those three sub-genres. The movie was flat and dull with a lot of talk ... until Charlotte's entrance at the Boston restaurant decked out as her step-sister. That was the scene that finally drew me into the movie ... an hour and 45 minutes into it! I'm surprised I stuck it out that long. This could have been a great movie, but maybe the director (Mervyn LeRoy) had other things on his mind. As I watched "Home Before Dark," I couldn't help but think about one of the greatest movies of all time, "Now, Voyager" as both leads are women named Charlotte who live in or near Boston and have been in psychiatric care. In fact, a trivia item on IMDB for this movie says that the soundtrack of Voyager was used for this movie. Maybe Warners was trying to rekindle the greatness of "Now Voyager." ... They didn't.

history.title: The Last Laugh
history.text: The restored German version of The Last Laugh by Kino is excellent. From the crystal clear raindrops near the first of the film to the end, this is one of the best restorations of a silent film I've ever seen. The score is exquisite, and, unique for a silent, there are no title cards to read. Speakers of any language can easily follow the simple story of an aging bellhop who is demoted to washroom attendant when the hotel employing him deems him too old for his job. The camera angles and viewpoints---especially a moving shot from a glass elevator---are ahead of their time and make this story very entertaining. The movie also includes great special effects for the 1920s----or any decade.

history.title: Knock on Wood
history.text: I have several DVDs manufactured by Olive Films, and most of the transfers are excellent. However, Knock on Wood is not a great transfer. The best way to describe the picture is that it looks like a movie that was filmed in 3D. It looks like two pictures that are not aligned, slightly off so that it looks blurred, definitely far from a sharp image. The audio is great, and the story is as enjoyable as any other Danny Kaye film.

history.title: UPA: The Jolly Frolics Collection
history.text: The technical quality of the UPA Jolly Frolics Collection of cartoons is great, although I don't see the vibrant colors of the Disney or Looney Tunes of the period. This is mostly due to a different style of animation, probably, but these don't seem to be fully restored. A few scenes here and there within the cartoons are blurred---very few, though. And despite the buildup of these UPA cartoons and their animators in the introduction by Leonard Maltin, the plotlines and characters are just ho-hum for the most part. The artwork is interesting simply because it is different from the major studios' artwork at the time, and I can certainly see the influence this style had on Jay Ward and the later Rocky & Bullwinkle animators. Only two of these cartoons really stood out to me, The Tell-Tale Heart (which is now on the National Film Registry) and Madeline, which is based on the classic children's book. I love classic short cartoons, but was overall disappointed with these from UPA.

history.title: Snows of Kilimanjaro, The
history.text: Be sure to get the 20th Century Fox version, and not some third generation reprint (this film has fallen into the public domain). When you see the Technicolor cinematography, you'll be glad you spent a little more for some of the most beautiful colors to grace the silver screen. You can easily see why it was nominated for Best Color Cinematography. The story itself sways greatly from the Hemingway short story (a lot more story had to be fabricated to reach the length of a feature film) and for a movie set in Africa and Spain, with scenes of safaris, bullfights and civil war, it suffocates in too much talk too much of the time.

history.title: MALEFICENT [Blu-ray]
history.text: I first saw the reviews, and the trailers. Plus it's Disney, so I figured it should be at least good. The second thing, I love movies based on "myth" and other such things. So I watched the Blue Ray thinking this would be a different version of the old classic, (which as a kid the dragon scared the heck out of me). What I saw was so different then what I thought it would be. It's has the basis of the original story, but made it much more "dark" yet not as terrifying. Even the soundtrack matched the moods of the movie so well. In short, I loved it. Malificent was as much a "dark" angel as a faerie. The special effects and computer animation drew you in and was done so well you didn't question it. Even the colors and hues of the scenes were excellent. Angelina Jolie did a superb job, so different from her norm. The rest of the cast did quite well also. There are flickers of humor throughout, which I liked. No spoilers here. A recommended movie.

history.title: Interstellar (Blu-ray + DVD Combo Pack)
history.review_title: Great SCI FI, with outstanding cast
history.text: I don't usually review movies, but being a Sci-Fi nut and seeing all the build up for this, I waited for the price to drop and bought the Blue Ray. ( a week later price went up again). I really only knew about the two lead actors, and was surprised at the level of the rest of the cast. Michael Caine? YES! To me the movie started up a bit slow, but I like character building and showing the scenario. It did this very well. As they went into space, the effects and such, I definitely got a Stanley Kubrick "Space Odyssey" feel too it, Which I Liked. I did get really engrossed in the movie. The reason? This is a very true Science Fiction Movie, not a "shoot em up got to have a laser in every shot" movie. Independence Day it is not, but it's not supposed to be. The science that goes through the discussions in "Interstellar" are reminiscent of the works of Asimov and others..very hard core. Thus the five star rating. I like science fiction! Note that this isn't for the 13 year old "Mom where's the funny aliens and stuff" movie. I believe that if you like sci-fi, you will like this.

history.title: Victory at Sea - The Complete 26 Episode Series - Plus 6 Bonus War Documentary Programs - Collector's Tin
history.text: To start off with, I remember watching this as a child. My father loved this show, and he loved the soundtrack, and as a result, so do it. Still have the original soundtrack albums. The songs " Beneath The Southern Cross" and "Guadalcanal March" are worth the listen. The show itself was done in the fifties, not that far removed from the war itself. "The Greatest Generation" was riveted to it on their black and white TV's..ours was. The narration is stirring, they used actual footage throughout, and its episode sequence built up to the finale. If you wish to expose children or teens to the history of this time, this is a great way to expose them to the feel of the time. This and the other excellent series "The World At War" are excellent ways to do that. This is highly recommended, and at this price, you simply cannot go wrong. I while back, I got this as presents for my relatives, (father, uncles), and they were astounded. At $5??? No better gift for those who lived it.

The kids loved it, (it was intense so not TOO young). I had my Surround System on, and boy did that ad to the effect. I rate it a five because, 1) it is entertaining 2) Special effects are excellent 3) It could happen 4)the Family loved it and "The Rock", and 5) I will see it again. history.title: Great Railways: The Age of Steam
history.text: I was really excited when this finally arrived as I had been watching the price to drop and when it did, I snatched it up thinking I had an awesome addition to my collection. I wish Amazon would allow for 1/2 stars, because it does deserve 2 1/2 stars. Unfortunately, this is as jumpy and jittery as a used VHS tape and I am watching it on my Blu-ray player! Many scenes are blurry. Apparently, all they did with this was transfer to DVD, no remastering, no form of clean-up whatsoever. I like to see the numbers and roadnames on the locos and most DVD's I have, it is visible. But due to the fuzziness, most text is unreadable. So disappointed, but since it is about steam trains, I gave it 2 (1/2, but again, Amazon doesn't allow for 1/2 stars. In short, the transfer was buggy, looks like they used a worn in VHS tape as the master. No clean-up was done, so the imperfections, e.g., video noise, spots and blemishes from the master remain. Some scenes are really out of focus. Then, there's the jitter and bouncing. Some shots are similar to streaming lags, causing the movement to be almost stop-motion. I did not expect Blu-ray quality, but at least cleaning up the noise and imperfections before copy would have been appreciated.

history.title: Star Trek: The Complete Original Series (Seasons 1-3) [Blu-ray]
history.text: This was a very thoughtful gift from my better half for Christmas. When I opened the box, I was momentarily speechless as I've been wanting the original series on BD ever since it was released. The new effects are superb and the extras are equally enthralling. Being able to toggle between the original efx and the remastered is great. Only thing is a feature with split screen showing both would be cool as well. However, its still fun to toggle. Picture is as crisp as you can imagine. Buy it. My advice. If you're a true Trek fan, this should be in your collection.

history.title: Emergency! The Complete Series [DVD]
history.review_title: Emergency! DVD Series Box Set Review
history.text: Love the series, 5-Stars for one of my old favorite television shows. This review is not of the show but rather the DVD product quality. I’m giving 1 star because the audio/visual quality is hit-or-miss at best. Many episodes really appear to be direct copies from either the deteriorated master or used VHS. This is a disservice to fans, especially customers shelling out $80 or so for this box set. While I realize this was not “remastered,” a LITTLE care to clean up the mess. Color is faded or very orange on many episodes. Muddy picture and sound on others. Some episodes, the audio track is so faded, in order to hear it, the volume needs to be cranked but the sound effects, e.g., sirens or music nearly blasts the viewer out of their seat! EX: Disc 1: “Wedsworth-Townsend Act” is acceptable but “Mascot” & “Botulism” are fuzzy & the red really overpowers. In some episodes, I actually caught a few production markers. Most episodes are riddled with anomalies and video noise which really is not that difficult to fix. Discs 4 & 5 contain some of the worst examples. I must add that the clips used for previews look very well restored, a shame they couldn’t put even half the effort into the rest. Bottom line is, had Great-tv-shows .com taken just a little time and care, this would have been better quality. Granted, it would cut a little into their overall profit but if they just spent a little more time and yes, money, they probably would have seen better profit in the long run. The old saying “Bad press speaks louder than good” applies here. This was pretty blatantly “You want your favorite shows on DVD, here you go” with high prices to boot. Since I received this set as a gift, I won’t be so crass as to return it. Since these are watchable, if many barely so, I am thankful to at least have access to this series. EDIT: 4/19/2017 ~ I've been running through the series disc by disc and really have to point out how TERRIBLE Season 4 transfer is. Greattvshows.com REALLY should be ashamed of themselves for the lack of quality and sloppy editing. Episodes really are nearly unwatchable. I could not even make it through Disc 3, let alone skipping through much of the other two. Volume is low, picture is unbearably poor, nearly "pirated" quality. At the VERY least, I think they should go back and clean up the master and reproduce Season 4 and send replacement copies to everyone that owns this! (It's unfortunate that Amazon lists "Verified Purchases" as if everyone else's opinions who received as gifts or purchased elsewhere do not matter. This was bought from Amazon,I'm just not about to tell her how disappointed I am with this, she would feel like I don't appreciate the gift, which I do, I just don't appreciate the quality (or lack thereof) put into this DVD set!)

history.title: Cosmos: A Spacetime Odyssey [Blu-ray]
history.text: Neil Degrasse Tyson delivers. Explaining things on a layman’s level, Tyson presents this topic well. Many reviewers criticize him and the material for being amateurish, on a child’s level. Perhaps that was the point! To help even youngsters understand and even enjoy learning about Astronomy, it’s necessary to bring it down from a scholar’s level. That said, there is much value even an adult can appreciate. I also found it to be a fitting tribute to the late Carl Sagan. That said, this BD (Blu-ray Disc) presentation was very well done. The stunning visuals and rich audio really pop. Crisp, clear, nearly 3D quality on a flat-screen TV nearly puts you there. Subject matter takes the viewer from the very reaches of the universe to the infinitesimal microscopic life. Each episode is so engrossing and informative; it’s over before it started. Tyson takes you on a trip with his “Ship of the Imagination.” This is one of the few TV shows of this era I found myself eagerly awaiting each week’s episode. It is a shame there were only 13 episodes. Brannon Braga (Star Trek: The Next Generation, Enterprise, Voyager; Threshold, 24, etc.) directed and was Executive Producer. Alan Sylvestri composed the fitting musical score. The packaging was done well. Discs are available on plastic “pages” in the typical blue BD case. This makes disc access easy, unlike some which are packaged on a spindle. If you find Astronomy fascinating, I have no doubt this will be a worthy addition to your collection

history.title: Apollo 13 [Blu-ray]
history.text: Picture quality and audio cannot be beat! Every time I watch this movie, I get chills. Apollo 13 shows the grit, determination, and ingenuity of American Astronauts & crew. A wonderful re-creation of this gripping event. Tom Hanks portrays Jim Lovel in a way no one else can. Sinise is almost a mirror image of Mattingly and Chris Ellis a fantastic Deke. If you love space and space movies, this will draw you in and you feel the emotional roller coaster as if you were there yourself. Ron Howard was the most appropriate director for this film. Remastering of this movie was done very well. Picture is clear and crisp. Best watched on a large flat screen TV with the surround sound cranked up along with a sub-woofer to capture the audio. The thrill of the engines blasting, coupled with the life-like video of the Saturn V rocket sliding into the atmosphere. The space shots are literally "out of this world!" As the crew orbits the Moon, you feel like you are part of the crew, looking out the capsule window watching Mt. Marilyn float by. Such a crisp and clear picture, you can almost reach out and touch the Moon! This ranks among my all-time favorite movies. The BD treatment only solidifies this ranking. Buy this, you will not be disappointed!

history.title: The Life and Times of Grizzly Adams: The Complete Series
history.text: Grew up on this show and loved it. Apparently I still do because despite the sub-par transfer, I still watch it though with a bit of irritation. In a day when TV is full of agendas, material not appreciated in our private living room, and supposed “reality” shows, collecting and watching these old TV shows is a blast from the past. This, however, is not a review of the TV series. That deserves no less than 5 Stars. The transfer quality is pretty dismal. Apparently, very little restoration was actually done on the master. Color is washed out, production anomalies are ever-present. It seems CBS feels the disclaimer at the beginning of the Season 1 Disks was enough to get them off the hook. It just seems to me that a little care should be taken when producing and distributing these old TV shows. If you are going to do something, DO IT RIGHT! It is very disappointing that so many old shows, like Emergency!, Battlestar Galactica, & The Six Million Dollar Man are redistributed on DVD with little to no restoration work done on the master. I’m not asking for Blu-Ray quality, just clean up the anomalies, true the color and audio. In many spots, the audio is “warbly” and flat. Sometimes it’s downright hollow and muffled. The Season 2 discs seem to look better than Season 1. However, part of me suspects the master was in better condition to begin with. There were still a large number of production anomalies and flat audio. Disc 8 has an odd ring at the beginning of each segment, during scene access or skipping. I do appreciate the fact that they didn’t spindle the discs. Page flippers are much better on the discs and makes easier access to a specific set of episodes. This was the saving grace from 1 star. I will rate this 3 stars based on the a/v quality as follows: 5 Stars – The show itself. -3 Stars – A/V quality +1 Star – Packaging I believe the 5 – star overall rating for this set is misleading. While Grizzly Adams is no doubt a favorite classic, technically, the picture and audio quality fall short of expectations. NOTE: "The Renewal" & "Once Upon a Starry Night" ARE included in this set, so don't make the mistake I almost did and buy them.

history.review_title: It's Groundhog Day today, and time for me to react with disqus and wonder at this film I love.
history.text: It's Groundhog Day, and time for me to react with disgust and wonder. I love the film. I own it on VHS tape, and I wouldn't want to view it any other way. I've watched the movie as often as 5 times in a month. Why "disgust and wonder?" Larry's comment about what Phil might do with the groundhog. Should we believe that this is just a guy kind of thing to say and try to ignore it? I don't think so. But even if a viewer isn't disgusted, the line interrupts a key scene, like getting ice cold water in the face. One of these days, I'm going to take the tape to someone who can edit out that gross and needless remark so that I can thoroughly the movie in its entirety.

These men were far better off with their grudges and pranks. Ariel, who you will notice, if you watch 'Grumpier' old men, turns from the high-spirited woman of the original movie, into the same kind of frump that 'Maria" did in The Sound of Music, immediately following marriage. But the Ariel character is one wicked woman, and the degree to which the old buddies are taken in, is pathetic.

history.title: Newhart: The Complete First Season
history.review_title: Female actors should seek other employment if demeaning work like this is all they can get. Just have all-male shows and movies
history.text: I hated the Joanna script then. I hate it now. Johanna had it right when, as in the episode, 'You're Homebody 'til Somebody Loves You/, when she tells Dick that she thinks the only reason he wanted the inn was to be able to walk through it, and say that he loves the place. Meanwhile, she functions doing everything, including the bookkeeping, and restoration work. The trigger was Dick calling Joanna a "homebody," during an interview. Even the title is a slur on women. (Nothing wrong with BEING a homebody, but Joanna certainly isn't). This show was created in the 1980s. There is no excuse for writing the female lead as worthless, except for window dressing. But the same is true of 'Emily' in the Bob Newhart Show. Gagged me then - gagged me now. If you remove the female characters from either of these shows, it would have been better than to perpetuate the belief that women don't need, and won't take "real" jobs, or have a thought in their heads other than to have a maaa--n. The 'homebody' episode has Joanna, not standing up for herself, but seeking employment and then quitting before she starts, because she really just wants to be with 'Dick' and keep him and guests happy. This, even though she quit her studies in order to support Dick when he began his writing career. How many women were refused work because their potential bosses were sure they weren't serious about work, and would just be working for 'pin-money' - or would quit, or be absent the second their husband or child became ill. The answer is - hundreds of thousands, although no one worried about that during WWII. I know countless women who were turned down for work because, even if they were single, and not living with anyone, (as very few did, even by the 1980s, employers were certain that the women would quit as soon as a man appeared in their lives. In 'Newhart', slow, dull, incompetent 'George' still gets housed and fed. That wouldn't happen to a woman. 'Emily' in the Bob Newhart Show is the same deal, but, perhaps, worse, because she inflicts her warped view of being a woman on the children whose 3rd grade minds she influences, the few times she has a substitute teaching job. Otherwise, a screwdriver would have to be explained to her. What is astounding is that MTM Productions produced these shows even as "Mary Tyler Moore" productions, advanced the 'Mary Tyler Moore' show, 'Rhoda', et al. Why did Moore allow these females-as-idiot portrayals in the 'Newhart' shows She probably even watched Miss Frances in 'Ding Dong School' - or Margaret Rutherford as Jane Marple. Or listened to Marlo Thomas' 'Free To Be You and Me'. In 'Newhart', slow, dull, incompetent 'George' still gets housed and fed. That wouldn't happen to a woman.

history.text: Great movie - I hope they make a sequel. I was pleasantly surprised. They took the Judge Dredd universe seriously and made it for adults. Very fast-paced but they manage to convey everything you need to know about Dredd and his world. It's also not the least bit pretentious like some other superhero movies (see Batman v. Superman). This movie is lean & mean and kicks ass. Would be a great start to a series of movies exploring Mega-City One and I would be in line to buy tickets!

Very entertaining for fans of Lovecraft and movies like The Thing, Prince of Darkness, and even The Mist. The best low budget horror movies take themselves seriously, so The Void comes across as dark, scary and sinister rather than jokey or full of one liners. This serves the movie well and keeps you engaged for the relatively short run time of 90 mins. The FX are outstanding. Some reviewers wanted more explanation, but what explanation could there possibly be? It's basically a take on the Cthulhu mythology.

history.title: The Vietnam War Ken Burns
history.text: Some great footage is undermined by Ken Burns' obvious one-sided view on the war. I don't mind differences of opinion or interpretation, but when Burns glosses over all communist atrocities, beginning even with the First Indochina War, the film feels more like propaganda than even-handed documentary. This was a tough time for America - Burns should have treated the subject with greater academic rigor.

history.title: Drone Wars
history.review_title: Just when you think they hit bottom, a new low bobs to the surface.
history.text: A marginal ID4 clone with little to call it's own. Grim infighting among the characters with Mad Max morality did not make up for the lack of a SPFX budget. I liked Corin better in his monster bug movies. He got to show more humor which is his strong suit in those low brow time burners. In this he just runs around shooting anything that moves. His lighter side was wasted. He might have shined better as the villain. Considering the script, I doubt it.The SPFX are passable but the story stole a lot from District 9 as well as a couple of others. If you are an incurable Sci Fi geek like me you will get it anyway. But get it cheap, guys. The less you pay, the better you'll feel about it. 90 minutes felt kind of long while watching this one. Should have been better. Could have been better. Wasn't. Sigh.....

history.title: Poltergeist - The Legacy - Season 1
history.review_title: What a delightfully horrific surprise! Like finding an old fiend, I mean friend.
history.text: Wow! I just finished the 90 minute premier episode of this series. There is no point in waiting any further before logging in this critique. If you saw the series in it's US release back in the 80s, you ain't seen nothin' yet! This is the European version of this show and is as R rated as any theatrical feature of the time. The scares are quite creepy with eye popping special effects and the sex includes a demonic seduction that leaves nothing to the imagination. Keep the kiddies in the other room, Mommy. This is Halloween for the grown ups! I suspect this film actually got a foreign theatrical release before launching its TV syndication. What ever the rest of the series has in store, I am sure it will be a monster mash worth watching, if you are so inclined. BTW, the show took itself quite seriously. So do not look for in jokes and characters mugging the camera. This is way beyond Tales From The Crypt. Deliberately horrific stuff,,,just the way we like it! Insert maniacal laughter here.

history.title: I Am Dragon
history.review_title: I was a teenage dragon heart throb.
history.text: The painfully low budget did not hurt this fairy too much. The costumes and other trappings looked sparse. But the cast was solid and the story and direction did not lack for the proper zeal. To keep it short I will simply say that this was an entertaining fantasy in spite of all the obvious short comings. It is easy to get spoiled by mega-buck master works and become jaded when other films do not measure up. But I cannot bring myself to degrade this film just because it does't look like it cost enough to pay off the National Debt. Once again Hollywood has spent many a misguided dollar on far weaker stories with far bigger stars and come up with nothing worth talking about lately. ( You know the dud I am talking about.) Obviously the powers that were did not relegate the flow of the limited bucks in a way that maintained the level of the magic through out the first season. I very much liked the cast and the interplay between the inexplicable mix of nationalities ( and maybe even time periods). There was a part Ray Harryhausen, part Terry Gilliam feel to production and that may have been part of the problem. The first episode set a bench mark they never quite hit again. And that may have been their fatal mistake. But that doesn't mean that Sinbad Season One isn't fun. It stands on its own merits quite nicely. But I think if one pays attention, one can see why the show didn't last. For what ever reasons,the producers did not support their young Sinbad properly. Ultimately the production visually starved to death. Sinbad is traditionally about spectacle. And they ran out of funds long before they ran out of episodes. It was a shame. BUT!!! That only explains why there are not ten seasons. The first season listed here is over all well conceived, impressively produced, and populated with a cast of interesting characters, creatures, and situations. It is a shame they could not maintain it with a life span like Hercules. We could have used eight or nine more seasons. Season One is a lot of fun.

history.title: The Accidental Tourist [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The Accidental Tourist - the Subtle Mid-Tier Film We Do Not Have Anymore
history.text: This is one of the 80's true gems. A Lawrence Kasdan classic, it comes on the tail end of the high watermark of William Hurt, who by that point had appeared in five Oscar Best Picture nominees: The Big Chill (83), Kiss of the Spider-woman (85), Children of a Lesser God (86) - he should have won his second Oscar for this, Broadcast News (87), and The Accidental Tourist (88), after a major turn in the neo-noir Body Heat (80), netting three Best Actor nominations and two wins. The film is a mix of light humor (witness Travel Writer Macon Leary's eccentric family) and rather dark drama, as Hurt and Body Heat co-star, Kathleen Turner, endure the destruction of their marriage after the loss of a child - until Hurt's life is re-ignited by a romance with a near-perfect Geena Davis, just prior to The Fly (86) with Jeff Goldblum. The eighties were a magic time in cinema. The seventies had pushed enough boundaries that pushing boundaries for the sake of that alone died out in a way, and we were left with a mature cinema that gave us The Right Stuff (83) and Amadeus (84), Dangerous Liaisons (88), among countless hyper-competent lesser luminaries. This sort of mid-budget drama could never be made in today's era of explosively budgeted special effects vehicles obsessed with creating shared universe franchises and we are all the worse for it, as is film. Bill Pullman is also excellent as Hurt's "modern" agent. Hurt was the Pacino of the 80s.

history.title: Friday Night Lights - The Complete Series - Blu-ray
history.review_title: The BEST Sports Drama TV Ever Produced
history.text: Forget "The Sopranos," which was wonderful in many ways, along with "Breaking Bad," and much of the so-called HBO-driven golden-age of the TV series as a true writer's medium, and embrace this all-too-often unsung character-driven classic, the dirty little secret of which was that football only served as the backdrop for one of the finest examinations of a community, here: rural Texas, ever filmed. "FNL" had the panoramic reach of a realist Balzac novel. You see every social class, race, type and people - and none of it veers toward cliche; when the final season strikes, and we find the Coach coaching the cross-town, under-budgeted, nearly all African-American rival, you have a moment worthy of truly classic storytelling in which the hero is reborn on the opposite side. The performances and direction are complete A-list. When the current (Bronze Age of TV) winds up, and the history of the show-runner as driving force is re-written, expect this seldom sung classic to rise to the top. This is TV's version of "Million Dollar Baby," and "Rocky."

history.title: 100 Years of Olympic Films (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: An Immediately Cinematic Genre Distilled to the Most Comprehensive Olympic Visual History Available to Date
history.text: This is an unimaginable historic archive. Not one I would have seen coming. Milos Forman and other high caliber talent filmed these games, reaping art from what French filmmaker Eric Rohmer (his beloved body of work nearly lacked dynamic physical action) thought sports a genre that almost immediately yields dynamic visuals. This set is representative of Criterion's ever-increasing commitment to cinema history, with non-standard fare included (they could have, for example, limited this solely to films and eras already marked in textbooks). There is also a strong argument for categorizing films prior to 1920, and simply collecting it in as restored form as possible. Like many, I desire want a Blu-ray of Joe Frazier and Muhammad Ali (in Rome) - as well as Eric Heiden, and Nadia Comaneci in their most iconic moments. Michelle Kwan alone has an Odyssey in Nagano and Salt Lake City. Boxing as well is a sport I've studied since a lad when the great Hagler, Hearns, Duran, and Leonard exchanged greatness over and over, but we see these athletes in nascent stages, often away from their collective primes. The price may seem high but not for a set this comprehensive - post discounts. Target has it for around 266.00 and change now, slightly above a 33% discount; Amazon often cuts prices closer to release date, as public demand and awareness shifts.

history.title: Batman & Superman 9-Film Set (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Great Fub Gets its Due - No Darkness Here
history.text: I'm the contrarian. Most people I talk to and most critics I read really dig the Richard Donner cut on “Superman II,” the classic of the Christopher Reeve Superman tetralogy (yeah, I went there.) Now, I don't know whether it's nostalgia or fine memories of eating popcorn with Goobers dumped in and Twizzlers and coca cola wiring me like Times Square on the side. Those were the days. But I still love the original lighter cut. The cast is perfect. The bit with the trucker when Superman surrenders his powers is a classic moment in 80s cinema, as well as my childhood, right up there with “Star Trek II,” “Empire Strikes Back,” my beloved “Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom,” the supposed “stinker” of that series - well, wait until people see “Crystal Skull” and redefine “Indiana Jones stinkers with a blindingly bad low. “Superman III” has Richard Pryor, the audacity of that simply kicks ass. “Superman: The Movie” made me believe a man could fly, had a wildly all-star cast with Ned “Deliverance” Beatty and the always great Gene Hackman who even saves (for five seconds) the nadir that is “Superman IV” - “Nobody wants war Superman. We just want to keep the threat alive." (Too bad Nuclear Man wasn't a villain in the DC canon) - imagine some B-lister like Toy-man essayed by Martin Short, and you have elevated that spectacle by Kyptonian miles. The whole however sent me to Seven-Eleven spinner racks to add comics to my Big League Chew order. The whole began my life-long love affair with Smallville, Kansas, Lois Lane, Lana Lang, and Big Blue in general - not to mention Reeve who revealed himself as a legitimate hero in life; all we needed was Lori Lemaris and the briefest Super-boy bit, and I would have been rapt. Hell, I was rapt anyway. The Burton Batmans are both great, with Michelle Pfeiffer's Catwoman every bit as beautiful as she could be at that time and place (and still is, talk about aging with grace): the woman who made The Fabulous Baker boys swoon, along with every other red-blooded male in the nation. And in Stephen Frears’s “Dangerous Liaisons” and “Age of Innocence” by Martin Scorsese she proves her acting chops match the good luck of her biology. “Batman Forever” is simply good fun.

history.title: Justified - Season 06
history.text: Elmore Lenard who died in 2013 must be rolling over in his grave. Great characterization by Lenard, coupled with lousy script writing. Actors were cast way out of character engaged in contradictory action. Example: Boyd lets the pathetic little prison guard (who accused Ava of his self-inflicted wounds), off knowing full well that if the guard resends his testimony, Ava is free. Un-freekin-real! The marshals find the pathetic love sick looser and use him as bait to confuse Duffy. Un-freekin-real! They know that Ava is not guilty of the stabbings. But still they keep threating to send her back to prison where she is under death sentence from the inmates, with the added incentive of being a snitch. They give the marshals service a bad name and ought to be kicked out. If Ava had a good lawyer, they'd all be walking the streets. I take it back, Elmore would not be rolling over in his grave, he'd be doing summersaults! And my, wasn't it just so gratuitous of Waylan to forgive Ava for her trespasses. He's such a peach. (Gratuitous, by the way means unJUSTIFIED).

history.title: Grimm: Season Five [DVD]
history.review_title: Sergeant Wu and Monroe are exceptional characters
history.text: It certainly doesn't hurt to have two of the main characters bare a striking resemblance to Christopher Reeves and Julia Roberts. But it's the supporting cast which makes the series work exceptionally well, especially the characters of Reggie Lee as Sergeant Wu and Silas Weir Mitchell as Monroe. These characterizations are spot on with their humorous tongue-in-cheek dialog helping to maintain a light-hearted atmosphere and medium even in its darkest moments. The cinematography is also exceptional; the fade-in and fade-out sequences are harmonious and fluid as are the close-ups when interspersed with the long shots. Direction is at least on par with the Jesse Stone series. Though, I cannot help but wonder if the exceptionally pretty girls take some perverse pleasure in seeing themselves transformed into hideous beasts.

history.title: Limelight
history.text: Thanks, Rudy. I'd love to still be able to go to Limelight (now a shopping mall, in a church), but all I've got left is the Lion King. Nice legacy. That said, this movie is a great reminder of NYC's nightlife in its heyday, albeit one that's a little one-sided (the movie is produced by Peter Gatien's daughter, after all), but even so, still entertaining and full of 90s nostalgia. I grew up right across the street from the Limelight in my early 20s, so I lived and breathed this scene. Still great to see so many quotes from all the people they included in this documentary, including Michael Alig. A good documentary in general, but more specifically for people who witnessed firsthand the nightlife of NYC in the 90s.

history.title: Back to the Future: 25th Anniversary Trilogy [Blu-ray]
history.text: This review is about the packaging, not the movies (which are great to meh in descending order). Why does Every studio that creates multi-disc box set have to pack them in customized, horrible, difficult to use, damaging to the discs-packaging? Back to the Future Trilogy is no exception. What's wrong with disc spindles? It's only six discs (including digital copy discs), not twenty, so why Universal felt it was necessary to lodge these discs in inflexible, brittle, plastic side-tabs is beyond me. In order to pull the discs out you need to wedge your fingers under the sides of the disc, on the disc-read side, and unsnap it from its housing. Same goes for the digital copy discs although those come out more easily. Putting the discs back in is a mysterious process that involves unnerving amounts of plastic grinding against plastic, and 'pinching' of the disc to get it to fit back in under the tabs, none of which is good for the longevity of your remastered blu-ray collection. I wish movie studios would get over trying to innovate with standard boxed collections like this and just stick with what works. I give the collection four stars because the movies shouldn't be penalized for bad packaging, but it's really the first movie that's the winner in the bunch. The second movie was decent, but it doesn't age as well. The third movie, like most third movies, didn't really need to happen, and is just a poor postcard of its era. Great to have them all in one place, so I'm glad for that, but these movies are not created equally.

history.review_title: I will admit, I fell asleep watching this movie ...

I'm here to tell you about the format of this particular blu-ray set (the 3D listing in case these reviews are all mashed together). One thing I didn't count on was that this package ONLY comes with the 3D version. That's a rarity these days, to find a 3D movie that doesn't come with the 2D version. So, buyer beware, if you're ever in the mood to watch this film without the glasses, etc., make sure you pick up the Western 2D blu-ray as well.

history.review_title: DOES work on North American blu-ray players

Still a fun and funny movie though. Worth it to see the French reinterpretation of Billy the Kid and Calamity Jane. Also, I ordered this from Amazon.fr and can confirm that it plays on my unmodified Region A blu-ray player. The description text that says it doesn't work on normal US BR players is just some placeholder text they must slap on all non-native blu-rays. PLUS, it has English subtitles, so it's super import-friendly.

history.title: Don't Think
history.review_title: The Best Thing Next To Being There
history.text: If you've ever seen The Chemical Brothers in concert, this is as faithful a representation as you can possibly get without being there. The audio quality captures the thrill of a live show, with the appropriate aural ambience, crowd noise, and bassy, thumping beats. If you've never had the pleasure of seeing the Chemicals in person, this is as close as you can get, with both the CD and DVD providing great audio and video quality. This is basically a run-through of their greatest hits (of which they have plenty), with the minor quibble that 'Galvanize' is relegated to a small but familiar sample, while the entire song is omitted. Besides this minor gripe, it's a seamless set that sounds great both in the car or home stereo, and in headphones.

history.title: Wicked City (Remastered Special Edition)
history.review_title: Fun movie, excellent picture quality. One of Madhouse's best.
history.text: In lieu of a blu-ray release, anyone on the fence about picking up this dark Madhouse cult classic should purchase without hesitation. Despite the fact that this is only on DVD, the image quality is fantastic, clean and with minimal artifacting. If you don't already know, Wicked City is from the same makers of anime classics like Ninja Scroll and the more recent Redline. Wicked City is one of their earlier works from the late 80s, and is rich with violence and over-the-top Japanese sexuality, but if a NSFW anime movie isn't a problem for you, this is film belongs in any serious anime collection.

To have the entire series in place on blu-ray is pretty amazing, but the wealth of supplementary material --not to mention a special diecast metal Hot Wheels version of the Batmobile-- just puts it over the top. This entire campy series that'll remind you of when comic books didn't always take themselves so seriously (Christopher Nolan/Zack Snyder I'm looking at you and your Batnipples). Now if only we could get the entire original Spider-Man animated series from the 60s on blu-ray.

history.title: Gaiking: The Movie Collection
history.review_title: The best mech from the halcyon days of early 70s giant robots meets TERRIBAD dub quality
history.text: I love Gaiking, I grew up with it. But I made the mistake of thinking this movie set would be on par with the vastly superior TV series published here by Discotek. Instead, this 3-pack of Gaiking movies features what might be THE worst English dub (no Japanese audio here, sorry) I've ever heard in my life, and that's saying something. I mean, it's so bad. It's soooo bad. It sounds like something some students did as a home video editing project for their junior high video editing class, which is to say it sounds like something I'd have done when I was 13. It's terrible. The animation is also pretty spectacularly bad as well, but chalk this up to early 70s Japanese animation techniques. It's terrible in a charming, low budget way. The voice acting, however, is bad bad. Like, "you hate your children and let them watch this DVD set" bad. I took one for the team so you don't have to. Avoid at all costs.

history.title: Terminator 2: Judgment Day Endoarm Collectors Edition 4K Ultra HD [Blu-ray + Digital HD] [4K UHD]
history.review_title: Nice arm, but no 3D, no soundtrack?
history.text: The UK version is about the same price (MSRP) and comes with the 3D version AND the soundtrack on CD. The 3D rights may be tied up with the distributor, since the 3D version in theaters displays that "the 3D conversion was made possible by Studio Canal" which is publishing the film across Europe. Since they're not the publisher in North America, it's possible they're the ones preventing the 3D version from being released here, OR Lionsgate just didn't want to pay Studio Canal for the rights to the 3D version for North America, knowing that it's kind of a niche market for 3D fans (like me). Whatever the reason, it still sucks. They should just sell the arm separately to be honest.

history.title: Zoo: The Second Season
history.text: I never thought a second season of "Zoo" would be received with the same kudos as Season One. Season One was based on James Patterson's stunning novel. Season Two takes the novel far beyond the book and it works well, especially by keeping the cast intact from Season One. This was very entertaining and intriguing...lots of twists and turns. Now I understand Season Three will be on CBS and NetFlix this summer. I can't imagine what new content will equal or enhance the first two seasons but I'm eagerly awaiting. If you haven't seen either season, I recommend you read the book first. Patterson is a master of suspense and now he has turned to fantasy and sci-fi. He's unique and concise with all of his books. But "Zoo" is the best...the very best he's done.

history.title: La La Land
history.text: I'm speechless. Just bought the Six-time Academy Award winning movie "La La Land" and finished watching it a few minutes ago. I've been trying to come up with some non-cliche words to describe it. I can think of only one. BEAUTIFUL! What a nostalgic love story of old...from the Fifties...even Forties...when we had amazing dancers show their love on the dance floor. It gets my highest rating. A true love story for both men and women...about romancing and dreams...fulfilling your dreams. If you are a romantic at heart, this one will cost you a whole box of Kleenex. Emma Stone won the Oscar for Best Actress...I second that emotion. And Ryan Gosling should have received it for Best Actor. We're talking about a duo that was made for the screen. Their chemistry is amazing. I've never seen an actor and actress so convincing. You knew from the get go they'd fall in love. And you must remember I'm the music man. The soundtrack is incredible...perfect. And Ryan's dreams in this film mirror my dreams. THIS IS A MUST! It is a one-of-a-kind film during an era where we are immersed in special effects and sterile but hypnotic visuals. This one is from and for the heart...just like it used to be. I agree with the New York Times..."SHEER CINEMATIC BLISS".

history.title: Avenged
history.review_title: A MUST FOR HORROR AND GORE FANS!
history.text: If you're a true horror fan and love lots of gore, this one's for you. This chilling flick about a woman that is abducted out in the middle of nowhere and brutally ravaged by a group of low-life freaks, is a classic "revenge" film...much like the Tarantino genre. Amanda Adrienne is the perfect actress in this role. The makeup is gruesome in transforming her from an innocent young woman into a she-devil from Hell. I gave it all 5 stars because it never dragged...always coming back with more thrills and twists until the very end. Give it a try. You won't be disappointed.

history.title: Absentia
history.text: Are you kidding me? This was total yawner. I bet they spent less the a grand on this bomb. It is an embarrassment to the horror genre. If I ever see the front of that house again, I'll cringe. It was so slow. This story could have been told in 15-20 minutes. They milked this for every second and it crawled along slower than a baby snail. Was there a scare factor? Absolutely not! The scariest part was enduring this until the end only to discover that this silly plot, script and acting would probably get no better than a C (average) grade in college film class. Don't waste on this crime.

So, without affecting my rating for the Humanoids, I give this a 5 on Amazon's scale. Humanoids is a classic sci-fi gem. It would make a wonderful stage production but in today's high tech, all about special effects world, it would probably bomb. If you appreciate sci-fi at its best, and enjoyed the TV series "The Twilight Zone", Creation of the Humanoids is for you. Well worth the cost. "War Room" explains how spiritual warfare works, and "God is not Dead 2" shows what it looks like when it happens. Both side of the controversial issue of talking about Jesus in the classroom are presented well -- no favor is given to either side, so the plot is as solid as life.
