history.title: Fear in the Night (Film Chest Digitally Restored Version)
history.review_title: Red herrings in store for everyone involved
history.text: Sometimes we have to go back to older films to find some of the charm that's missing in today's world, and some of the technology that was missing in the past. Some of the language used in these movies is almost quaint, innocent even. In this particular movie, a man is wearing a wire to get a confession. The fun part is that it is being recorded on a phonograph record, not a cassette, or computer. This is part of the joy in watching older films, and I'll never understand why younger people think that the only good movies have to be in color. Film Chest Restoration company brings us Fear In The Night. In this 1947 film Vince (A pre-Star Trek DeForest Kelly, looking a little like Gary Sinise) is haunted by a dream in which he kills a man he doesn't know, when he is accidentally handed the murder weapon by the dead mans female accomplice. After waking from this dream,, he finds that he has the closet key in his pocket in which he hid the body in, and also a button from the dead mans coat. He calls in sick to work in order to talk to his brother in law detective Cliff (Paul Kelley). At first, Cliff just brushes this off as a bad dream, and the key & the button were just things Vince happened to have and forgot about. As the film progresses though, things become clearer and Cliff is starting to wonder if Vince truly is a murderer, and using the dream angle just to try to get sympathy. As the story plays out you'll find there are surprises and red herrings in store for everyone involved, including the viewer. Being a 1947 ultra low budget film, you have to wonder how this is still even a watchable print. Well, we can thank the good folks at Film Chest Restoration for that to a degree. I still wonder what the source print was that they had to work with. This restored print still has a lot of damage, dirt and debris. There is also a faint humming sound in the background throughout the duration of the film. The print is also quite dark in places, and I wonder if that could have been improved. All of these questions will have to go unanswered as this film is a bare bones release with no extras whatsoever. I was hoping at the very least for a feature on the restoration process, but there is nothing but chapter stops and the film itself on the disc. It's shot in the regular aspect ratio 1.33:1 and the sound is a sometimes muffled mono. If you're a fan of this film, I'd advise you to try to find a way to see it first to see if this upgrade is worth a purchase. If you've never seen the film before, a rental is still advised before spending the money for a copy.

history.title: Yes - Live Hemel Hempstead Pavillion, UK October 3rd 1971
history.text: Taken from the BBC show "Sounding Out", Yes-Live at Hemel Hempstead Pavilion October, 3rd 1971 is an exercise in contrasts. First of all this should be a budget priced item. At only 23 minutes long and no extras, the distributor is banking on the fact that this is rare material to get people to shell out the money for it. Established, long time fans who have most everything that the band has put out will probably pay the price. Those who are newer to the band, and coming to the video side of thing for the first time will undoubtedly look elsewhere to find a better bargain. This DVD package is just about as well thought out and made as it can be for what it is. Inside the case is a semi replica tour program that talks about each of the band members, and even has a page dedicated to the opening act. It's a pretty nice 12 page booklet with plenty of pictures. The DVD case is clear, and when you open it up, there are even more pictures of the group in concert, and interview. Stills obviously taken from the television show. The program is in full frame, and it would have been nice if it would mention somewhere on the outside of the case that this was from a BBC half-hour special with partial performances and interviews. I would feel like I was getting ripped off, expecting a concert. The only thing that hints to something unusual is the 23 minute run time on the back of the package. Fans know that some of the bands songs are longer than this whole program and would probably wonder what was up. Here is the setlist for the (Partial) performances; 1.Introduction 2.Long Distance Runaround Pt.1 3.I've Seen All Good People 4.Perpetual Change 5.The Fish/Stage Setup 6.Long Distance Runaround Pt.2 7.Heart Of The Sunrise 8.Long Distance Runaround Pt.3 9.Mood For A Day 10.Yours Is No Disgrace Still, we're talking about 43 year old footage here, and it's not in bad shape either. Its fun to see the simple setup of a rock band in the early 70's. Kids today would have a heart attack trying to watch this without the million dollar laser show, dozens of barely dressed dancers, and auto tune on all the vocals. That's what makes this a little piece of history, a little time capsule that shows that true musicianship was the way to make a living. That talent counted more than an expensive light show for entertainment. This is also the simple reason why the band are still around to this day, almost 50 years on they're still making music that's worth hearing.

history.title: Petty, Tom - Dogs On The Run: A Musical Documentary
history.text: Wow, what a mess. Not Tom Petty of course. Tom would sound good covered in molasses and strung through an 40 year old 8-track player. That doesn't mean that he doesn't deserve quality though, because he does. Tom Petty & The Heartbreakers are one of the great American rock and roll bands. They deserve the best because they give the best. However, Laser Media has seen fit to try to screw up as much of this release as they possibly can. Beware of Laser Media, because they seem like a hit and run type operation. The type that puts out big name bands on DVD, but gets the concerts from a 3rd generation VHS tape recorded from television. That's not to say this release or others aren't unique or rare, it's just that the releases are so shoddy you'll need to have music that you really love to be able to handle all of the crap that the company lazily puts out. This concert comes from 1980, and tom had just released only his third album, Damn The Torpedoes. That statement alone is eye opening. We get to see Tom & the band in a 34 year old concert. The fact that this exists is amazing on its own, but then you remember who put this DVD out. There are no credits at the beginning or the end of the show. It's called a "musical documentary" when its clearly a 45 minute concert. The cover shows Tom from maybe 2000-2005, when this is a 1980 show. The DVD starts in the middle of the first song, and ends in the middle of the last song. Lastly, how did this company get away with this without being sued? I'm sure this could be cleaned up a lot and have added extras with a professional job done by a reputable company. There must be a gray area of copyright that I'm missing that allows these shoddy releases to come out. Now mind you, as much as I bash on this release, it's still good to have this time capsule unearthed, it's just disappointing to see it done so haphazardly. Here is the tracklisting for the concert; 1.Shadow of A Doubt (one of my favorite Tom songs, and the DVD starts in the middle of the song!) 2.Anything That's Rock And Roll 3.Even The Losers 4.Here Comes My Girl 5.I Need To Know 6.Luna 7.Stories We Could Tell 8.Refugee 9.Breakdown 10.American Girl (DVD ends right during the climax of the song) So there it is. But then there is the problem as well. Are you a big fan of Tom Petty? Do you have a lot of his stuff? If you answer yes, you'll probably want to add this to your collection, but ONLY because of the rarity of seeing the band near the beginning of their career. Newcomers need stay far away from this release, and look for the Soundstage DVD if you want to see Tom live. Established fans can give this one a go, but only if you find it on a really big sale price. Laser Media, you need to step up your game, or get out of the business.

history.title: Uriah Heep - One More Night: Collectors Rarities
history.text: It's been said the Uriah Heep were the real Spinal Tap of rock and roll, and although you can hear it in a few of the lyrics and over the top theatrics, this disc is made in such horrible quality that most of the time it's hard to tell. Once again we have another DVD from the fine rip-off artists at Laser Media. 41 Minutes of torture at the hands of poor DVD authoring, horrible sound quality, bad picture quality and a straight up lie on the front cover of the music that is contained inside. The worst thing about the disc is that there are moments, even though this is obviously recorded from an old VHS tape, that the audio and video of what could have been shine through for several moments during the running time. If someone reputable had got their hands on this material and cleaned it up, we could have had a nice hodge-podge of a collection to enjoy once in a while. However, thanks to Laser Media all we get is a coaster to throw in the trash. Uriah Heep were giants of heavy stoner prog rock back in their early to late 70's heyday. They put out big, bombastic albums that somehow sold like the cheapest new drug in town. They were a mess of hair, falsetto vocals, loud Keyboards and songs about witches, wizards and stealin'. Some form of the band still tours to this day, and I'm not sure if there are any original members left in it. Well, this video tries to show them doing their greatest hits. The front cover makes it sound like it's a T.V. broadcast from the 70's. While most of the material is from that time, there is some 80's garbage thrown in, and the live clips only make up about 3/4 of the DVD. The rest of the clips are promo videos, and the best of all of this is only in barely passable VHS quality. The sound is surprisingly decent throughout, and quite good in a few clips. Here is the track listing; 1.Stealin'(Live) 2.Tears in My Eyes (Live in Japan) 3.Easy Livin' (Promo Video) 4.Gypsy 5.I Won't Mind 6.Sweet Lorraine (Live-Horribly distorted sound) 7.Wizard (Nice Sounding promo video-"highlight" of the DVD) 8.Traveler In Time (Live in Japan) 9.Blind Eye (Footage doesn't even match the song) 10.One More Night (dubbed "live") Uriah Heep may be hard to come by on DVD. but don't get tricked into buying this mess. This DVD is in full frame with barely passable sound. There are no opening or end credits, and no information about the band or where these clip come from. The back of the case says that this release is in Dolby Digital, and I highly doubt that. I tend not to believe much from a company that can't even spell the titles of the tracks correctly on the back of the package, and trick the buyer into thinking their getting a 70's concert. Stay very far away from this release. No price is low enough to bother to have it in your collection.

history.title: R40 [6 Blu-ray Box Set]
history.text: It's too bad you have to put stars to say anything. I also have all the material here besides the bonus stuff. I was wondering, however, if this has the deluxe version of R30 included? Does it have the two guitar picks, and the two extra CD discs that were available only in that package at the time? Someone said earlier to just trade your old versions in and get this, but if I'm going to be losing exclusive goodies & audio material by doing so, I think I'll be waiting for a stand-alone release of the bonus material. I've gone down the "feeling ripped off" road already by buying the Working Men CD AND DVD for 1 song. history.title: The Martial Arts Kid DVD
history.text: Don “The Dragon” Wilson (Bloodfist) and Cynthia Rothrock (Shanghai Express) are back in action in The Martial Arts Kid, a coming of age story about Cleveland teen, Robbie Oakes (Jansen Panettiere), who moves to Cocoa Beach, Florida to live with his Aunt Cindy (Rothrock) and Uncle Glen (Wilson) after getting arrested in Ohio. Upon his arrival, he meets Rina (Kathryn Newton), whose boyfriend, Bo (Matthew Ziff), has made it his personal mission to make Robbie’s life as difficult as possible. Now with something in his life to stand up for, Robbie soon finds himself learning martial arts from his Aunt and Uncle to protect himself and the people he cares about. The film boasts an impressive cast of over a dozen real-life Gransmasters and/or World Champions. Some of them - and a few others - have pay-attention-or you'll miss-them appearances in the trailer, including: Christine Bannon-Rodrigues, Dr. Robert Goldman, Natasha Blasick, Rick St. Clair, Eric Kovaleski, Nassim Little Dragon" Lahrizi, JJ "Golden Dragon" McParland and Olando Rivera. The anti-bullying message may, to some, be laid on a bit thick - but it's a message that sticks.The positive messages that run through The Martial Arts Kid make it perfect for youngsters who are in the martial arts, as well as those who should be. But there are plenty of gems that make it fun to watch even if you're a generation removed from that target audience.

history.title: Mad Men: Season 1
history.review_title: Revolutionary in Its Honesty and Doesn't Glamorize the 1960s As Much As You Think
history.text: What's great about "Mad Men" is that it doesn't indulge in the usual cliches about the 1960s. All the characters are depicted as living only in the moment and oblivious to how history will later view that era. Yes, we have the obligatory mentions of JFK, RFK, Martin Luther King, et al, but there is no dramatic underlining of these figures, no breathless nostalgia for how people looked and acted. This is a refreshing change from shows that are set in the past but are too self-conscious about it (think "That 70s Show", or "Happy Days"). "Mad Men" is more than a history lesson and an excuse to trot out vintage pillbox hats and white gloves. I think this is because creator Matthew Weiner is a member of Gen X, that often maligned offspring of famously narcissistic and self-congratulatory Baby Boomers, rather than the retro-loving, surface-is-all hipster crowd who think clothing and protests (whatever they're for) are what made the 60s cool. In addition to great characterization, dialogue, plot, etc, it shows how people of that era really acted toward one another with unblinking honesty: no one here apologizes for having racist, sexist or anti-Semitic thoughts. They will do Al Jolson in blackface, insult Japanese or Jewish businessmen, pull up women's skirts and call them "honey" and "sweetheart" and think nothing of it. That honesty in itself is revolutionary, and serves as a frequent wake up call to anyone yearning to idealize that era. No, this is America in all its ugliness, even at the height of its money and power.

history.title: Fabulously Frugal Feasts
history.review_title: Not Frugal - Meals Made Out of Canned and Ready Made Food
history.text: The host was pleasant but the meals were not really "frugal." While she shows you that a few corncobs from the farmer's market can be used to make a tasty dish, every recipe includes a lot of canned or ready made food. For example, she used pre-made stuffing from a bag, Pillsbury Crescent rolls and even instant gravy from a jar. How is this frugal? You can make your own gravy and pastry dough for far cheaper. Worse, the host seems slightly contemptuous of frugality. She tells viewers not to reject pasta "as a poor person's dish," which I found condescending and insulting to all the Italian chefs out there. Then, like a host in an info commercial, she shows off a bunch of kitchen gadgets, like the Nutri bullet blender and a portable stovetop, which she brags was only $20. Seriously, she reminds me a friend who's always broke but loves showing off all the unnecessary crap she buys. Overall, the quality was on par with a typical homemade Youtube video. I'm not sure how Amazon Prime chooses videos to add to its "included with Prime" collection, but this was mediocre.

history.review_title: Ricci is Beautiful and Touching as the Doomed Zelda
history.text: Not since "Mad Men" have I enjoyed a period drama as much as this! Each episode is barely 30 minutes long but you never feel the writers packing every minute with action and rushing the story. If anything, the opposite is true - the pace for each episode is slow but so detailed that you savor every small epiphany and by the time the episode ends, you feel you've watched something deep and meaningful. Ricci, while not physically resembling the real Zelda all that much, manages to capture her youthful vigor and southern belle spunkiness. Her wide eyed expressions, musical Southern accent and delicate physique makes you feel protective of her and hope that everything will turn out well, which is hard to bear when you know what happened to the real Zelda. The real-life story of F. Scott and Zelda is quite poignant, and this first season is so affecting I hope the second season continues the quality of the first!

history.title: Candleshoe
history.review_title: One of Disney's Best From the 1970s
history.text: Next to "Escape from Witch Mountain" (the original), this was my favorite movie as a kid, and while some of it now seems a little dated and hokey, it's surprisingly "adult" and quite moving, especially at the end (won't give away a spoiler). Jodie Foster does some mugging for the camera early on, but then she really settles into the role and proves why she is such a great actress (it's hard to believe she did Taxi Driver before this film!) David Niven is charming and Helen Hayes is a sweet old lady and the pair give the film a classy Old Hollywood feel. I really prefer the 1970s Disney movies- they have a grittiness and honesty that make them so much more "real" than what came before them (the saccharine, Technicolor saturated 1960s) and what came after (today's loud, crudely drawn and cliched Disney films).

history.title: Escape To Witch Mountain
history.text: This film mesmerized me as a young child, and I remember insisting on seeing it twice (though my poor father had to sit through this and another Disney film, back when Disney did double features!). I refuse to see any of the remakes because, to me, Kim Richards and Ike Eisenmann ARE Tony and Tia, though I know the new ones must have better special effects. This film is pre Star Wars and so the special effects may seem primitive compared to today's CGI, but the story is so good you forget how awkward and embarrassingly fake the effects are. The music is great also, back when even Disney films had memorable, catchy soundtracks. A great film to watch with your kids on a rainy day.

history.title: A Hologram For The King [DVD + Digital]
history.review_title: Better Suited for the Small Screen, with Great Acting (As Usual) By Hanks
history.text: What a difference a small screen makes! I originally saw this in the theatre and felt it was slow moving and went nowhere. Then, a year later, I decided to download it since it was a free Prime Video, and I was blown away by it. I suppose the introspective nature of the story and the pacing simply work better on a small screen, and since you're watching it at home, you can always pause it when needed, so you never feel like the story drags. Tom Hanks plays Alan Clay, a middle-aged father who's been financially struggling to support his daughter ever since he made a bad decision to outsource the jobs at the Schwinn bicycle factory to Chinese workers. Not only did the Chinese workers do the work more cheaply, but the Chinese management copied the company's product and took over the business as well, putting Clay out of a job. This irony is just one of a series of ironies for our sad-sack hero, who resembles Bill Murray in "Lost in Translation" but is far worse-off. I thought the cab driver character who keeps helping Clay out of a jam felt like a stereotype, the wisecracking native who becomes the tour guide for the white hero, but the love affair between Clay and the reserved Muslim doctor felt compelling and natural, which was a relief. The underwater scenes were beautiful and you really felt Clay's pain. This film really seems made for an older audience and asks viewers to look at themselves, which explains why it flopped at the Cineplex. It's really too bad because these types of introspective, quiet films are few and far between, and yet they leave you with a more profound understanding of life than a dozen of those shoot-them-up, blow-them-up blockbusters and mindless superhero movies you see advertised everywhere.

history.review_title: Chilling Documentary That Exposes How Fast Food Companies Exploit Poor Countries to Make Money
history.text: Entertaining and shocking documentary on how fast food in developing countries (India, Brazil) is loaded with more fat and fake cheese because companies take advantage of those countries' corrupt governments and lack of regulation. McDonald's, KFC, Coca-Cola, Domino's etc., are exposed as being nothing more than a type of drug dealer, shipping toxic food to unsuspecting victims. No wonder so many people around the world hate US corporations. It's all about the money and they don't care if people worldwide get diabetes.

history.review_title: Superficial Treatment of Mental Illness in 90s Romantic Comedy
history.text: Quirky 90s movie that dates pretty badly today. A very young Johnny Depp plays a wacky old movie fan who dresses like Buster Keaton and sometimes acts like Charlie Chaplin. He falls for a mentally ill young woman who's being cared for by a protective but apparently controlling older brother (played by Aidan Quinn). Of course these two "misfits" fall in love. Being a "misfit" is one thing, but suffering from a serious medical issue like schizophrenia is something else. Once again Hollywood decides that miracles are possible and that true love is so strong that it can even cure mental illness. Unlike "A Beautiful Mind," the heartbreaking reality of psychological illness makes this "feel good" film hard to stomach.

I'm a big fan of "Mad Men" and hoped this show would satisfy my yen for vintage drama, but this show has very little subtlety and comes across as loud, crude and annoying self-conscious in its portrayal of an affluent Jewish woman in the 1950s. She is so narcissistic and entitled that the "feminism" of her being a stand-up comic is almost entirely lost. The show actually makes me glad I live in present-day NYC where I don't have to hear that dreadful "Noo Yawk" nasal accent as it was in the 50s and 60s (yes, it's still there but seems limited now to only certain areas). Sorry, but I'll stick to "Mad Men" reruns.

Take the early 2000s comedy hit "Borat" and mix it with the 70s classic "The Cheap Detective" and you get the tone and style of "Comrade Detective." Like "Borat" the audience is asked to believe that what we're about to watch is actually restored footage from a lost and obscure Communist propaganda film, only it's an American-style "cop show" from the 1980s with, of course, Communist twists - instead of "criminals", the detectives have to fight evil "capitalists" bent on sowing discontent among comrades and promoting toxic items like Jordache jeans and Monopoly. It's all very funny down to the faux "badly dubbed" mismatched lip synching that makes any exchange seem ridiculous. But what worked as a long, extended joke for one film may not translate well to a regular series (for an example, see the 1990s show "Police Squad!" which offered "Airplane!"-style humor but bombed after a few seasons because the jokes became repetitive). Hope this doesn't happen to "Comrade Detective," but for now, I'll enjoy this "vintage" Cold War-era show that was "rescued" from obscurity.

I was surprised at the level of violence that the child faced, and some of the violent interactions between the animals, it seemed a little extreme for a PG movie. Obviously there is no comparison to the Disney animated version, the characters are similar, and they even tried to push in some of that old Disney music from the original movie, but the charm and enthusiasm were missing. The only part of the movie that I found interesting involved Scarlet Johansson's voice-over as the snake, whatever they did to modify her voice was amazing! Listening to her voice was hypnotizing! Overall, I thought this movie was a little too violent at times, annoying in others, and boring for the remainder. Sadly not a movie I have any interest in seeing again.

history.title: Masterpiece: Poldark
history.text: Beautifully made, well acted, and addictive to watch. I never read the books, so I knew nothing about the Poldark drama beyond what was written on the back of the DVD box. I was hooked the first episode! The scenery locations are stunning, as are the costumes and the buildings used. The acting is amazing, and the character of Poldark just draws you in. You come to truly care for him, his loved ones, and those less fortunate he tries to help and care for. You come to see that he is truly a good man, with a beautiful heart. I loved watching Demelza transformation from a "kitchen wench" to a strong beautiful lady. Ross and Demelza are so wondefully matched. I eagerly look forward to Season 2.

history.title: Pride + Prejudice + Zombies [Blu-ray]
history.text: I wasn't sure I would like this movie, but I decided to give it a try. I love Pride and Prejudice, I enjoy watching zombies (thanks to The Walking Dead) so I figured, why not watch something that combines the two. I was pleasantly surprised to find that after 30 or so minutes into the movie I was actually looking forward to seeing how this would all end. I have to say I LOVED the scene where Darcy proposes to Elizabeth, that was absolutely hilarious...I rewound that scene a few times. While I was originally skeptical of what I thought would be a cheesy horror, tongue in cheek movie, was really very entertaining! I did not care for the little clip after the credits, I thought that was unnecessary, I like my movies all tidily wrapped up, but overall I actually have the desire to watch this crazy movie again!

history.title: Legend of the Seeker: Season 2
history.text: One of the best TV shows I have seen in years. I have missed it for a long time since it was taken off the air. I still hope that someday they decide to make a movie, but won't hold my breath. The scenery and costumes are gorgeous, and the actors/actress are well casted into their roles. The story line is excellent, and well-acted. I watch it and re-watch it a couple of times a year, and it never gets old. I actually find or catch things that I may have missed prior, little nuances or quips that were over looked. People get all bent out of the shape that it doesn’t follow the books, I can care less about that because I only read the first book, and didn’t enjoy it. The TV show clearly says “based on”, nowhere does it say “an actual representation of the books.” So people can get off their pedestals and enjoy the show for what it is, and not what they want it to be. Overall, I love the TV show, and can’t recommend it enough.

I saw the movie on 4/21 for a school field trip. I really enjoyed the movie until the last 10 or so minutes of it. Prior to that everything was beautifully filmed and tastefully shot. For almost the entire movie the "predator/prey" sections were shown in such a way that the children were not exposed to any dramatic death scenes or graphic scenes of animals trying to kill and eat other animals. Even the hawk trying to catch the baby monkeys, and subsequently catching one of them only showed a one second clip of a faraway hawk with a monkey in its claws. All of this began to change when the Snow Leopard scenes began to progress. Prior to this any "predator/prey" scenes were only a second or two, and shot in such a way that we never saw the actual kill, just the limp prey’s body after the fact. Spoilers.... First we see the mother Snow Leopard injuring her paw on sharp rocks beneath the snow, there is some blood on the snow. Things become more dire as time progresses and she is unable to catch any prey to feed her 2 babies. The last 10 minutes of the film show the mother Snow Leopard desperate to catch anything as she and her babies are starving. She decides to attack a baby yak and the movie shows her clinging to the baby’s neck trying to drag/kill it. The mother yak shows up and begins to head-butt, stomp on, and gore the Leopard with her horns. This dragged out "predator/prey" scene is in my opinion unnecessary, and way too graphic. Whereas the prior scenes were only a second or two, this one went on for at least a minute, minute and a half. Why should any child have to see a Leopard trying to tear the throat out of a baby yak, or see that same Leopard brutalized by a yak. You can hear the sounds of the mother yak stomping on, head-butting, and goring the Leopard. The Leopard eventually releases the baby, and then we are left with the mother yak comforting her baby, and a mother Leopard that will suffer and die from her injuries. I know this is what happens in nature, however it’s not something that should have been shown in such a dragged out way. The mother Leopard is clearly going to die from her injuries, and her babies left without a provider or protector. This whole tragic ending just ruined the film. Disney of course tries to make light of it by talking about the circle of life, and showing birds jumping up and down in sun, and revealing a brand new baby panda, but the whole thing is ruined by seeing this mother’s death. According to the producer the 2 Leopard babies are "safe" but I am sure if they said anything otherwise the film would have been boycotted. I would never recommend this movie, nor ever consider watching it again.

history.title: Beauty And The Beast
history.text: I was really looking forward to this movie. Beauty and the Beast was one of my favorite Disney movies growing up, so I was excited to see the update! Unfortunately, I was deeply disappointed. The actors were lackluster, and the music/songs were not as good as the original. The "beast" was not very beastly nor convincing. Belle was boring, and just lacking charm. The CGI was alright, I didn't appreciate nor care for the added songs, it just seemed like they had to add something to make the movie longer. The back story of Belle's mother, and the Beast's "horrible" childhood were unnecessary and just seemed goofy. There was no point to either one of them, and it felt like another attempt to extend and further drag out the movie. There were a few scenes that I thought were lovely, but not enough to ever make me want to see this movie again. A very boring, and disappointing remake!

history.title: Passengers [Blu-ray]
history.text: I did not like the movie when I first saw it, but after watching it, it stuck with me. I have watched it a few times since, and really enjoy it! The graphics are amazing, and the actors are really good! The only thing that bugs me is the ending. I would have liked to have seen something that shows their life together, the years they had together. Maybe a few clips showing the progression of time...did they have kids? How did they die? How long did they live? What did they do together? It just seems to end abruptly, and we are left hanging with questions about their future.

Saw it at the show 12/21, and I absolutely loved it. I am eagerly looking forward to seeing it again, and will definitely purchase it when it comes out. I loved what they have done with the characters thus far, I felt like everything was handled appropriately regarding Luke's character, and Leia's. Kylo Ren and Rey had an amazing story line, and I am eagerly looking forward to the 9th episode. Compared to George Lucas, these new directors and story writers far exceed all expectations.

history.review_title: Still like a wonderful new feature film ! NEVER AGES !
history.text: Great HD BluRay encoding of this movie. High rez makes some of the special effects look real 'star trek' like ! Sooo many extras, information, deleted scenes, gag reel, interviews, and interactive information about the planets and star system of Firefly. You do not have to watch the FireFly TV show to enjoy this movie. But if you like, you can watch FireFly on Netflix or Amazon, then see this movie. Knowing more of the back story makes enjoying Serenity the movie even better ! :-) PLOT : The TV show has River Tam and her brother run away from the Alliance government. In Serenity, River and the whole crew from Firefly discover why the Alliance wants her back, and why they will do anything to stop her.

history.review_title: How patient are you ? Draggingly slow movie puts most kids to sleep...
history.text: 15 minutes to the start, anoth 5 minutes to get in a space ship, 20 minutes of your life lost waiting for the beginning. They start translating words while the paranoid human race goes crazy. Skipping all the details, Arrival is a pro-life movie against abortion. If you want to figure out why, watch the whole movie. But for a SciFi movie with big spaceships, almost no violence, and that's very good!

history.title: Groundhog Day (15th Anniversary Edition)
history.review_title: Welcome to Pennsylvania. You are Home.
history.text: An all time forever eternal classic that calls into play the very meaning of living, in a ddeper way than you'll feel, because Bill Murray is just that much fun.

history.review_title: Watch the warnings from the past to prepare for today.
history.text: More of a clip show than a History Channel review of Science Fiction. True to the Form, the low budget review seems copied from VHS tape, but that adds charm for people who remember Old TV the way it was, static, black and white, fuzzy color with even worse sound - No 4K HD Stereo here - and that is a good thing. The media changes in technology threaten to erase our history - from nitrate film, silent film, to black and white, to color film, video tapes, DVDs, Blurays, and now 4K digital. This reviews things as they were seen back then. If you are wondering what old movies would be a good viewing - here are dozens of films for you to consider. Some you may have seen already. Oddly enough, in the first episode, one film predicted robotics to be replacing humans by 2071. 2017 as I write this and already drivers and fast food workers, ambulances, taxis, trucks, and construction machines being automated to work as robots. No humans needed. It is VERY interesting to see the SciFi predictions of the past, what they missed out on (social decay) and what they predicted (cell phones, etc) A good view for when you want to see where film was, and realize some of the big time movies of today are just re-makes of films from the 1950s

history.review_title: Insults the Military that gives him the freedom to make these films.
history.text: Insults the Military the defends America. The Purpose of War is to WIN. Destroy other countries and make your country more powerful. Michael Moore must have never learned that in Military History 101. The LOST wars, WW-2, Korea, Veitnam, etc. where because civilians with NO Military training and NO military background, come up wih bad commands, stupid instructions, and just plain wrongful thinking. USA Needs a new Constitutional Amendment: 4 Years Military service to hold office in the Senate or higher Executive branches. How can you become the Commander in Chief of the WHOLE PLANETWIDE USA MILITARY - if you have never carried a rifle, commanded a squad, or took care of your men and women in uniform on your own base ? Every ''Lost'' war has Dozens of books explaining how they could have been won. War is a constant state of being for USA, which grew up from a war based economy, and continues from the revolution through today as a war based economy. Ideally - Business is the Business of USA, War should only be used as a last resort against those who harm U.S.
Fairly good overview of how a few guys literally created their own world wide industry of entertainment with lights and electronics, and almost no actual musicians.

history.review_title: Great Show with a few flawed ideas and stupid war story
history.text: Top notch all the way. Great story and Characters. Although it rapidly degraded into yet another generic war story, just like Deep Space 9. If You want to watch war stories, plenty of those in real life !!! If you want some real science stories set to fictional plots, well... you probably expect more than this show delivers. The U.N. totalitarian government feeding the whole Earth is a bit far fetched. Everyone living in poverty is believable. Our current Nation-States quibble and fight too much, but if EARTH met an Alien race and expanded a bit out into the stars maybe people would see themselves as 'Earthings' then ? Also, no real explanation on why planet Earth nedds to go digging in space for resources, when harvesting respurces ON Earth is far easier and cheaper, faster and not as life threatening as exploring space. If Space flight became cheap and clean, sure ! But facing the hard cold dark of space is a bit beyond the reach of flying Hondas... Also, we have fully automated machines now that can dig for resources... The future of humans mining of space will be done by robots. AI robots work for free, can not die, and require far less resources to function and maintain in space. Colonization and teraforming of Mars is firstly a job for automation... humans would come much later.

history.title: The Cult of Mary
history.review_title: Thought provoking, very detailed, amazing photography.
history.text: Well... if an outer space alien visted you and made you pregnant with a superhuman hybrid, you would be famous too ! I LOVE JESUS 100% and I believe people should not only follow teaching of love and kindness and peace, but also people should be figuring out HOW Jesus did these wonderful things. Or more directly, set aside the mythology and research the science that can help us cure illness, regrow missing limbs, heal blindness of eyes, minds, hearts and souls. I never realized Mary had so many temples built for her all over the world. I do believe Mary and Jesus would have been African in appearence, but their message of faith and hope can be enjoyed by all people of the world. I look forward to the time when science and medicine has developed the many skills Jesus demonstrated so long ago. Some say since he is God, he can travel through time and was showing us such wonderful inventions are possible. Certainly people 2,000 years ago wpuld think our technology today is magic. Sadly our war like civilizations are still growing and have yet to bring Heaven on Earth. Blessings to all who watch this beautiful video.

history.title: Humanity's End
history.review_title: A so-so film with a good ending, after the 10 minute intro, you can skip to the last 40 minutes...
history.text: The First 5 Minutes are hard to get through, but the last 36 minutes is where the actors really start to shine. Humanity's END seems like a single take rough edit, but it's filled with special effects that probably ate most of its budget. The middle hour of the movie is just drawn out, and it could be edited down to a 45 minute TV episode by cutting out a lot of the middle. The story is of different races fighting to destroy humanity and recover the DNA secret for immortality. The last 36 minutes is worth watching, and has a really good ending. So for that I give it four stars. Good job to the actors who worked hard to make the best of the script they were given!

history.title: Dan In Real Life
history.text: This movie has some good moments, but overall it is so-so. The dialogue is often bad and the situations are hard to relate to my own experiences. I have yet to have a relative discuss with me the merits of masterbation, for example, especially in a big family gathering situation. The performances are good and even likable, even when the characters are unreasonable brats. While I see what the filmmakers intended, this movie does not really go over well. If you are in the mood for nothing special then by all means give this movie a try; otherwise, don't bother.

history.title: Fireflies in the Garden
history.text: This is a terrible film. The title, which sounds delightful, refers to the protagonists gleefully slaughtering the said insect population on summer nights. (Apparently, fireflies explode like fireworks when swatted with a tennis racquet.) The massacre scene is the only time in the film when the characters are happy -- maniacally so. The rest of the movie is about the miserable lives of odious people. The main character remembers unfair and borderline abusive moments from his childhood throughout the film as he plays out his adult resentment of his father in the present. The problem is that the man is a supreme jerk. He was a brat as a kid and he is a creep as an adult. There is not one character who is sympathetic. The father is abusive, the mother is a doormat, the assorted other relatives are all horrible people. This movie has a stellar cast and I hated them all. Who green-lit this bit of rubbish? Save yourself the agony of trying to figure that out by avoiding this debacle.

history.title: The Maiden Heist
history.review_title: Do Not Be Taken In by the Stellar Cast
history.text: This movie is simply not very good. Morgan Freeman is the only one who does credit to his character. Museum guards decide to steal their favorite art works before they are moved to an unappreciating new home. The pace is slow and the details are far-fetched at best. What should be a charming, gentle tale is realized as dull and plodding. Despite the quality cast, avoid this stinker.

history.title: Scandal: The Complete First Season
history.text: This show is for people who do not need good acting or writing. Shallowness abounds in all aspects of the production. If you want unrealistic grandstanding, then by all means give this a go. Otherwise, watch "The West Wing", "The Newsroom", or "House of Cards".

history.title: Room [DVD + Digital]
history.text: I cannot believe that anyone was nominated for this film. It is okay and the idea is fresh -- a woman and child being held hostage in a room for years -- but the execution is mediocre. I recommend this film in a tepid way. There are much better movies out there.

history.title: Sleuth
history.text: This is a stellar film that I have waited for many years to get on DVD. Witty dialogue, perfect casting, great direction -- what's not to love? For anyone who likes smart films, this is for you. I highly recommend it.

history.title: Grace and Frankie: Season 1 [DVD + Digital]
history.text: Perfect cast and smart, funny writing make this show a hit. Anyone familiar with Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin will love this show, especially if you are of a certain age. (The characters are in their 70s.) Martin Sheen and Sam Waterston are icing on the cake. The opening titles cleverly explain the premise of the show, so dive in immediately to this quality program.

history.title: The Big Short
history.review_title: Nauseating Filming Style Ruins Important Film
history.text: This movie is based on fact and does have an important message and some potentially entertaining gimmicks with guest stars and the like, but the filming style is awful. The picture is made for people without attention spans. The jerky, constantly-in-motion camera work is better suited to distract cats than it is to inform and entertain a thinking audience. This could have been a really good film. Instead, it is a shallow, hip-hop version of a quality movie. If you must see it, take some Dramamine and watch it for the facts.

history.title: Aftermath with William Shatner, Season 1 (2 Discs)
history.text: This is a really good idea for a show. I always wonder about what happened to various figures in the news when their 15 minutes of fame is up. Shatner does a good job of getting them to talk. The show suffers from being low budget, but it is fascinating. I wish they had done more episodes.

history.title: Eye in the Sky
history.text: This is a well done movie from a technical perspective (direction, acting, cinematography, etc.) It is an interesting movie from the perspective of how a military strike is decided, from the political ramifications and the cost - benefit analysis. It is even a thought provoking movie from a moral standpoint. Where this film loses stars is in its overwrought emotional stand. EVERYONE is emoting to within an inch of their lives because one child may be hurt in a drone strike. If the strike does not happen then many people would almost killed. I am as sympathetic towards children or innocent deaths as the next person , but this sap-a-thon was irritating.

history.title: One Step Beyond 6 DVD Collector's Set (70 Episodes)
history.review_title: Get creepier the more you watch them
history.text: I can't believe that I have never seen any episodes of this show before. Granted a lot of the stories seem made up but even so they can get kind of creepy with their beyond the grave theme. If you are a fan of EC comics from the 1950's these are kind-of a milder journey but still good. The stories remind me of some of the ghost story comic books printed by Dell and DC in the 1960's. Certainly comparable to, if not up to the same quality as "The Twilight Zone". I really enjoy seeing all of the famous stars in their early roles. Cloris Leachman and Louise Fletcher (Nurse Ratched) used to have quite the curvy figure! Who knew? And it's great to see Suzanne Pleshette in one of her early roles. Babes and ghosts, what's not to like?

history.title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers
history.text: The dog with the human face still creeps me out.
Painful to watch.

history.title: Thomas Hart Benton
history.text: One of Ken Burns' first documentaries and it still is the best on Benton. Too bad he doesn't do a series on Eakins, Henri and "the Eight", Benton, and Marsh. I wish I had the connections to do a decent history of the precedents of modern art and art education in America. It is almost as interesting as the paintings. It is amazing how many American painters went over to study in France. Even good-old Robert Beverly Hale hobnobbed with the 1920's crowd in Paris. This video will also give you the basics on the teacher/student relationship of Benton and Pollock. Benton is very underrated and Pollock is very overrated in my opinion. Pollock was mostly a self-destructive drunk who belittled Benton's goodwill. Heck, Benton bailed Pollock out of jail and very often gave him a sanctuary to retreat to. Benton was actually an intellectual who tried to come across as a homespun tough-guy. His Memory needs an upgrade and this is a good start.

history.title: Tucker - The Man and His Dream
history.text: An entertaining look at automotive history. I missed it when it first came out. Glad that Amazon makes it available for those of us without Netflix.

history.title: Risen [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: At this point, any corpse could be the Nazarene
history.text: I was enthralled with this depiction of a Roman Tribune witnessing the origins of Christianity until the cure of the leper. I cannot "white-wash" the suffering of anything as profound as leprosy, especially with a miracle. Why can't people accept that metaphors, allegory, and parables can be their own truth? Other than the leper-cure everything else is first rate, truly inspired film making, even if it came out of Hollywood. Actually it is more of an Anglo-Italian-Spanish production. One of the best Biblical epics ever done. Fundamentalists and Atheists will have trouble with it, the rest of us just wish that we could break bread with Yeshua and enjoy God's blessings.

history.title: Carnival of Souls (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I love the scenes where a sparrow's song brings Mary Henry back from transitioning out of the land of the living. You will never take a simple bird's song for granted again. I know I don't after seeing this film.

history.title: Cutthroat Island [DVD]
history.review_title: Bring on the special features ye, stingy scallywags
history.text: I have wanted to see this for a long time as I missed it when it first came out and avoid watching it when I catch it half-way through on TV. I enjoyed it despite all of the negative reviews it has gathered over the years. Frank Langella steals the show as the villain. My only complaint is the lack of special features. Not even a dialog track with the director... just a trailer. Geena Davis appears to do many of her own stunts and is quite the athlete. Now I understand how she actually thought she could compete in the Olympics in archery.

history.review_title: Break the windows, then try again, then drive through them
history.text: I absolutely loved this movie. Elizabeth Moss, of Mad Men fame is wonderful, as always. The twisted approach of couples therapy via your fantasy date versus your significant other's worst side is nigh profound. My only complaint is that if I had been Ethan I would have busted every dang blanged window in that guest house. And if I couldn't break the glass then I would have gotten the heebie-jeebies out of there!

wonderful...I will watch this one over and over

history.text: Didn't get past the first 10 minutes. I didn't know anyone could use the F word that many times in one sentence. Reminded me why I don't watch R rated movies.

history.text: Interesting story and great acting, but kind of exceeded my "weird" level. Matthew McConaughey is one of my favorite actors so that made it more palatable.
I'm a western fan but didn't like this one at all.

history.text: One has to be a true western lover to enjoy this movie. In a lot of ways it's pretty "artsy" and different for the genre. It's biggest drawback is its length. About half way through you want to say, "Just get on with it!" Still, it's a classic Eastwood and I like having it in my collection.

history.text: I love this movie. Sandra Bullock's acting talent is what makes this one special.

Now You See Me 2 [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD]
Gone with the Wind (70th Anniversary Edition) [Blu-ray]

history.text: This movie is two parts Short Circuit to one part Robocop...both movies that were much more entertaining and believable than Chappie. After the wonderful District 9 and Elysium, I was excited to see Chappie...but it's incredibly weak, especially considering that studio's pedigree. From the AI programmer character to Hugh Jackman's over the top maniacal character, there are too many situations where the viewer has to suspend disbelief. The ending seems tacked on: Chappie is still a "child", yet he miraculously figures out how to transfer peoples brains to a robot's digital hard drive? To top it all off, between the south african accents and synthesized robotic voice, I couldn't understand what most of the actors were saying. Two stars just for the computer graphics.

history.title: The Maze Runner
history.text: If you're gonna title a movie "maze runner", there should be a lot more maze and a lot more running...instead, you get a lot of wall and a lot of walking. The acting is good and the creatures are well done, but the story within this chapter of the series is not very interesting and has no sort of resolution...it's just a blatant setup for a sequel. The entire series may end up being acceptable, but this movie, alone, is weak...I wont mind skipping the sequel.

history.title: The Divergent Series: Insurgent
history.text: Better than the first movie (Divergent), imo, because this one has many more sci-fi elements and the CG is more present. Like the first movie in the series, this one is a complete story with a strong resolution...not just a means to a sequel and no resolution (like Maze Runner). One thing that stands out to me is the lead actress is too frail looking for the character. Hard to believe this wimpy looking girl is an elite athlete...lift some weights, woman! It's a good a standalone movie for a series, but people who haven't seen the first move will be confused because they don't re-explain the factions. Also, the sound engineering is poor...there's a lot of whispering so, half the time,I could barely tell what they were saying.

history.review_title: I like this mature Keanu...a lot
history.text: John Wick kept my attention from beginning to end...and that's saying something due to my ADD. There were a few areas I didn't quite understand (coins, hit man hotel, etc), but it's a really good movie, overall. Ever since "Bill and Ted", I never took Keanu seriously...in fact, I haven't paid to see any of his movies since B&T. In "John Wick", Keanu looks exponentially more mature than any of his previous movies both in appearance, stage presence and believably. Based on his performance in this film, I definitely have a new respect for Keanu and will keep watching his material. WARNING: This movie is extremely violent with a lot of people graphically getting their brains blown out. I had a nightmare from watching it.

The 3D is first rate (Pixar quality) and so is the voice acting. However, the story is a kinda wonky...pretty sure 99% of the kids that watch this aren't going to have a clue whats going on (but the movie looks and sounds so good, they wont care).

history.title: The Martian
history.review_title: First decent Ridley Scott movie since Alien
history.text: Nothing not to like in this movie. The story is enjoyable (not predictable, but not convoluted), it's well acted, well directed and the CG is well done. After the god-awful "Prometheus", I had given up on Ridley Scott...but, with "The Martian", he's redeemed his name.

Cute movie that tugged on my emotions...but it lacks the seemingly spontaneous comedy Ellen DeGeneres developed in Finding Nemo. Also, many of events/scenes are so exaggeratedly impossible, I found my suspension of disbelief failing.

history.title: The Boss
history.review_title: starts out funny, but last half not so much
history.text: As far as Melissa McCarthy movies, I'd say it's somewhere in between "Tammy" (1 star) and "The Heat" (5 stars).

history.title: Valerian and the City of A Thousand Planets [DVD + Bluray]
history.text: I expected and received a good story (not too convoluted) and decent acting, but the glorious and practically continuous CGI visuals are what push the rating into the 5 star range. For me, Valerian ranks up there with "The Fifth Element" and "Avatar" and I actually liked it better than the non-original Star Wars movies. Valerian completely satisfied my sci-fi fix, but my friend didn't like it. Still, I think anyone who gives this movie a one star rating is just maliciously skewing the results.

history.title: Léon the Professional (Theatrical and Extended Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Was wondering if anyone would make a Ranzerox movie
history.text: So I just rented Valerian (loved it). Luc Besson directed both movies, so I thought I'd drop a review of The Professional. When I first started watching the movie, I realized the similarity to the "Ranxerox" comics I bought in europe during the early 80s. Besson definitely borrowed the round glasses, the pre-pubescent girlfriend, Gary Oldman's character, the over the top violence, etc from Ranzerox. Great interpretation, anyway, and great casting and story resolution. history.title: The Revenant
history.text: In this film we have disjointed nonsense hung upon the framework of adventure, something like a drunken housewife hanging laundry all akimbo upon a clothesline. Rarely, expect in B-movies, have I seen so many improbabilities and inconsistencies. Hugh Glass, played by Leonardo DiCaprio, is a scout for a fur trading expedition that ostensibly is organized like a military unit, expect that whenever there is a crisis, anywhere in this film, good military discipline does not prevail. This coincides with left-wing belief systems about the uselessness and ineptitude of anything military, so this worldview is presented to the audience and is nonsense. Here is an example - central to the plot is the conflict between Glass and his antagonist John Fitzgerald (played by Tom Hardy) in which Hardy essentially blames Glass with being a dangerously (even treasonously) incompetent scout. Of course, this charge has to be false to maintain the hero status of the protagonist. In fact Glass's job IS security (and scouting) for the fur trading expedition. While he is away (within hearing distance of a rifle shot) hunting meat for the expedition, the expedition is attacked, and the majority of the party is killed. Straight-forward enough except that in the attack it is clear that the Indians have infiltrated into the treetops the night before, so Glass really is culpable of incompetence (or at least negligence). Later, as Glass leads the survivors of the massacre on an escape route, one morning he again goes out to scout, this time alone, and is almost mortally wounded by a bear. Anybody with any knowledge at all of basic military procedure (or common sense) would understand that for the key leader of the party to be out scouting alone in hostile territory when they know they are being pursued be enemies is ridiculous or utter incompetency. Oh yes, men do get mauled by bears but it becomes a bit more difficult for the bear when there are two or three armed men in the group than one. So really, Glass is an incompetent scout, but in this film he is the hero, and Fitzgerald is the deranged, despicable cad. Then there is the whole business in this film about white race relations with Indians. In this film, everything the white man does to the Indian is bad,, but everything the Indian does to the white man, no matter how barbaric, is neutral at worst, since the white man allegedly deserves what he gets. For this reason, it is "understandable" when blacks kill white cops in our society today, because at the end of the day the cops allegedly deserve it. In short this film serves up a confused mish-mash of politically correct vignettes in the framework of backwoods adventure. And by the way, apparently in the 1820's nobody lived beyond 40 because everyone in this film is 40 years old or younger, much younger, even the senior commanders of the fur trading expedition. This film was targeted at the millennial generation who actually believes the nonsense this film serves up. I gave the film two stars instead of one because the scene where Leonardo DiCaprio gets mauled by a bear is fairly realistic (well done).

history.title: Shining Through
history.text: Don't be deceived by the positive reviews for this film here and elsewhere. This so-called drama is really a melodrama cum chick flick. Michael Douglas plays Ed Leland, a top level New York lawyer who is also a top level spy for the United States into Germany prior to and during WWII. He holds the rank of colonel. Nevertheless despite his elite education and high rank in the military intelligence, Leland can't read, write or speak German. You know, that's kind of like being Vice President of Ford Motor Company but not knowing how to drive an automobile - happens all the time. Melanie Griffith plays Linda Voss, a kid with no education from the Bronx who has no problem winning the affections of an elite lawyer and colonel in the armed forces. This kind of thing, too, happens all the time. Leland agrees to use Voss, who DOES speak German, in an covert operation into Germany to uncover the plans for the V-2 Rocket. Since in real life, Germany managed to launch over 3,000 V-2 rockets against the Allies, it is hard to see what Voss's penetration into Germany accomplished, even in fiction. Other incredible aspects of this film include Voss running through the deserted streets of Berlin at night in a full length formal evening gown,pursued by the S.S. and somehow escaping their detection. I live in a small town in the American Midwest and I couldn't escape detection from the police, let alone and elite military unit, if I was fleeing in blue jeans in the streets. Also at the very end of the movie it falls upon Leland to get himself, who can't speak German, without proper papers, and an unconscious Voss across the Swiss border at a regular German-patrolled border crossing.
