history.title: The Dictator - BANNED & UNRATED Version
history.review_title: He should have stuck with his formula
history.text: I admit that I enjoyed [[ASIN:B009EE87NK Borat]]. It was original, truly funny in many places, and provided an uncomfortable insight into several aspects of the American character. Cohen's follow-up [[ASIN:B002TL08FU Brüno]], however, fell flat as it was essentially the same joke - an outrageous foreigner playing the unsuspecting locals for saps, but to make an impression on audiences, it had to be even more over-the-top and ridiculous. It failed because it was trying too hard and was too self-conscious. Fortunately, Cohen is now too well known to be able to pull off yet another stunt in that vein, so he abandoned it in favor of a straight-up comedy. The result isn't much better, and while it might have been possible to fool enough people into playing along with the possibility that they were meeting a real, deposed Middle Eastern dictator, we instead have a script that plays it safe by trying to mimic the results of improvisation. This has never worked, and the script that imagines the effect of inflicting a blatantly arrogant, hateful, and misogynistic cretin onto the denizens of New York City comes across as completely unbelievable, especially the love interest that occupies most of the screen time. The convoluted "political" segment of the plot is as ludicrous as can be expected in what is supposed to pass for a comedy, although Cohen manages to squeeze a speech in toward the end that might qualify as social commentary. [[ASIN:B004NWPY7A The Great Dictator]], it's not. Stupid, insulting, and forgettable, "The Dictator" cannot even be recommended to those dedicated to seeing every film ever made.

history.review_title: Nature is beautiful. Civilization is not.
history.text: "Seasons" is not a documentary; in the "making of" featurette, the director describes it as a fable, a story of the natural world told from the perspective of the animals. In most films taking place in this sort of environment, the animals are an afterthought; here, they're front and center, with human beings showing up on the periphery and only gradually taking on a greater role. The photography is jaw-dropping as we race through the forest with a pack of wolves, follow migrating geese, and get right in the faces of birds and other creatures that normally stay far away from humans. This was accomplished not through training, but "imprinting," where the animals became so used to human beings that they pretty much went about their business with no more self-consciousness than if the filmmakers had not been there at all. The goal was to show the animals up close, rather than through telephoto lenses, and in this, the film succeeds completely. It begins with an "80,000 year winter" and as the earth warms up, turns into "the age of the forest." The scenery is that of a wild and primeval Europe. The message is a low-key version of that in [[ASIN:B000068OCS Koyaanisqatsi - Life Out of Balance]], that humanity is a blight upon the purity of Nature, only without the stupendous Philip Glass soundtrack. Animals may be an afterthought in other movies, but the music was definitely an afterthought in this one. So much time and energy must have been expended on filming the animals, that there wasn't much left over for anything else. Worth seeing if you enjoy shots of cute animals (even when the predators kill something, the bloodshed is obscured behind a log or some other obstruction), "Seasons" is a triumph of the art of photography if nothing else.

history.review_title: What a woman must put up with
history.text: This delightful yet cynical film brings the last work of Austen's "juvenilia" to the screen in a spectacular period piece. The jaw-dropping sets vie with the sharp and witty dialog to immerse us in a world disconcertingly similar to our own. Kate Beckinsale stars as Lady Susan Vernon, a beautiful and intelligent widow forced by the rules of her society to focus her considerable talents toward the clever manipulation of everyone around her. She would be doing the same thing today, although in a law office or business setting, but the result would be the same. One criticism of the film is that the actors deliver their lines as if they were performing a cold reading, but the emphasis of talk over action is deliberate. Of course no one talks the way people do in this film - unfortunately. Even Tom Bennett's Sir James Marvin - the perennial dingbat that appears in all of Austen's works - steals every scene he's in with his halting yet enthusiastic delivery of inane observations that leave others stupified. With a well-crafted script (that admittedly drew from some great source material), "Love & Freindship [sic]" is a great addition to the canon of Austen screen adaptations.

A film that Martin Scorcese wanted to make for 25 years, "Silence" is a complex, difficult, and profoundly serious work that steadfastly refuses to answer many of the questions it raises. Telling the story of two 17th century Portuguese priests who travel to Japan to locate their former teacher, who reportedly has become an apostate, it asks whether religious faith is something that can be communicated between people. Japan is described as a "swamp" where the tree of European Christianity cannot grow. I was reminded of a scene in [[ASIN:1573623903 Black Robe]], another film about Christian missionaries in a strange land, where at one point someone asks "what about the converts" to which the response is "there are no converts." Can a religion based on the idea of offenses against and redemption from an invisible, all-powerful, yet very personal deity make sense to people who have no concept of such a deity? But at some point in the past, a Middle Eastern desert religion took root in Portugal - why there and not Japan? Against a backdrop of violent and senseless repression, people manage to maintain their faith, but as it turns out, faith in what? One promise of all religion is that it will improve the believer's life - how were the lives of the villagers improved by their adoption of a foreign religion to which the authorities were implacably hostile? And was that religion, despite its name and familiar images, anything like the Christianity practiced in Portugal? As one man says of the priest who taught him the Portuguese language, "he taught much, but learned nothing." The wretched Kichijiro, who renounces his faith by stepping on an icon ("it's just a formality"), may be the most faithful as he keeps returning for "confession" whenever his guilt overcomes him. He seems to get more out of his shallow Christianity of convenience than anyone else does. Symbols are merely representations, but we imbue them with our own reality, and in that way, they gain value. And a man who defaces a sacred symbol may have outwardly renounced his faith, but no one can see into his heart. The film offers no easy answers to the question of the value of outward religious practice as opposed to a private belief, and the inevitable role of religion as a political activity. Long and even tedious, "Silence" balances the inherent meaninglessness of life against the meaning we give it, whether from ourselves or something ultimately unknowable beyond us.

history.title: Lady Jane
history.text: Although not an accurate historical account of Jane Grey's nine-day reign over England in July of 1553, this film takes that incident as a starting point to examine the use of power to positive ends, and how two completely different people can complement each other. Helena Bonham Carter, in one of her earliest roles (and first starring role) plays Jane, presented as a deeply religious, bookish young girl whose sole interests are prayer and Biblical study. Through the machinations of her father and other noblemen, the dying teenage King Edward VI names her as his successor. She's forced into a marriage of convenience with Guildford Dudley, the son of the Duke of Northumberland, and a dissolute libertine whose main qualifications seem to be his "controllability" and his obvious incompatibility with Jane. We soon learn that Guildford is not a dissipated burnout, but is genuinely frustrated with the limitations of the viciously cruel and stratified society he lives in, where the ruling class, of which he is a member, conspires to keep the common people in hopeless poverty. When Jane, who has been sheltered from this truth her entire life, finally learns how her world is built on injustice, she understands that as queen she has no choice but to address this by ordering the breakup of the large noble estates and their redistribution to the peasantry. If allowed to continue, this would have amounted to a Marxist revolution, only from the top down rather than the bottom up. Instead, the revolution is aborted as the nobles take control. If Jane had had her own Robespierre or Beria, to behead the nobility before they could behead her, the result might have been different. In reality, of course, this never happened - Jane was not overthrown to prevent her from turning medieval England into an anarcho-communist worker's collective, but because the nobility switched their allegiance to Henry VIII's daughter Mary, who had a stronger claim to the throne. Jane was declared a usurper and imprisoned, and executed after Wyatt's Protestant rebellion even though she was not involved in it. The film takes liberties with the historical record to ask what would happen if a completely selfless leader decided to upend the class structure. The depressing conclusion is that even this is impossible, and we are left with the same society we have now.

Asghar Farhadi returns to the theme he explored in [[ASIN:B0094G427S A Separation]]; the effect divorce has on children. "The Past" shows a far more complex and disturbing family dynamic; Berenice Bejo plays a woman who has two daughters from her first marriage, and is getting a divorce from her second husband so she can take up with her lover, whose wife has been in a coma for the past eight months following an unsuccessful suicide attempt. There are no elderly grandparents this time; the young parents and children provide enough drama. Farhadi employs the same claustrophobic framing on display in "A Separation," where the characters are never out in the open, but always boxed in and limited by their immediate surroundings. The first scene, in which Ali Mosaffa meets Bejo in the airport as he returns from Iran to France to complete their divorce, sets the stage for the rest of the film with the device of placing them on opposite sides of a soundproof glass wall - they can see but can't hear each other. An exploration of the harm that unhappy people can inflict on each other, and how much responsibility we bear for others' poor choices, the lesson of "The Past" may be that if you aren't willing or able to commit to someone for life, maybe you shouldn't have children.

history.title: Yi Yi (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I don't pretend to be an expert in Chinese cinema - the only Chinese films I've seen that come to mind are [[ASIN:B000R3BMM0 Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon]], [[ASIN:B000PMFS6O Raise the Red Lantern]], and [[ASIN:B0000B1A4J The Crippled Masters]], which I saw many years ago in Togo, dubbed, I think, in Portuguese. They must have sent the French version to Brazil by mistake. I came across "Yi Yi" on a list of "the greatest films ever made," and in that regard, it's somewhat of a disappointment. There's no real plot, per se; the characters' lives unspool as if a camera were present at the most ordinary moments. A family deals with an elderly grandmother falling suddenly into a coma, a group of business partners must decide on the course to save their struggling company, a teenage girl takes her first cautious steps into romance, and a young boy gradually becomes aware of the larger world around him. There are a few emotional explosions - an attempted suicide, an angry breakup, a petty tyrant of an elementary school teacher - but overall the emotional tone is as muted and subdued as the film's color palette, suggesting comparisons to other mumblecore like [[ASIN:B002SAMMKQ The Puffy Chair]]. Yet it is not an easy or trivial thing to evoke the wider panoply of characters' lives and relationships with a few images and scraps of dialog, and at close to three hours, "Yi Yi" succeeds at this to varying degrees, especially with the main character N.J., whose "revelation" ===================== SPOILER ALERT ===================== after meeting an old lover, consists of musing on how the course of his life would have been different if he'd made different choices. This can either be "universal" in that everyone over the age of sixteen has wondered about that, or trite as in, "yes, Einstein, your life would have been different if you'd married someone else." This is either profound, or as Nietzsche described women, "not even shallow." The ending, where the young boy reads a letter he wrote to his dead grandmother, where he shows his growing awareness of life's beauty and the inevitability of death, is something every adult in the film takes for granted. Whether this is sufficient payoff for the time required to arrive there will depend on the viewer. Although the film takes place in Taipei, there's not much in the way of tradition or culture; the characters and the urban setting could be transplanted almost anywhere - Tel Aviv, Karachi, Montevideo, Cleveland - without much alteration. As a commentary on the human condition, the primary observation is how uniform and interchangeable urban culture has become worldwide in the 21st century.

Unusual in that it takes the form of an animated documentary, "Waltz With Bashir" is also the first feature-length Israeli animated film produced in several decades. It concerns the filmmaker's quest to regain the memories of his participation in the 1982 Lebanon invasion, as a teenager in the IDF. The film alternates between his present-day discussions with his fellow soldiers, and dramatic recollection of the events themselves as he struggles to recall his own role in them and in the Sabra and Shatila massacre of Palestinian civilians by Lebanese Phalangist forces. The soldiers are presented as children, not completely understanding the scope of the conflict or its ultimate goals. The soundtrack includes covers of songs by Cake and others that both augment and comment on the action. The Max Richter score is outstanding, although I was annoyed that obvious allusions to Bach's F-minor concerto, Schubert's E-flat trio, and what I am certain is a passage from [[ASIN:B0027534EU Koyaanisqatsi]] were not credited. Overall, however, "Waltz With Bashir" is both an examination of a specific historical event as well as an exposition of the effect warfare has on both its victims and perpetrators.

history.review_title: Where there's smoke, there's fire, but not in this case
history.text: The filmmaker admits at one point that the subject of UFOs is overwhelmed by at least 90% sensationalist nonsense. He then claims that this is how "the truth" is "hidden" - by turning a valid topic into supermarket tabloid material. His argument is that there is so much information on UFOs and aliens, and so many reasonable people believe in them, that they must really exist. The problem, however, is like religion - there's definitely a lot of discussion about God, and a lot of people believe in him, but there's no objective evidence of his existence. UFOs fall into the same category. We're presented with voluminous evidence of alien contact, craft sightings, "unexplained" phenomena, and a succession of very reasonable specialists who assure us that there can be no doubt. We're then told that "the government" has all of this high-tech, top-secret alien material, that is being used on a daily basis, and that "the media" is under careful control to ensure that none of it gets out - except, of course, that a lot of it does. But there's an explanation for this as well - if UFOlogy can be made to look like it's in the domain of tinfoil-hat conspiracy theorists, "the truth" can be hidden in plain sight. No credible researcher will want to commit career suicide by taking seriously what sounds like nonsense. This becomes a self-perpetuating cycle - as UFO study becomes loonier, fewer people want to touch it. If the only people who report contact with aliens are backwoods types who look like they've never seen a pair of shoes, then no Nobel Laureates will want to touch this subject. Fortunately, Greer himself seems to be protected from retaliation by the powers that be - surely, if anything happened to him, that would create too much suspicion. So we learn that there's a lot of information, and a massive conspiracy to conceal or obfuscate it. But other than a few tantalizing glimpses of the child-sized, almond-eyed "aliens," there's none of the hard, objective proof that would set the matter to rest once and for all. Otherwise, the documentary is well-made, with a good balance between talking heads and action, and voiceover by Giancarlo Esposito, "Gustavo Fring" from "Breaking Bad." The overall professional and dignified presentation might convince a few people, but for the rest of us, "Unacknowledged" is still "nonexistent."

history.title: Rumble: The Indians Who Rocked The World
history.text: A good documentary should present something to the audience that they don't already know about, and "Rumble" definitely succeeds there. I must admit that I had not known that Charley Patton and Jimi Hendrix were Native Americans, and while I was of course familiar with the titular song, I'd never heard of Link Wray, or the equally inspirational Mildred Bailey. The contribution of Native Americans to American popular music - the blues, jazz, and rock & roll - has definitely been overlooked. The problem with this documentary is lack of focus. It's not sure if it wants to be an ethnographic study of Native American music, an elucidation of how traditional music informs popular music, or an overview of popular musicians who just happen to be Native American. While the influence and effect of the two and one-half minute "Rumble" is indisputable - it has that aura of inevitability that some compositions of Beethoven and Mozart have, imparting the sense that one has heard it before, even when one is hearing it for the first time, as if it is part of the essential fabric of the universe. But the song really has no relation to traditional Native music other than the fact that a Native American wrote and performed it. The attempt to characterize the blues as derived from Native American traditional music comes across as wishful thinking, especially since no clear analysis is provided of what the Native music of the Mississippi Delta sounded like. Other examples toward the end of the film seem almost grasping at straws in the attempt to equate an evocation of past tradition with the unbroken continuation of that tradition into the present day. The most interesting parts were the explanations of the relationship between Native and African-Americans. It's pointed out that Charley Patton's vocal style was derived from Native musical elements, and once you hear this, it can't be unheard even if the resemblance is coincidental. The New Orleans portion was fascinating, where we learn that part-Native people who could identify as black would do so to avoid being shipped off to a reservation, "because the Indians were treated even worse than the black people," and that Mardi Gras was welcomed as the only time when "black men could wear feathers." I would have appreciated more of this kind of ethnographic exposition, which is a different film entirely than "look, a Native American wrote this." However, the Native American contribution to popular music is one of its essential elements, and this documentary was long overdue.

history.title: Chicago P.D.: Season 2
history.text: There are too many cop shows on Television. Most of them are ridiculously inaccurate. Some are just SILLY. (Hawaii 5-0/Rookie Blue). This series is as close to the gritty NYPD BLUE as you will get. But the interesting thing about this show is that in Season 2 NBC let the directors and special effects go full on with Action sequences that would NEVER have passed NBC "standards and practices" only two years ago. There is actual blood shown on gun shots. One episode showed a knife cutting out a bullet lodged in a chest wall (and effects done very well). The WALKING DEAD series had a huge effect on what is now allowed on television. In the Days of "HUNTER" or MIAMI VICE NBC used to COUNT the gunshots per episode and had specific guidelines on how many episodes per season gun impact shots ( blood squibs) were allowed. In most cases they were NOT allowed. Only a scant number of old NBC police/action series were allowed to show any blood or realistic fights. It was not the fault of the writers or producers there really used to be censors who would "nix" anything too violent. There are few "extras" on the DVD release so 4 stars. I wonder why current TV release features so little in terms of out takes/alternate shots/ teasers/previews to next week/ or network sales presentations. The producers of CHICAGO PD are aware of this and I see them using the loosening censorship as a way to incorporate more realistic, engaging and harrowing action scenes that used to be reserved for "R" rated films. I am not going to comment on the characters or hoe "realistic" they are. In truth..there are NO Police television series that actually mimic how a real take down or shoot out. In the REAL WORLD a cop unloads his clip at a perp shooting at him. 8 or more shots..depending on weapon choice. On these television shows a cop fires ONCE ot TWICE. You have no idea if a perp will GO DOWN in one or two shots, if they are wearing body armor, If they are on drugs..so let's not call this show "totally realistic". (Obviously showing cops unloading a full magazine weekly will make some unions unhappy) But compared to the cartoon like other current crime shows *(what happened to the days of Kojak or Dragnet?>)..this one has solid acting, writing, and action. Well worth the watch.

history.review_title: The GOOD.. What amazing and wonderful acting performances from ...
history.text: The GOOD..What amazing and wonderful acting performances from Christoper Walz. Dicaprio, AND Sam Jackson (his finest acting role). The BAD--Tarantino goes for the "commercial" sales aspects and incorpprates (BADLY) modern "Hip Hop" "rap" and even Jim Croce music into a film set in 1858. He painstakingly goes to the trouble or trying to portray the time period accurately...yet he uses music made in 2015 as his soundtrack. Makes NO sense, seems a cheap exploit to sell a soundtrack. What music SHOULD have been used. Period music--Gospel, Blues, Spirituals of the South. The COEN Brothers make sure they are accurate when they do a movie soundtrack (OH BROTHER for example) It also makes little sense that Sam Jacksons character is so eager to rat out Django to Candie. Why not exploit this to his OWN ends and make a considerable profit. Instead he is loyal to his former Slave master in a way that is so off that it makes Stephen out to be an insane and confused character MISGUIDED and DELUSIONAL that CANDIE will return the favor. Candie never t to offer Stephen anything for his betrayal of Django...sicne he is killed..but even if he were not shot---does anyone beleive Candie was going to reward Stephen adequately? I assume this wwas written by DESIGN to show just how damaged a psyche is STEPHEN but in reality...one wonders why Stephen still LOVES Candie so. There is no scene, no background gien to show WHY Stephen is so in love with Candie. THE UGLY--The last 45 minutes of this film. He destroys what he created in a number of ways. The Violent finales are all shot in some sort of Orange hued or imperfect color scheme. Blood is not the right color (Yes it is defintely tinted orange). His EGO--He puts himself in the film in a POOR acting performance with a terrible Australian accent. Now this would not be so bad except it clashes with he incredible performances of the other actors. He does his own cast a HUGE disservice by his placing himself in arole that could eaily have been given to Russell Crowe ,Hugh Jackman or any GOOD actor. He almost ruins the film. Yes.the GOOD of the film outweighs the bad..and the first 2 hours are so well done, clever, and emotionally engaging it can be viewed as favorite over and over...but this last 45 minutes is just too silly, poorly acted, hastily written and all in all not a satisfying conclusion. WHat could have been a masterpiece of film making turns cheap in the last hour and even cheaper by Tarantion;s bad acting. A shame since these actors give such deep perfect performances.

history.text: Loved Season One. It was unique well paced with lots of thought provoking scenes and dark corners. When it was revealed that Mr RObot was HIMSELF---it was the beginning of the end. The fact they stole the entire plot AND gimmick of FIght CLub (take down the credit card companies and credit files wipe everything clean).and then they had the audacity to use the TYLER DURDEN/MR ROBOT alter ego is just plain plagiarism. It was mildly excusable in Season one as the writing held my interest. Season two--is SLOW, meandering ,off point , obsessed with FBI torture tactics and lack of true focus. Who is hacking who? when? how why? What exactly is the point now? What happened to hacking all credit and returning everyone to ZERO. They abandoned that or side swiped. Locations were changed (the original Dumpling House where they shot the first season is actually out of business now). I still think that turning this into a Fight Club parallel is just too little for me with such slow scripts. I really had to find ways to stay awake for many episodes. Def. major lack of script flow. As far as violence--I dont see anything extremely violent. People seem to copy others in these reviews. What is so violent compared to Season one or compared to Walking Dead? history.title: Gangs of New York
history.text: The movie itself is excellent. Daneil Day-lewis's performance spectacular . My issue --Scorcese a New Yorker..spent ample time researching (mostly through newspaper articles and stock photos /drawings) the scope of New York in the time of the Civil War. Unfortunately--he recreated the "Five Points" a section of lower Manhattan thar meets between five streets . Although he has recreated a reality for New York...what he failed to do was display the extremely horrendous physical conditions of the area and buildings. These buildings were forthe most part wooden worm down shacks, tenement buildings and places of squalor. Poor plumbing (IF ANY), combined with unsanitary wash conditions and poor lighting created a poor Downtown of new York filled with rats buidling decay, soot, and just plain rot. Scorcese makes some nice buildings out of red bricks..but it hardly represents the filth and decay of the real new York Five Points and surrounding areas of 1855-1866. Sorry..just isnt gritty enough . The performances and tone of the film certainly is..not the decor.

history.text: Let me just tell you about one scene in this movie. 15 year old Stacy is working as a waitress in a pizzeria in the mall. She takes a guy's order. He asks where she wants to go, and if "the point" would be okay, and she giggles that it is okay. So, they drive to an open area, outside, in half-darkness. After less than a minute of conversation, he kisses her. She lets him lay her down. He immediately undresses her. He immediately takes her virginity - - of course, they don't use any protection. Then he just takes her home. E A S Y . . . CHEAP DATE IN MORE WAYS THAN ONE. The guy could have done anything he wanted to her, including killing her.

Did you see the perfect, straight, white teeth on that crackhead mother? And her smooth, flawless skin? She is clearly not all black, she is mixed, with the baby being much darker. She kept saying, "Look at me, I'm his mother," but she didn't look like his mother to me. Are you kidding? This boy didn't stand a chance. He could live in poverty with an addicted single mother - - no one mentioned the fact that addicts could start using again at any time. Or he could be the only black in a rich white neighborhood. Either way, he loses. This child belonged in foster care instead. No one mentioned what would happen to this boy when he was older, such as his teen years. If he lived with the white family, he would probably rebel against them and want to know his real mother at some point. If he lived with the black mother, he would probably get into drugs, just like she did. And, where was the court-ordered therapy for the boy and his mother? No social workers ever came to check on them. I felt bad for Hannah. No one cared about her feelings. Did you all understand the ending? I looked it up on Wikipedia to make sure. The crackhead gave the child back to the white mother, saying that he is better off living with the white family until he is "older" and can understand everything.

Why would a couple with a baby and a small child hire a "nanny" to live with them without checking her out? Peyton could not have had any references or anything at all to check because she was never a nanny and she even used a fake name. This couple obviously never even asked her for ID. At their first meeting, Peyton said that she would leave a letter of reference on the table - - what happened with that? Peyton said that she only worked with one family - - maybe she was a nanny before she married Dr. Mott - - but that still could not have been recent. The couple were listed with an agency. When Peyton admitted that she was not from the agency, that should have been the end of the conversation. Why would this couple take this woman into their house? However..... I actually was on Peyton's side. Peyton lived in a gorgeous house with a successful husband and was expecting her first baby. Then, because of accusations which Peyton probably did not believe, her husband committed suicide and then she lost her baby and had an emergency hysterectomy. She was thrown out of her house and all of her money was frozen. She said that she didn't have anyone to go to after the deaths of her husband and baby. So, she was all alone, grieving, with no money and nowhere to live - - she probably had no skills because she was a housewife so she couldn't get a job. I felt for Peyton.

I loved this movie. I enjoyed seeing the way that New York was in 1974. I mostly loved seeing how different the subway was. The trains look like antiques. There were "straps" which is where the word "straphangers" comes from . . . you don't see those anymore, now they just have long vertical poles to hold onto. The seats were just one long gray piece . . . today, there are individual seats that are painted yellow and orange and red and blue, with labels that say, "Please give these seats to the elderly or handicapped." The subway platforms looked so antiqued, with the old white labels naming the stations, such as "28 Street" and the old white labels naming the fronts of trains, such as a big white 6 . . . today, the stations are labeled in big, clear letters, and the trains have bright electronic lights on screens at the fronts and the sides, and there are horizontal maps on screens with little lights moving across, letting you know where you are and what the next stop is. Some trains today actually have small TV screens which play ads, such as advertising the new Second Avenue Subway Station, and public service announcements. Today, the conductor does not shout out the stop (except, rarely, they do). Today, there are male and female robot voices announcing the stops, such as, "This is Times Square, 42nd Street, the next stop is Grand Central, transfer here for [long list of train letters], please take all of your personal belongings, and have a nice day..." Today, there are robot voices with public service announcements, like, "Please offer your seat to an elderly or pregnant person because courtesy is contagious and it begins with you" and "Ladies and gentlemen, a crowded subway is no excuse for unwanted touching." There were ads for cigarettes, which you will never see today. Instead, there are ads such as two men kissing, warning that you should be tested for HIV, and ads like, "If you see something, say something." There is some artwork where some ads used to be. There used to be stickers on the doors, such as, "Please keep hands off the doors." Now, there are electronic screens that keep changing, telling you the time and the next stop. In this movie, I was hoping to see someone put a subway token into the turnstile. Of course, today, tokens don't exist anymore because now there are Metrocards. The subway used to have separate names, such as the IRT. They used to call it the TA, but now they call it the MTA. I was surprised the most that the subway workers wore little blue hats - - just like, in those days, nurses in hospitals wore little hats - - and that the fare was only 35 cents (I remember, in a Shirley Temple movie, the fare was 5 cents, and it was discussed how it was too much). This movie was action and entertainment all the way through. When they were looking over the names of the motormen who were fired, they didn't look at the men who moved away. I didn't think that that made sense. Just because you don't live in New York anymore doesn't mean that you can't travel back to New York to attempt a crime that seems worth it to you. I read something in Trivia - - it is a little bit difficult to see because some of the scenes are dark, but the men, Mr. Blue, Mr. Gray, Mr. Green, and Mr. Brown, each wore hats that are the colors of their names. My favorite part was the ending, the very last moment, the expression on Walter Matthau's face. I love Walter Matthau.

I thought that this movie was very dated, in other words, it wouldn't work today. This movie was from 1980, but it felt a lot older to me. I didn't understand why these rich married women would be seen in public, such as in their country clubs, with a "male escort." If they wanted to have sex with Julian (Richard Gere), they could do it in a hotel or even in their house. If they wanted to be taken out and if they wanted attention, then they could have done it where people don't know them. Couldn't anyone they know see, at any time, and then tell their husbands, that these women were out with a 30 year old man? I thought that the whole point was to be discreet - - but how could you be discreet if you are seen having dinner in your country club with a 30 year old man, which everyone seems to know is a male prostitute? I found the relationship with Michelle (Lauren Hutton) unbelievable. She sees him from across the room, realizes that he is a callboy, and hits on him. She falls in love with him, but I honestly could not see why. As Leon (the black pimp) said, Julian only cares about himself and doesn't feel anything for anyone else. And as Michelle herself said, when he has sex, he just goes to work. I couldn't believe that Michelle would throw her whole life away for Julian. What did she expect would happen next? Did she think that Julian could be faithful to her? If he could, then how would the two of them support themselves? Michelle said that she could not go home because she just gave Julian an alibi, so how can we assume that she still has money to pay for his defense? Julian said himself that he is getting older. He cannot be "in demand" for too many years more. What will he do when he can't sell his body anymore? Was working as a chauffeur and a translator real work that he could support himself with? We see Julian "working" all the time, but we don't see what he does when he is not working. He said that he prefers older women, so are we supposed to believe that he really did fall in love with Michelle? I found this movie very slow and very boring. This must be the only movie that I have seen that was about sex that didn't hold my attention. Richard Gere is, of course, attractive in this movie, but it is a shock to look him up on Google and see how he looks today.
Every minute of this movie held my interest - - I didn't want to blink because I might miss something. The ending is a twist that I did not see coming.

The trailer shows too much. If you don't like spoilers, then don't watch the trailer. I have watched so many horror movies, and I rarely get really scared. But this movie terrified me - - I was on the edge - - and, at one point, I actually screamed. The ending was really scary - - and the ending was a surprise that I did not see coming. I usually find endings of horror movies disappointing, but I loved the ending of this movie. If you love horror movies, but they never really scare you, then you will love this movie. If you, as I do, have ever had sleeping problems, then this movie will really scare you. Also, it was good to see Jesse from Fame playing a doctor in this movie.

I love this movie. I have watched it many times. I just wonder why Tim Allen lives alone in a big house - - I would expect him to live in a nice apartment or condo. I guess it wouldn't make sense for Santa to fall off of his roof if he lived in an apartment building. I also wonder - - the adults don't believe in Santa - - So, how is it explained when toys are found under the tree and no one knows who they are from? Also, when Tim Allen shows up at the North Pole as the new Santa, everyone accepts him, and no one misses the old Santa or cares at all what happened to him. We can assume that the other Santa worked there and lived there for a very long time, but no one cared at all that he was gone.

I really enjoyed this movie. I did not see the twist coming. But thinking about it after the movie was over, the clues were there. SPOILER ALERT....... I did think that it was strange that a very large chandelier would be hanging directly above a baby's crib. I also thought that it was strange that the house was not baby-proofed - - electrical outlets are always covered when you have a toddler. And if you have a child that is accident-prone, why would you take him to a place where there is a cliff? Why would the mother lie and say that she had only been with her husband when her husband was not her child's father? Then it was revealed that the mother wanted to give him up for adoption when he was a baby.

If the neighbor guy could find addresses for these women, then he certainly could find out which one has a 19 year old son. And, the neighbor guy could probably also find phone numbers, so Bill Murray could have made a few calls instead of traveling all over. And, if Bill Murray received an anonymous letter, then he certainly could write a letter to each of the women whom he suspected wrote the original letter to him.... one letter deserves one letter in reply. No matter what, I don't think that it is right to just show up at someone's door unexpectedly, whether you haven't seen them in 20 years or 20 minutes ago.

history.title: Elaine Paige Live
history.text: I've just finished watching this, and all I can say is, "Wow!" After a career spanning forty years, Ms. Paige is still in glorious voice, with a relaxed-yet-total command of the stage. If you bought the CD, you still have to get the DVD as there are several songs and passages that were not included (also, the CD is not taken from this concert -merely the same playlist). Brilliant as she is, Elaine is not well known in the US, as she was never given the opportunity to take the roles she made famous in London (Eva Peron in Evita; Grizabella in Cats; Florence in Chess) to Broadway. She finally arrived in New York to breathe life into Sunset Blvd. for its final year on Broadway. The songlist is mostly classic: Overture Life Goes on Tomorrow Easy To Be Hard Broadway Baby I Don't Know How To Love Him Small Packages Hello Young Lovers Shoot The Breeze (by Dustin Hoffman and Bette Midler) Yesterday Don't Cry For Me Argentina As If We Never Said Goodbye By The Sea I Get A Kick Out Of You I Dreamed A Dream Someone Else's Story I Know Him So well Poor Old John Non, Je Ne Regrette Rien If You Love Me Cry Me A River Memory With One Look There are bonus features, including a behind-the-scenes interview, and she performs with a first-rate orchestra. Especially notable are her performances of songs from Sunset Blvd. and Piaf in character and costume. Stunning! If you love musical theatre and/or classic vocalists then you'll fall in love with Elaine Paige. If, like me, you're a long-time fan -You'll fall in love all over again.

history.title: The Yeomen of the Guard
history.text: Clocking in at 79 minutes, this made-for-television production of Yeomen of the Guard is clearly abridged, but at least it was done with a knowledgeable and loving hand. Fortunately the very fine cast makes up for any omissions in the score. Alfred Drake and Barbara Cook are at their finest, and the rest of the cast is quite strong. Originally produced in 1957 for the Hallmark Hall of Fame program, and broadcast live in color, all that remains is a kinescope -which VAI has done an excellent job of mastering. The sound is clear throughout, and the video is surprisingly crisp for a kinescope. Some will dislike the added speeches for Jack Point (Drake) that provide additional continuity, but they do help the audience through all of the cut sections of the book and score. Fans are still waiting for a well-produced, well-cast, complete video of this Gilbert & Sullivan masterpiece, but in the meantime this long-lost version is the best thing out there, and very much worth adding to your collection.

history.title: An Evening with Quentin Crisp
history.review_title: The Last of the Great Stylists
history.text: Please ignore the negative comments about the sound and picture. There is nothing wrong with this DVD. The original camera work isn't the best, but this was clearly shot as an archival video by a camera operator who wasn't as familiar with the presentation has he perhaps should have been. The sound is perfectly fine for a live theatrical event. What's important here is the content -And what wonderful content it is! Quentin Crisp performed this one-man show off and on for over twenty years, captured here in 1999 only a few months before his untimely passing at the age of 90. Twenty years ago, when I bought the audio recording of Mr. Crisp doing this show in New York I found it highly amusing, but I doubted both the sincerity and the accuracy of what he was saying. Now that I am older I realize just how sincere (and how right) Mr. Crisp was. Whatever your age Quentin Crisp will make you laugh and make you think. And the more you think, the more you'll laugh.

history.title: Sleepers [DVD]
history.text: Just watched this again last night -All four hours in one go. It really is one of the best series the BBC has ever produced. Well-written, tightly-directed, and cast with actors who totally "got" what they were doing. Nigel Havers and Warren Clarke in particular were perfect as the two soviet sleeper spies who refuse to come back in to the cold. They brought tremendous depth to their characters, elevating the series to something better than typical television. Like a good book, the plot takes its time unwinding, but the twists and turns continue to the very end, with plenty of emotion, suspense, and laughter along the way. The satire is wide-ranging, targeting cold war and glasnost politics, counterespionage agencies, and the British class system. If you're too young to remember the 80s-90s you might not get some of the humor, but spy story will keep you engaged and entertained. It's a shame that it took so long for this to be released on DVD, and that it has fallen out of print. It's a classic from the time when they still made television for grownups.

I had trouble following the flashbacks (until the middle). Also the art was far below the quality of WAR. At least one character (never named?) I had no clue of and he ended up being a key to the final conflict. In fact, there were a lot of characters thrown in that I had no idea of (and I like to think I am knowledgeable of comics). While violence to children was done off-screen, gratuitous mayhem and dismemberment seemed to be the norm. One of the final "shots" was the classic - looking through the large hole in the guy's forehead at the person who shot him from behind. Over the top, and unnecessary. It turned my wife and daughter off - if it had happened at the beginning we wouldn't have watched the rest. I understand the want to make it gritty and even dirty because of the story's premise - it could have been done much more tastefully, and better. Sorry I bought it. Of course, these are just my opinions - and I should note that I LOVE watching superhero movies (animated or live action) - especially anything made from a comic (with characters I read when I was young)

history.review_title: Not bad at all...just not spectacular either
history.text: I read the reviews and because of the low rated ones (mostly the 1s) I decided to rent before I bought. A good choice anyway. I just finished watching it and I can't agree with the lower ratings. It was a good movie. I thought the acting was fine. Especially the genius company owner. I liked the interactions between the two male characters. I did not find it to be predictable at all. And am surprised at those who felt it was. The only comment that I saw that I agree with was the illogical lack of an off switch. Definitely one of the best offerings I can remember from Lionsgate. Now on a personal note - I like movies with happy endings or at least where the good guy (girl) wins in the end. This is the first movie I've seen in a long time where in the end - there wasn't anyone I was rooting for. So it left me wanting in that area. history.title: Superman: The Movie [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A great sci-fi classic brought to Blu-Ray quality
history.text: If anyone out there has not seen this great film yet, I'd be surprised. So, we are talking about seeing it again, or seeing it on Blu-Ray for the 1st time. Either way, it's worth it and this is one film you will see at least once a year and not put it in perpetual storage like the rest of your library. This film had been long awaited by fans of the comic book. It came out in true Hollywood style, where even the film credits were awe-inspiring, let alone the Sfx, the stars( Marlon Brando, Gene Hackman, Christopher Reeve, Ned Beatty, Margot Kidder, Glenn Ford) and of course the story. As we all remember, the story has the people of the planet Krypton facing doom. Marlon Brando is Superman(Reeve)'s father and tries to rally the people to act before the planet is destroyed. Noone has the integrity to agree so he and his wife will send their child to a distant planet: Earth. Thereafter, Superman has a 'normal childhood' with Glenn Ford(a rural farmer); a transformation into Superman at a fortress of solitude; his newspaper job with the Daily Planet in Metropolis(New York?); and so the legend grows. The film was made with a sense of humor(Gene Hackman and Ned Beaty), drama, and pathos. It's more than just a comic book brought to life. In many ways, it was 3 films in one: the first part was true science fiction, with weighty themes presented by the lead marquee star: Marlon Brando. The 2nd part was a family story, childhood on the farm(briefly told). The 3rd and final part, the only part that was Superman as we know him, had him in Metropolis, fighting 'bad guys' and doing super things. All in all, it will seem like you've experienced all the wonders of the world in just 146 minutes of screen time...

history.title: Giorgio Moroder Presents Metropolis: Special Edition [Blu-ray]
history.text: More than any other film out there, Metropolis requires a careful consideration. Because it's so old and there are missing elements to it, the version you get will doubtless be different from versions sold elsewhere. THIS version is unique as the producers chose to add a film score, and one contemporary. SO, you must choose to have the traditional presentation, perhaps with more original footage, or this one, with an application of music. TO ME, the choice is clear. Though Metropolis might've been great at the time, in its complete form(now lost?), seeing the versions in silent film form leaves you 100% unmoved. Catharis...emotional feel...to a film is essential and the rock score adds just that element. I strongly encourage you to view film history via this version. The film itself concerns the struggle of labor versus management, with an intermediary(the hero?) who joins those two worlds. In this odd plot, there is a cyborg(female) that's created in order to control(or free?) the servile workers. You must see it to appreciate it as descriptions fail. The director, Fritz Lang, was so valued by the Germans that a certain 'German leader' offered him almost anything if he would stay in 'that Germany' of the 1933-45 period. Fortunately, he chose otherwise.

history.title: Papillon (DVD)
history.review_title: An adventure and quest from history
history.text: First things first: Some films are mostly dialogue or film noire; this film has vistas and big skies. The point being, you should spring for the Blu-Ray edition if you can afford the extra green. OK, the film itself is about Steve McQueen and Dustin Hoffman. They are 'doomed men', sentenced to the penal colony of the republic of France in French Guiana, in South America. There is some interplay between the mainland and the offshore facility, infamously known as 'Devil's Island'. That storied prison(actually several small facilities) existed for a century, amazingly not closed until 1953. What important is we experience the quest of the men to escape the confinement and conditions and make it away, freely, to almost anywhere. What is great in this film is that it allows you to understand somewhat the more famous case of Captain Dreyfus, the French officer wrongly convicted of treason(to France) and exiled to Devil's Island until a reprieve and exoneration. Whether you look at the film in this vein, or as the more simple story presented, you will be overwhelmed by the concept and challenge of oceanic voyage by people equipped with only courage. The film is not a simple 'escape film' but instead was almost a detective story, with a labyrinth of confidence placed in persons, some paid and some merely sympathetic. The problem was that it required 100% reliability and in real life, nothing works that well...

history.title: Deal of the Century
history.review_title: War and peace and other things...
history.text: Chevy Chase, Sigourney Weaver and Gregory Hines This now overlooked comedy featured Chevy Chase as an arms dealer in a world awash in military hardware sales. He is not the worst person out there, but when a questionable sales deal falls into his lap, he takes credit for it and becomes a new star. His friend, played by Gregory Hines, is a pilot who will do anything to be in the air but also a realist who has qualms about aircraft sales to countries who can barely afford school books. Now there'd be a moral dilemma as to doing the sale, with the requisite reward, or to do the 'right thing'. Vince Edwards is perfect in his role as the corporate president selling an advanced drone (remember this was years before the current age of real-life drones and robotic aircraft.) Although this film has an obvious political slant, it is so well-done and nuanced, you can overlook that. The basic questions of military budgets and the nation's needs have been at the forefront since this nation was formed, trying to defend us against the Crown... For a good comedy and one that is thoughtful, I recommend this little film...

history.title: Platoon
history.review_title: For once, a realistic war film
history.text: Tom Berenger, Willem Dafoe and Charlie Sheen starred in this brilliant tome about war, in particular Vietnam. Unlike the larger than life Apocalypse Now or the other Vietnam films that seemed to either overstate or understate the travails of war in 'Nam, Platoon seems to have tried to steer right down the center, showing war unvarnished or gussied up. We see Charlie Sheen as the newbie cleaning latrines, given the worst assignments, and given the usual (good and bad) advice by people about to end their tour of duty. The film takes us on a tour of duty with Charlie Sheen being 'everyman' thrust into the seemingly endless and pointless jungle warfare against an enemy, unseen normally. We go on night sentry duty, cave or tunnel rat work, etc. There is very little that is sentimental or romantic about any scene. Sheen is forced under the cirumstances to interrogate innocent (sic) citizens who might be harboring the VC(Viet Cong) or even actually be them. What is implied for the educated viewer is the fact that this was tough but actually might have been warranted; in other words, these innocents farmers could be, and were in fact, loyal citizens by day but VC supporters and suppliers by night. Oliver Stone, the director/auteur of the film, indicated that this was a personal journey for him, partially or totally basing it upon his actual experiences. We can't be sure of that, but the film is very personal, visceral, and affecting. I strongly recommend this as the definitive Vietnam film, showing the range of soldiery conduct that was, in the end, wasted by political forces beyond the scope of the men in the field...

history.title: Air America [DVD]
history.review_title: As much fun as we can associate with Vietnam...
history.text: The film is a brilliant add-on to our pantheon of films in re the Vietnam era. It is very much like Apocalypse Now insofar as the operatives that hire Sheen in that are similar to the mysterious agents that hire Downy to fly for 'Air America' (unofficially) in a field of battle that we(America) are not officially fighting. Gibson is brilliant as a self-absorbed pilot/operator who is out for himself while (co-incidentally) helping his country by flying supplies to our 'friends' in the region of Vietnam(i.e. Laos and Cambodia)...He(Gibson) is confronted by moral dilemmas, like Downy's questions about their helping control the poppy fields for related 'trade', or a friend's charitable activities which will ruin his(Gibson's) huge payday before retirement. Gibson has to decide whether to do the right thing(sic) or cash in. The choice is clearcut...or is it? Anyway, this is a brilliant semi-realistic rendition of the air war that we fought for the 'hearts and minds' of the area people around 'Nam. Best of all, it's funny and engaging while showing historical events.

history.title: The Errand Boy
history.text: This is quite simple: The Errand Boy was almost 100% Jerry Lewis, with him as star, director, and co-writer. If that intrigues you, then this is a must-have. If you are of the group that either dislikes Jerry or has pretty much forgotten him, then you might want to keep on truckin'... The Errand Boy was a wonderful family comedy about the movie studios of the time. You have to remember that the studios of the time had had 50 years of dominance; they were factories for movies with massive numbers of actors, extras, and management. That studio system is pretty much gone with the wind so this entire concept is dated. Nonetheless, it's a fascinating and amusing look at the arrogance of management, and you can relate to that for any industry. I'm not totally unbiased here; when Jerry came to Miami on vacation, he would always visit my father who was his personal physician down there...

history.title: Bat 21
history.text: Gene Hackman and Danny Glover star in this air action drama set in the Vietnam war epoch. Having read some of the reviews, positive and negative, I will say that the film, whether 100% accurate or not, is a riveting drama. Bat 21 is a perfect follow-up for you if you like Air America or any of the other Vietnam great films (Apocalypse Now, Platoon, etc.) Gene Hackman plays a specialist who goes out in the field by air and is brought down by enemy action. Suddenly, the war is not an intellectual pursuit for Hackman but is tangible; he has to fend for himself: evade the enemy and contact our forces to arrange a rescue (evacuation). It's touch and go whether he can make it out and you really experience how narrow an escape it will be...if he makes it home.

history.review_title: Only meant for a dumb audience
history.text: I really wanted to like it. The first two episodes were somewhat entertaining. You can see right away, its not to be taken to seriously, and is actually pretty dumb in many cases (like lost in space dumb). The aliens look pretty stupid. Must be one of the worse budgets in a long time. Ship looked okay, special effects, I can live with. I got past all that, and thought, okay, I can watch this goofy show. I liked the idea behind the show, and Kevin S, is cool. However, episode 3 was just too STUPID. I was okay with the Mad Max Theme (from beyond the Thunderdome), but really Kevin and crew acted dumber than the kids. They just destroy a solar system, and Kevin is still playing nice. They don't even give his vampire friend an escort with all these crazy kids, esp after what they just did?? They get their ship taken over by these dumb kids who don't really know anything, and made to look like fools. It was a bit much. I mean these kids can't even read, but they can destroy a star, and know all about jamming. What a load of BS. I just lost interest immediately. If you like dumb, this show is for you. Its amazing it made it through 5 seasons. I mean was this playing during Saturday morning cartoons? 1 star for Gene R. 1 star for concept and Kevin S.

history.title: Xanadu [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Finally on Blu-ray, and absolutely beautiful!
history.text: I won't go into the merits of the movie itself here, but rather want to comment on the Blu-ray release. Simply put, this movie has never looked better on home video. It's a bit grainy at times, as was the case for the film stock used during the period, but that also means it doesn't suffer from excessive noise reduction. The audio is presented in a 5.1 DTS HD mix, which I have a few misgivings about simply because the original film was only mixed to Dolby Stereo. There seems to be excessive channel separation applied but it still sounds good with no "phasing" artifacts. However, flipping briefly over to the Spanish and French mixes, they are very, very bright and harsh, musically. The Spanish mix in particular was so bright as to be painful to listen to. The extras are nothing special, just the Back to Xanadu documentary from 2008 and a trailer. Still, it's awesome to have this title on Blu-ray at all, and it looks much better than the HD version floating around the pay movie channels for several years and the streaming version available for purchase from the iTunes store, among others. Especially for the price, it's definitely worth it for any fan.

history.title: Carole King: Natural Woman
history.review_title: Great documentary, but not in any way different from what was broadcast along with audio issues.
history.text: While it's great to have this PBS special on disc, there's something about the mastering of the audio on this Blu-ray that gives it a bit of an echo as compared to the version broadcast on PBS. The good thing is the effect only seems to affect the narration, not the musical sequences (the audio of the PBS broadcast did NOT have this issue, so it happened somewhere in the disc mastering process.) I was, however, quite disappointed that the disc does NOT include the full, unedited acoustic video of "(You Make Me Feel Like a) Natural Woman" that PBS posted to their web site, so on-disc you're left only with the interrupted by narration clip that is part of the show itself. Still, if you haven't seen it, it's well worth your time; personally I would not have purchased the disc if I had known the version of the above song included as an extra was not the unedited clip from the documentary as seen on the PBS website.

The liquid satin gowns in the finale look as sumptuous as they likely did in person. The movie is enchanting and perfection itself, an incredibly sweet story that gets far too little airtime at Christmas. Do yourself a favor and pick up a copy and avoid the commercials and resolution drop of cable or satellite.

history.title: Peanuts Holiday Collection (4K Ultra HD + Blu-ray) [4K UHD]
history.text: The video quality on this new UHD collection is absolutely wonderful - the best these specials have ever and will ever look. However, the audio quality is the problem. As when they originally released them on Blu-ray, Warner decided to include a fake simulated surround audio mix on these specials, which means that you get to hear an echoey fake stereo mix for the Vince Guaraldi soundtracks that made these specials famous. They could have done the right thing and included an original mono track, but they did not, and because of the echo even if you set your sound processor to "Mono" it doesn't sound quite right. The only way of hearing these with the correct audio is to sync up the disc with a copy of the old DVDs, which had a mono soundtrack. This is truly sad and disrespectful to these classics; it's like if Miracle on 34th Street and It's a Wonderful Life were ONLY available in the horrible colorized versions rather than the original Black & White.

BTW there is only a bit of nudity at the start, by the time you get to the nudist zombies most of their flesh is rotted and is hanging strategically.

history.review_title: This is a mess don't bother
history.text: WTF? Apparently this is a weird (and poorly done) homage to 2001: A Space Oddyssey, Almost nothing happens, this movie is 95% filler and the stuff that isn't filler only makes sense once or twice. The rest of the time they are pretty much random scenes. I expected bad, but not like this. How this got a 5.3 rating on IMDB I will never know, there are three 1 star reviews and one 2 star review. How does that translate into a 5 star ratiing, maybe some of the people rating the movie just looked at the title and thought it was something else.

The story is familiar, a human raised by wolves. But the movie itself is horrible, limited sets, terrible special effects, awful editing, there may have been a plot, but I don't remember it. The only good thing about the movie is that Pearl Chang Ling is easy on the eyes.

history.review_title: The dinosaurs are the best actors in this movie
history.text: Bad, but not that bad. The dinosaurs are a joke, and the acting is adequate, at least for the four women in the movie, the dudes are terrible. The male lead is so unenjoyable that I wanted to kill him in the first 5 minutes, and the other guy I wasn't sure about but he died before I could decide. The CGI is terrible, the characters have absolutely no common sense whatsoever. This is a low budget movie and it shows.

history.review_title: There's a really loud scream in the movie, but there are no vixens
history.text: At first I thought this was a repackaging of the Darien Caine movie, except with all the sex and nudity taken out of it. But instead it is a movie with no vixens, nudity or sex. The best part of the movie, besides it finally ending, was a man screaming louder than a porn star having an orgasm. It's essentially a waste of time, luckily it is only 31 minutes long.

Just OK, nothing more. As others have said it's plain jane, like a cake with no icing. Nothing spectacular happens until just before the end. And as others have said there are better and worse movies out there.

history.review_title: Too stupid to believe a single thing about it!
history.text: SPOILERS FOLLOW: OK, so, let's send a multi-billion dollar spacecraft on a voyage and let's not bother to have safeguards in place to protect it from the initial event in this movie. Then, let's decide to touch down on a planet we know nothing about, have no helmets/self-contained breathing apparatus for any of the landing party, and have no trained personnel who can deal with medical emergencies calmly and efficiently. That was it, for me: I turned it off, and returned the disk. Too stupid to believe, unlike other installments in the Alien franchise. How Scott allowed himself to be a part of this project is hard to fathom. If he came up with this abomination, shame on him! Don't waste your time. STRONGLY NOT RECOMMENDED!

history.review_title: Strange movie about a strange guy.
history.text: Kind of an "out there" flick, based on a real-life series of events. Black does a good job at playing the weird guy.

history.title: The Mindy Project: Season 3
history.text: I know Season 4 has not run to completion, but I want to warn those of you who may be considering watching it: The writers have run out of steam. The first four episodes are terrible, and Mindy has become very unlikable, as I see it. She always was shallow, a glutton, flighty, etc. Now, she's more so, and showing just how fickle and vapid she is. I started disliking her after reading part of her book (I couldn't complete it) and I think that added to my dislike of this final season. In the end, for me, it's a matter of good riddance!

The first two seasons were pretty good, although the whole "When will she officially lose her virginity?" thing got annoying as heck to the point where I didn't give a hoot anymore. Then, they introduced a look-alike character and the plot got convoluted and absurd. I lost all interest, and never tuned back in. Not Recommended.

history.review_title: Excellent! : Star Trek, but with a little more humor.
history.text: OK, I've written it in my title, and I stand by it. This is solid Star Trek quality material and acting, with a bit more humor added to the mix, but not typical, over the top McFarlane yucks. The only thing missing from this show is in the credits. Where it shows: "Created by Seth McFarlane," it should also include: "(With warm thanks to Gene Roddenberry.)" I find it more original Star Trek in nature, but the later shows are also in the mix. Very highly recommended. I look forward to it, every week!

history.review_title: Would you like some brutal violence with your corny humor?
history.text: Violent garbage! I watched two episodes: Both had scenes of violence complete with head punches, blood, bruising, etc. One had a scene where the main character shoots a guy in his rear end because police were already on the way to her house on a "man shot" report. None of this was funny. The writers of this dreck should be ashamed of themselves, as should those of you who think this is a great show. It's not! And we wonder why our kids are desensitized to violence to the point where they easily commit horribly violent acts! STRONGLY NOT RECOMMENDED!

history.title: Stranger Things Season 1 4-disc DVD / Blu-Ray Collectors Edition Box Set (Exclusive VHS Box Style Packaging)
history.review_title: This series is pretty good BUT - - -
history.text: Winona Ryder may be one of the worst actresses I've ever seen. She overplays her part to a comical extent. Nothing she says is said in a believable fashion. Everything is just terribly overdone. I'm only a few episodes in, but I have a feeling the director has no clue how to rein her in. Too bad. I'm starting to ff through her scenes.

Not my style. I had to keep getting up and walking around to keep from falling asleep. Also, when Redmayne kept doing that annoying expression, where he did this little sick smile and sort of batted his eyelids/eyelashes, looking like he was about to get sick, I wanted to throw my shoe at my TV!

history.review_title: Just as good as Season 1, just
history.text: in a different way. The plot development is tight, and there are some twists and turns that keep you looking forward to each episode. Ron Perlman should get every acting award out there. He does an incredible job. Highly Recommended!

history.review_title: Fell asleep, twice. The second time, I slept right through it.
history.text: It's simply another Wood Man movie. This time OW plays Woody. I'm not sure how Allen can keep cranking these almost identical movies out, each year. I guess younger people, who've never seen his truly great stuff, buy tickets, and rent the disks, and thus keep a cash stream still flowing to his door. To me, it's sad. Oh well, people have to make a living. It doesn't hurt that the acting elite like to line up to be in his flicks.

history.title: All the Wrong Reasons
history.review_title: There are good reasons to watch this movie
history.text: A really good, well-acted movie. I just am not content with one thing: the ending. I don't want to play down somebody's fears, not at all, but I do know people like Kate who use their fears as a weapon, who do not even try and cope with them and brace themselves - and why? It is so pleasant if everybody gives attention and has consideration and dances around you like the golden calf. Nicole - I do not approve her actions, but I do understand her and have sympathy for her - is absolutely right when she says (spoiler alert) that Kate ruined James' life!! Well, he is to blame too, but not for the affair, but he should have divorced Kate long ago or at least not supported her this long and with this he enabled and reinforced her dwelling on her misery. I do not blame her for having the fears, but if she does not want to fight them for their own sake ( and she does not) and not for the sake of the people around her who she terrorizes completely with her madness, she should have left James and at best get a job where she can work at home without fellow workers. If she is alone she can be afraid and crazy as much as she likes, but if she wants attention and people around she has to fight to get better and not be so hideous and ruin James' life, who had been so kind and patient all along and does not deserve this, and Nicole's life. Not after what Kate did to James and what he did for her nevertheless. I am (only)quite happy with one person's ending, and that is Simon's. He has truly suffered an awful fate, and he fares remarkably - completely the opposite of selfish, mean Kate. And I am happy that he gets a bit of happiness back in the end. Unfortunately with Kate, I really hope she treats him much, much better than James. She was James' doom and is an evil being if she doesn't change. But also good to see Kevin Zegers again in a role he deserves.

history.title: Glee: Season 5
history.review_title: Glee is a great show for many reasons
history.text: Glee is a great show for many reasons, and keeping the fascination up for a fifth season without Finn and even mostly without Mr. Shu(e)ster, Sue and even the/a Glee club itself and still being entertaining is an achievement. But the thing I like most about Glee (and surely a relevant reason for its success) is that it is trying to be fair. But just for this reason I had to take off one point here: One would have thought that it is possible to watch a show like Glee, which is so much about being correct, doing justice to everybody and condemning hostility and bullying without having to be afraid to be insulted AGAIN, that a just, friendly show like Glee would refrain from cliched offensive bashing, but oops, in Season 5 it becomes clear that nobody, just nobody gives a damn about justice to Germans. They are the welcome scapegoat if a villain/negative example/whipping boy is needed. But apart from not being original or decent, it isn’t even true/correct/just. Stating that Lesbos is overrun by Germans isn’t even the whole truth,the true problem is/ it is mostly overrun by British tourists showing their worst behaviour, but you do not want to bash the British, right? No, you want to offend the Germans like all other shows, because they are the easy patsies, they have "no" feelings/are not allowed to feel offended and hurt and being treated justly/correctly. And if there was a grain of doubt then this was washed away in episode 5-17 when the producers managed to sneak in a Nazi-remark into this musical high-school show!!! Unnecessarily rude like all the others. But, breaking news, the Germans are NOT your patsies/whipping boys to torture and misuse. And moreover: if you want to offend, check the facts first. But honestly: better do not offend anybody at all. And the times when that power-hungry AUSTRIAN came along and stirred things up are long gone and have been put on stage and thereby criticized AND avenged a billion times by each and every bungler or fool who doesn’t even care about the facts but just wants to live out his hate (and target people who don’t fight back). So stop, look for something else – and best: put your own house in order first/tackle your own problems for a change instead of using ancient stories and hurting innocent non-participants.

history.title: D Train
history.review_title: Different, but that's a good thing, delicate, original and funny
history.text: To say it plain and simple: I enjoyed this movie. I am shocked (not by the movie but) by all the negative comments. I thought that Jack Black was great in it -not that he isn't great in his other movies (Kings of Rock- grrreat!), but I think it is because there was a bigger depth to this character than most of his other movies), D-Train does not reach the greatness of Black's Orange County or Shallow Hal (both superb movies!), but it was a fresh and entertaining look at midlife crises and Highschool reunions. James Marsden stars as Black's equally great counterpart, I really liked him in this maybe morally a bit deviant but likable role - in the end his character is not a mean guy, but actually (and sadly) just pretty lost. Sure, the movie was not the obvious alumni meeting movie/what I expected, but this is a good thing. I was afraid it was gonna turn out as something about long-kept jealousy and some only rooster in the yard clinch, but fortunately it wasn't. It was a delicate, tender story about life choices, desire for friendships, attention and recognition, and coming to terms with your place in life. And done in a very entertaining, funny, original way. I did not see the turns and twists coming, but they did not shock but entertain and enjoy me. Come on, it also features the great Kathryn Hahn and cultish 80ies music - gotta love that! I only felt bad for the nice boss, Bill, but if I understood the ending right, this side story ended well, too. So give it a shot, be prepared for something different and enjoy!

history.title: The O.C.: Season 1
history.review_title: This is how it is done - an example for everybody- A plus
history.text: The O.C.-one of the best shows ever and forever, and that’s why: not only is it an encouraging, positive show that lifts you up when you need to watch something to forget the world and its cruelty, it does so without being destructive/not at the cost of other people/values. There is no clumsy, obvious affirmative action (which is always reverse racism underneath), there is no bashing of Europeans/non-Americans for the sake of a nasty political agenda/clumsy propaganda, there is no twisting of historical facts (especially European ones), no turning European legends into villains and so on. And yet, it is a thrilling, entertaining, sometimes thought-provoking show – yes, it can be done, and it can be done successfully and artfully. True, there have been shows about teenagers in rich neighborhoods before, true, there have been shows about unlike couplings/brothers. There have been shows about noble criminals and teenage romance. But this show unites it all in a unique and charming way, and adds a lot of heart and soul and smartness. This is not just a dumb teenie/romance/hypocritical family show, these are beautifully written, round (and perfectly cast) characters with heart and wits – entertaining and educating at the same time (without being overly didactic). This is the show I would recommend to parents to show their kids in order to show them how to behave in the world. A truly uplifting, funny and also instructive show – for viewers and writers alike, this is how it is done, you can entertain/be entertained without violence and xenophobia. A plus!!
