history.title: Unbroken
history.review_title: Good Film but Painful to Watch
history.text: After reading the book I wanted to watch the film to see how well it portrays Louis Zamperini's true story as told in the book. For the most part I felt the film follows the book fairly well. I had avoided seeing the movie in a theater when it was first released because the preview emphasized the brutal treatment afflicted on the American prisoners, most painfully on Louis Zamperini, and I do not like to see violence. Three advantages of the DVD over seeing the movie in a theater are (1) the film can be fast-forwarded through disagreeable scenes, (2) closed captioning provides clarity for dialogue that can be difficult to hear, and (3) the film can be reversed at any time to see an earlier scene again. This DVD is of good technical quality and the acting, costuming, and scenery are credible and convincing. I'm glad I purchased and watched the DVD, but if it had been available in my local public library I would have preferred to see their copy because I do not think I will want to watch the difficult experiences of the downed American airplane crew again. It's good to know that eventual release, a good life and active, productive old age came to Louis Zamperini, but for the most part the film is a painful experience to watch.

history.title: Brideshead Revisited (25th Anniversary Collector's Edition) [DVD]
history.review_title: Beautifully Produced But Disappointing In Its Ultimate Message
history.text: Recently I completed watching this entire set of four discs and overall I can say I enjoyed it. It was intriguing and highly entertaining in the beginning, but frankly I found that author Evelyn Waugh apparently had a negative view of life which caused the story line to become increasingly disappointing as it neared the conclusion. Although he might have been trying to portray the unpleasant realities of life, Waugh's conclusion was, to me, very unsatisfying and somewhat depressing. The acting, lush landscapes and interior scenery are of the top quality we have come to expect and enjoy with excellent British productions. I wish I could say the same for the outcome of the story line, which seemed so promising in the beginning. Being a natural optimist and one who enjoys a cheerful outlook on life, I wish that Brideshead Revisited could be re-written so as to be as satisfying and enjoyable throughout as it could have been.

history.title: Falling for a Dancer
history.review_title: Worthless to me without captions or subtitles to translate the indecipherable accents
history.text: This movie would have been intriguing and enjoyable, I'm sure, if there were closed captions or English subtitles. The accents of the actors are totally indecipherable to my native Southern American ear. Apparently, Falling for a Dancer is well respected and highly reviewed by many who have posted reviews here. However, I was very disappointed that I could understand hardly a single word spoken. Although, as I said, my background is native American Southern (born and reared in South Carolina), I have travelled widely in the U.S. and to several countries in Europe, and have lived in various locations in the north, midwest and west of the U.S.A. I have friends from Germany, France, Ireland, England, Australia, Italy, etc. and have no problem understanding various accents and variations of spoken English. This film was a total loss to me. Fortunately I found it at my local public library, thus there was no financial cost to watch it. I'm sure I would enjoy it if I knew what the actors are saying. If anyone knows of a DVD that does include captions or English subtitles, I would be grateful for a comment here to tell me where to find it. Thank you.

history.title: In Bruges
history.text: Stupid, stupid, stupid. That's how I feel about my decision to buy this absolute piece of trash. How any sane, halfway moral person can enjoy the repetitively filthy language, the animosity and hostility disguised as something acceptable, the perverse morals, and sheer disgust of senseless guns and murder is a complete mystery to me. Unfortunately, I was misled by my appreciation of Colin Farrell's acting ability in a few good films he's appeared in to think this one might be worth the one cent plus shipping charged for it. Serious mistake on my part! It's going into the trash right now, because there's no redeeming quality in it whatsoever for any reasonably intelligent person. I will make certain this copy of the DVD is destroyed so that nobody else will suffer the misfortune of watching it. Not even the amazon.com "top critical review" of this film provides a just and fair revelation of what it's actually about. In my opinion it was a great waste of talent that could have otherwise been invested in something with redeeming value. Hopefully my error in buying it can be justified to a tiny extent by offering this review. My recommendation -- do not buy it or watch it. Period!

history.title: Spotlight [DVD]
history.text: This film is spellbinding; I could not stop watching. Supremely well cast, the actors performed so well they were convincingly the "real people" in this true story. The scenery, the pacing, the thoroughness of details and facts moved the film along as though I were watching the events and the investigation unfold as it it happened. Rarely if ever have I seen a film telling the story of actual events so well done. Fortunately the DVD was in my local public library, in excellent condition, and I was privileged to check it out and watch it almost immediately after I learned about it. Very, very well done, informative, believable in every detail, and I highly recommend it for anyone who cares about excellence in journalism, significant historical phenomena, real life human experience, intelligently written scripts, and superior dramatic presentation. Simply superb.

history.title: Trumbo
history.review_title: One of the best DVDs I've seen recently, and I do watch a large variety of them
history.text: Trumbo is a fascinating film based on the life of a real man who lived a significant, impressive and successful life as a screenwriter and a champion for free speech, freedom of expression in all aspects of life, and the importance of government serving the people rather than controlling and manipulating them. The actors, especially Bryan Cranston, were exceedingly well cast and marvelous in their performances. Although I may tend to highlight my enthusiasm for the excellent film, it was thoroughly well written, performed and produced. I enjoyed every minute of this true-to-life presentation. Although I was growing up during the era of the actual events, I knew very little about them and virtually nothing about the people involved. This movie is both an excellent history lesson and throughly enjoyable entertainment.

history.title: Intermission
history.review_title: Indecent, not worthy of the time to view it
history.text: In the first 17 minutes of this miserably odious film, I saw and heard nothing but disgustingly foul language, crudeness, and almost total lack of decency. There is no evidence of intelligence in the characters portrayed, just a poorly written, foul script. I'm not watching any more of it. Fortunately I did not pay for this dvd; I borrowed it from the interlibrary loan service of the local public library because it includes Colin Farrell in the cast. Colin has appeared in some very good roles, but clearly this is not one of them. He seems to have used very poor judgment in his choice of some of the roles he has agreed to in the past, and in my humble opinion this is one of them. I did read the reviews here on Amazon.com before requesting the dvd from the library, but I saw no clue about the filthy language and indency in the script. I would not recommend this film to anyone who cares for well-made, decent movies. I give this one and Colin Farrell's role in it a thumbs down.

history.title: Whiplash [DVD]
history.review_title: Enjoyable but with some serious exceptions
history.text: This movie was difficult to watch because of the almost incessant tension and the overly-gratuitous, totally unnecessary outpouring of filthy, abusive language. I was far more interested in Miles Teller as Andrew Neiman, a kid who really wanted to be a great drummer, than I was in the unending abuse by the sadistic, maniacal conductor Fletcher, played by J.K. Simmons. Teller's acting and facial expressions are nuanced and absorbing to watch. The ending of the movie was a climax without adequate explanation, but the drummer took control with a triumphant solo, Fletcher submitting and guiding him to his triumphant ending. Note: Don't bother watching the commentary in the special features, it has little to do with what's happening onscreen. The commentary is little more than an egotistical indulgence by the director and J.K. Simmons into their own interests and prejudices with a lot of comments far afield that give little insight into what's happening in the film. Even though Miles Teller has presented an excellent performance in his role, the director and Simmons in their comments unfairly, to my mind, insult and criticize him. Even if it was meant "tongue in cheek", it was in very poor taste. The commentary would have been better left out completely.

history.title: Love and Honor
history.text: First off, I absolutely detest any DVD that forces the viewer to wait through several long previews of cheap second-rate, mostly violent movies to get to the title film, with fast-forwarding barred and no way to get past them except to let them play. Secondly, the movie is way past its time. The attractive young soldiers make a stupid, ill-advised trip back to the States from the battlefront in Vietnam to get enmeshed with a bunch of brainwashed juvenile college students who, like so many other people at that time, thought they were right to denigrate the brave military fighting under orders for their country. Of course there was a huge controversy about the rightness of the Vietnam war but there's now little point in rehashing those times in a poorly-thought-out movie plot and bad acting in scenes that make no good sense now. Thumbs down! I stopped watching and ejected the DVD within just a few minutes of trying to appreciate what was presented. I do not recommend this DVD for any thinking, mature adult.

history.title: The Lucky One /Walk to Remember (DBFE)(DVD)
history.review_title: Zac Efron Is Excellent as "The Lucky One"
history.text: This DVD was an economical and surprisingly good purchase. "The Lucky One" with Zac Efron is an excellent, somewhat unusual and satisfying movie. Efron portrays a strong, stoic, capable, resourceful, and caring young man recovering from a troubled past. As a former Marine who miraculously was spared from almost certain death, he has sought escape, relief, and a specific goal in a cross country journey on foot and alone. His ultimately unfolding relationship with the beautiful young but skeptical daughter of his lady employer, the owner of a dog training and kennel service, develops sensitively and beautifully. Efron's character's emotional reserve and control, and his development into a gentle but strong, sensitive, fun-loving friend and eventual lover are inspiring to watch. In this movie Zac Efron has grown into a surprisingly matured actor compared to his teenage efforts. I had read and enjoyed Nicholas Sparks' "A Walk to Remember" several years ago. This DVD has given me an opportunity to see that movie. It's well acted and produced, not quite as entrancing as "The Lucky One", but a pleasant portrayal of another Nicholas Sparks story of a beautiful young romance .

targets.title: A Home at the End of the World

history.review_title: A surprisingly wonderful film despite a few flaws
history.text: I did not have high expectations for this movie, especially after watching how it begins (with Bill Murray's character Richie Lanz lying to an older woman with a weird singing style that she "has talent" just so he can bilk her out of a promoter fee of $1,200). I thought, "Another cheesy little film with a plot derivative of all other cheesy little films, I am sure." But over and over again the film proved me wrong. Sure, I could have done without the Pretty-Woman-cliche Kate Hudson plays (prostitute who is not only drop-dead gorgeous but classy and smart about business) and many other improbable aspects of the plot. But still: Zooey Deschanel's character is hilarious, the first time you see Bruce Willis he is genuinely scary and psycho-looking (after that his character is never again scary or even interesting), the story is not at all predictable (until near the end) . . . BUT! The real gem is Bill Murray, who is just HILARIOUS. For me, Bill Murray is not always a joy to watch, but he certainly is in this film. This could literally be one of Bill Murray's finest performances, and that is saying a lot. Groundhog Day may be a better movie, but the character Bill Murray plays in Groundhog Day is not as funny as the character he plays in this movie, Rock the Kasbah. I am serious. Being upbeat and always able to see the silver lining in every situation is Richie Lanz' job as a promoter, Bill Murray is completely believable as Richie Lanz, and Richie Lanz is, quite simply, very fun to watch. This film is a comedy because Bill Murray is the star AND the 'comic relief.' You know why this film has so few 4 & 5 star reviews? Because the film is sympathetic towards natives of Afghanistan and realistically portrays the devastation which U.S. involvement in that country has wrought -- period. Too many Americans do not want to be reminded of the negative consequences of our military presence, and the discomfort this film no doubt causes them completely outweighs the humor of the story. At least that is my conclusion, based on things I have read in Amazon reviews.

An excellent documentary. It is true that paradise is not a place but a condition, and that wherever you go you still take yourself with you -- so if you are the problem, then there is no place you can go to get a fresh start (as Dr. Ritter almost certainly discovered). The story of these individuals who sought to abandon civilization and create their own 'paradise' is thought-provoking on so so many levels.

history.title: Hotel
history.review_title: There is a reason that almost 60% of those who watch this film hate it!
history.text: The 5 star reviews make a few good points and the 1 star reviews make many good points . . . meaning that a few ideas/moments in the film deserve 5 stars, but many, many more -- most actually -- deserve a 1 star rating. (BTW, I've almost never encountered anything more hated by Amazon reviewers than this film! Almost 60% of those who watch this film hate it, and it is NOT because none of us know how to identify 'good film-making' or that we do not understand the cutting-edge creativity of independent film-making. Please: cut the 'art film pretentiousness' already). I would have been generous and given this film 3 stars EXCEPT the light pornography about 30-40 minutes in completely destroyed what little interest the film had generated and caused me to turn it off for good. I mean, there is so much which is horrible and wrong with this film that it was barely keeping me interested ANYWAY, but then it had to divide into 4-scenes-at-once (4 picture-within-a-picture boxes containing different scenes) with each simultaneously depicting a different scenario of light porn? No, no, no. This was supposed to be a horror/mystery film -- or so the back of the DVD case indicated. If your film is so bad you need to induce lasciviousness in your audience just to keep them watching, please, next time, just SCRAP THE PROJECT, okay? My teen sons were watching with me and they don't need to see that crap. (Note: many parents watch R-rated films with their teens because that's infinitely better than the teen watching alone or with other teens: a parent can discuss what needs to be discussed about the film as it progresses, as well as decide if, and when, it is time to simply turn the movie off). One final comment: how in the hell did this director get so many A list actors to participate in this farce of a film? Was there even a script? Were any of the actors given the opportunity, before signing on, to actually READ the script? Did they give John Malkovich a fake script such that he thought there was actually a real MOVIE with a PLOT attached to his one (interesting, yet bizarre) scene? Did any of these actors sue after the completed film was released because it was not at all what it had been represented to be, upfront? Enquiring minds want to know! (P.S. Since I did not watch the entire film, maybe John Malkovich had more than his one scene at the very beginning . . . but I suspect he did not.) For those of you who are going to hate on me because of what I said about the 'eroticism' of this film: true eroticism is something completely different than sex used to manipulate an audience. A woman dipping her bare breasts into glasses of milk in order to arouse a man is just weird, not erotic. A woman wearing a miniskirt and no panties who pulls a gun from between her legs (insinuating that she had it up inside her) is crass and gross, not erotic. Showing disembodied female legs parting to permit the entry of a disembodied hand while simultaneously portraying a nude man and other sexual imagery in separate picture boxes) is pornography, not eroticism.

history.title: Saving Face
history.review_title: Interesting, but I think Matt Kern has everyone hoodwinked
history.text: This documentary was not especially well done, and it is easy to see why many would find it boring. It certainly would never be considered for a film-making award! You will only find it worth watching if you are deeply interested in the subject matter, which is essentially 'An Inmate's Spiritual Conversion: Was It Real?' I was interested enough in the subject matter to look beyond the boring film style . . . but there were a lot of things about Matt Kern's story which disturbed me, and it seemed obvious by the end that the documentary was one-sided, intentionally skewed towards the premise that Matt Kern is a bona fide "changed man" who deserved to serve only 12 years of a 60 year murder sentence. Pivotal to the Grant of Clemency which Kern received is the belief that Kern had a spiritual conversion while in solitary confinement, but I cannot shake the feeling that it was all a manipulative act. Here is what disturbs me: for a man who has supposedly found Christ and feels 'great remorse' for his role in the taking of a human life, Kern sure does continue to shift blame and accountability for his conduct! He repeatedly implied that he engaged in stealing cars and other criminal anti-social acts as a teen 'because that's what we were seeing on TV' (i.e., popular culture is to blame), and that he only brought a gun the night the murder occurred 'because one of the other guys wanted me to' (i.e., the other guy is the one to blame). Then he says the gun was only there for show, they were never planning to use it -- but when the victim didn't cooperate (i.e., the victim is to blame) they 'had' to shoot (i.e., the unanticipated circumstances are to blame). Etc. etc. And keep in mind this is not Matt-Kern-the-unredeemed-criminal who keeps slipping in these subtle little 'not really my fault' comments, but Matt-Kern-the-converted-man-who-is-now-supposedly-walking-with-God. Where is the devotion to truth and accountability? I just read an interview Matt Kern did with the 700 Club, and found more evidence of Kern trying to sound innocent. Someone convicted that God requires truth does not keep changing his story, but in this interview Matt Kern did. First, he claimed someone else brought the gun that night, not him (not true). Second, he said the victim died from 'the gunshot' as if there was one quasi-accidental, regrettable gun shot. The reality, as vividly stated in this documentary, is that Kern's buddy shot the victim once; they all rushed into the victim's car to steal it and make a quick getaway; before leaving they realized the victim could identify them if he lived; Kern's buddy got back out of the car and shot the victim four more times at point blank range. I.e., the murder was not an unthinking accident by a single gunshot, but a cold-blooded execution, with multiple shots, purposefully intended to kill and silence a witness. The icing on the cake is near the end of the documentary when Matt Kern is asked what he owes the man who was murdered. It's like someone suddenly hit Kern with a train: his smooth-talking demeanor changes abruptly as he becomes absolutely speechless. It is clearly a question he never anticipated (and, thus, did not prepare a rehearsed answer for) and he is desperately trying to think of what he should say in order to sound legitimately like 'a changed man.' When he realizes he is blowing it, he tries to give the impression that he is wrestling with the question because he is humbled and it is a weighty question . . . except you can tell by the look on his face that he honestly does not feel he owes the murdered man anything . . . because to Matt Kern, EVERYTHING ABOUT THE MURDER WAS SOMEBODY ELSE'S FAULT. It is a truly telling moment. Meaningful coincidence: the night before I watched this documentary, I 'just happened' to watch The Queen of Versailles, a documentary about manipulative timeshare mogul David Siegel and his dysfunctional poser trophy-wife Jackie Siegel. Jackie is also a blame-shifter, and I see many similarities between she and Matt Kern -- despite the radically different context of their lives (and lies). Just had to throw that out there.

history.title: Kids' Ten Commandments
history.review_title: I wouldn't ever show this series to a child
history.text: First, I thought this series would teach kids how to follow the Ten Commandments -- meaning that each story would illustrate the applicability of a commandment to modern times. I don't need an animated movie to tell my children the story of Moses and the burning bush, or what happened when Moses returned to the Israelites and discovered that they had fashioned an idol to worship: there are illustrated children's bibles for that purpose. But there are not many good resources to show children how to apply the commandments today, in modern situations. Second, just because kids are young does not mean they are stupid and like stories that are idiotic and 'dumbed down.' Accordingly, the talking animals really rubbed me the wrong way. I also rolled my eyes at the inclusion of two 'Broadway production' numbers (first when the calf sings about how famous he is going to be and second when the 'evil doer' and a woman dressed like a harem girl sing a duet and (literally) do a soft-shoe dance in front of the golden idol. Gag me. Both are completely unnecessary for the telling of the story and weren't very interesting. Parents: get your children a nicely illustrated Children's Bible and skip this ridiculous series which is only LOOSELY based on the Bible.

history.title: The Salesman
history.review_title: Stick with this quiet, subtle film until the end and you will be TREMENDOUSLY rewarded
history.text: I love great films, including great foreign films -- and this film did not disappoint. Since I believe in the importance of Arthur Miller's masterpiece Death of a Salesman, I was especially pleased when I discovered that the film's primary characters were acting in an Iranian production of Death of a Salesman while undergoing the events which make up the film's primary plot. But then to discover how skillfully Death of a Salesman weaves into the resolution of the film's plot and conflict?? MINDBLOWING! As the film ends, it becomes crystal clear that this film is, quite simply, a masterpiece of story, theme and meaning. It reminds me of watching the 1978 TV mini-series of George Eliot's Mill on the Floss (starring Judy Cornwell, Barbara Hicks and Pippa Guard, which I stumbled upon on DVD at our local library) which similarly tied everything together in the final moments in a SHAZAM of meaning, correlation, symbolism, you name it. Simply fantastic. This film Salesman may at times take you out of your comfort zone, but please persevere even if it does. For example, for me, the wife's refusal to go to the police to report an assault caused her husband to become something of a vigilante -- which really made me cringe, and I was very uncomfortable for a significant middle portion of the film. But these were authentic reactions by believable, realistic characters: if I truly want to understand the motivations and actions of individuals different from myself, I have to be willing to tolerate, and bear with, being taken temporarily out of my comfort zone. Despite the fact that the protagonists are gentle people, and the film is predominantly non-violent, there was tension you could practically cut with a knife and the suspense of where everything was heading kept me on the edge of my seat until the final moments/resolution. An incredibly well done film that leaves you KNOWING you have just witnessed great art.

history.review_title: An excellent must see for the history of the Armenian Genocide and portrayal of Ottoman Empire culture
history.text: The Promise gets 4 stars for the story and drama, which I assumed was entirely fictional -- but when I learned at the end of the film's historical importance (I had never before heard of the Armenian genocide which occurred in Turkey during WWI), that elevated my opinion of the film's worth to the level of 5 stars. The Promise is an interesting, engrossing, and HISTORICALLY RELEVANT film I recommend everyone see. The acting was well done, and despite the obvious use of a green screen to show panoramic views of the Sea of Marmara (or the Black Sea: IDK which one) in early shots of Constantinople (now Istanbul), the cinematography is fine as well. But what makes the film exceptional is the portrayal of Turkish society and culture at the close of the Ottoman Empire followed by a history lesson about the Armenian Genocide and the events at Musa Dagh (the mountain where Armenian resistors, fleeing genocide at the hands of Ottoman Turks, were saved by a French warship).

history.title: Faith of Our Fathers [DVD]
history.review_title: Stupid, facile, unbelievable, don't waste your time
history.text: I can usually watch almost any movie all the way to the end -- but not this one. It was a waste of time. First, I am so sick and tired of the stereotypes one finds so often in Christian films. For example, to stress that modern day Christian women are not expected to be 'barefoot and pregnant,' Christian films often swing to the opposite extreme and portray women (like John's fiancee) as hopelessly unable to perform the most basic of domestic chores. [I'm pretty sure this same stereotype was used in The Resurrection of Gavin Stone, another recent Christian film.] Please, give me a break. The opening scene of, "Honey, please don't cook: let's order pizza!" (because she is a horrible cook) was stupid and insulting. Second, the story line was idiotic. Like John is REALLY going to fly across the country three weeks before his wedding to confront (whomever answers the door) because after a lifetime of not knowing anything about his father, he just CAN'T wait 24 hours to see if he can get the guy he's trying to reach (Wayne) on the phone? And he is REALLY going to sit outside all day waiting on Wayne to let him in the house and talk to him? And Wayne has absolutely nothing going on in his life that he can spur of the moment say "We're going to Washington D.C." with a total stranger -- the same total stranger he made wait outside an entire day before he would deign to even speak to him? And you are REALLY going to leave your car empty, with keys in the ignition, with complete strangers you picked up as hitchhikers the day before milling around with easy access to it? No one is that trusting. And, like, REALLY that every letter Wayne's father writes home from Vietnam is going to be completely about how wonderful John's father is, a man who is a total stranger to his family? Give me a break. So unbelievable. Third, the 'humor' was juvenile, predictable and HOKEY TO THE MAX -- as it often is in Christian films, which is so sad and embarrassing. About the time the hitchhikers stole the car, I couldn't take any more. My reaction was, "Clearly this movie isn't going to get any better or more realistic; why waste any further time?"

history.review_title: A very well done film, vastly superior to the American version
history.text: First, I have not yet read Herman Koch's novel -- though I plan to soon. Second, I watched this film after having just watched the DISASTROUS American film starring Richard Gere, Steve Coogan, Laura Linney and Rebecca Hall. I almost immediately gave this film, the Italian film, 5 stars just because it is so so so so much better than the American film . . . but in reading other reviews I suspect that it does not live up to the novel, so I compromised at 4 stars. The moral issues are important and timely ones: I hope Koch's novel goes in to them further than either of the films. I look forward to reading it.

history.title: Certain Women (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.review_title: In some ways this movie deserves 2 stars, but in other ways it shines
history.text: Why it can be argued that this movie deserves no more than 2 stars: it was almost unbearably slow, I hated the way it ended, and the stories of the three primary female characters -- played by Laura Dern, Michelle Williams and Lily Gladstone -- are woefully under-connected. That said, I have given the movie 4 stars because I respect the filmmaker's vision and goal: each of the three stories reveals something very true about human nature, and the revelation of that truth redeems the film's other very-large flaws. The first story of a female lawyer devalued and mistreated by her male client hit very close to home for me. I practiced law 6 - 8 years before devoting myself full-time to raising a family, and I repeatedly found myself in situations where my analysis was devalued, or not trusted, SIMPLY because of the fact that I am female. Thus, I have personal experience that the dynamic between Laura Dern's character (a lawyer) and Jarred Harris's character (as her client) is real and valid, though it irritates me that Dern's character allows herself to be treated like a doormat. Jared Harris's character was injured on the job and received a settlement at the time of the injury, but later hired Laura Dern's character to figure out if he could still sue because he now considers the settlement too small. The whole point of the story is that Dern's legal opinion has no credibility with him because she is a woman, and he doesn't "get it" that he waived his right to sue (by accepting the settlement) until a male lawyer tells him the same thing. It is after he gets the second legal opinion from the male lawyer that he becomes outraged enough to take a guard hostage, at his former place of employment, demanding to see the company's file on his claim. Laura Dern's character steps in to help resolve the crisis, but Jared Harris's character continues to devalue her, even stating that no one would blame him if he killed her because "she was his lawyer" and look how he got screwed! (Except that she wasn't his lawyer until after he had already screwed himself.) The point of this first story line is the misogynistic way Harris's character repeatedly takes advantage of Laura Dern's character; so, why she visits him in prison or agrees to become his pen pal is BEYOND ME. I.e., she is way too "nice" for her own good -- meaning, as I mentioned, that she allows herself to become a doormat. She's also a doormat in her affair with Gina's husband as well, so this is clearly a huge part of her personality. The second story line is about the personality of a woman (Gina) whose husband is having an affair (with Laura Dern's lawyer character) and how Gina's personality might be a factor in her husband's decision to cheat. On the surface Gina appears nice enough, but really Gina is a sociopath. Gina only cares about what Gina wants (for Gina) and she bulldozes over anyone in her path (though she is very polite and sweet as she does it.) For example, Gina promises her teen-aged daughter that if the daughter goes camping with them, they will return home first thing Sunday morning so that the daughter will still have one weekend day to herself -- but Gina never has any intention of honoring the promise. Gina then takes advantage of an elderly man (Albert): she manipulates Albert into giving her sandstone rocks on his property even though she knows the rocks have sentimental value to him and he clearly doesn't want to part with them. Even though Gina ostensibly wants the sandstone for a house she is building, she admits she has no idea what she is going to do with them: she just "has to have them," probably because Albert so obviously DOESN'T want her to have them. I.e., Gina gets a thrill manipulating people to do things they do not want to do, and that makes her a SOCIOPATH. Finally there is the tale of the lonely character played by Lily Gladstone. I very much enjoyed Lily Gladstone's performance: she does an excellent job portraying a character SO lonely and bereft of human contact (while working solo as a winter caretaker of a large ranch) that she becomes obsessed with the possibility of connection to a woman her own age who drives in twice a week to teach a night class at the local high school. Many will assume Gladstone's character is a lesbian who becomes interested in Elizabeth, Kristen Stewart's character, for romantic reasons, but the reality is that someone as deprived of human connection as Gladstone's character will go to a great deal of effort JUST TO HAVE A FRIEND (and/or some human conversation and connection). The story is UNAMBIGUOUS that the motivation for the pursuit is the alleviation of loneliness, period.

history.title: Fushigi Yugi Eikoden
history.review_title: Horrible main character can't save this already stupid, pointless OVA
history.text: First there is no reason to watch this. Mayo is an evil, stuck up b** *h who reminds me of Stroke Face. There is no redeemable quality that she has and her back story is so pathetic that it doesn't give her an excuse for her actions. Oh boo hoo! My parents don't get along! Boo hoo oh f*****g well! She should have died miserably then maybe I would have rated this waste of an OVA 2 stars. The CG in Sailor Moon Crystal looks way better than the ugly CG you see here. Skip this! It has nothing to do with the original manga by Yuu Watase.

history.title: Lucky Star: The Complete Series [BD Combo Pack]
history.text: I'm so glad Funimation got the rights to Lucky☆Star and The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya! Both are really great anime series that were extremely popular in Japan and released im the US by Bandai around a decade ago. It's great that Lucky★Star is gonna finally be rereleased. For those of you who don't know, Lucky Star is a slice-of-life anime that peeks into the lives of ordinary Japanese High School student girls while referencing many Japanese culture and popular Anime...as quoted by character Akira Kogami herself as she explains this in show to the Anime Store manager ;) It's really one of those "talking head" shows where you watch characters have conversations with each other about what's the end of a chocolate cornet. The fat end or the skinny end? Since we already know Lucky Star is a great series there's no doubt this rerelease will ALSO be great since Funimation is releasing it! We'll expect reversible cover art and hopefully bonus features... unlike Sentai Filmworks' horrible releases. Seriously, have any of you seen how they releases Clannad?? That big, tacky, bulky box with the discs stacked onto each other on a cheap spindle with a foamy sponge to keep it in place? Shaking my head. On top of that they don't offer ANY bonus features on their releases except Textless Opening and Ending Animations and other Sentai Filmworks previews...which is usually only just that series opening... so we don't actually get a trailer. Shaking my head again. So glad Funimation secured this and Haruhi and NOT Sentai Filmworks. I actually had a BAD dream that Sentai Filmworks got Haruhi and REDUBBED IT! The cast was awful: Kyon - David Matranga Haruhi Suzumiya - Brittany Karbowski Yuki Nagato - Emily Neeves Mikuru Asahina - Hilary Haag... I don't even know who do Koizumi's voice ans frankly I don't care. I'm not saying these voice actors are bad...THEY JUST REUSE THEM in every one of their shows! Clannad, Angel Beats and ef...BUT thankfully that was only a dream and Sentai will for sure NOT redub Haruhi. Lucky Star is one of the English Dubs that I truly love and prefer over the Japanese voices. Wendy Lee is amazing as Konata Izumi and so is Michelle Ruff, Karen Strassman, Kari Wahlgren, Stephanie Sheh and Sam Regal...all personal favorites of mine in the English dubbed world of anime. I REALLY hope Funimation includes a new English dub for the OVA episode! That'll definitely be a marketable feature and secure my decision to definitely buy this product!

history.title: Little Busters Ex
history.review_title: More secrets to the world after Refrain!
history.text: This was a great follow-up to the Little Busters anime series, Little Busters (season 1) and Little Busters Refrain (season 2). Little Busters EX is an extended release of the Little Busters visual novel but adds three new heroine routes for Sasami Sasasegawa, Kanata Futaki and the new heroine, Saya Tokido. All three stories are great and just as enjoyable as the other six girl's stories in the main series but for a precautionary measure, I do not recommend this OVA unless you've watched the first two seasons because you will be clueless as to what's going on. More importantly, their stories revolve heavily around "the secret of the world" that has not been revealed until the end of Refrain. EX is 8 episodes long. The first four episodes revolve around Saya Tokido, the next two, Sasami Sasasegawa and the last two, Kanata Futaki. As per all Sentai Filmworks releases, we can expect all Clean Openings, all Clean Endings and Sentai previews. With a character like Saya Tokido and with Sentai Filmworks' habit of having all similar characters be played by the same voice actor/actress, I would expect someone like Brittany Karbowski to play Saya, the only problem is, she already played Rin Natsume in this series. I pray that Sentai does not cast Shelley-Calene Black as her! Although Sentai Filmworks will not be releasing a DVD or Bluray for this series until 6 December, I will come back and review both the DVDs and Blurays once they are released. 10 DEC UPDATE: So I watched all eight episodes on a slow graveyard shift at work. I have NEVER seen the English dub of Little Busters or Little Busters Refrain but I did watch EX in English just because I've seen the Japanese version with subs dozens of times already. Riki has a girly voice as usual...I think the same person who usually does young boys voices him (Young Yuichi Aizawa from Kanon). Hilary Haag does...alright...as Saya Tokido. That whiny voice really shows when she does over the top lines (when they were scaling down the pyramind). There were a couple lines she shouted that I could not understand leaving me to say "what?" It's a really typical Hilary Haagish voice. Although she does dramatic lines really well. Saya's arc in the end made me teary eyed but that's it. Sasami's arc is the next two episodes. Her voice sounds good too...then...I heard Kud's voice... THEY FLIPPIN GAVE HER A RUSSIAN ACCENT!!!!!!! WHAT?!!!!! IT SOUNDS...no comment. It just threw me off. I knew what Rin, Komari and Yuiko sounded like from English promos but this was the first time I heard Kud's, Mio's, Haruka's voices in English. Haruka sounds very Peppermint Patty or a female character from Franklin the Turtle series... -_- This is why I don't watch English dubs. I have such high hopes only to disappointed just cuz my preferences want something better. Anyways... without spoiling Sasami's story...I balled my eyes out in the end. I cry at the end of episode 6 every single time I see this. Kanata's arc is just meh. Unlike the previous two, there are no supernatural elements to toss the story around, it is purely slice-of-life. Those of you who missed seeing the Little Busters all together doing missions like in the first season will surely enjoy these episodes because they are somewhat important in these episodes instead of having no lines in Saya's and Sasami's stories. The only thing I hate about Kanata's story is that sick, twisted family gets brought up again...but I'll get over it. Basically it's just a continuation of Haruka's story from season 1. Kanata's English voice...sounds very butch. With that I mean she sounds like she can play Riki's voice and come off as a guy. Overall, I'm more than happy that EX got an English release. That's all I've asked for from Sentai Filmworks for the past two years and my wish came true. Really, this is a great early Christmas gift to myself. I probably won't watch the English dub again though. One thing I really want to gripe on is the TV I was watching this on. I hope its just because of this TV's screen ratio, BUT I was disappointed that at the very end of episode 8, Saya was cropped out of the group picture... I need to rewatch this on my laptop or my TV at home to see if it was just the ratio aspect...but it's a really great scene showing all the Little Busters, Saya, Sasami ans Kanata all together. To recap, EX is a great follow-up to the two seasons of Little Busters and can be considered a love letter to the fans who wanted the EX routes adapted on screen. Saya's story is hands down the best out of the three stories, making you shed a little tear, Sasami's story will have you balling your eyes out especially if you love animals. Kanata's didn't have me feel anything but I still love her character and seeing the Little Busters go on missions to help their friends out is always fun. Thanks for reading this review and pick up this set if you watched the first two seasons!

history.title: Sailor Moon S:S3Pt1 (DVD)
history.text: The S Season is arguably the best of the five seasons of Sailor Moon and probably the darkesr with its themes of the Apocalypse and Sacrifice. The Outer Guardians appear for the first time (except Pluto who briefly appeared in R) and they steal the spotlight every time they're in screen! It looks like ViZ media is going for a "rainbow" theme with these chipboard boxsets. Season 1 was pink, season 2 orange and now we have yellow for season 3. By the looks of it, SuperS will be green and Stars blue. I like it! For those of you who preordered this Bluray/DVD Combo pack on rightstuf.com you'll also get an exclusive Cosmic Heart Compact coin! I think its cheaper there than Amazon. I preordered this back in July the day it was announced at the official Sailor Moon panel at Anime Expo and got a special screening of the English episodes "The Rod of Love is Born! Usagi's New Transformation, A Beautiful Boy? The Secret of Haruka Tenno" and "Bond of Destiny! The Distant Days of Uranus!" As far as what I've seen, the new voice actresses for Uranus, Neptune, Kaolinite (who did Usagi's mom and Temari from Naruto) sound great!! Special mentions go to Keith Silverstein who plays Professor Tomoe! He's one of my favorite voice actors and he's such a great guy too! The veteran's Stephanie Sheh, Michelle Ruff and Robbie Daymond all sound great and bring the characters to life too! I can't wait tk hear Christie-Marie Cabanos when she does Hotaru's voice in the next half of the series. Sob, that'll be such a long wait!! This uncut version will do this series justice unlike the previous Pioneer releases. I mean, I live that Pioneer used the original cover art and that they had English Subtitles for the Japanese voices, BUT they completed omitted the first and second opening songs and only used the third one throughout, spoiling Hotaru Tomoe's appearance much earlier in the series as well as hinting Super Sailor Moon is the messiah (she flies with butterflies and purges the dark clouds making way for light to come through). They also CUT the next episode previews. They were labeled "ORIGINAL UNCUT VERSION" but making edits like this doesn't say "uncut" in my book. But now with VIZ rereleasing the entire series, that shouldn't be a problem anymore. I can't wait to own the first part if this set this November, as well as the usual special art booklet and coin! Back when I became a Sailor Moon fan in 2005, it sucked because there was nothing! Sailor Moon's license in America had expired, the Tokyopop manga and DVD's were pulled from shelves and no one shared the same interest. Now is definitely the perfect time to be a Sailor Moon fan, with Kodansha's new English manga, its 20th anniversary, all the new products and merchandise appearing in Japan and American stores like Hot Topic and Barnes and Noble, ViZ media's acquisition on the license, the fan clubs and the new Sailor Moon Crystal anime! Sailor Moon is back and here to stay! "Crisis! Make Up!!"

history.title: The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya: Seasons 1 & 2 [DVD]
history.review_title: GREAT Re-release of one if anime's most popular franchises!!
history.text: I bought this at Fry's Electronics and I am absolutely happy with this product. Since Bandai's rights to the series expired a while back, finding complete sets of seasons 1 and season 2 and the movie were difficult! You wouldn't believe the crazy prices people and scalpers have been selling these for online! I own the Bandai set but I did not own season 2 until now. I'm glad Funimation decided to release all 28 episodes at once instead of dividing the seasons into two separate sets (really...would Endless Eight sell separately??). The DVD cover art uses the Anime Legends art from Bandai's season 2 set and the reversible cover is the Regular Edition of Volume 0 released in Japan. The disc art also takes the artwork from the Limited Edition DVDs from Japan for seasons 1 and 2. I watched the Sigh Arc already and I don't notice any frame issues. Everything looks great even for DVD quality. Funimation has the on screen text and Japanese subtitles at the top and bottom if the screen in a way that it does not obscure the image like Bandai's release. I notice the next episode previews are gone but I think they are included in the Extras disc. Speaking of Extras, I did not have the time to look through all of em yet. I'm assuming they're the same extras seen on Bandai's releases. I know the regular Bluray and the Limited Bluray sets come with 5 hours worth of bonus content though as opposed to this one's being 4 hours less. Anyways, I got this just to be able to own Season 2 and I couldn't be happier with this product. This is one of a rare select of anime titles where I watch the English dub. I love the English dubs to this and Lucky★Star! Crispin Freeman's voice as Kyons, Wendee Lee playing Haruhi, Stephanie Sheh as Mikuru, Michelle Ruff as Yuki and Johnny Yong Bosch as Koizumi. They're all great voice actors who play voices in multiple anime and video games and they really bring the characters to life. One small gripe I have is the simple cover art. I know the title name-drops the central character, I thought a little more creativity could've been used besides using Season 2's art and throwing it over a plain red background. But I gueas this is okay because there are too many group photos of cover art featuring many characters. What makes up for this is what I mentioned earlier: Funimation using Volume 0 of the Japanese Regular Edition as the reversible cover art. I flipped it around to that on my DVD because that just happens to be one of my favorite cover artworks, featuring Waitress Mikuru Asahina agaibst Witch Yuki Nagato. This is unmistakably a must-have for any hardcore anime collector. I totally reccommend it. However, if you don't have $35 to spare for the DVD version (Bluray is $55 and the Limited Edition Bluray is $139!!) wait for Funimation to release a S.A.V.E. version of this...if they're still doing that. But if you're an anime fan this show is one not to be missed. It was extremely popular with its original light novel series in Japan and is beautifully animated by Kyoto Animation, the studio responsible for shows like AIR, Kanon, CLANNAD, Free! and Full Metal Panic. It blends a bit of every genre into one and its funny and has a nice, casual feel, taking place in a high school setting yet being totally sci-fi at the same time. Haruhi Suzumiya has been an iconic character in the world of anime and in my opinion, her popularity continues to grow! Buy this set! You won't be disappointed and it's worth every penny spent!

history.title: Stephen King's The Shining (Two Disc Special Edition)
history.review_title: Annoying brat needs to be punished.
history.text: Terrible CGI hedge animals. Check. Seeing a hornets nest and make a stupid decision to try and grab it. Check. Stupid, annoying characters. Check. This mini-series was utterly boring and stupid. I watched it as a freshman seven years ago. I decided to watch it again because all I remembered were the hedge animals, the hornets nest and the grotesque woman in the bathtub singing "Old mac donald." Danny is such an annoying brat and reminds me why I don't have kids yet. The way he speaks is annoying, his ugly hairstyle and his inability to follow simple orders and expects to be forgiven. AND his constantly repeating "It's just pictures in a book" make me cringe and adds to the sheer level of disgust I feel for that pustule. No wonder the father wants to beat the crap out of him, I was hoping to see it. And the wife is just another stereotypical clueless house wife who tries to keep an otherwise disfunctioning family under control with ridiculous results. Give this garbage a pass. The effects are bad and the characters are unlikeable and you feel no sympathy for these stupid people. The characters and actors in the original 1980 Kubrick films may have been ugly but at least they had some charm and they weren't as unlikeable as the cast in this terrible remake.

history.title: My Little Pony Friendship Is Magic: Exploring The Crystal Empire
history.review_title: How many "Theme DVD's" will Hasbro dish out?
history.text: Wow! This is a great DVD! I started seeing it at Target. It contains two 2-parters, the Season 5 finale, "The Cutie-Remark Parts 1 and 2," the Season 6 opener, "The Crystalling Parts 1 and 2" and finally the episode "The Times they are a Changeling." I think its the 2nd Crystal Empire themed DVD. Now I know y'all adults probably think themed DVD's are pointless and would just wait for the season box sets, but Hasbro has to sell DVDs to the target audience, little girls, so they're always going to dish out themed DVD'S no matter what. The thing is, I've always had a problem with the themed DVD's, in that a handful of them don't have a themed episode centering around the theme the DVD is about. Make sense? An example I'll give is the 3rd official Mlp fis DVD, "Adventures in the Crystal Empire." Sure it had the season 3 opening, "The Crystal Empire," but the other 3 episodes? Not so much. We get a Rainbow Dash episode (probably best to be on the Dash of Awesome DVD), the Princess Luna episode (...prooooobably best to be on the Spooktacular stories DVD...oh wait, I think it is!) And the "It's about time" episode (huh?). I thought they could've put the "Games Ponies Play" episode there...BUT they placed it on the Princess Twilight Sparkle DVD. The Princess Twilight Sparkle DVD carries the same problem. We get that one episode where she becomes a Princess...and in my opinion, SHOULD have come with the Season 4 opener "Princess Twilight Sparkle Parts 1 and 2!" How awesome would that DVD have been? It would make sense since Season 4 hasn't aired yet I think but still...we get a crystal empire themed episode, a Trixie episode, which is alright, a detective episode which was more about Pinkie Pie than Twilight Sparkle, AND a repackaged episode "Lesson Zero" that can be found bundled with the Wedding Playful Ponies Brushables wave. In fact, I don't think the Season 4 openers have been issued on a themed DVD yet. The "Keys of Friendship" DVD is one I actually own and even reviewed here on Amazon. I thought it could have been perfect if they included the Applejack and Pinkie Pie "Key" episodes instead of putting the random "Pinkie Apple Pie" there. You get my point though, right? The only perfect DVD Hasbro put out in my opinion was the "Royal Pony Wedding" DVD. It had great episodes. The epic Canterlot Wedding episodes, "Sweet and Elite (shares the celebration theme with Twilight Sparkle's Birthday), "Hearts and Hooves Day (shares the wedding/trying to get two ponies to love each other plot)" and "The Best Night Ever (the great Season 2 finale, piggybacking off of the Canterlot Wedding celebration theme). This "Exploring the Crystal Empire" seems to be the newest DVD in the themed MLP DVD's line and if you ask me, Starlight Glimmer should be the focus...so why is she not on the cover? There were many themed DVD'S released since "The Friendship Express" and I've stopped collecting em after "Keys of Friendship." I own: - The Friendship Expess - Celebration at Canterlot - Adventures in Ponyville - Royal Pony Wedding - Princess Twilight Sparkle - Pinkie Pie Party and - Keys of Friendship Overall, I'm happy Hasbro tried with this DVD since every episode is indeed a "Crystal Empire" one, well...except the "Cutie Re-mark" but it still makes an appearance in it. Its just weird how Hasbro released 2 Crystal Empire DVDs and 2 Scary story themed DVDs. Since I have Netflix, I see no reason to spend $9 on this DVD. Only if your a collector, I'd reccomend it. Or else, just collect the season sets. Kids will probably enjoy the sing-along and forgive Starlight Glimmer's corruption. Hope this helps!

history.title: My Little Pony Friendship Is Magic: Royal Pony Wedding
history.text: Out of all the Friendship is Magic DVDs Hasbro dished out, they actually got this one right. We get the 2-part Season 2 finale "A Canterlot Wedding" which is one if the greatest stories in FiM, the Rarity episode, "Sweet and Elite" which carries on the celebration theme, celebrating Twilight Sparkle's Birthday, "Hearts and Hooves Day," a Cutie Mark Crusader episode that still shares the wedding theme of trying to have a couple hook-up, and finally "The Best Night Ever," the great Season 1 finale which is as good as "A Canterlot Wedding" and also shares the celebration theme. Not many special features. Just 2 sing-alongs and coloring sheets. I will point out the only two 1 star reviewers here. Uh, just what part of these episodes is dark and violent? There's not even any blood in this and its no darker than a Disney Movie. You crazy, sensitive parents have a really warped idea of what "scary" and "violence" really is, smh. If you can't even expose your children to a TV Y rated batch of episodes, what do you expose them to? Give me a break.

history.title: Sailor Moon S Part 2 (Season 3) (combo pack) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Another solid release from ViZ Media
history.text: As June comes in, here we have Sailor Moon S Part 2 Bluray/DVD Combo pack. I think this release was a shorter wait than Sailor Moon R Part 2 which is a good thing. As with the past Sailor Moon releases by ViZ media, I'll be comparing some good and bad in this release. Minor spoilers ahead, but I expect only fans of the series who have watched it already in subs and the Cloverway dub will read this. I also won't get into the plot because everyone should know it by now. If not, look online. I will only be reviewing the product. The box art is nice, continuing the yellow background used in S Part 1. Pictured is an S image if all 10 Guardians I've seen on a previously released binder as I expected I totally knew theywere going to use this image...). Same with the reversible image, utilizing a shot of all 10 Sailor Guardians. ViZ also distributed this image as a poster and post card during AX 2016 and Otakon 2016 so I have a lot of copies. Disc 1 has an image of Super Sailor Moon, Disc 2 Sailor Chibi-Moon and Disc 3 Sailor Saturn. This pattern goes for the Blu-Rays and DVD's. Bonus features include a standard art gallery, textless opening and ending, trailers and cast interviews. I have only seen the Keith Silverstein interview (he plays Professor Tomoe and Kenji Tsukino) but there are more such as a commentary and some convention stuff. If you really want, I'll reviewthe bonus features and rewrite them in this review. Now for the episodes. Obviously this set has the remaining episodes for the S season, starting out with "A time of shock! Secret Identities revealed to one another." As you can tell the series is halfway through and picking the plot up strong, showing the talismans, Sailor Pluto's return, the remaining Witches 5 and of course Sailor Saturn and Hotaru Tomoe's mystery. As usual, the English cast does a solid performance, sticking close to the original Japanese dialogue with minor changes here and there. Cristie-Marie Cabanos is amazing as Hotaru Tomoe/Mistress 9/Sailor Saturn. It takes a talented voice actress to play three characters' alternate personalities at once and she was great going from a cute, frail little girl to a menacing, evil she-demon, to a firm, solitary guardian. I had my doubts hearing her as the title character on Puella Magi Madoka Magica but rest assured, she did a great job (not that she did a bad performance in Madoka, I just didn't think her voice would fit Saturn's character). Funny how she and Cristina Vee (Sailor Mars) are nearly in everything together? ;) As for the other voices, Keith Silverstein as Professor Tomoe nails it compared to Jeff Lumby's voice in the Cloverway dub. Keith is one of my favorite voice actors I regularly follow on social media and I met him a couple times. He's a great, talented guy and when I first heard him do Tomoe's voice is the first S trailer and he did his menacing laugh, it sent chills down my spine! As for the Witches 5, I'm not sure what happened. Besides Eudial's deeper voice courtesy of Erin Fitzgerald, the remaining Witches 5, Mimete, Tellu, Viluy and Cyprine all sound the same and pretty boring. That's not to say they didn't to a good job portraying their characters, its just that there's no way to distinguish who is who. Cloverway's dub was good at portraying their voices. Eudial/Eugeal had a whiny, "I'm the boss" voice, Mimete/Mimet had a really strange, bimbo voice matching an idol-has-been that wasn't really high, Tellu/Telulu had a deep, sexy, but oddly older voice, Viluy/Byruit had a snobbish, valley girl voice and Cyprine and Ptilol had a haunting, creepy voice...if that makes sense. An example I'll give is the scream Cyprine and Ptilol make as they were vaporized by each other's attacks. The scream we hear in the new ViZ dub was just one generic scream that didn't linger. Cloverway's dub, they screamed for a while and we were able to notice a certain gasped-out linger which was great, showing thay dying by vaporizing is painful! And because of the similar sounding, generic women voices in the ViZ dub, it makes it hard to remember what kind of voice Tellu, Viluy and Cyprine had, whereas in the Cloverway dub, they each had a unique voice. Yes it sticks to the script, but I sorta missed Tellu's deep voice and Viluy being a snobby bitch to everyone. Guess they're just the Nostalgia goggles talking... -_- Other than that, the main cast do well for what they were given, especially Johnny-Yong Bosch as Artemis and Robbie Daymond as Tuxedo Mask who don't get much screentime this season. When the comedy is there, the voice actors and actresses deliver the lines right. When its dark and serious, especially during the final battle its all there and sounds fitting. One episode worth mentioning is "A Bright Shooting Star! Saturn and the Messiah." I can't tell which dubbed episode I like more, Cloverways or ViZ? Cabanos like I said portrayed Mistress 9 well, but the woman who did her voice in the Cloverway dub was very convincing! During the line when Hotaru was trying to take control of her body, she even added gasped chokes, when saying "This body is rejecting me! Remove yourself! REMOVE YOURSELF!!" It helps by the fact that that was the most accurate, dubbed episode Cloverway has ever gotten when comparing to its original Japanese one, meaning it wasn't a Lisa-Lumby Richards episode. She did the movies and directed numerous, poor episodes with bad dialogue -_- but I'll move on to picture quality before I get ahead of myself...bur first...shout outs definitely go to Stephanie Sheh as Sailor Moon who is able to sound convincing especially during the dark moment where she was trying to perform Moon Crisis Make Up. I instantly got chills and emotional as I heard how desperate she was trying to transform to save Sailor Saturn just like in the Japanese version, so bravo to Ms. Sheh! Returning to Keith Silverstein as Professor Tomoe, I was surprised that he kept his creepy scientist voice even after he was free of Germatoid the male daimon. I assumed he would use his Kenji Tsukino voice but I think its for the better. Picture quality. Ah, this. One of ViZ's most harsh criticisms when it comes to the Sailor Moon releases. I'm watching the Blurays on an old LG screen since I moved and my other TV is in storage. When sitting far away, the quality is...good at best. The lines are sharp and the colors are bright...but when sitting closer, you can see all the grain and ghosting. This is the only complaint I have because we should have the perfect Bluray transfers from Japan that Italy has received -_- Come on. The R Movie Bluray looks nice, so why can't we have it? If I were going to buy the Bluray/DVD combo set, I'd buy from Rightstuf.com because its cheaper than Amazon and they send bonus cards featuring the heroes and the Death Busters which is always nice. That wraps up my review for ViZ Media's Sailor Moon S Part 2 Bluray/DVD Combo pack! Hope it was helpful! --Sailor Orthos
