history.review_title: Wonderful entertainment for all ages and conditions
history.text: Excellent acting by all, nice sets, pleasant music, you know what’s going to happen but it’s all heart-warming anyway. It takes place during the Christmas holidays, and one of the characters may be an angel, but the religious aspects are soft-pedaled. There is simply nothing in this movie that can offend anyone, and lots that can please everyone. I didn’t notice any rating, but it is suitable for a child of any age and his/her parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents. I do have one reservation, though it doesn’t affect my rating. The male lead is super rich – mansion, butler, maids – so money is never an issue. For many people, money is an issue, and watching the lifestyle of the super rich can be off-putting. But hey, this is a fantasy, and a lovely one at that, so don’t let that bother you. Highly recommended.

I am willing to suspend disbelief within reason for a good story. But there is a limit, and this movie exceeds it from the beginning. An executive is being transferred from Florida to Minnesota to take over the running of a factory. She arrives at the airport in Minnesota with a huge amount of heavy luggage all of which she lifts by herself from the carousel and swings onto a cart. In the real world, she would arrive with one bag with sufficient stuff for a few days, while her company shipped the rest of her stuff to their office in Minnesota from which it would be delivered to her hotel. If for some reason she had to have all that stuff right away, for a few dollars she could have a porter transfer her baggage from the carousel to a cart and from the cart to her rental car. It is inconceivable that a corporate executive, a relatively small woman, would do all that heavy work by herself. Then she arrives in Minnesota in the wintertime without a coat. Really? She didn’t know where Minnesota is on the map and that it gets bitterly cold there in winter? She doesn’t know how to look up weather reports in a destination city and doesn’t have an assistant who knows? Are screen writers an extinct species? I’m sorry, but this was all so absurd that I stopped watching at this point.

Amazon left one little fact out: the entire narration is in German! When someone is speaking in English or Italian, he or she is overdubbed by a German translator. I have enough German to follow most of it, but shouldn't a film directed at an American audience mention that it's not in English?

history.review_title: A great film; everyone should see it
history.text: A terrific reconstruction of the convention which determined the structure of the new nation's government. The Faustian bargain whereby the southern colonies voted for independence as long as their slaves remained their property has been called the original sin of the American nation, and its effects are still felt. Should Franklin and Jefferson et al have made that agreement? Or should they have chosen instead to form a smaller nation without slavery? Or even have remained British? Those are issues which, it seems, will never be resolved to everyone's satisfaction, but they are made dramatically clear in this fine film. As for the music, there is less of it than I had anticipated, and while it fits the time and place well enough, you don't finish the film humming any of the melodies. But it doesn't get in the way of the drama, either, and helps in delineating the different characters of this large, almost entirely male cast. In the end, all my reservations are minor; this is a wonderful film that every American should see - and foreigners could learn a lot about our country if they watched it too.

The scenery is gorgeous. Gwyneth Paltrow is beautiful. The American is a slob, unshaved, uncombed, sloppily dressed – and a thief to boot, stealing mss from the London Library (of which I used to be a member). The story is virtually non-existent, the parallelism with a Victorian couple forced and unbelievable. The mood is sad throughout. It's even sad when Paltrow offers to have sex with the American; incredibly, he declines because, as he later says, he didn't want to spoil things. Most men would welcome the opportunity to spoil things with Gwyneth Paltrow. Sad.

history.title: Smiles Of A Summer Night (The Criterion Collection)
history.text: A comedy? Perhaps by the standards of Sweden in 1955, since no one actually commits suicide, they’re just miserable and only one actually tries to kill himself (but fails). During most of the film everybody is unhappy, though everybody is fabulously rich (except, of course, for the servants who serve them – and service them). A sommelier serving wine with dinner at home? Certainly not; the sommelier only carries one bottle as he leads a troop of wine carriers, each with a bottle, around one per dinner guest, into the dining room. In other words, these are the trials and tribulations of the almost unimaginably rich in their servant-run castles. If you like to watch such-like at play, agonizing over what dress to wear to the theater or whether to consummate her marriage with her husband or instead with his son, this is for you. But I doubt even you will get many laughs over this alleged comedy.

This is an infomercial for Chez Panisse in Berkeley, CA, where dinner this Saturday will cost you $125 per person not including wine. You can wash it down with a Spanish bubbly for $12 a glass (you can buy a bottle of Freixenet Brut in my Safeway for $10); a bottle of rosé will cost you $45 to $96; or you can bring your own wine for a corkage fee of $35 a bottle. Extras and tips are not included, so if you can buy dinner for two for less than $400 you can consider yourself lucky. If you can’t eat at Chez Panisse but, poor wretch, must make do with what’s on offer at your local supermarket, then you are inviting diabetes and any number of other modern chronic diseases which result from our awful food production and distribution system. The stars of this infomercial, especially Alice Waters the patronne of Chez Panisse, are portrayed as back-to-nature anti-Vietnam flowery-dress types who disdain the filthy lucre that keeps capitalism going. Sorry there’s no rating below 1-star.

I totally agree with the reviewers who found this series to be awful, unwatchable. Where I disagree is where they say it is not up to Woody Allen’s usual standard or where they blame Miley Cyrus. In the 1-and-a-half episodes I suffered through, I thought it was entirely up to Allen’s standard, in fact it was indistinguishable from everything else he’s ever done, the same neurotic, whiney, sniveling little nebbish he's always played. My father was a captain in World War II, my mother’s brother a full colonel, they would have had nothing but contempt for such a character and would have assumed, since he is always depicted as Jewish, that it was written by a raging anti-Semite – his shtick is in fact a virtual caricature of what you will find in traditional anti-Semitic literature. (Lest I be guilty of contributing to this caricature by mentioning that Allen is Jewish, as if anyone didn’t know - he makes a big thing of it – let me mention some other Jewish actors: Dustin Hoffman, Leonard Nimoy, William Shatner, Tony Curtis (born Bernard Schwartz), Edward G. Robinson (Emanuel Goldenberg), Kirk Douglas (Isur Danilavich Dzemski), Harrison Ford (Jewish mother), or Paul Newman (Jewish father). Can anyone imagine any of these actors playing the Allen character? In fact, though I grew up in a Jewish neighborhood, and in fact went to the same high school in Brooklyn as Allen (he graduated a year after I did), I never met anyone like the character he plays. In fact, I can't think of any Jewish person like that character. Leonard Bernstein? Georg Solti? General Sharon? General Dayan? Fah.) As for Miley Cyrus, or Elaine May, it is unfair to place any of the blame on them. This is an Allen production, written by him as a vehicle for him to play his standard character yet one more time. This series, at least what I watched of it (and other reviewers say it gets worse), is simply appalling and the likelihood that Allen was well paid for it is a disgrace. If he doesn’t know it’s time to quit and find a sound-proof room where he can play his clarinet, it’s past time for his paymasters to tell him.

history.review_title: Don't pay attention to what these people say, pay attention to what they do
history.text: This purports to be an examination of the status and future of print media, so it starts off with rapidly moving images of talking heads and children using digital machines, lights flashing in our faces, and then, when someone actually starts talking, what he’s saying is made difficult to hear by loud background music. In other words, the people who made this movie aren’t the solution, they’re the problem.

history.title: The Thomas Crown Affair
history.text: A travesty of a heist movie. I sought it out because I knew Michel Legrand had composed the score. I have been collecting his music for many years, still have the original vinyl records I bought in France a half century ago. But I cannot agree with the people who find fault with the plot. There is no plot. A heist at the beginning, which is just short, or maybe not short, of ridiculous, then Faye Dunaway in one ravishing outfit after the other and the attitude of a Sam Spade, but nothing makes any sense at all. Even the R rating is ridiculous; today it would surely not be rated more than a PG-13, perhaps just a plain PG – the sex, and the movie is largely about sex, involves no nudity, in fact no sex, just, well, chess. I used to play tournament chess, yet never played anybody who looked or dressed like Faye Dunaway. I guess I played in the wrong places. Am I rambling? If I am, then this review fits this movie perfectly.

history.title: Tremors 5: Bloodlines
history.review_title: TECHNICALLY WELL MADE WITH MUCH BETTER CGI, BUT DOESN'T HAVE THAT OLD TREMORS CHARM!
history.text: I'm a fan of the Tremors films, I even liked Back to Perfection regardless of the horrible CGI work and if they had used practical effects more in that film, I think it would have been better received. Bloodlines uses a lot of CGI, but it is much better this time around. Unfortunately they lost the charm associated with these films somewhere, it just doesn't feel like a Tremors sequel. The effects are well done, but the new reimagined monsters are uninspired and borrow elements of Predator, Blade and too many other creatures in other films. I think what worked in the other Tremors films is that the creatures were more original, but that being said, it is interesting how these creatures evolve with each film. Technical this is a well made film, but for me it just wasn't very fun, maybe after repeat viewings I'll warm up to it, I own all of the movies including this one so I will watch it again the next time I'm in the mood for a complete Tremors franchise fix. I have heard rumors of a 6th film coming with Bacon returning, If this is true I can only hope that they will return to the tone that made the Tremors films so enjoyable. It's not a total lose, but if part 3 had CGI that was this convincing, then that film would be way better than this one. As it is, it's worth a look for fans, but keep your expectations very low. I'd give it 2 stars, too bad because it certainly could have been one of the better sequels.

history.title: The Natural: Director's Cut
history.review_title: A MISSED OPPORTUNITY! POINTLESS DIRECTER'S CUT RELEASE!
history.text: The Natural has been criticized for being too predictable, not following the original book and a director's cut of the film could have been a perfect way to remedy this or at least put all of the controversy to rest. Unfortunately it is not. Unfortunately the directer's cut adds very little to the story and for the most part clutters the storytelling, if this version had changed the tone of the film used original ending in the book, then I could see this being an interesting release, but it doesn't so it ends up being a lesser version of the theatrical release. The bonus features almost make this worth the upgrade, but without the original theatrical version of the film being included. I just can't recommend this release at all. I like this movie a lot, it has a few small quirks, but overall it is a movie that is entertaining and I have watched it many times. I have never read the book, but watching the bonus features and doing a bit of research I can understand fully why some could take a disliking to this film. The film turns the original dark and depressing tale into a inspiring redemption tale. For me, the way this film is laid out the original ending wouldn't have worked. The film would have had to be completely reworked to fit the tone of the book. I enjoy all types of films, so I'm no stranger to less conventional endings. I just can't see how the original ending would have worked using the direction chosen by the screen writers. Maybe they should have changed the title of the movie so that fans of the book wouldn't have compared it to the book? If you're interested in owning the film, buy the Blu Ray release which includes all of the extras from both DVD releases, much improved visual and audio, but uses the theatrical release in place of the inferior directer's cut. The Blu Ray can be found on the 2 disc double feature with A League of Their Own, both films include all the extras from their single released Blu Rays at a bargain price in a space saving case.

history.title: Ben (Bluray/DVD Combo) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: BEN FINALLY MAKES ITS DEBUT ON BLU RAY, BUT WITH ORIGINAL NEGATIVE LOST THE TRANSFER LEAVES A BIT TO BE DESIRED!
history.text: In 1971, I saw a trailer for Willard, it was a film that would be forever etched in my mind, while not nearly as good as it wanted to be or I want it to be, it did have its charms and with the help of Bruce Davison the title character became part of horror folklore. Why am I taking about Willard you ask? Well, I remember when Ben the sequel to Willard was released in theaters and I also remember how awful it was. No Davison, no Borgnine and no Locke was like stripping Jaws of Shaw, Dreyfuss and Scheider by comparison, leaving Ben with very little human interest and some goofy rat nonsense to fill the void. Between the silly rat melodrama and some familiar character actors giving their hammiest performances Ben feels more like a parody to Willard than a sequel with the worst qualities of Willard being exaggerated. Silly to the point of so much unintentional laughter in what truly feels like a bad TV movie of the week. Ben comes to Blu Ray for the first time and had only seen a VHS release prior. this is great news regardless of my disappointment in the film itself. This release has it's share of disappoints as well. With the original negative lost, Shout Factory has given us the best transfer possible I believe. All things considered it looks pretty good, having watched it immediately after the Willard Blu Ray, it is quite a downgrade in quality, but it is also the best it has ever looked on home video. I wish they had released Willard and Ben on a double feature Blu Ray and ditched the DVD's altogether or had a separate release for the DVDs. I ended up buying Ben anyway, but it will be a film I seldom revisit. The Blu Ray features an audio commentary with the star Lee Montgomery, 31 photo stills gallery, a brief (9 minute) on screen interview with the star, Ben and Willard and Ben double feature trailers (A Highlight!) and radio spots. It's about as good a release as one could hope for and a long time coming for fans of the film. If you like this film, this is certainly worth picking up, but keep your expectations in check as the transfer is not nearly as appealing as Willard's.

history.title: Willard
history.review_title: JUST ANOTHER SO-SO REMAKE WITH A GOOD DVD RELEASE! 2 1/2 STARS!
history.text: With the original Willard and Ben finally being released on Blu Ray/DVD, I decided to revisit the remake of Willard with Crispin Glover. Going back to when I first heard about this film was being made and hearing of the casting of Crispin Glover as the title character, I had high hopes. I thought Glover was a wise choice and someone who fit the role perfectly. While I enjoyed the film the first time around, it had its share of disappointments. Watching the film now, I liked it a little less and still think the original is far superior. The remake doesn't allow Willard to really evolve, he is creepy from the moment he is first seen on screen. In fact almost everyone is a bit creepy, Mr Martin, his secretary, Willard's mother and or course the rats. I prefer the set up in the original, where Willard stubbles across the rats and makes friends instead of going to the basement to exterminate them. The best part about the remake are the rats, the rats are the star and for the most part are convincing as threats. In the original there never seemed to be enough of them to really keep someone from getting away with only a few nasty bites. There is a bit of overkill here though, Willard is submerged in an elevator full of thousands of rats on his way up to see Mr Martin for their big show down. It's just too much and pretty cartoonish. I also found the scene where Willard puts Chloe the cat in the house with the rats to be out of place and spoiled the tone of the film with it's video montage of the song Ben. The ending is different and not in a good way, oddly enough they changed the ending before it was released which followed the original films ending. I think it was more appropriate, but I suppose they were hoping to make a sequel if this film had done well at the box office. The DVD release is very good though, with lots of deleted scenes, commentary and music video and a few interesting lengthy feature-ettes. It is a flipper disc with widescreen on one side and full screen on the other. This remake isn't a total loss, but hardly an upgrade to the original.

history.title: The King of Queens: Season 1
history.review_title: GREAT SHOW! SLOPPY MENU AND EPISODES ARE NOT IN THE CORRECT ORDER!
history.text: King of Queens is one of the few shows that holds up watching it a decade later. James is comic gold and Leah Remini is the perfect counter part to his good natured buffoon antics. If that weren't enough, Jerry Stiller as Carrie's live-in father is there to add some chaos to the already hilarious mix. It's amazing how early on the three main characters have such great chemistry, Chello Goodbye is a favorite early episode (number 3) and shows just how good these actors work together. The silent fight at the Chello concert is both brilliant and hilarious. The episodes look very good, but I would love to see a more compact Blu Ray release of the complete series. There are some extras mostly on the last disc, but the biggest complaint with this set is that the episodes are not in the running order as they aired. It's extremely frustrating to have to look on line and figure out how to toggle back and forth between menu pages and in some cases actually have to put another disc in to watch the correct episode and then have to return to the previous disc to continue. The menu design is awful, confusing and sloppy. 5 stars for the series 2 star deduction for the horrible menu. Please release this show on Blu Ray with a smart menu design and save us all some valuable shelf space and a huge headache. 9 seasons of King of Queens takes up a lot of space on DVD.

history.title: Ray Harryhausen Collection + BD Live (20 Million Miles to Earth, Earth vs. Flying Saucers, It Came from Beneath the Sea, 7th Voyage of Sinbad) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A MUST BUY FOR HARRYHAUSEN FANS! NICE TRANSFERS AND HOURS OF BONUS MATERIAL!
history.text: I’ve been a Ray Harryhausen fan ever since I was big enough to reach the knob (and UHF dial for those old enough to remember that) on our 19 inch black & white TV set. At the time (the early 60’s) I wasn’t aware of who Ray was, but I knew the difference between stop motion monsters and guy in a rubber suit monsters. I always preferred stop motion to the latter and by the time I was 7 or 8 I had become familiar with the man known to me as Harryhausen. I would search the TV guide weekly to see what new treasures would be coming on Saturday mornings and afternoon. At the time, stop motion films on TV were limited to Kong Kong, Son of Kong, Mighty Joe Young, The Beast from 20,000 Fathoms, It Came from Beneath the Sea, Earth VS The Flying Saucers, 20 Million Miles to Earth, The Beast from Hollow Mountain and maybe a few more that I can’t recall at this moment. I was also lucky enough to see The 7th Voyage of Sinbad and Jack the Giant Killer on a double bill matinee at my local theater. They would run films that were a few years old for a mere 15 cents or 25 cents for a double feature. At the time I thought that Jack the Giant Killer was also the work of Harryhausen because of the similar design of the creatures and fantasy story. I also saw Jason and the Argonauts and One Million Years B.C. in that same theater. Having a theater that showed these old films enabled me to see many pictures I would have missed on the big screen, several early Godzilla films, Hammer Horror films, The Gorgon, Hammer’s Curse, Revenge and The Evil of Frankenstein films and many others. I have owned Harryhausen’s films on VHS, DVD and now Blu Ray and I have never regretted a single purchase. Okay, now for the product review, Its hard for me to review a Harryhausen product without going into a little personal history first. Ray Harryhausen, Jack Pierce and Walt Disney probably influenced me through film more than any others. This Blu Ray box set contains 4 of Ray’s early works with Charles H. Schneer, It Came From Beneath The Sea, Earth VS The Flying Saucers, 20 Million Miles To Earth and The 7th Voyage Of Sinbad. Each film comes in their own individual case with cover art that coincides with the film within. The 3 black & white films have the colorization option carried over from the previous DVD editions. I am not a fan pf colorization, but Mr. Harryhause over saw the project and he was happy with the results, so it is hard for me to argue with the inclusion of that option. If the original black & while versions of the films were not included there would be hell to pay! Truth be told, I enjoy watching the films in color, the colorization process is done very well overall, sure sometimes the skin tone of the actors is a bit artificial looking but in general we watch these films for the fantastic creatures created by the incomparable Master of Majicks. The Blu Ray transfers of the first three films excluding The Sinbad film all look very impressive on Blu Ray, they all come with a wealth of bonus features including commentary, feature-ettes, onscreen interviews with Mr. Harryhausen, Stills Gallery, digital comic book etc. I really couldn’t be happier with these three titles. All three films are every entertaining and have been part of my life for close to 5 decade. The 7th Voyage of Sinbad Blu Ray looks better than ever here and any grievances come from the original source material and not a lack of effort. The film looks very good, but it is inconsistent. This was Ray;s first color film and unfortunately the effects process is enhanced by Blu Rays ultra high resolution. I really have no problem with this transfer, but I can see why some have rated this title lower than it deserves because they expected the impossible. There is no way to make this film look like a new film made in these times. Back plates, adjusting for color film,type of film, lighting, there are so many factors in the inconsistencies of this film. I think what stings a bit is this is one of Rays most beloved films it not the most beloved. The creatures have influenced generations of filmmakers and monster kids since the film came out in 1958, so a sparkling flawless transfer was in all of our dreams. There are times when the film reaches the level of detail we expect, then there times when the long shots just look flat, one good plus is the creatures look great, especially in close ups \, The the Cyclops face shots are a big Wow! moment. This edition also has a wealth of features so I am not complaining at all, but hoping to justify the disappointed fans who wanted more out of the transfer. The four films are housed in an outer sleeve and I am proud to display this box set on my shelf. The DVD’s can be sold or traded as this new Blu Ray edition carries over all the bonus features and with the new improved picture and sound of the films they are no longer necessary. While I would have loved to see an amazing transfer of The 7th Vuyage of Sinbad I think this is about as good as the film(s) will every look and I’m pretty happy with this set. This is a highly recommended box set for fans of Ray Harryhausen.

history.title: Spider-Man Trilogy Limited Edition Collection [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: BEST RELEASE OF THE ORIGINAL SPIDER-MAN TRILOGY TO DATE!
history.text: I’ve just finished watching the new Spider-Man "Origins” Trilogy Blu Ray Box Set and I have to say I think the upgrade is substantial and well worth the purchase price I paid ($10.00). Anyone who bought the first box set knows it was a huge disappointment. No bonus material for the first two films, the transfers were rushed and not nearly what we have come to expect from Blu Ray quality. The new set fixes most of these issues and then some. First off, the films look and sound much better, though I’m not sure why, Spider-Man 2 didn’t received a 4K transfer, (I suspect it will be done for a future release making die hard fans purchase yet another box set.) The new set is housed in a book type holder with laminated sleeves for the four discs. This is not a major issue with me, I’ve never had a problem with these types of holders, but I've read many reviews with buyers who have so I will not discount their findings. I would have preferred hubs, but my discs were not scratched and in nicely fitted sleeves. They needed a slight pull to remove them. It’s an attractive case with illustrated pages from the films storyline to look at. Each disc is house in its own sleeve and mine were fit tight enough so they won’t fall out if the case is held sideways. Disc one Spider-Man, the groundbreaking film that put superhero films back on the map and for the first time we see the potential of a serious super hero film that is fun. I love the first film and it edges out the second film because I love it’s quirkiness. Sure it has it’s flaws, but Toby McGuire made Peter Parker a real person and does a surprisingly good job as Spider-Man too. The film is cast well, Dunst, Robertson, Harris and Franco all do a great job as well as smaller character parts for Betty Brant and Dr Conners, but stand out performances go to JK Simmons and Willem Defoe. Defoe’s Goblin is spot on even if the costume design is a little disappointing. Defoe’s facial features resemble the goblin so much it is a wonder why they didn’t come up with a more joker type make-up to emphasize his facial expressions more. I suppose it made more sense within the story to have him in a suit with a helmet, but I think this was a missed opportunity. Defoe was the perfect choice, they should have let him loose and be the maniacal menace the goblin is in the comic books. McGuire really shines as Parker, his Spider-Man is very good too, though fanboys will miss the wisecracking attitude he has in the comics, he comes off slightly whinny especially mooning over M.J. It’s all good though, this is a terrific film and one that can be watched many times even by folks who are not in to “super hero” films.. This film sees the biggest improvement as far as video and audio on this release both being major improvements over it’s predecessor with a new 4K transfer. There is a fair amount of extras (carried over from the original DVD release)on this disc too, three commentaries, making of features, gag reel, easter eggs etc. So this disc alone is worth the purchase price for me. Disc two Spider-Man 2 and Spider-Man 2.1 both films look and sound better than the first release, though it is odd that neither of them received the 4K royal treatment transfers here. I can only imagine one will be coming for a future release. (this is one of my biggest gripes with this set.) Spider-Mam 2. History was made with this film, A "Super Hero" movie that fans and critics both loved. It doesn’t happen often in the superhero universe (at least up until this time) and this film deserves all of its praise. Never before has a film captured the weight of being a super hero better. Once again perfectly cast film, this time with new villain Dr. Octopus played to brilliant perfection by Alfred Molina. As great a film as this is, I still like the first film just a little bit better. The bonus material on this disc includes some features and commentaries, but because the disc holds both versions of this film it doesn’t include as much as the first disc. Spider-Man 2.1 is a novelty at best and it is by far the lesser of the two versions of the film. It doesn’t add anything to improve the story and the pacing isn’t as smooth as the theatrical version. Disc three holds everybody’s favorite Spider-Man film (YES I am being sarcastic!) Spider-Man 3. Truth be told, Spider-Man 3 isn’t the disaster that many fans claim. In fact, the first hour is actually very good. The problems with the film could have been fixed if it had been broken up into two films. Spider-Man 3 should have dealt with Sandman and the new Goblin. They could have teamed up against black costume Spider-Man maybe even had dark spider kill one of both of them. Eddie Brock could have been introduced towards the end of the film sort of as a teaser for what would have lied ahead. Venom is one of Web Heads best villains and way too cool to be an add-on....and who in the hell thought Topher Grace was a good casting choice for Eddie Brock/Venom!?? Carnage maybe, but not Venom. if Spider-Man 3 had ended with Sandman’s defeat and Harry’s death, the film would have been much better. This could have left plenty of room to explore the dark side of black costume Spidey, he could have been much darker possibly because he may have had something to do with Harry’s death? Spider-Man 3 has it’s flaws, but a lot of them can be forgiven if Venom had been treated with more respect. Emo Parker acting like a huge tool with his disco dancing and other D-Bag antics could have been easily brushed off as comic relief (which for me it was, I did find it all very funny), if it was all leading up to a more serious look into the dark side of black costume Spider-Man in the next film. The scene where Spider-Man sheds his black costume in the church is great, it just needed to be done in the first act or middle of Spider-Man 4, then we would have an entire movie dealing with Venom and maybe even Carnage. This probably didn’t happen because Raimi was probably thinking he was done after 3 films, otherwise he wouldn’t have tried to cram a resolution into Spider-Mam 3 that tied up all the loose ends. If they didn’t want to go with a two film part one and two scenario, I think the film would have worked better if the story shifted to Parker going through his dark metamorphosis a little sooner. He would have reached the church tower sooner and when Brock became Venom we could have established the character in more depth perhaps even lengthen the film by another 20 minutes. Venom is an interesting foe in Spidey’s Rogue Gallery, he knows who Spider-Man is, he goes undetected by Spider-Man’s spider sense, he can basically do all that Spider-Man can do, he’s even stronger. Of course a three hour film could have become tedious, so fixing this bloated sequel would not have been easy. All things considered I have to give Raimi credit for putting together a coherent film even though it is a bit too ambitious. A missed opportunity, but even with it's flaws I like Spider-Mam 3, even though it is by far the weakest film in the trilogy, it isn’t a bad film. The good news is the transfer is excellent and a definite improvement over the last blu ray release. The disc includes the usual bonuses, commentaries, features etc. carried over from the original DVD release. Disc 4 holds the remaining bonus material and a new incentive to buy this release, a Director’s Cut of Spider-Man 3. The new cut is interesting and more intriguing than Spider-Man 2.1 as a variation, there are things I liked in it and some not so much, none of it really fixes the film as a whole, but I can see it leans towards trying to fix many issues. I liked the added score and it does seem to make the black costume adventure a little more dark, the Scene where Flint Marko is made into a sandcastle to see his daughter is interesting, but a scene where Peter apologizes to Mr. Ditkovitch the landlord has been replaced by Peter telling Ditkovitch’s daughter Ursula he’s sorry, it doesn’t work at all, Peter is a stand up guy, he would apologize to the actually person his did wrong to. Her response is out of character too, she tells Peter it’s alright and that he is a good boy, when she is clearly smitten with him in both Spider-Man 2 and 3. I wish this director’s cut had added more to Venom’s storyline, the rest of the film works fairly well. Both of the alternate cuts are poorly edited and while I’m glad they are included on this release, I will not watch them often. The bonus features on this disc include some for each of the 3 films. I haven’t checked this officially, but it appears that all of the original bonus from the DVD’s are on this release. If not, I can’t imagine anything significant has been left out. If you’re a fan of this trilogy, this is the way to go, while the Best Buy exclusive set all of these discs plus the 2 Amazing Spider-Man films in a 7 disc set, the discs are stacked on hubs which is just as if not more irritating than these sleeves. I ended up buying the Amazing Spider-Man 2 film set too. It’s design is very similar to this set. I will review that on later and post on the appropriate page. The Raimi Spider-Man trilogy is one that has stood the test of time and it remains the best of the Spider-Man incarnations overall. I like all of the Spider-Man films since, but none of them were better films even though they may have fixed or been more accurate with some of the characters traits. I have a sneaking suspicion there will be another Spider-Man box set coming where all the films will received the same 4K treatment and perhaps some new bonus material and even the Homecoming movie included.

history.title: The Amazing Spider-Man 1 & 2 Limited Edition Collection [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: BEST RELEASE OF THESE FILMS TO DATE!
history.text: With the release of two new Spider-Man limited edition blu ray sets I decided to revisit Mark Webb’s interpretation of the wall crawler on its new 2 film Blu Ray set that mirrors the Raimi trilogy’s 3 film set. The new set is housed in a book style case with pages from the films and three laminated sleeves that house the three discs. I know a lot of people hate these types of sleeves and I am not crazy about them myself, but I haven’t had any problems with them scratching the discs and or them falling out. I like the packaging overall but hubs would have been a better choice. As far as the films, Webb had a lot to overcome with the undertaking of the character after such a successful run with Raimi. I’m not sure if doing the origin story again so soon after was the wisest choice but it does work even if it all seems a little too familiar. Like the Raimi trilogy story changes from comic to film are evident. It’s all forgivable especially considering Webb couldn’t make the same exact films that Raimi made. The first disc holds The Amazing Spider-Man and some bonus material. The film looks and sounds great, but I am not sure if there is any upgrade to the transfer, but there is nothing here to complain about. The Amazing Spider-Man, The bad, I found the subplot about Peter’s parents a bit tedious and distracting. I also found it odd that Peter seemed to only be disturbed that his father left him and not his mother as he barely mentions her. It takes close to an hour before Peter begins his Spider-Man adventure. Garfield's interpretation of Peter Parker seems a bit too confident and cool for me. There isn’t enough contrast between him and his alter ego. It’s not terrible, but because we have the Raimi trilogy to compare these films to it is difficult not to. I also thought that Aunt May worked better with a more elderly looking actress. Sally Field is a wonderful actress she just doesn’t give off the Aunt May vibe for me. (not nearly as wrong as Marisa Tomei is in Homecoming, but I suppose in a world where there are 6 Spider-Man films in less than 15 years you have to change it up a little.) Most of what I wasn’t crazy in the two Amazing Spider-Man films about can be rationalized because of the obvious Raimi trilogy comparison they would receive. Spider-Man’s origin is rushed through, the thug who kills Uncle Ben sort of just fades away with Peter’s remorse for letting him go not really being an issue. It’s a big part of the original story, but I do understand why it was changed. The Good, I was excited to see The Lizard as the villain in this film, in part because I had dreamed up a concept for Raimi’s Spider-Man 4 if it had come to fruition. It featured The Lizard, Six Arm Spider-Man, his Doppelganger and Man Spider. Yeah it would have been a mess, but a lot of fun. The Lizard works well in this film and visually it works great for the battles with Spidey because of the color and size differences. I thought Garfield captured Spider-Man’s wise guy attitude really well and while I wasn’t crazy about Emma Stone as Gwen Stacy at first, I was won over by her portrayal and her and Garfield’s chemistry on screen. The action sequences are top notch with all the Spider-Man action looking breathtaking and way cool! Naturally being newer films Webb’s special effects department had the advantage of new advancements in technology. Stan Lee’s cameo is his best cameo ever!!! The second disc holds The Amazing Spider-Man 2, the film looks and sounds great and this disc also included several bonus items. The Amazing Spider-Man 2, The Bad, With the origin out of the way the film is lightened of the repetitive nature the first had, but revisiting the Green Goblin so soon is a little bit of a downer. For me, the villains in this film are poorly designed, Electro is a great choice, but I wasn’t thrilled with the actually design of the character. While a goofy lightning bolt mask would have looked ridiculous, I do think that the electricity could have been shooting out of his head to sort of form the mask associated with the comic character. I thought the Osborn disfiguring disease was unnecessary and I would have liked for Goblin’s costume to be a little more interesting. This film is a bit brighter than the first, but that may have been intensional to balance out that dark ending, the death of Gwen Stacy, it was bold to do and I applaud Webb for doing it. The Good, this film has some very points, the relationship between Gwen and Peter and the potential of the third film are the stand outs. Watching the ending of this film, we are teased with what would appear to be The Sinister Six although not exactly faithful to the comic book line up it sounded like one hell of a movie. I think that the only way for this many villains to work would be to bring Electro back from the dead, Green Goblin would be involved too, this would leave room in the film for character development of the remaining 4 villains. Rhino who in part has already been established in the second film, Doctor Octopus, The Vulture and hopefully Mysterio. I think the Rhino at the end of this film would have been better received if he hadn’t been shown in the trailer. It gave the impression that he would actually be in the film, but instead he is used only as a tease for a future installment that would never be. The third film would have been an extremely hard film to pull off with so many characters but I think it would have given Webb a more appropriate amount of films to complete his vision.I would have loved to have seen it. The third disc holds the lion’s share of the bonus material and to my knowledge includes all the extras from the first releases. I’m not sure if there are any new exclusives for this release, but there is more than enough here to be considered a definitive release. If you don't own these films and want them in your collection this is the way to go, I ended up buying these because the price was too hard to resist ($10). It’s probably going to be the definitive release at least for a long while. Buy It!

history.title: The Mummy: Complete Legacy Collection
history.review_title: BEST MONSTER COLLECTION SO FAR WITH ONLY ONE REPEATED FILM!
history.text: Universal surprisingly released two new monster collections to blu ray well before October this year, With Dracula and The Mummy collections done and the Frankenstein and Wolfman sets released last year the remaining classic monsters Creature from the Black Lagoon and Invisible Man sets are sure to follow. The Mummy set may be the best one yet not so much for the group of movies quality, but because we only get 1 double dip in this set. The original Mummy starring Boris Karloff is by far the best film on this set and the first disc features that film along with all of the bonus material (except trailers for the individual films on the other discs). The Mummy remains the best mummy film ever made and Jack Pierce's make up design is unsurpassed to this day. Karloff was still very thin at this time and his emaciated body only makes this creature look all the more authentic. Disc two features The Mummy's Hand and The Mummy's Tomb. Both films like great in high def showing impressive detail, the sound is also improved. The films themselves are kind of silly, but for monster kids who grew watching these films they are still very entertaining. The Mummy's Hand runs 1 hour and 6 minutes so the brisk pace works well for these types of films. Tom Tyler plays the mummy in this film, but Lon Chaney Jr. takes over the role for the next three films until the series ended. The Mummy's Hand has a little too much comedy for my taste, but overall it is fun and we get to see a lot more of the mummy compared to the original where the actual mummy is only on screen for a few seconds. The second film on disc two is The Mummy's Tomb which runs an hour, actually less if you consider the first 12 minutes are mostly stock footage from the previous film and Steve Banning tells the tale of the mummy thirty years later in the intro to this film. Funny note, Banning tells how the mummy kills certain people in the last film, but he was not present when they were murdered and no one else is alive to tell about it. It's just one of those little things that makes me chuckle. Chaney is unrecognizable under the make up which looks good but it's huge down grade from the original 1932 film. Trailers for each film are also included on this disc and that is it. Disc three holds The Mummy's Ghost and The Mummy's Curse both film look great. The films are pretty redundant having the same basic plot, but all four of these films are fun for those of us who grew up with them The Mummy's Ghost is one of my favorite of this series, I like the ending with the mummy and the princess sinking to the bottom of the swamp with the princess aging back to mummy form as she goes down under the water. The Mummy's Curse is more of them same but a continuity issue really has you scratching your head on this one. In the previous two films the location of the mayhem takes place in Massachusetts, so when the mummy and princess sink in the swamp there it is mind numbing when the princess (now young and beautiful again) rises out of the mud in Louisiana? It's all good fun though and as a kid I loved this series probably because the films were short and showed the mummy through the majority of the films. Trailers are the only extras on the disc. Disc four holds Abbott & Costello Meet The Mummy and while I love most of the comedy teams monster films this one is a little too long in the tooth and we don't get any horror comedy action until the last 20 minutes or so.The film runs close to 80 minutes which feels long. It's great that they included it and for the $24 I paid for this set I am very pleased with the upgrade. The case is familiar looking, but it is a nice package, no sleeves, we get hubs and no disc stacking either. The films all look and sound great so there really isn't much to complain about other than it would have been nice to get commentaries for the new films to blu ray as I'm sure fans would have enjoyed hearing stories regarding the making of these fun minor classics.

history.title: Dracula: Complete Legacy Collection [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: DRACULA FILMS NOW ALL ON BLU RAY! EXCELLENT UPGRADE WITH MORE OF THE SAME DUPLICATES!
history.text: Universal surprisingly released two new monster collections to blu ray well before October this year, With Dracula and The Mummy collections done and the Frankenstein and Wolfman sets released last year, the remaining classic monsters Creature from the Black Lagoon and Invisible Man sets are sure to follow.....or will there be a 30 movie collection on the horizon? The Mummy set is the best set with only one film duplication, but the Dracula set I’m reviewing here is also very good. The original Dracula starring Bela Lugosi is by far the best film on this set and the first disc features that film along with all of the bonus material (except trailers for the individual films on the other discs). Bela’s portrayal of the vampire remains the best Dracula ever. Included on this disc is the Spanish version of the film which I like as it has several shots that are very impressive. The running time which is almost twice as long as the U.S. version drags too much and of course no one can match or surpass Lugosi;s performance. Disc two features Dracula’s Daughter and Son Of Dracula. Both films look great in high def showing impressive detail, the sound is also improved. The films themselves are not as iconic as the main features, but are atmospheric and of good quality. I’m glad Universal gave these sequels the restoration they deserved. (I am still a little salty over the lackluster treatment of Werewolf of London and She-Wolf of London!). Disc three holds the third duplicates of The House of Frankenstein and House of Dracula, the only plus here is that we get a new disc that only has two films instead of three omitting Frankenstein Meets the Wolfman. Disc four holds Abbott & Costello Meet Frankenstein which again is the third duplicate if you've been buying all of these new monster collections. Great movie and I guess I can rest assured that I will always have a copy on blu ray that works with three discs of the same film in my collection. Overall I am happy with this upgrade and at $24 it is certainly worth it. The case is familiar looking, but it is a nice package, no sleeves, we get hubs and no stacking either. history.review_title: Pro Choice meets the Whackadoodle Religious Nutbags in a Divine Comedy
history.text: Citizen Ruth is a classic 1990s film, with a lovable, but damaged lead character played by Laura Dern. This film takes a comedic swipe at the abortion issue in America at the time, with the perfect bad-parent-to-be as an individual who is the process of making the deeply personal and conflicted choice between choosing to keep or terminate an unwanted pregnancy and the two sides who nearly pull her to pieces in the process. "Ruth" becomes a battleground between the Sensible, but vocal party who believes abortion is a personal issue that should be left to the individual and what she chooses to do with her life, versus the Lunatic party, which contains the usual lineup of indignant, rabid, anti-choice nut-jobs who think that draconian and wildly outdated religious doctrine should hold sway at all costs over what a person decides to do with her own body. With the Lunatic party and their primitive beliefs in "God" and other such childish nonsense and the Sensibles, with their belief that an adult can and should control what they do with their life and their body, the fireworks really start going off in all directions. The genius lies in how such a serious and deeply divided issue can be made in comedic form and work so well. I highly recommend this film. It is definitely one of a kind.

I stumbled upon this circa 1980 Russian film "Air Crew" today purely by accident and I am so glad I watched it at once. The film isn't even over yet and I'm writing this review, purely because it is simply one of the most interesting, bizarre and over-the-top pieces of film making I have ever seen. I had no idea of what to expect, but I have a keen interest in early jet flight and Russian film, much of which was not available in the U.S. while I was growing up during the Cold War. The first half or more of the film is not exactly action-packed, however, it is an amazing peek into Russian 1970s and 1980s culture, as seen through an "Americanized" lens and viewpoint. Well into the film, I was not really expecting much to change, which was okay, but at a certain point, everything goes completely berserk. I can't give away any spoilers, but try to picture a 1970s Hollywood disaster epic (or maybe all of them) done in Russia, with Russian sentiment, in an attempt to make a Blockbuster of their own. I'm hoping to see a disclaimer at the end, which states: "No humans were killed or injured in the making of this film". Amazing!

history.review_title: An Adult Fantasy Drama of the Highest Order
history.text: "Pan's Labyrinth" is an adult fantasy-drama which takes place in Spain right around the time when the Fascists there were in league with the Nazi's and all their cronies. The film is made from the viewpoint of a girl whose mother is married to a Captain in the Spanish Fascist military and how she plunges herself into a world of fantasy to escape the violence and oppression of those who surround her. Labyrinth is an excellent film that garnered a 20 minute standing ovation at the Cannes Film Festival, so if you are a tweenie-bopper who hates subtitles or are not able to comprehend complex historical subtexts that require deeper thought perception, you will probably not like it. For those who appreciate films of high caliber and deeply symbolic meaning, this is a wondrous movie you won't soon forget. This is not a children's movie because of the adult themes and some scenes with fairly graphic violence, so be forewarned not to watch it with your five-year-old. As for the negative reviews left by people low on the bell-curve because their DVD didn't play right, or they refuse to watch movies with subtitles, or they don't know how to turn on the subtitles, or they are one of the minions of narcoleptic viewers these days who "fall asleep" during movies, please ignore them. Those people are either mentally lazy, mentally stunted or simple-minded and should be ignored at all costs. Too bad more movies like this are not available, as this is a masterpiece that melds serious themes and CGI fantasy together in an unusual epic achievement.

history.review_title: Vichy French Murderers, Traitors and Collaborators Exposed
history.text: In this film, you will see the true story of the Vichy French collaborators and other Nazi sympathizers among the French, who were responsible for the meaningless deaths of tens of thousands of their own countrymen; men, women and children of the Jewish faith, all to appease their filthy Nazi "handlers". You will also see some of the French patriots and heroes who did what they could to stop the slaughter of innocents. It may be satisfying to know that many of the bloodthirsty gendarmes (French police) and other disgusting traitors in league with Nazi swine were either killed, sentenced to death, deported, imprisoned or given the status of Persona non Grata at the end of the war for treason and crimes against humanity. Over 6763 of these French war criminals were sentenced formally to death in court, while another several thousand were given swifter justice by enraged French citizens and killed by "mob rule". It is estimated that 9000-40,000 French Nazi collaborators, were killed between the last few years of the war and immediately following, during the wild vigilante purges and more legal purges via the court system. In that, there is a small amount of satisfaction.

history.review_title: Training Film for Psychopaths and Terrorists
history.text: A certain co-worker of mine keeps tormenting me by showing me the "church scene" from KINGSMAN on his iPhone. He is 35 years younger than I and he loved it when I introduced him to the classic tune "Free Bird" by Lynyrd Skynyrd. He was quick to note that "Free Bird" is playing during the church holocaust scene in Kingsman. I decided to give this silly, violent movie a chance and I simply couldn't believe the overt violence and incessant use of the F-Bomb. I'm no prude and maybe even use the word too much in my own dialect, but having the F bomb in the film over 6,587,933 times is overkill. Speaking of overkill; the death rate, especially in the church scene, was so orgiastic that I couldn't even keep a body count. I'm all for so called "free speech", but I think the Founding Fathers meant us to have the right to speak out against injustice and government corruption and not the "freedom" to interject the F-Bomb 34 times in each sentence. With the horrendous recent events in Las Vegas and elsewhere, I can't help but think that kids (and some adults) are going to watch this revolting film (in spite of the R rating) and decide that the frenetically violent scene in the church can be adopted as their "acceptable means of dispute resolution". People wonder why our society is so violent. Just watch this movie and you will get your answer.

history.review_title: Rogue Nukes in the Modern World
history.text: Great. Another disconcerting program showing the ease with which a rogue country, state or group could kill hundreds of thousands of innocent people with ingredients from Home Depot and an underworld connection to fissile material. Don't get me wrong; this program is an excellent pre-9/11 view of the potential nuclear disasters that lurk in the underbelly of the world on an everyday basis. It is especially alarming to hear the 1990s sentiments and concerns about North Korea, which were as strongly worded then as they are today. One thing that bothers me though. I do wish that in spite of this material being very interesting, that programs like this would stop giving terrorists ideas. The Cold War was a time of fear...but the potential rogue use of atomic weapons is much, more unsettling.

history.review_title: Emperor-God Hirohito at the Moment of Defeat
history.text: "The Sun" is a remarkable film by Russian filmmaker Aleksandr Sokurov, which imagines the Japanese Emperor Hirohito in his daily activities just before, during and after Japan's defeat in World War II. The filming style is diaphanous and tense at the same time, with emphasis on the anachronistic gentleness and cultured manners of the Emperor God during the cataclysmic bombing of Tokyo. Hirohito is confronted by General Douglas MacArthur who “invites” him (by way of armed MPs) to a one-on-one dinner, so that MacArthur could determine for himself if Hirohito would be tried as a war criminal. The film has a very Zen-like quality to it and may not be interesting to younger viewers or those with no deeper interest in history, but this film is an absolute must for visionaries and historians who are fascinated with the period. “The Sun” is one film from Sokurov’s tetralogy of films about power and empire, particularly regarding World War II axis leaders.

history.review_title: Epic Disasters Buried by the Sands of Time
history.text: Without much expectation, I watched "Great Tragedies of the Early 20th Century" and was absolutely amazed at the forgotten tragedies and disasters of the early to mid 1900s. Beginning with a hasty summary of WWII, this collection of dramatic newsreels continues into a maddening and exciting laundry-list of early 20th century newsreels of mostly forgotten "modern" disasters, including floods, derailments, earthquakes, tornadoes, assassinations and other mayhem. I could watch these all day. It's incredible how horrible some of the events were and how history has all but forgotten most of them. I would like to see more if they are available.

I usually devour a series like this with great relish, being an American History enthusiast, researcher and a "free-lance" archaeologist, but I found this lacking; especially as a PBS release, from whom I have come to expect the very best. Although this "team" uncovers some interesting tidbits and has some "modern" theories and equipment, the show ultimately fails to enthrall the viewer. The GPR, magnetometer and GPS guided equipment is not exactly new tech and it is fairly good for mapping and locating anomalies, but the results are often as difficult to interpret as finding shapes of animals up in the clouds. The host is a nice enough guy, but when uncovering a fort, he seemed completely helpless in simple tasks like knowing compass directions, putting stick flags in the ground and has trouble with common words in the field. He asked one of his experts to explain what the gentleman meant by who "sutlers" were and what a fort "bastion" is. The "expert" carefully and pedantically explained to him that the bastion was for the enfilade. Ha! The host should stick to his artwork, which is quite nice in its own right. The antique bitters bottle the team discovered is a pertinent and interesting find, but it is dismissed with little explanation. The bottle is a highly desirable early Western bitters blown in a cabin form, embossed "GOLDEN BITTERS GEO. C. HUBBEL & CO." and is worth several hundred dollars in good condition. Made from high-proof spirits and an amalgam of spices and root and bark extracts, bitters was considered to be "healthy" and was the "hard liquor" of choice in the mid 1800s in America. There were literally hundreds of distillers who made their own version of it. Prohibition put an end to Americans' passion for the beverage and it faded into obscurity. If you are not a seasoned archaeologist, paleontologist or historian, this series is good to tweak your interest, but don't expect much in the pay-off department, because even with all their so called experts and fancy gadgets, the most you will see in the completely inadequate "three day limit" for each project is not much more than one would expect from a very smart child with a Radio Shack metal detector. This is like watching a murder investigation thriller, where when the first clue turns up, they close the case and walk away. THREE DAYS! What the hell were they thinking?

history.text: 3-1/2 stars out of 5. Good movie. Not so much 'horror' as much as it is a thriller/ghost story. Although there are 'scary' moments it's not a creepfest like most horror types. Basically, this is about an American family living in India where the grieving mother (played very well by the lead), who cannot shake the guilt of having to abandon her son to save their daughter from drowning in a car accident. She thinks she has found a way to alleviate the episodic breakdowns of her loss. Approached by their Indian maid, she is told how to make amends with her dead son and how to correct the self-inflicted mental wounds and accidental mistake of allowing him to die. The only caveat is to follow just 1 rule - no matter what, do not open the door. Well guess what - she opens the door. Now it 's on! Spirits and demons and natives bring all hell to earth. Including her not so sweet son. I enjoyed this film...good acting, great setting and cinematography and a somewhat predictable ending made for an entertaining ghost story.... history.review_title: I knew this was going to be a good ride just from the publicity and the talk but ...
history.text: I'm a late bloomer to the fold. I picked up seasons 1-6 just last year and season 7 is on the way. I knew this was going to be a good ride just from the publicity and the talk but I don't always jump on the wagon until I'm ready...and having just finished S4 I can say with no reservations it was worth the wait. So many things can be said about this series, but there is really no need to for those that know what I mean. For the uninitiated, if one has time, watch this! So much going on and it covers pretty much every type of genre' one can pack into a show like this. You name it: drama, deceit, battles and war, mystery, action, sci-fi, adventure, swords and sorcerers, life and death, the setting and the scenery, love and loss...it goes on and on. And wine - lots and lots of wine! There are so many sub-plots it boggles the mind. You will find yourself hating the good guys and loving the bad ones. Just as soon as you think you've figured it out it will twist and turn out of nowhere. The acting is so good you forget they're acting. Some of the dialog is so subtle, dark, and sarcastic it makes your head spin. The set pieces, the background, the attention to detail and the SPEFX are so good you forget too that they are just show sets. Also important to note - if you're overly-sensitive or squeamish or easily offended, don't bother. This is an in-your-face, brutal and apathetic piece. Pay attention because there is a LOT going on here. Your emotions will roll. To make a long review short - this ain't your grandmother's soap opera!! - 'The night is dark, and full of terror.'

history.title: King Kong
history.review_title: Overblown, overwrought, overdone, please god, make it be over.
history.text: Tripe banal wasteful remake of a classic. This wasn't even as good as the '76 remake with Jessica Lange and Jeff Bridges, it wasn't even as good as 1963's KING KONG VS GODZILLA. Okay, it was slightly better than KING KONG LIVES which deserves the MST3K treatment but that's saying something. It's disappointing that Hollywood keeps churning out these overblown over rendered special effects (CGI) laden films designed to get teenage boys to see them four or five times to drive the box office. The real shame is that the general public continues to flock to these mediocre examples of pablum with little or no heart or story. The crime here is that Peter Jackson is allegedly a fan of the original 1933 classic. I understand the thought behind remaking that one; done with what at the time was state of the art technology you'd think we could blow that out of the water today, well it shows you that having something that actually exists as an effect, like a stop motion puppet, is vastly superior to anything a computer can generate. Jackson's never met an editor he liked so we get double the "fun" with this mess. Jackson completely missed the very most basic point of the original-- Kong is a more than a giant gorilla, he's the missing link. He's that creature between man and ape, so therefore he walks upright like a man. Having Kong as a potbellied silverback gorilla takes all of this away. We should have had an Ultraman sized Dian Fossey come out and talk to Kong with some sign language. The movie mercifully flopped at the box office, saving us from the threat of a Jackson helmed sequel. Don't waste your time on this steaming pile of monkey doo.

history.title: 007: The Roger Moore Collection, Vol. 1 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The Set to Get if you want to get a taste for Moore as Bond.
history.text: Roger Moore was my favorite Bond growing up in the 70s, then I matured and appreciated Sean Connery's original performance in the role, and Daniel Craig is killing it as the current Bond seeming to come right out of the pages of Fleming's books. But back to Moore. He's sillier and campier than Craig or Connery. He's better than Lazenby, Dalton and Brosnan, but only in the early ones. My favorite of his is either MAN WITH THE GOLDEN GUN featuring Christopher Lee as the villain or THE SPY WHO LOVED ME which is the most lavish of the series and features the great assassin Jaws. Truthfully, Carly Simon's theme song makes me cringe when I hear it, but I just fast forward through the credits. Also included on this set is Moore's first outing as Bond in LIVE AND LET DIE which is equal parts black exploitation film, creepy voodoo film and probably the straightest Moore ever was as Bond-- there are very little quips and silly parts in this one, but it's also a bit less fun because of that. Still, this is the set to get if you want to see Moore at his Best Bond.

history.title: James Bond Connery Coll Vol 2 (BD)
history.review_title: Connery's Run Comes to and End with a bloated gasp.
history.text: The second half of Connery's run as 007. THUNDERBALL was about as big a Bond as Bond could get. By the time this one was made he was an institution and Connery was getting tired of playing him, and it shows in his performance. YOU ONLY LIVE TWICE is noteworthy for it's glimpse of 60s life and style in Japan, but Bond as a Japanese is ridiculous in a series that was getting more and more ridiculous. Connery's hairpiece and waist line seem to be suffering a bit but it's only worse in... DIAMONDS ARE FOREVER which is sort of like if your Uncle Ned played James Bond. Its hard to imagine a bloated middle aged man as suave 007-- it would be 40 years before middle aged Daniel Craig would come along and show the world that age didn't matter where Bond was concerned.

history.title: The Daniel Craig (Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Craig will be remembered as the Best Bond
history.text: Initially I balked at Daniel Craig as James Bond. He's blond, he's short and he's not the classic handsome (at least in the early publicity stills) as I thought Bond should be. Boy was I wrong. Craig is as old as Connery was in Diamonds are Forever, but he shows that doesn't mean he's got to be paunchy and winded. Craig is the first Bond in the entire series even including classic Connery to look like he could actually do the things he's doing on the screen. This collection features all of Craig's Bond work with the exception of SPECTRE (and he says he's doing no more after that). These are much more akin to the original Fleming books. Gone are the quips-- Craig doesn't fire off a punchline after killing someone, he takes this business seriously and the series is refreshed and better for it.

history.title: 007: The Sean Connery Collection, Vol. 1 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Connery's BEST as Bond in this set.
history.text: Until Daniel Craig came along, this was the penultimate Bond. Now loyal Connery fans please hear me out. I too think Nobody Does it Better (ha-- see the pun?) than Connery did in FROM RUSSIA WITH LOVE which is out bonded by GOLDFINGER a year later. If Connery had stopped right there with three films we'd have a clear winner. Dr. No is not a bad film by any means, but it's the slowest and most dated as Bond was just figuring out his ways. THIS is the set to get if you're getting only one. Sean Connery sets the standard as James Bond and GOLDFINGER is the best Bond film in the entire series.

history.title: Batman: The Dark Knight Returns (Deluxe Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Mediocre Adaption of a Classic Graphic Novel
history.text: Frank Miller's seminal graphic novel THE DARK KNIGHT RETURNS is a brilliant story-- not just a brilliant Batman story or a comic book story-- it can stand with anything sitting with literature on a library bookshelf. I'm not sure what went wrong with this adaption which disappoints right from the very beginning. There are so many great lines in the graphic novel that are watered down and re-written here for no reason other than to spoon feed what we're seeing. In the book- there's a great exchange between Jim Gordon and his friend Bruce Wayne which goes something like this: "To Batman, I'm glad he survived retirement." The glasses tink together. "He didn't," Bruce responds "But Bruce Wayne is alive and well." "Well, he's certainly learned to drink. Spoken to Dick lately?" "Not in 7 years, you know that Jim. Let's call it a night." Look at that-- it's brilliant dialogue that moves the story along at a fast paced clip. Compare it to what's done here and the dialogue is done in that awful "let's sum things up for the viewers manner". Gordon has to sit and explain to Bruce (and us) that Batman wouldn't be accepted today, that crime is out of control, that the Mutant gang is worse than anything Batman ever faced-- all facts we LEARN in the graphic novel by seeing evidence of it-- so why sum it up so early in the film? The film makers also opted to leave out the first person narration from the book, which is understandable but regrettable. Some of the best lines in the book are ones Bruce/Batman delivers in his thoughts and we lose those here. The worst offense is the storyboarding-- the choices for shots for many of these are just bad anime compositions-- Miller did perfect storyboards in the book and adapting those would have been much more successful. In the book the race car scene which opens the story is handled in an abstract way so that we aren't really sure what's happening while here it's spelled out for us so blatantly as to make it bland and uninteresting. It's a terrific book, this is a mediocre adaption.

history.review_title: "Sad" about killing Germans? Wah-wah-wah. Spare me.
history.text: Much preferred the original docu from 1951. This one had some irritating politically correct crap that I found annoying. Like what, you ask? The little chat between two of the crew about things that happened during the War about which, apparently, one was having some remorse and feelings of guilt. For instance, mentioning Torstein Raaby's involvement in the blowing up the of German warship the Tirpitz where "One thousand men went down." And how he, personally, had shot four Germans...probably SS....when they caught him with his wireless. Norway endured horrendous cruelty and war crimes under Nazi occupation; the Norwegians were among the toughest soldiers of that war and I seriously doubt that a survivor of occupied Norway would be sitting around whining about things that put an end to one of the most ruthless regimes in history and saved millions of lives.

A rather lame story but if you like blood and limbs flying everywhere, this is the flick for you. The thing that REALLY got my goat was the dedication at the end of the movie: "Dedicated to all the men and women who fought and died on BOTH sides....." Made me sick. What kind of PC-BS is that? Those Nazi thugs were the dregs of the most reviled form of humanity and any simpleton should regard what they did -----at every corner of the planet------for about six years with pure revulsion.

The acting was good but the story was hackneyed and the writing lame. The love affair between the maid and the officer was bizarre as we are meant to believe that they fell madly in love over a few short days; a bit of sex and no real conversation over than a few monosyllabic responses and some loooong, sad, yearning, looks. They hardly ever spent more than a few hours with each other on ---what appeared to be----one or two occasions yet that was enough to launch a heavy romance for which they were both willing to die for one another. The frontal nudity and required sex scenes were there, of course, and a nuisance.

history.title: Dunkirk
history.text: Good, historical portrayal of the evacuation of over a quarter of a million soldiers who were surrounded by the Germans(well, three sides) and stranded on the French coast in the first weeks of WW2. Fills in the blanks where the new movie, DUNKIRK, does not.

Can't blame the actors.....they did their jobs but aspects of the story were far-fetched in the extreme. I.e., yes, Stanley is former SAS but--- can even they fight the good fight of beating down a strapping young hoodlum; force marching same hoodlum through thigh-deep snow; run home through snow to kill the killer of his mother; carry the dead mother's body off and dig a grave in the snow and bury her ----all the while with (according to my count) several bullets in his body? Again, acting was good but the "Huh?" value is high.

history.title: Battle of Britain
history.text: Was very disappointed watching this movie which should have been stellar----considering the great cast. The story was disjointed and left some big questions.....e.g., the tenuous marriage between the Susanna York/Christopher Plummer characters. Then, Ian McShane's entire family was wiped out in a direct-hit bombing, but a few minutes later Ian was fine and dandy. But then, we never really find out if his family had died or not. One minute they're there, the next they're not. Any grief Ian felt dissipated, apparently, overnight. Early in the movie, it looked as if the Robert Shaw character augered into the Channel but darn if he didn't re-surface 30 minutes later. That, I suppose, was my mistake but it is very difficult to follow who is whom with their oxygen masks on. During the battle scenes, we never know who is being blasted out of the sky......Brit or Kraut. As in the real battle, we just have to take the word of battle command for numbers.....

history.title: Oblivion
history.text: Oblivion is a movie that projects great expectations, delivers even greater CGI (its smoothless and does not detract from the movie as some CGI in other movies has a propensity to do); however the ending causes this film to fall quite flat on its face. If there is one major fault with Oblivion its that there is a sense that it draws far too much on past Sci-fi movies (I found myself comparing particular scenes with previous movies - some now quite dated - and such reminicising drew me away from the premise of the movie itself) with the ending (no-spoiler here) pretty well much a re-make of a well known, but now quite aged, sci-fi movie (and thus a real dissapointment). Oblivion is an enticing journey into a post (dare I say) apocalyptic earth where mankind has truimphed over an alien invasion and Jack Harper (Tom Cruise) is left behind with his 'partner' as a cleanup/srvice 'mechanic' of giant sea converters. I am not a particular fan of Tom Cruise however here he harks back to his better days of acting and carries this film with a degree of aplom. Like other reviews here, I agree that there is far too little exposure of humans and how they have coped with life in this new earth and much more could have been done to explore this aspect, furthermore I was very dissapointed at the 'Alien' content and the ending of the film reinforced this, as in how they, the aliens, were portrayed. Oblivion started well, built at an excellent rate, maintained my interest - and then suddenly fell completely on its face at the end :( (hence only 3 stars and 2.5 of them are for the CGI and the futuristic technology). Oblivion is still a good movie to see, however in my 'humble' opinion its not a GREAT movie - watch it, enjoy it, just don't have too many great expectations (sic).

history.title: Erased
history.text: I really enjoyed this movie; however, please be aware, it is also called 'The Expatriate' (which is the title by which I purchased this movie). Erased (The Expatriate) is stylised an old fashioned thriller which pits the wrtiter against the viewer with a good set of actors(actresses) along for the ride. Though some scense are almost somewhat chiche in their presentation, this by no way detracts from the movie which moves along a reasonably quick pace (though not so fast as to wash over the story line and leaving the viewer wondering what just has happened or whether a scene was deleted and left on the cutting room floor). I enjoyed this movie from start to finish, I did not give it 5 stars as it did lack a certain 'WOW' factor but for the opportunity to tune out and enjoy some good TV/DVD then one cannot go far wrong with this film.

history.title: Phantom
history.text: I bought this DVD on the basis of previous reviews and whilst I did 'somewhat' enjoy watching it, I felt that it was by no means the "absolute thriller" and "awesome cold war" movie that such reports portrayed. David Dushovny's first appearance was simply embarassing (due mainly to his appalling attempt to speak with a Russian accent)and his acting was very VERY wooden - HOWEVER - to his credit his acting slowly grew on you and towards the end he did finally portray a reasonably good (SPOILER......) evil man - not his best work that I've seen (2.5/10) The fact that all the Russian's were portayed by American actors, who constantly spoke with American idioms (ie saying the word "crewmate" instead of "comrade" which is a Russian verb at its purest) detracted from this movie and indicated the glaring inadequacies liberally sprinkled throught this film. This film could have been an excellent 5 star movie indeed; it portrayed a little known cold war atomic (not nucular) 'missadventure' that could have nastly blown out to cause WW3 - on an atomic scale (parden the pun). With such an interesting topic to create a film around its a pity that not enough was done to develop more authentic aspects to carry the film just that much further in the enjoyment factor. Ed Harris (8/10)- well I can't remember a bad film he has ever done and in PHANTOM he quite literally carries the whole move on his shoulders (if Ed was missing I shudder to think of how bad this film would have actually been). PHANTOM is a somewhat enjoyable film; the actors make it worthwhile watching and its one easily watched, but so much the better if you know/understand the context of the time(s) and socio-political background when this 'incident' occured as it helps to brush over the short-comings of the film. I have bought it to add to my collection; however, it will be a film that I'll only ever watch again if I have ABSOLUTELY NOTHING ELSE to watch at the time.

history.text: I have not yet seen this film yet (and now will most likely not; I was very interested in watching it however a review I read by someone who has seen it has helped me immensly inasmuch as whether to buy/watch this film or not. I am not a prude; however in my opinion there is far too much nudity in films today, and not just 'some flesh' seen, but too often raunchy full body/nudity scenes that boarder on X-rated material - so my thanks to the reviewer who indicated the significant amount of nudity in this film. I think that every film commentry should mention whether there is nudity in it, and to what value, so movie lovers such as myself can make a better, more informed, choice, and not be so surprised by the torrent of nudity in many films of today. For those who like nudity in their movies I say "well ok, good for you" however for those of us who are tired of being surprised by its content in a movie that did not at first indicate such content, reviers like the one I'm talking about are a God send.
