history.title: Jimi: All is by My Side
history.text: On the positive side, Andre Benjamin (Andre 3000) is great as Jimi Hendrix. He has the mannerisms and the dialect down perfect. Sometimes when he speaks you think it’s actually Jimi. Andre even fakes a good left hand guitar technique. Kudos to Andre 3000, and even more kudos to whoever cast him! On the less than positive side, the movie is a challenge to watch. In many places the pacing is painfully slow and could benefit from some editing. Several pregnant pauses could be shorter. The majority of the acting is subdued and laidback; so laidback it’s behind itself! There are also many scenes utilizing a hand held camera which results in a lot of movement and shaking of the frame – very distracting. Even the color of the film is muted. I don’t know if is the type of film stock used, but the film seems “overcast.” Maybe that’s just London. The one splash of color and illumination comes near the end when Jimi makes his triumphal appearance at the Saville and he takes the stage under bright lights wearing a yellow jacket. It feels like cataracts have been removed from your eyes and you can see again. There is a particular scene that musicians should appreciate. Starting around 12:30 Jimi is on stage playing with his band, and the drummer drops a stick. The musicians may have actually been playing and their performances used in the film. The drop and reaction seem genuine. That was the one scene I could relate to! There are no extras related to Jimi. The one bit included in the special features is an interview with Waddy Wachtel, the guy who supplied the music, and he ends up talking more about his signature guitar. It would have been appreciated to have some kind of information about this time period in Jimi’s life. This film will have a hard time finding its audience. True fans have ripped it, the casual fan will learn little, and the main stream soccer moms/dads won’t have time to endure it. To me, this project does more for Andre Benjamin’s legacy. Perhaps a more definitive biopic will be available someday.

history.title: Give My Regards To Broad Street
history.text: No plot. No passion. No inspiration. No payoff. It takes a long and winding road to go nowhere, man. This may have been a major release "back in the day," but it has not aged well. If you must watch it, do so with your thumb on the fast forward button and skip the "dialogue."

history.title: The Great Caruso
history.text: In our current day, it’s hard to imagine this movie was a huge financial success and even earned Oscar nominations. It definitely reflects the sentiments of the time with exaggerated sentiment, no hint of scandal, and emphasis on the classics. As with many Hollywood biopics, the facts are used when convenient. For example, no mention is made of the children he sired before he married, the vices he partook of, nor the impact he had on the still emerging record business of the early 1900’s. Even his decline in health and eventual death are portrayed with no explanation. But then, the focus is really the music. Produced in a time when musicals were still popular, the movie is a good introduction to many operatic classics, all superbly performed by Mario Lanza (Lanza has his own interesting story that might have been a successful biopic had it been made close to his death). This is definitely a product of the times. I doubt audiences today would even consider watching a movie about an opera singer – unless it had some scandalous and salacious story line! Times sure have changed!

history.title: I Want My Name Back
history.review_title: Watch This Before You Make Any Moves in the Music Biz
history.text: Informative and revealing documentary about the inner-workings of the music business as experienced by rap pioneers, the Sugarhill Gang. It's unfortunate what happened to Wonder Mike and Master Gee, and shameful that the legal system did not, or does not, have enough common sense to do the right thing. It's nearly unbelievable to watch what happened to this group, especially the shenanigans their label (and label owners) pulled. It'll make you shake your head in disgust! The production value seems less than high-budget, and it could benefit from some editing. But overall, these minor points do not take away from the overall impact. One lesson to take away from this project is to not go into this business without knowing how the system works - regardless of the genre of music. Much of what happened is - with a good attorney and some understanding of the "biz" - preventable. Any person who desires to be in the music business should watch this documentary. I also highly recommend "20 Feet From Stardom."

history.title: Sweetwater - A True Rock Story [VHS]
history.text: In this well told production, Amy Jo Johnson does a convincing job of portraying Sweetwater's lead singer, Nanci Nevins. Those familiar with 60's music and/or Woodstock already know the story of the group Sweetwater. This made-for-TV has a smart script, above average production value, a good cast, and is ample with examples of Sweetwater's music. Kudos to whoever decided to cast Michelle Phillips as an older Nevins. Many bio-pics, especially those made for TV, often suffer from inadequate budgets and "cheesy" acting, but this VH-1 production gets it right.

history.title: Streets Of Compton [DVD]
history.text: This documentary seemed to me like it was two intertwined. One aspect of this DVD was the very informative history of Compton. With the footage and commentary, I must say I learned a lot. The other aspect of this documentary were segments featuring rapper, The Game. I have to admit I've not heard of The Game, and his segments seemed to be more about promoting his background and career. Which is fine, but it might have worked better if it was just The Game's life as it relates to Compton, and then information solely about Compton. If you just want to know about the history of Compton you may have to forward through some chapters. If you know The Game, and you're a fan, you should enjoy the whole thing.

history.title: Sample This
history.text: This documentary is NOT about the birth of hip-hop, nor sampling. If fact, you're nearly 50 minutes into it before anything substantial about hip-hop is mentioned. This documentary is really about producer Michael Viner and his career, specifically the formation of The Incredible Bongo Band. Time is also spent featuring the members of the group. The song "Apache" is highlighted and that's the only connection in this documentary to hip-hop. If you're looking for a documentary about Michael Viner and The Incredible Bongo Band, this is it! For what it is, it's well made. Good production, good interviews, and good narration by Gene Simmons. I actually learned a few things. However, to actually learn about the birth of hip-hop, as well as sampling, look at other documentaries.

history.title: Surviving Compton: Dre, Suge & Michel'le
history.text: I have to admit, I did not know much about Michel’le and her career. What little I did know was more like a footnote to the careers of Dr. Dre and Suge Knight. “Surviving Compton” enlightened me! The bio-pic provides good detail as to Michel’le’s start in the music business, her relationships with Dre and Knight, and where she is today. Unique for a bio-pic film, Michel’le actually provides narration for the film, and even appears at various points in the film to further explain the events. Many of her songs are included, and I had no idea what kind of voice she had! The movie appears to have had an ample production budget, and is well cast. Of note is Rhyon Nicole Brown as Michel’le. Brown is totally believable and carries the picture. Curtis Hamilton plays Dr. Dre, and R. Marcos Taylor plays Suge Knight. Both are convincing in their roles. Produced and released not long after “Straight Out of Compton” Michel’le’s story is her effort to add more insight to the NWA legacy. Being her story, it’s slanted to her experiences and recollections. Dre fans might not appreciate her “version” of him. Looking beyond that, viewers could look at this story as one of overcoming adversity and not giving up on oneself. Her story could have ended very differently!

history.title: Can't You Hear the Wind Howl
history.text: For me, the best thing about this 1997 documentary was the interviews with people who actually knew Robert Johnson. They provided the most insightful information and added authenticity to his story. Another high point was the inclusion of many of Johnson's songs. Other than that, this movie didn't really hold my attention. Using Danny Glover as the narrator may have been a big deal in 1997, but now his vibes seems out of synch with the subject, and I didn't really take him as a blues fan. The credits list the appearances of Keith Richards and Eric Clapton, and they do appear, although briefly toward the very end of the documentary. What little comments they make sound/look like they could have been taken from an entirely different interview, and only included here because they happened to mention Robert Johnson. I did learn a few things about the Johnson legacy. However, with such little historical records there is only so many ways you can tell the same story. This telling didn't intrigue me.

history.title: John & Yoko: Love Story [VHS]
history.text: Produced and aired at a time when the media and paparazzi were not so pervasive and the Internet was still years away, this movie provided one of the few glimpses into lives of John and Yoko. Many parts of their story were already known, but there were still events to learn about. A die hard Beatle fan might be bored with the movie, as the outcomes and timeline will already be known, but the casual fan should gain some insight to their story. John is played by Mark McGann, and he - in my opinion - carries the whole project. Kim Miyori was a good choice as Yoko, but was a little too "anglo" to fully portray Yoko. Even so, McGann and Miyoir make this movie watchable. The other Beatles are terribly miscast; almost to the point of being comical. The good thing is they don't get a lot of screen time. All the major events about John and Yoko are presented. However, hardly any time is spent on Lennon's murder, and the movie ends at that point. On a more cheery note, the movie has plenty of Beatles/Lennon songs to enjoy. This movie is at least worth a look, and a good reminder of what the Walrus went through post-Beatles.

history.title: Ted
history.review_title: Teddy Ruxpin he's not, but kids don't know that
history.text: The idea of a talking teddy bear that remains long after the novelty has worn off is a clever one. The story of a boy that needs to grow up when confronted by adult life and crises is a time honored tale. The animation and voice acting was fabulous. So, where did the story go wrong? I appreciate Seth MacFarlane's sense of humor (and his singing voice, check out [[ASIN:B004T5IW2K Music Is Better Than Words]]). He has been willing to gore sacred cows in many walks of life. MacFarlane's irreverence is refreshing, and like [[ASIN:B005CHTXWC Robot Chicken: Season Five]] about 10% of his jokes are pants wettingly funny, 80% are amusing, and 10% just fall flat. Those are pretty good odds for humor across such a wide front. Unfortunately in the case of Ted, there was about 25% that were just horribly offensive. I'm no prude and can certainly laugh at myself, my culture, my religion, etc. "Family Guy" and "American Dad" have their moments, but generally there is only one or two missteps an episode. In Ted, the level of callousness and crudity were past the line enough to make the film unfunny. I'm not talking about political correctness. When Ted tells his manager that he used produce to fornicate with and then sold it to an indigent family, it does not come off as funny. And, the examples are legion. The other major issue I have is that Ted drew in a fair number of kids. It is a movie about a talking teddy bear after-all. I heard a couple of boys that appeared to be between 9-10 talking about Ted on the Metro last week. Sure, sure, where are the parents, but I could imagine some parents screwing up by letting their very young kids watch a movie about a talking teddy bear. You don't want to know which parts the boys were hooting about. :-( I just watched a new episode of Family Guy last night and mostly enjoyed it. Seth you let me down on Ted. Sorry, I cannot recommend this movie.

history.title: Cowboy Bebop - The Complete Series

history.text: This is widely viewed as one of the best Anime series ever done. The characters are interesting and unique, and the plots are both reasonable given the universe and tell a story arc. The animation graphics are at just the right level of detail and very well done. A few notes to parents ... this might not be suitable for the younger viewers. It is not hideous (some movies are), but you would be well advised to exercise some caution.

history.text: There have been many versions of this classical tale done over the past four decades, some live action, some animated, but this is my favorite. Chris Walken is simply amazing in this film. He dances, he sings, and delivers an amazing performance. (Honestly, I cannot shake imagining him as Gabriel from his most notable role, but he is great in this movie.) Also, the film is very true to the original tale. (Some of the other versions embellish quite a bit.) One caveat, this is not done in HD. It is clearly a VHS quality video transcribed to DVD, but for the little fairy tale lover in your family will not mind.

history.title: Killing Hasselhoff [DVD]
history.review_title: My Gosh it's full of stars ...
history.text: This movie was done by a number of stand-up commedians and consisted of a very fun (if wildly silly) plot. Ken Jeong stars as the very unlucky night club owner who has everything fail on him at the same time. Unfortunately, our night club owner has borrowed money from a Zen, Brooklyn, ... guy who is deadly serious about getting his money back. Where does the Hoff fit into this? He has a cameo at the beginning (as do about 700 Hollywood A & B listers), but the main connection is that Ken's character has been entering the Hollywood Death List every year for years. The idea is that if you pick the celebrity who dies that year first then you win the pot. By the time our movie story starts the pot is up to $500K, slightly more than our Zen friend cum loanshark needs. Ken finds himself in an increasingly crazy set of plot twists until ... (it is shown in the opening scene so it is not really a spoiler) Ken actually saves the Hoff's life. Roll happy ending. If you do buy, rent, or watch this movie, you should watch the end takes as there is some funny stuff there. It also demonstrates that this movie was largely ad lib by some highly trained professional comedians. (Justin Beiber is even in it!)

history.title: Lucifer: The Complete Second Season [DVD]
history.review_title: The show has hit its stride
history.text: The first season of Lucifer was a surprise hit. The chemistry between Tom Ellis (Lucifer) and DB Woodson (oldest brother Angel) was palpable. This season builds on the good points and keeps the chemistry going strong. Second season introduces a complex character, sometimes villain, Tricia Helfer,, as the “supreme goddess of creation/God’s Ex.” Truth in lending. This is completely recast as her role as the lead, evil humanoid Cylon from Battle Star Galactica. She did a great job in BSG, and she does a fantastic job in Lucifer – sometimes provocative, sometimes evil, and sometimes genuinely caring, but always with an undercurrent of conniving treachery. My favorite new character is Elle, God-fearing, Hispanic, forensic pathologist. She self describes as spontaneous, un-self-aware, and fun. Elle is a fantastic foil to Lucifer’s brooding and Chloe’s relentless responsibility. If you’re a Lucifer fan already, then the new season won’t disappoint, and if you are a newcomer then you can jump right in without fear of getting lost. Two nits – one of the fun things about season one is that it held to commonly held views of angels and devils in Judeo-Christian theology. Alas, in season two, the theological train leaves the rails. The introduction of a co-creator leaves monotheism in the dust. The second nit is that Tricia’s character felt a little muddled at times. By episode four, it was clear that she was very conniving and capable of killing at a whim. Then, there were attempts throughout the season up to the final episode to make her appear more sympathetic. That didn’t work as well as a might’ve. All in all though, a very nice outing for the Lucifer crew, and we’re all looking forward to seeing season three.

history.title: The Big Sick
history.review_title: Interesting premise, but falls downs based on two unlikable protagonists
history.text: I watched the DVD, not through Amazon Prime. The movie has some positive points. It shows the dynamics of a family from Pakistan that are religiously devote, but struggling with the assimilation of their youngest son, who wants to be a stand-up comedian rather than a doctor or lawyer. He also struggled with his views on the familial religion. Throughout the first half of the movie, his mother brings over a string of good Pakistani, unmarried ladies to see if there is a good fit for an arranged marriage. Some of the humor performed by the stand-up comedians is kind of funny. Some of the jokes were abysmal. In other words, the stand-up routines felt real. That said, it was hard to relate to either of the main characters. ** Beware Spoilers Follow ** Our stand-up, male protagonist lies to his family and his would be friend with benefits (several conversations early on in the film make it clear that he intends on pursuing an intimate relationship without ever becoming more than ... I'm not sure what a good phrase is. He is asked by Emily "can you imagine a world where we get together permanently?" His answer, "no." OK, so, maybe he is a schlepp, but Emily is nice, right? Um, no, we find out that she has been hiding the fact that she was previously married and divorced. OK, that is a common thing in modern America. What makes her tough to relate to is that she left her husband, because the sex got boring. He did not cheat. He was not abusive. He was not a drug user. By all accounts he was loving and supportive. Emily left him simply because "life is too short for boring sex." After the couple breaks up and our stand-up friend sleeps with another woman almost immediately, he is called, because Emily is in the hospital. He pretends to be her husband and signs for a dangerous medical procedure, and then, at last, he contacts Emily's parents. The middle third of the movie is about him coming to terms with the parents who know about his background, lies, etc. Ultimately Emily's parents are much more accepting that his are, and they come to like him. Emily however is not so easily convinced. They break up again, and he moves to New York City. They could have ended there, but there is a scene at the end that makes the audience believe they might get back together, but ... it might not be so. The premise of the movie lead me to believe that there was going to be an exploration of cultural integration on all sides, but in the end he is kicked out of his Pakastani family and left to go to New York as a sexually promiscuous comedian with low prospects for ever making it big.

history.title: The Exception [DVD]
history.review_title: A very well done film that is 9/10 love story and 1/10 moral dilemma
history.text: I really enjoyed this film. This review has the benefit of seeing previous reviews. Yes, as stated, there is some relatively obvious sex and nudity. This is not a movie for the kiddies. If you were going into the film expecting an expose of the deposed Kaiser (which, honestly the trailers do kind of imply) then I could see those aspects being undesirable. The movie actually revolves around two characters, and the Kaiser, the Princess, and their entourage are bit players to bring out the main plot. ** Beware Spoilers Follow ** The main characters are Hauptman (Captain) Brandt and an attractive, female member of the house staff. We find out almost immediately that the maid is actually a British spy, and Brandt figures it out pretty rapidly too. By the by, so does the Kaiser who is still a very cagey person despite his staff's feelings about his capabilities. She is also Jewish, something that she reveals to Brandt almost immediately. So, the story really revolves around what to do with conflicted loyalties and what does devotion and honor mean when your country has devolved into a despicable morass. (Just to be clear, there were no parallels either obvious or even implied with history after World War II - in other words, this movie steers well clear of any current controversies, and for one this viewer appreciated that.) The Kaiser, the Princess, their Aide de Camp, Brandt, and the love interest cum spy were all very well developed characters and all of them were appealing in some ways -- and clearly not in others. All in all, a very good film about a difficult period in human history.

history.title: The Quatermass Xperiment (1955) aka The Creeping Unknown [Blu-ray]
history.text: I was 10 in 1963 and had been begging my Mother for a week to sit up at midnight on a Saturday to see this movie. A friend talked me into it from school. We spent the last half of the movie hiding behind Mom peeking through our fingers and she finally frowned at us and said," You made me sit up all night for this creep fest you better sit up and take it like men, I'm getting more coffee. You can watch it,YUCK!" ,LOL! I got the DVD a few years ago a watched in in it fuzzy black a white glory while having the memory of that night come back and still asking myself,"Wow,How did they make that monster look so real?" If you see it,it still holds up very well today. creepy and very organic for early 50's. The story was very well written and acted. The Old Lady drunk in the police station talking about seeing "Hob goblins" was a hoot. "You mean it was REAL?" Then she passes out. I've since gotten all the "Quatermass" movies and the TV series that they based the movies on,also very well done. I definitely suggest to anyone who like old B&W Sci-Fi movies and are Hammer fans,get this on Blu-Ray when it comes out. I can't wait to see it in HD.

history.title: Mozart: Le nozze di Figaro
history.review_title: Fine Figaro, but with a technical caveat
history.text: There are many Figaros on DVD and Blu ray and this is one you can safely choose, even if it's the only one you own. It is no superstar performance, but a lively, compelling rendition done by a very capable regional opera house. The singers are all quite good and act their roles with vigor and humor. I really like the spontaneous, realistic feel of this production. It just feels fresh and sexy. A souffle of a Figaro, and that's not a bad thing. There is, though a fly in the ointment. Unless the DVD company has upgraded the disk (I got my copy 13 years ago), its viewing on a modern widescreen TV will be compromised. It is not anamorphic widescreen. It was a letterbox version made to appear widescreen only for an old CRT TV. Meaning the show appears in the center of your modern widescreen, surrounded on all sides by black bars. When you resize it to fit your screen, most of the subtitles vanish out of sight. So that's no real help, unless you speak Italian.

history.review_title: Great show but Netflix arrogance on parade
history.text: This is an average rating, taking into account several factors. First, the show itself is terrific—a wonderful extended monster movie that mashes up Steven King, small-town Indiana, the Goonies, govt. conspiracies, and the 1980s. Just a glorious celebration of the '80s. Five stars for all that. Now on to the negatives, the one and two stars. For an 8-show season, a $25 price is arrogant and stupid. Moreover, there are no extras, zippo. Worst of all, Netflix forces you to sit through nearly six minutes of previews and other garbage at the beginning—allowing no fast forwarding or jumping forward. My advice: Stick the first disk in your machine, go make a cup of coffee and come back six minutes later. Oh, and I almost forgot the nasty rubber hubs the disks come on; you really have to pry them off. The faux VHS box is fun, though.

history.title: Catch-22 (1970)
history.text: I read Catch-22 as a senior in College in 1967 and thought 'what an excellent, though sometimes confusing, anti-war satire, Heller's really onto something profound here'. Then I saw the movie when it came out in 1970 and said, 'Look at all those hot Hollywood stars, this must be a really expensive and important anti-war movie, even if the movie is way more confusing than the book'. Now almost 50 years later, my opinion of the movie has changed significantly: It does not hold up well at all, especially if you have read the book. This is, at best, a confusing pretentious silly pile of crap. The cast tries, but for the most part they are way over the top in their characterizations of military life without any real explanations or motivations. it seems that much of it is played out for unfunny comedy. Seeing this again was a big disappointment. Maybe it was the anti-war times of 1970 and my callow youth that made it seem more topical and hip back then. Within 2 years I was an infantryman platoon leader, one of life's little ironies.

history.title: The Lovers [DVD]
history.review_title: Overall a passionless and boring look at a unsympathetic couple
history.text: A strangely unmoving film about the dissipation of a relationship that is barely on life support when we meet the couple. And their choices for extramarital partners seem poor at best. There aren't any sympathetic characters here and the pace and plot are crushingly boring. There seems to be no rhyme or reason for anyone's behavior, other than let's do this because 'I'm bored'. That's what I got out of watching this: boredom and a lack of passion. Not recommended.

history.title: Gifted
history.text: This is a moving well-acted movie by all concerned. Everyone contributes and there are no false steps in this little gem. It's a story about a gifted child math prodigy and how to raise her and all that that implies. Hint: the little girl steals this movie with her on-the-spot characterization of a kid so smart and trying to fit in via her uncle's tutelage in both the kid and adult worlds. Highly recommended.

history.title: Cloud Atlas
history.review_title: Interesting but slow and hard to get into 3hr semi Sci-Fi movie
history.text: An interesting almost 3hr long semi sci-fi movie that starts very, very slowly and gradually picks up steam about 1/2 way into it. It is very hard to get into, so one must have real patience to see and understand and make sense of what will happens and how most of the 6 scenarios are interconnected. I would like to say that all scenarios are 'equal' in meaning, but to me they weren't. That will be left to the individual viewer to discern. interesting acting, mostly good, especially by Hanks. It is a bit slow and confusing in parts, so this won't be for everyone. I think it needed a good editor as not all stories were created "equal". If you have the 3hr time and an open mind, this might be worthwhile for you. I rate it somewhere between 3 and 4 stars.

history.title: Alien: Covenant

Too many silly mishaps by the stumbling crew - let's count them as they die. Truly one bad decision after the other, resulting in havoc.for all. Let's get to the fact the the new "David" has become "The New and Improved Creator" for all future generations (sound mild applause and cheers). Well what I see here is a megalomaniacal Mr know-it-all droid employing all that's bad in the human race, coupled with the creators shortcomings and vengeance tiltings,which makes for a nasty little robot that nobody wishes to play with. David takes this badly and very personally also, so that no one appreciates his toys (new improved aliens) nor do they want listen to his crap science ideas (from which death - theirs - results) - so by default he ends up the Total Bad Guy Redneck Droid who employs everything, every device, every embryo, every cheaterbug method to help eliminate the entire human race because they are flawed beings.This movie was a huge disappoinment on almost every level, plus it makes no logical or scientific sense. history.review_title: Pitiful non-interesting, non-imaginative series. Do yourself a favor by NOT watching this tripe.
history.text: Ok, if you have read the book by King and seen the pretty good 2007 movie - then do yourself a favor by NOT watching this TV series (10 episodes) because it's a pitiful non-dramatic, non-horrific, non-interesting mess. This was so disappointing on all levels that it bears little resemblance to King's original ideas except for the fact that there is a mist/fog covering the town that simply makes people do bad things to each other. Reaches for big ideas but falls flat. Big whoop! Is this mist even explained in the series? No. Let's just blame it on Army research that's gotten out of hand somehow since there are soldiers in it. Wait, maybe the plot (what there is of it) got out of hand also by mist-inspired soap opera writing demons - they must have inhaled too much mist! This could have been so much better but it's not. Not worth the time or effort or imagination to watch it, otherwise you'll be sorry. Very sorry!

history.title: Kingsman The Golden Circle
history.review_title: Overwhelming cartoonish violence in a spoofy political plot can be amusing, but not for the faint of heart.
history.text: Viewers seem to either love or hate this movie. If you accept it as a parody of violent spy films in general, then its cartoonish violence will seem not too much over the top. In many respects it's fairly amusing and cleverly derivative. However there are lots of F-bombs throughout the film and the violence may seem repugnant to some viewers. But I was entertained nevertheless and for what it is (not pretends to be) I think it's OK. As far as any political message, well folks it's a spoof and fiction first and foremost, so try not to read anything else into it. I thought it fairly clever on a humorous 'freshman political level' however. The one thing that stood out for me was Colin Firth - without him to lend some class to this entire Kingsmen enterprise in general, the movie would rate as 2 stars. Also the American 'Statesmen' actors in this film are wasted for the most part and have little screen time. Finally the killing off of Malcolm (plot spoiler) who helped hold the British Kingsmen faction together with real class, seemed unnecessary and cruel and pointless. Three stars for the action sequences and Colin Firth's resurrection.

history.title: Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit (Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD)
history.review_title: Full of cliches, wooden acting, bad script
history.text: An embarrassment with the world's most vapid villain ever. Chris Pine saves this movie from being the total embarrassment it is. It's as if the Hollywood fools talked among themselves and said "we need a good fight scene here" - hey, don't tell me about what makes sense! I don't care that a few hours later you'll hear that the entire scene was completely unnecessary, begging the question why you'd go through with the charade if that's the case. Movie needs tension here so give it to me!" You'll know it when you see it and shake your head. Knightly is abysmally frigid as the girlfriend and there is ZERO chemistry. Jack Ryan PhD. is so dumb, as written, that he doesn't know how to dispense of a movie ticket properly (such as once he's already in the theatre). Cosner is not convincing as the veteran agent. And his character is so poorly written that he doesn't bother explaining how his crack team could have whiffed detecting the issue Jack Ryan has upon his arrival in Russia to start the main area in the film. And poor Kenneth Branagh. So brilliant that he falls for the most obvious and glaring lame gags that have been in movies for decades. HIs character in summation "scowl, look angry, say something menacing." And the pitiful plot. Suddenly the bait shows up. It's an insult how it happens. Nothing in the dialogue suggests it and how it's known to everyone but our protagonist is mind numbing. Again, the Hollywood geniuses said "fit plot mechanism in here to drive the movie in this direction which you've all seen before." The truth is this movie might be deserving of one star because of the dialogue but at least Pine makes it semi-watchable, which it is until the middle. I wasn't expecting this bad. But it's bad.

history.review_title: Good style but with B-movie editing, script and gaping plot holes
history.text: Good style over substance that devolves into shlock. It starts off promising and the two lead actors are excellent and make this film watchable, even during it's cringeworthy moments. Any comparison to Bladerunner is purely superficial with the 80s type soundtrack and dark, bleak visuals. While the movie begins with some promise about an experiment gone wrong, it's apparent rather early that the story is told in disjointed fashion and the science quickly devolves into total shlock scifi cliche. There is a connection between the doctor's sick daughter and his new assistant but the connection is not made clear, neither scientifically nor emotionally. "Cool concepts" are introduced that make you think that there is more going on, which there is, including the presence of your typical cardboard villain. There are many gaping plot holes and things that make you go "huh?" (such as why greater care wouldn't have been taken with machines... which is answered by the fact that the plot couldn't have moved in the direction it did if the script made too much sense.) Unfortunately the middle and ending are predictable and rather silly. Caity Lotz does a phenomenal job to pull off a believable android and Toby Stephens does a great job as the lead actor. But the script makes him a 2 dimensional character and all of the characters in this film are pure cardboard. There is no reason to care about them. What made Bladerunner such a great film is where this one fails by a very large margin. Someone could have helped with the choppy editing and a second and third pair of eyes to create a more plausible script with a meaningful message rather than what we've all seen before numerous times just done with a little more visual style. Watchable but if you're expecting Bladerunner or even decent scifi, you'll probably be disappointed.

history.title: The Island
history.review_title: Typical Michael Bay, sucks the intelligence out, explosions in
history.text: Michael Bay has a talent for producing lots of explosions and stripping films of intelligence, realism and emotion - ruining a good tale with terrible dialogue. It's watchable but there are so many awkward moments that the film just becomes a tiresome bore and exercise in frustration to watch. Do not believe the ratings. They grossly overestimate the intelligence of this film. McGregor lives in a facility along with all the others who are told that there is contamination above and that eventually they are being trained to go to "The Island" to enjoy life on the outside. Eventually he and others become a little curious why obvious questions aren't answered - and so will you as a viewer, finding the entire artificial existence implausible and unfortunately not so well thought through. Security is remarkably lax for such an important facility. While there he meets Johansson, another member of the white clad population. Eventually a situation arises and things change. Bean is excellent in his role as the doctor, a seasoned actor. Hounsou is wasted and sounds like he's reading his lines off a prompter. Embarrassing. I won't say his role because it will ruin the film. Buscemi is an out of place supervisor whose role is to help fuel the curiosity of McGregor even though his entire existence and what he has to arouse curiosity is so bizarrely out of place and is illogical. Throughout the movie you'll be groaning at being engrossed to then hearing some really dumb or awkward words come out of a character's mouth, including conspicuous product placement. Hello Heineken (among others.) I'd give this film a 2.5 solely for the visuals and having an incredible but wasted cast of actors who are the only reason this drivel is even watchable. Disappointing because in the hands of the right director, this would have been an intelligent film. Instead it's a very long chase with a bunch of explosions, car chases, etc. and is completely forgettable. High production value, very low scale of intellect. Any comparisons to Bladerunner, Dark City, Gattaca or even the Matrix (with it's ridiculous illogical ending about "guns") is absurd. This is a watchable, cable rerun on a lazy Saturday afternoon too keep yourself momentarily entertained.

history.title: Non-Stop
history.text: This is an amazing film - a script that continues to get more laughable, less intelligent and more implausible as it plods along. The only thing more amazing is how many people rated this film 4 stars. If you've been in an airport and on a flight before, it's even more insulting to the intelligence. Don't say you weren't warned. Liam Neeson plays the same role and character he starred in for the past 5 films. He's very good at that role but the script is horrendous. A situation arises on the plane and none of it is plausible. A who done it situation arises and the perp is so amazingly adept that stuff just happens as if it as magic. Every possible cliche imaginable is pulled out, every red herring and the ensuing conflict continues to get stupider and more farfetched as the situation arises. I've seen many bad movies but this one is as bad as represented. You'll probably stick with it because Neesom is a good actor and you'll probably want to just figure out who done it to end your curiosity. And when all plays itself out, you'll be rolling your eyes and laughing at the film. None of it adds up, only in a Hollywood boardroom. Don't say you weren't warned.

history.title: The Recruit
history.review_title: Terrible script ruins a great cast
history.text: Don't be fooled by the very high rating of this film. It's terrible. It starts out with a decent premise. Despite being awkwardly constructed and very difficult to believe, it's on the edge of suspension of belief. But soon after you're given the premise for the movie to kick into the next gear, the script shifts into serious B movie mode. Without giving away important parts of the movie, there is a scene where a character knows he's being followed. He could easily kill the follower. Oddly the character opts to just startle the follower and move on. The only explanation for this has to be that the move had to move in a certain direction. There are also such awkward moments to construct the plot moving forward that it's just laughable. Pacino does his usual superman cool performance, nothing special, as the star is Colin Ferrel. And while his acting is decent, he's really left with stilted moments because the script is so darn awkward. This is a B movie at best. Fine for a cable view on a lazy afternoon but don't expect anything near satisfaction based upon the star rating.

history.review_title: Frustrating example of Hong Kong Style and Form without any substance
history.text: This movie is frustrating. The look, feel and acting all have an attractive style. There is a chemistry between the protagonists. There is lots of mood, good sets. But everything else unfortunately reeks of amateurish B grade film making - at best. This movie is defined cliche, nothing you haven't seen before in poor, low budget, poorly written movies. My guess is that all the good reviews come from fans who don't care too much because they just like the style and "cool" the actors ooze, including when they walk into ridiculous odds and come out victorious or knowing that certain death probably awaits them. It's sad that this film delves into looking and feeling silly. Everything in this film is about "honor" yet none of it makes sense. Nobody is honorable but there is some type of contradictory code between hit men that we are supposed to admire. And they aren't really bad guys, just ordinary folks like you and me. Instead of making pizza or delivering mail, they kill people. Can't fault them for that, right? It's just a job. For all the "crack" shooting you see done by people who can't miss, it's amazing how often they do. I'm not sure if it's intentional but it's almost laughable how actors get shot, get hurt, pick themselves up off the pavement and carry on with their mission because this is what must happen in the movie. A man can't see faces clearly but he sure can shoot the lights out of a moving bicycle at 50 yards away. The longer the movie rolls, the more it looks like a set on a stage. If you watch this movie to the end, all I can say is that "if the jacket fit you can't acquit." Unless you're a fan, this is just a lot of flash with a predictable plot that has no real purpose other than move the film to different sets for lots of gunplay. Waste of an opportunity.

history.title: Cold Eyes (2013) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Another good, well acted, Korean crime drama
history.text: Like all Korean movies, the acting is very good and the dialogue is important to the film. While the film was predictable (for me) and lacks back story or details of the intricate plot you'd expect, it's still an entertaining watch. I wouldn't rank it near truly great films like the Vengeance trilogy. This is more like a good slightly bubble gum crime film. I think that the beginning is fun and part of what keeps you in the film. The premise is a young rookie police investigator with fantastic ability to recall people, places and things she observes on the job becomes acclimated with the difficulties on the job. Her first mission is to help the team stop a crime group that has already pulled off one extremely well planned heist.

history.title: CHOSEN - SEASON 01
history.review_title: Has early promise but becomes pointless and repetitive quickly
history.text: On the bright side - the lead does the best he can with the script. I'll give him that. On the dark side - what on earth is this? Basically it sucks you in with the "who is behind the crazy turn of events and why are they doing this?" After the first 2-3 20 minute episodes you begin to stop caring because the script becomes ridiculous and feels like an attempt to prolong the show and that most won't care about sloppy writing, cardboard cliches and artificial dialogue that only makes sense to move a plot along. You're best off just finding a spoiler to find out the why and getting over watching this silliness to the end. In short, Milo finds a box with a gun and a photo at his door. Through a strange turn of events, he discovers that he's supposed to kill this man he's never met and doesn't know. Over the course of time you realize there are others in this "game." A morality play is introduced and doesn't make much sense and it's like Saw all over again. Put people in a terrible situation and chances are most will do whatever it takes to survive. Got it. Seen it before. And every situation the characters say the same thing - same lines, different victim. And in each situation these idiots never learn from their previous experiences. So.... why bother with any of this? Saw didn't really make much sense either except become an exercise in torture porn, which much of this series seems to be. It's unfortunate because this series seems like it could have been something more than just "hey, this is a cool idea we've seen before so let's just roll with it and kind of connect the episodes." The actors around Ventimiglia vary from OK to pretty weak and it's probably because the script just doesn't allow for anything remotely realistic. It also requires you to buy into the premise that somehow these characters live in a vacuum and the rest of the world just allows it to go on.

history.review_title: Rehashed, poorly cast, cash in on Bourne's name for one last score
history.text: Greengrass called Damon and asked him if he'd like to score one last huge paycheck. Since Renner wasn't successful in the attempt to continue milking this franchise and the success of the first three films with "The Bourne Legacy", something had to be done to milk it just one, last time. Let's get in some big names to replace the usuals like Tommy Lee Jones and hot name newcomer, Alicia Vikander. Script, writing - doesn't matter. Just do something that relates to Snowden since all the kids love that kind of anti-establishment, government is bad and invading our privacy stuff. This film is a confirmation that the Bourne series is dead. Lazy writing, casting, research, acting and a gratuitous amount of shaky cam - it's all here. Story. You've seen it before. But we thought that Bourne had regained his memory. OK, he's still struggling with that one. And the man with his special set of skills can only resort to being paid menial amounts of money in bare knuckles boxing, living like a vagrant.At the same time Nicky Parsons is working on something we can't really decipher which involves her walking into some unidentified place, hacking into top security that no one else could prior access (because this film needs a McGuffin to chase) and the government is able to somehow plant a super virus onto her USB drive which she store files which would dictate the location of the drive the next time a computer tries to access it... even if it is in Iceland, unconnected to the Internet (I didn't see a connection) and opened by someone who is supposed to be a computer genius. This type of lazy, confusing story is evident everywhere. Bourne used to have to act smart and "doesn't do random", is carefully planned and doesn't make mistakes. Yet here he not only does random but he walks right into a US customs area to waltz into the country. We're worried about some Snowdenesque plot and todays computers can't even perform a simple facial recognition test? And America's most wanted isn't even up on border security? Unfortunately the laziness is abound everywhere and things just work because, well... they have to in order to move the plot forward. These inconsistencies with Bourne notwithstanding (still searching for the past, milk it, milk it...), the casting was terrible. Alicia Vikander is a capable actress but couldn't be more miscast. Perhaps it's also the directing. She has an absolutely invisible, tepid presence. Not for a minute does she convince anyone that she has any true skills other than touch typing commands into a computer that would embarrass anyone who works in IT. And her struggle to maintain something resembling an American accent is painful. Tommy Lee Jones looks like he's about 3 decades past retirement and the camera pans in and does close ups just to make 100% sure you didn't miss how ancient he looks and how miscast he is for the part. Was told "just do Tommy Lee, big dog, bark out orders and then lament that you knew Bourne was coming for you all along." VIncent Cassel - another great actor - is totally wasted. He's relegated to angry hit man who is part of the film's action time which goes on far too long for its running and enough to bore you silly. He does very little in this film other than play 'the asset" which is code for "agent to take out Bourne but will fail in some spectacular way." Add in copious doses of "shaky cam in dark" and you'll get motion sickness along with an inability to digest what it is you think you just saw. Which leaves us with our main character. Like Craig in Spectre, Damon looks terribly bored in this role. He's lifeless, humorless and driven by something we don't really know. Oh yes, there is a minor plot twist that might explain his motivation but it doesn't do so convincingly and in terribly confusing fashion. Same thing you've seen before (must... remember.... flash...) yet out of place considering how far Bourne had progressed in the last film. While I have seen worse, this is a total retread, same story, bored characters, grim and totally humorless dialogue, unbelievable characters, mail it in for the money script and performances. I doubt anyone wanted to do the film but it was easy money and guaranteed profit for just on more time at the box office. Watchable but not enjoyable at all.

history.title: Moss Two-Disc Special Edition (or Iggi)
history.review_title: Chilling, suspenseful and difficult to turn away for the entire duration. Great film.
history.text: Another unique, fantastic Korean thriller. This is a very long, creepy and sinister film - about 2 and a half hours. But it is never boring. And it is worth the payoff. The plot - a strange man who has repented from his sins seems to attract the village locals who fund him for his teachings. A police officer is influenced by a local priest who is jealous that all his donations are going to this strange man. But after a strange twist, the police officer is convinced that the strange man is the genuine article he seems to be. But after the man passes away under mysterious circumstances, his loser son is notified about the man's death. And while attending to his father's affairs, he can't help but notice that the village elders can't wait to try to push him out and back to the city as quickly as possible. But the son decides to stay on and continues to discover the strange workings of the town and his father's past... Riveting. Great acting. Very tense. Not a horror film but certainly chilling in every way, including the human interest side. They don't make them like this in Hollywood.

history.title: Shoot To Kill
history.review_title: A great movie.....but, don't get caught out.
history.text: Is this some sort of a scam, a sham, a rip-off, or what? Shoot To Kill is a dead set copy of Deadly Pursuit. Deadly Pursuit has been around since 1988.Suddenly Shoot to Kill appears on the scene (also 1988) as an exact carbon copy of Deadly Pursuit. Why the name change? With both being available from Amazon it seems to be an outrageous rip-off that will catch some unwary buyers on the hop. Two movies, exactly the same, sold be Amazon, same actors, same story. Although this is a great movie, I have to tell you people, don't get scammed by this. I believe this to be fraudulent, so ....watch out.

history.title: Lilo & Stitch Disney Read-Along [DVD]
history.review_title: Beware of what you order, beware of what you receive.
history.text: If ever there was a fraudulent acquisition, this is it. After waiting some weeks past its due by date, the parcel finally arrived. It did NOT contain what I ordered, the blue covered disc. My parcel did, in fact, contain a yellow, well worn cover that couldn't close properly (and still doesn't). It contained the book and a dirty, scratched cd. It was also supposed to contain a cassette tape. That was missing. After contacting the sender with my complaint, I heard nothing. Sending them another e-mail, I was told the item was the "real thing". Another e-mail from me was sent, threatening to inform Amazon of this fraudulent transaction and the non compliance of the sender. Two days later, an e-mail arrived from the sender, informing me that as it would cost too much money to return the item to them, they will refund my money. This they did. But, this was an abhorrent scam, a scam they no doubt were hoping to get away with. As it stands, I still, to this day, do not have what was listed on Amazon.

history.title: The Culpepper Cattle Co. [DVD]
history.review_title: If you like westerns, this is up your alley.
history.text: I first saw this movie a long time ago on tv. I knew that sooner or later (it was later) that I would buy it....and I did. Since I bought it a while back, I have watched it again three times. A great western movie, you will enjoy it.

history.title: National Geographic Classics: World's Deadliest
history.review_title: Don't play games with these animals, you may not live to tell about it.
history.text: The cover claims "The worlds deadliest". But, are they? We often read, see and hear, about the worlds deadliest creatures. This collection claims that the Lion is a deadliest creature. But, is the lion worse than the Tiger? Both are killers of animals and humans. Both are deadly. But, all creature depicted in these dvd's are certainly deadly. These animals require the greatest respect from people, cross their paths and you are likely to die. Buy it, watch it and decide which YOU would consider to be the worst.

history.title: Blackboard Jungle
history.review_title: There never has been a dance since rock and roll that can surpass it.
history.text: This was probably the first rock and roll movie I saw prior to that almighty classic Rock Around The Clock. It was so long ago that I don't recall which I saw first. But, I'm sure it was BJ. As soon as it starts, that humungus all time rock and roll classic, Rock around the clock, is pounding the eardrums. I cannot imagine there being any person above 60 years who hasn't seen either or both movies. Blackboard Jungle, always has, it does now and it always will, sit beside Rock around the clock, as the two best ever movies of the 1950's. I can't believe I'm writing this.....but. if you have never seen Blackboard Jungle, then make sure you buy a copy of it now.

history.title: Rango (Two-Disc Blu-ray/DVD Combo + Digital Copy)
history.review_title: I wonder if we will ever see a Rango 2 !
history.text: There is not a damn thing I could, would or dare say, to discredit Rango. What a great movie. Yeah! Okay, it's basically a kids movie. But, hey! We are all entitled to revert back to our childhood now and then. Buy it, watch it, you'll love it.

history.title: Rio
history.review_title: If you can't go to Rio, then Rio can come to you.
history.text: Everyone who has seen this movie would surely agree that it is worth a 6 star rating. But, as there are only 5, I can only give it 5. Its 6th star would have been for its inclusion of a digital copy disc, unlike Rio 2 which has failed to live up to Rio by NOT supplying a digital copy disc. (PLEASE READ MY COMMENTS ON RIO 2). I had bought Rio and Rango at the same time . I can't believe there may still be people who have not yet seen Rio, But, if this is so, then please go and buy get it. It is just sooooo enjoyable.

history.title: Born of Fire
history.review_title: THERE IS NO GREATER EXPERIENCE THAN TO WATCH MOTHER NATURE AT WORK.
history.text: I have always had a distinct liking for volcanoes. I think they are awesome in their displays. Having seen Mt. Pinatibu in action as well as Mt. Mayon and the Taal volcano, all in the Philippines, it's an awesome experience. Add to that, the fact that, as a member of a group, we climbed a volcano in Guatemala (near Antigua). To be able to look down the volcanos throat and see the molten lava bubbling away is awe inspiring. Although, this documentary does not include the ones I have mentioned, it does give you a documentary as only National Geographic knows how. Watch how awesome Nature can be and is. It is a great Documentary. Buy it and you will agree with me.

history.title: Galapagos: A Musical Odyssey
history.review_title: A beautiful documentary, set to beautiful music.
history.text: I was, at first, somewhat disappointed with this as there is no commentary of any sort. But, ten minutes into watching it, I began to realise that this was actually better, much better, than a voiced over documentary. It enables the viewer to absolutely relax, sit back and thoroughly enjoy seeing the beauty of the Galapagos Islands to the relaxing music initiated to coincide with what the viewer is seeing. It is a fabulous back ground display to have running when you are entertaining.

history.title: Nature: Extraordinary Birds
history.review_title: Who cannot resist the beauty of our Avian friends?
history.text: Although I enjoyed all of these documentaries, for me, the one that really stood out was PALE MALE. A great story. Don't get me wrong, this is a great buy. You will enjoy them all as I did. But, as with everyone, we all have our favourites.....and PALE MALE is mine. It is a good buy, you will enjoy it as I did.
