history.title: Half Light
history.review_title: IS THIS THE SAME AS THE TWILIGHT ZONE?
history.text: In case anyone hasn't noticed it, this movie has MUCH in common with GHOST including the fact that Demi Moore appears in BOTH films (which I believe to be deliberate in its casting).1) A loved one is killed off early in both films; 2)Demi Moore (aka Rachel Carlson - NOT Carson which is the name used for her character on the DVD cover [doesn't anyone proofread anymore?]) is left alone to grieve and resolve the fall out from the deaths;3)I'm not entirely sure who left the deadly gate unlocked in HL since DM's husband (her second) possesses the key and lock for said gate to use later on (the movie is not totally clear on this point despite a brief conversation early on regarding the unlocked gate). Thus, both deaths may be deliberate; 4)The ultimate baddy turns out to be a relative, business associate, and/or best friend; 5)A psychic helps to bring about a positive conclusion in both films - remember Whoopy Goldberg; 6)Supernatural forces help to bring about justice in the grand finale. In any event, HL holds your attention and plays well when it comes to the hallucinatory/reality conflict. There are indeed many loopholes. But this genre always has them While the musical score for HL is well above average, it cannot compete with the tear jerking strings courtesy of Maurice Jarre; and the love relationship between DM and Patrick Swayze in GHOST is hardly comparable to the emotional ties that are established in Half Light despite the sad and moving tragedy contained in the latter. But, all in all, this is an interesting twist on an old theme. An afterthought: What is the significance of the Lighthouse if any?

history.title: Vera - Series 7 [DVD] [2017]
history.review_title: she is like a general based in a war room
history.text: Season 7 is another triumph for Vera. Four engaging murder mystery episodes on 2 discs comprise this latest offering which follows the format of the six previous seasons. Vera is once again the energetic relentless detective determined to get her man or woman no matter what. With her most able minions, she is like a general based in a war room, planning her strategy, connecting the dots, and pressuring her associates to get the job done. This latest season, like its immediate predecessor, is much brighter and more colorful (literally) than the first four seasons. Filmed in Newcastle and the Northumberland countryside, we have a ringside seat to the action which requires as much physical activity (if not more) than the intellectual side. Based upon characters created by noted mystery writer Ann Cleeves, we are led through a maze of tantalizing clues up to the final denouement. No two episodes in all seven seasons that I have seen are alike. The brilliant originality of the writers stands out on this point. And everything is fully explained and makes sense in the end even if we are thrown an occasional "red herring". I won't repeat any discussion of the individual episodes here which one fine reviewer has already done. Suffice it to say that the fun in watching VERA is not the solution but how she gets there. Indeed, while the episodic conclusion may be an "Aha!" moment, it is the journey that grips our attention. Knowing the outcome, one is often tempted to view an episode again to see how deftly it all comes together. One last caveat: USE THE SUB-TITLES! VERA may be in English but the pronunciation of a number of words is quite different than what an American audience is accustomed to hearing.

history.title: Kept Boy
history.text: This story of a "kept boy" has more substance than one might think when considering the title on its own. It is a real "human" story that shows how true love can manifest itself even though the beginnings of a relationship were based upon monetary considerations and sexual usage. Once again, the complexities of bonding between two people is revealed to be something that is far from simple, and things are not always what they seem. The concern over the possibility of being tossed aside for a younger replacement, the fear of losing what was once bought and now is more meaningful, jealousy, and misunderstanding are all well presented without being trite. The star of this film and its subject, played by Jon Paul Phillips, has the necessary good looks but also has depth. One feels that you are watching the unfolding lives of real people who are relatable and can conjure empathy. While there is nudity (no frontal) in this film and the sex is not hard core, both have a relevant place in the story it is trying to tell. I would give it a soft R. My only criticism of this film is that it seemed rushed and could have been fleshed out more prior to what turned out to be a somewhat surprising but not necessarily unexpected ending.

history.title: Rift
history.text: The jewel case for this DVD, compliments of Iceland, proudly proclaims: "...A Mesmerizing Exercise in LGBT Horror Done Right" and "...An Atmospheric Thriller...". What it really is is an incoherent mish-mash involving two young men whose relationship is on the rocks trying to resolve their differences while occupying an isolated cabin in the Icelandic wilderness. Someone appears to be lurking around. A knocking on their door reveals no one is there when opened. Like a merry-go-round revolving endlessly, this is what this puzzling story seems to feel like. The English sub-titles are so small that this only compounds one's ability to figure out what's going on. In the end, it makes no difference. The only horror here is this piece of trash masquerading as a "horror" film. The LGBT twist is only there to ensnare the unsuspecting LGBT audience. Beware of this "Rift". You might fall in. Caveat Emptor!

history.title: EastSiders Season 3
history.review_title: A ROAD TRIP OF DISCOVERY AND AFFIRMATION
history.text: This season completes (one is tempted to say fulfills) what has become a trilogy in the lives of gay couple Cal (Kit Williamson) and Tom (Van Hansis). From the outset (Season 1), which depicted uncertainty, betrayal, a sense of disconnect, and lack of firm commitment in their relationship - thereby leading to an eventual (and temporary) separation - through a reunion and the rebuilding of trust and acceptance ultimately achieving a positive resolution (Season 2), we are now shown the two as a legitimate intimate loving couple (Season 3). This current "Season" comprises an actual road trip from NY to CA - a return to their original home in more ways than one - which serves as a kind of metaphor for this couple's relationship. Along the way that relationship is tested by a variety of mishaps, challenges, and revelations which inevitably leads to a new understanding, a sincere expression of love, and genuine commitment. This Season is divided into 6 stand alone Episodes that are also interlinked in one way or another. The campiness and shrillness of previous Seasons has been replaced with a much more serious and mature air. (This also applies to all the original characters from past Seasons.) But it is not overbearing and has many a laughable moment. Indeed, it is far more true to life than what you might find in comparable films of this genre. The dialogue (thanks to Kit Williamson) is credible and the behavior is quite natural. As is the case in other movies that revolve around a "road trip", this is also one of discovery. (As an aside, the titles of some of the Episodes is a humorous double entendre.) The acting is uniformly excellent and the entire story is most satisfying and never preachy. There are a couple of noteworthy "cameo" appearances and Traci Lords makes a brief but critical appearance as Cal's mother. With Season 1, I felt that the story of Cal and Tom was a work in progress. I'm happy to say that this work has now been satisfactorily completed. Bravo!

history.title: Stories We Tell
history.text: This is a thoroughly engaging film. I love the narrative voice and think that it is way underutilized in straightforward, dramatic films. This piece is nothing but narrative voices against an excellent visual background. These are real people, sometimes struggling, telling the story of their mother/wife/lover. It is a complete success in drawing you into their world and holding your attention. I considered giving it five stars. Its limitation, I think, is that the mother's secrets were not all that remarkable, far from it, actually. Most of life is, I suppose, not all that remarkable -- the familiar dramatic themes of domestic life tend to play out again and again, which is not to say that we ever should or ever will lose interest in them. But I was somehow set up for some more surprising events that became secrets. I also thought that the film was not really successful in the effort to demonstrate the familiar phenomenon of different observers coming away with different stories -- there was not much disagreement. What we have here is unremarkable human drama in slightly exotic lives told very engagingly and with a lot of feeling. Pretty much anyone raised in a family has equally compelling family material although few would be so successful in bringing it to life on the screen.

history.review_title: Failed attempt to knock off "The Company"
history.text: A production that appears to be inspired by the film, "The Company." Especially obvious was the attempt to reprise the brilliant performance of Malcolm McDowell as the artistic director of a ballet company, now seen as an orchestra conductor/director. What was magic in the "The Company" is ho-hum here, and it may still have been the best thing in the production. Otherwise, it was just a less tasteful and much less convincing swirl of the off-stage lives of the mostly young, sexy artists. (Amazon is wonderful, though, at shipping packages on time and without error.)

history.title: The Appalachians
history.review_title: So much ~bigger~ than I first imagined
history.text: I stumbled on this series as it aired on my local PBS station and ordered it after watching the first episode. I have not yet gotten around to watching my own copy but I keep stumbling across it as it continues to air. Every episode startles me just as the first one did -- it is one majestic story piled upon another. In the beginning, of course, I did not know what I was watching. I first thought it was about the folkways of improvised American religion in the hinterlands. But then it morphed into the wonderful story of Appalachian music, which I supposed to be the wrap-up. Only slowly did I grasp that it is an epic history of a region and its people, profound and heartfelt at every turn. This is a wonderful series; I hope that they are watching it in Manhattan, Hollywood, and wherever clueless elites gather.

history.title: Charlie Rose (February 18, 2005)
history.review_title: Exploitation of the American story...by Charlie Rose
history.text: The asking price for this DVD is obscene. Charlie Rose has a right to be paid for his work...we are not communists, after all. But this strikes me as egregiously exploitative and greedy. Arthur Miller was a profound voice in his literary critique of a certain aspect of American life in the middle of the last century. But that was a half a century ago, and I resent Charlie Rose, Inc. bottling up the later-life reflections of this man and making them available only at an extravagant price. It is Miller, after all, who was an important figure, not the shallow and posturing Charlie Rose. I do not at all deny that Rose -- in his best moments -- has a great interviewer's instinct for going after what is important. But he is very well paid for his work without treating a national treasure as his own property.

history.title: Bicycle Dreams: A Cycling Film [DVD]
history.review_title: Helped me redefine my attitude toward the bike
history.text: I found both this film and the similar "Race Across America" boring and unpleasant. I cared about no one in the films, there is no story nor is there any sense of the magnificent panorama of America rolling by. At some point, grit and heroics (in a pointless endeavor) reveal the tedious characters of the participants. I recognize that with distance cycling -- as in other endurance sports -- the capacity to tolerate the suffering is a big part of the endeavor. Folks who need this are welcome to it, but it is uninteresting as they flatten themselves into this blinkered, one-dimensional obsession. I have recently returned to cycling as a senior citizen after a half dozen years completely off the bike. The recovery of fitness is exhilarating, and I find myself beginning to think about more modestly demanding cycling adventures like a 500-mile, non-competitive tour across my own state. For me, an endeavor of a mere 500 miles (including a couple of mountain days) would be fanatical and desperate and dangerously unhealthy endeavor, although I recognize that it is not at all an unreasonable thing for very fit cyclists who routinely put in a lot of miles. But I turn away from the siren song of the irrelevantly heroic. I will challenge myself within reasonable limits and try to extend myself on the bike, but I will not get crazy. And this RAAM thing is a crazy stunt for anybody. Anybody who could do it is not someone whom I would like to have a beer with or even care about (or want to watch a film about). (All of this cannot help but make me reflect on the Tour de France, which I follow and enjoy. I must say that I have thought a few times that many of the TdF stars are essentially uninteresting and one-dimensional. The Tour, though, is somewhat redeemed for me by the team aspect and all of the complexity and the various goals within the race short of being the overall GC winner. And then there is the fact that the athletes do, at least, sleep at night, eat well, and get a lot care. So it is not like watching to see who can hold his hand in a flame for the longest time.)

history.title: The Story of China with Michael Wood DVD
history.text: Gorgeous. Even more gorgeous than most excellent BBC or National Geographic DVDs on China/India. But beyond the gorgeousness is the fascinating history. I must admit that I am slightly concerned about some criticism I once saw of Michael Woods as perhaps being a better storyteller than a historian. Don't know about that but he certainly is a grand storyteller. I saw part of this on PBS and instantly came here to order it. As I write this review, it is due to be released next week. Edit: Saw more on another PBS showing, the story -- in some detail -- of how a young Chinese seeker (monk?) sometime around the fifth century CE set off on foot to travel west through China skirting the Himalayas, swung around them through Afghanistan, and then trekked eastward into the heart of India. He was after knowledge of Buddhism. After many years he returned bringing many scared scrolls and introduced Buddhism to China. Had adventures, etc. The Emperor was intrigued.

history.title: Clatterford: Season 1 [DVD]
history.text: Sorry but this should be trashed..no story line...just a bunch of real oddballs bumping into each other...and since when is a SEASON three hours...and not three full hours! The third season ends with no explanation...I LOVE PBS but this is as bad as any inane American TV garbage..The writer has run out of steam..not worth watching let alone paying for it. I am really stunned at just how pointless this whole thing is. Lots of talent wasted. Best thing is the scenery. My first real disappointment in over 40 yrs of PBS AWFUL.

history.text: I like both stars of this movie, but can't give it higher than 3 stars...writing is limp and it could have been done in 20 min start to finish. Any other actors and it would be a bomb. Live in NYC and this movie catches all the angst and ick...my opinion but after all that is what this review is about. history.title: Deceived [DVD]
history.text: Goldie Hawn is great in this twisting mystery...very taut WELL written story without the gorey stuff they use now. What happens when you find your partner is not the person you felt was your soulmate, but a cold ,calculating somebody? I highly recommend this..it is not on Netflix etc and so DVD is it but worth it. Made when movies were real entertainment and worth the price of admission...you won't regret buying this!

history.title: Pajanimals: Meet the Pajanimals
history.review_title: Creative characters help kids calm down
history.text: the Pajanimals are a sweet foursome who each night sleep in a large dorm room and have a different topic each episode. Just the rightt balance of sassy and innocence with cute songs and lessons from playing and sharing to conquering the Boogeyman under the bed. Speaking of beds, they fly on one of the beds on learning adventures. Great for afternoon nap or bedtime to wind down after bath. There are several in the series designed by Jim Hensons daughter

history.title: The Second Best Exotic Marigold Hotel
history.text: Most follow up movies are not as good as the first hit. This is comparing apples and oranges a bit but both these Marigold Hotel movies are FEEL GOOD entertainment. The first a group of English retirees head to India to try to live in better comfort on reduced circumstances and arrive at their prepaid ramshackled hotel run by a Pie In the Sky dreamer. Learning to adjust and acclimate requires effort but for most pays off. This is the second follow up and the entire first cast, including Judi Dench, Maggie Smith, Bill Nigh,...then add Mr Gere and one ladies upon seeing him utters Bless my Ovaries...the raciest remark in either movie. The colors , customs, music and dancing are so uplifting and various plots very endearing that the youngsters wedding is the big climax. Indian weddings are legendary . Be sure to watch the Extra bits ...fun hearing the stars talk about the thrill of all coming together again, reactions to Richard Gere, and their love of how the Indians reacted to them returning to film again. This is a movie that can lift your spirits whenever you have " one of those days" ...great script and actors we all know and love. Buy it!

history.title: Barefoot Contessa: Back to Basics
history.text: Ina Garten, The Barefoot Contessa is so pleasant and relaxed she is a pleasure to watch in the kitchen. This series is great for beginners and experienced cooks alike. Fresh ideas to perk up meals with her attitude of How Hard is That? Cooking should be a fun time in the kitchen not a grind. She starts with Chicken 101 with her fabulous roast chicken. Some meals just never lose their appeal and so every Friday she fixes it for her husband. Next is Baking...one episode is all Italian, one French...all are easy to follow and she gives great tips and reasons for doing things as she is doing them. I have cooked for years and still enjoy watching her...Rum Raisin Tiramisu...had to watch that a couple times! Lol this would be a great gift for granddaughters/nieces grandsons/nephews just starting out. Ina was my 4 yr old Grandson's FRIEND...if I watched it while babysitting him he would stand up at 14 mos and wave saying Hi Ina! He really got excited seeing her! Ina makes cooking easy and relaxed...no need to stress out while making great food! Her guests are chefs and people who have a name in food industry, visiting to share some great recipes. Cooking real food from scratch is a necessity with all the chemicals etc in processed /fast food. Highly recommend this and the second season as well!

history.title: Martha Stewart Living Television: Martha's Favorite Cookies, Vol. 10 [DVD]
history.text: Worth every penny! But have to wait u til people stop askin $45 for it! I just couldn't bring myself to pay that kind of money and suddenly a kind person listed for mUCH less! Great recipes and Martha alone in her kitchen...funny thing...all sorts of rumors of her crankiness but she sure knows what she is doing in the kitchen and her demos are so good anyone can learn to cook anything watching her ! The fact that she was the ONLY person who served time for breaking law in investing....ONLY ONE and she did t hurt anyone else...insider info a friend warned her about. She served her sentence and came out and went to town ...can highly recommend any of her videos...I have OLD VHS tapes of her Turkey Hill programs that are GOLD! Lol be patient and wait til someone drops the price ...really great recipes and loads of tips while she makes them!

history.title: Pajanimals: Pajanimals Party
history.text: This is from Jim Henson's daughter...sweet animals who share big dorm bedroom and their problem solving on flying bed...with cute sings and solutions. Good way to get hard charging boys even to wind down and settle before bed! No saccharine here either!

history.text: The show seems to be suffering due to Stars not being committed and into other things. This has only 7 episodes and plays out like a miniseries instead of separate stories. It is dark , grisly, and due to the ploy of saying Amazon streaming , but then only in UK , have frankly lost enthusiasm having to wait a year for 7 episodes. Murdoch Mysteries for instance is making 18 episodes and all actors seem enthusiastically involved.

history.title: Batman: The Killing Joke
history.text: Terrible Batman film. I have read the GN and most of the well-known Batman GNs, as well as having seen most of the animated DCU movies, and this one is the worst WB has produced. It seems rushed to me. There's a lot of pointless back-and-forth banter, a lot of dreadfully dull monolog, and painfully drawn-out scenes (especially with Commissioner Gordon at the amusement park). Even a Batman or DC uber-fan with OCD can skip this without feeling any loss in one's movie library. I did not quite finish it the first time--started skipping thru the pointless scenes, and even the ending was deflated and anti-climatic. If I owned this bluray, I would never watch it again. Thankfully, I rented it. Which is kind of unusual; I tend to read reviews and buy a lot of movies, but "redboxed" this one. I suggest you do the same before buying.

history.title: Logan
history.review_title: Academic exploration of the psychological impact of f___ inundation for 2 hours
history.text: Disney used to make child-friendly movies. Marvel used to make good films. Ah, I miss the good-old-days... Remember X-MEN? Such a great film. By the way, shame on you, Patrick Stewart! First, for being in this crapfest, and second, for reading your lines. A classically trained actor who could have demanded that Xavier would never have spoken in such a manner, especially in front of a child, and doubly especially in front of a mutant child. SHAME! All of this is sarcasm, by the way, Marvel fans. I have a suggestion to improve your grammar and intelligence: put the comics away for a while and read some real literature. If you want to see a very detailed example of a review, see my opinion piece on Ghost in the Shell. I don't waste that kind of time on crap like this one.

history.title: The Lord of the Rings: Original Theatrical Trilogy (Triple Feature BD) [Blu-ray]
history.text: I wanted to share a review of this edition (http://www.amazon.com/dp/B0086B89JO/) for those of you looking for a good, affordable edition of the trilogy. There are two new sets including The Hobbit trilogy that I didn't want, but you may enjoy one of those if you're a fan of Tolkien and have never purchased them before (one is Extended, the other is Theatrical, both with all 6 films). I've owned many versions of LOTR over the years, starting with the basic DVDs, then the extended DVDs (bookshelf format), and settled on the extended blu-ray release in the beautiful gold case. I love that edition. However the extended editions become tiresome after viewing every year for the last 15 years. Sometimes they're just too long! That's why I bought this edition, to continue our family tradition of watching them every Christmas, without the exhaustion of all of Jackson's unnecessary stuff (including Bilbo's kitchen sink). This theatrical version can be had for around $15 and each film is less than 3 hours long. Perfect!

history.title: Ghost in the Shell Arise: Borders 1-2
history.review_title: Bit of a slow start but picks up in eps 3-4
history.text: These first two episodes were a bit slow going and a bit rough around the edges, so to speak. I enjoyed this prequel series and found the new character artwork and voice acting refreshing but it was a slow start with a vague plot. In contrast, episodes 3 & 4 are much more familiar to a Stand Alone Complex fan with hard-hitting bang-em-up action and intense cyber warfare, "in the trenches." That's okay. There were some slow eps of SAC as well. I feel it's helpful to note that SAC episodes were 20 minutes long each, so what we have here is equivalent (overall between Borders 1-4) are 12 episodes of comparable length to SAC eps. Not bad at all. The 1-hour format was done to tap into the "American recipe" with popular shows like 24 (according to director

history.title: Ghost in the Shell: Arise - Borders 3 & 4 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Good prequel series but not easy to understand for a newcomer
history.text: Similar to my review of 1 & 2. I enjoyed this prequel story. The new character artwork and voice acting was refreshing but it was a slow start with a vague plot. Episodes 3 & 4 (this one) are much more familiar to a Stand Alone Complex fan with hard-hitting bang-em-up action and intense cyber warfare. I don't expect a non-fan to buy this show. It probably doesn't make any sense unless you've seen the movies and previous series. Despite being a prequel. Character development is nonexistent here, that's a clear flaw (which I did not take a star off for, because I feel they made this for fans, not trying to capture a new audience). SAC episodes were 20 minutes long each so the two 1-hour episodes here are equivalent to 6 in the old series. That's good. It's more than it seems.

history.title: The Thing
history.review_title: Excellent prequel with much replay value and a great companion to JC's original
history.text: Having just bought and watched [[ASIN:B01GSW5VD4 The Thing [Collector's Edition] [Blu-ray]]] (an extraordinary release), I decided to revisit the prequel and found I had not reviewed it. I enjoyed this film by Matthijs van Heijningen. There is a mix of puppetry and CGI, and you can tell but still, kudos for the effort. I genuinely enjoy the portrayal of the Norwegian camp which was such a gory scene in Carpenter's film. I enjoy watching these two back-to-back. Heijningen did a good job of capturing Carpenter's original claustrophobic feel as the team mistrusts each other. Generally, I only buy films I intend to watch 2+ times, which is how I judge a film, more or less: the repeat value. There are some films I enjoyed but never want to see again (such as Arrival), which might be well done but I have no desire to buy the BD. That ultimately affects my opinion of a film, and that is why I have such mixed feelings about films by M. Night Shyamalan and tend not to buy them. He's a brilliant writer/director who knows how to create a tense scene. But, when the tension is released, it can't be recreated a 2nd time. That's just my personal opinion and how I rate movies. I might give a film like Arrival 5 stars, but never want to see it again nor own a copy. This prequel to Carpenter's The Thing was well done. I understand the opinions of others and disagree. The CGI was not "atrocious" as one reviewer poorly observed. It was actually very well done, and done in conjunction with some real physical effects. You can tell a couple of times but those are the exceptions. And, one might argue that today, it would not be possible to recreate Carpenter's film with such effects because those techniques are a lost art. Well, it's highly subjective at any rate. Being a fan, I may be more forgiving, but in my opinion, being a hardcore fan of the JC film, I found that this one similarly scared me, and repeat viewings continue to scare me. That's a successful horror film in my opinion. I give this 5 stars because I loved it. I'm a fan of THIS material and a horror fan AND a sci-fi fan as well. I'm subjective. This may not be a 5-star movie compared to, say, The Fellowship of the Ring. Just as a comparison. But films should not be compared directly to each other, nor across genres. How does this compared to the JC film? It's like a kid brother or a son. Son of The Thing. Watch them back-to-back, starting here, and enjoy all of the recreated scenes, and ask yourself, does this film contribute positively? The answer is absolutely yes, it does. Together, it's 3.5 hours of fright and I won't take off stars for CGI or little-known actors or poor character development. I'll just sit back and enjoy it and pick up the popcorn every time I spill it.

history.title: Passengers [Blu-ray]
history.text: Probably entertaining if you're not a real science fiction fan and enjoy characters with the emotional depth of a rock. The bartender was funny, the actor somewhat reprising his role as Castor. I rate movies based on whether I'll ever watch them again. If it's entertaining but stupid, I won't buy the bluray. There are sometimes worse ways to waste 2 hours of your life, I say, and I don't mind that I watched it. But, I could have taken it or left it (note the grammar there, kids, and please start using that cliche correctly). 2.5 stars because if I give it 2, I'll get censored.

history.title: Ghost in the Shell: The New Movie
history.text: I didn't really "get" this film. I own every show and film from the series and watched Arise several times, but this film was confusing and scattered. I did not enjoy it aside from the visuals and characters I enjoy. The plot requires multiple viewings and that's a failure. It is not even in the same ballpark as Solid State Society. I became kind of irritated after the halfway point. I think this was just another group of "episodes" of Arise bundled into a film. A lot of style over substance, unfortunately. 3 stars is generous.

history.title: Night of the Living Dead - 50th Anniversary [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Horrible!! It's not even VHS quality!
history.text: Horrible. Absolutely horrible. Looks like a web video upscaled to DVD and then upscaled again to 1080p. I'm sending it back to Amazon. Mill Creek is taking advantage of this public domain film and screwing customers with their lies. This is not 1080p, it is upscaled, and the DIGITAL copy is BS--it's a HTML5 web video that you have to watch in a WEB BROWSER. On their site! Why didn't Romero's company renew the copyright on this film so we wouldn't have to put up with charlatans like Mill Creek? Anyone, and I mean anyone, can download the PD version of the film and burn it to a BD and produce a cool-looking cover art and sell it on Amazon these days. Shame on you, Amazon! I am a Prime customer and expect better product filtering than this.

history.title: The Mummy Ultimate Collection [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Just buy the first two films instead
history.text: This was well worth the cost since I got it at a steep discount, but even at full retail it's a fair value if you are a fan of the series. However, in my opinion, only the first two films are worth watching unless you're a hardcore fan of the genre. For instance, I also own the Universal Monsters collection and this is an enjoyable follow-up of the original B&W Mummy film. Which... when you think about it.... should have been included in an "Ultimate Collection", right? This is the ultimate farce if that's the measure of the word. But in fairness, it's the ultimate collection of the NEW films. Okay, whatever. The Tomb of the Dragon Emperor is SO HORRENDOUS that I simply could not finish it this time through. I'd watched it on release many years ago and thought it was passable but not this time, especially not after becoming a bigger fan of Rachel Weisz. Replacing her was a disaster. They should have modified the stupid script instead of replacing her because her fill-in was terrible. And, no offense to the actress, but she had an impossible task and should not have taken the job. But, it beats spending a few minutes alone with Weinstein to get ahead, right? No, seriously, this film is a plot disaster and it's unwatchable. The Scorpion King is kind of fun and funny as an early role for The Rock (his first film?). It was a bit too comical, but I think Johnson is a natural entertainer after his years in the wrestling ring (er, box--why do they call it a ring?). If I were doing this again, I'd just buy the first two Mummy films and call it a day. The first one is the best, of course. Lots of humor missing in the follow-ups.

history.title: Noah (Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD)
history.text: and yes, this movie is different from any other previous film versions of Noah! The Bible does say that 'in those days, there were giants in the land'...the Watchers. I think the stone beings are an interesting interpretation of this part of the scripture. The entire Bible is read with 'man's interpretation. I'm sure there were parts of this movie where artistic license was used, but Cecil B. DeMille also used this process throughout his bibical interpretations. I enjoyed this movie and the fact that it makes you think and sometimes draw your own conclusions. Great acting by all, eye-catching special effects and tense and beautiful music scoring. I will add both movie and soundtrack to my collection!

history.title: Walk On The Wild Side
history.text: Just discovered this gem. Fabulous acting by all, but I'm a big fan of Anne Baxter and Barbara Stanwyck, so will need to add to my collection! The score is by the wonderful and talented Elmer Bernstein, so you can' go wrong with that as well. I highly recommend this motion picture! Five Stars!!!

history.title: Into the Grizzly Maze
history.text: Great movie with great cast! I love Thomas Jane and had only seen James Marsden in one other movie. Both guys were very solid male leads and playing brothers gave the movie a great plot twist and backstory. This movie is action packed and a total thrill ride! Highly recommended!

history.title: Brokeback Mountain [Blu-ray]
history.text: A Beautiful film from beginning to end! Applause for all involved in this film. Each time I watch it I truly believe it should have won the Oscar for best film. Ang Lee's direction is moving and all performances are awe inspiring!!

history.title: The Beverly Hillbillies: The Official First Season [DVD]
history.review_title: Can't wait for the entire first season of this beloved ...
history.text: Can't wait for the entire first season of this beloved show! Fans have waited patiently for a long time! Thanks again and hopefully we'll see the fifth season coming soon as well!

history.title: Ben-Hur
history.review_title: Not even close to the original!
history.text: I saw enough in the trailer to know the remake could never live up to the original 1959 classic, which is in my top 5 movies of all time (#4 to be exact). Next Hollywood will try for "Gone With The Wind" and "The Wizard Of Oz". Paramount would have done better if they bought the original from MGM and showed it again in movie theaters across the country.

history.title: Jurassic World [Blu-ray]
history.text: If you are looking for an intense fun filled adventure ride, then look no further! This movie has great thrills and wonderful casting, especially Chris Pratt and Bryce Dallas Howard! Five stars!!!

history.title: Vacancy
history.text: Great suspense film! This film really delivers if you love horror and suspense and edge of your seat action/tension. Add to your collection!

history.title: I Know What You Did Last Summer, When a Stranger Calls, Vacancy - BD Triple Feature [Blu-ray]
history.text: Love all of these films and to have in one collection on blu ray is great!

history.title: Walker Texas Ranger: Season 7
history.text: Love Chuck Norris! As it turns out, I missed quite a few episodes back in the day from season 7, so my husband and I are enjoying the season very much.

history.title: Red 2 [Blu-ray, DVD, Digital HD]
history.text: FUN! FUNNY! Did I say fun? When I'm in the mood for something light-hearted and silly, I watch either "Red" or "Red 2". The ensemble cast work great together and the characters they came up with and portray are so, so, uh, funny! : ) Did I say funny? Enjoy!

history.title: Agatha Christie's Poirot, Series 13
history.review_title: Gonna miss you, Poirot--these are great btw!
history.text: Gonna miss Poirot. These final 5 episodes are a nice way to say goodbye to Poirot and many favorite characters from the series. David Suchet IS Poirot. If you wanna see the final brand new episodes ever starring David Suchet, this is it. Enjoy!

history.title: The Hobbit: The Battle of The Five Armies
history.review_title: Strays from the book but not so far that you can't have a good time with it!
history.text: Strays from the book but not so far that you can't have a good time with it! We thought the first two Hobbit movies tedious and often so far from the book we loved, we could barely stand watching them. Also, they seemed to have been stretched out with plenty of nonsense, mostly not in the book, they just seemed like money makers for Peter Jackson because the Hobbit story could have been done justice in two movies. However, this final installment is loads of fun/excitement, not tedious at all and close enough to a beloved book, we're gonna give it five stars when we only gave the first two awful ones one star each. If you watched the first two movies and were as disappointed as we were, you might give this one a try. Its not strictly by the book, but we think you will like it.

We're big Harry Boesche/Michael Connelly fans and after viewing 3 episodes of this series, are pretty pleased and entertained! I recognize some of the story lines from the books but since its been years since I listened to many, I am okay with that. My husband has only listened to a few of the newer Michael Connelly books, so this "Bosch", which seems to stretch back a ways, is brand new to him. We're gonna continue to watch and hope the quality of the first 3 episodes continues. Right now, great big thumbs up!

Amazon's "copy" of this excellent, fun movie is HORRIBLE! It looks like some old boot legged copy you might recall from old VHS tape days that is how bad it is. It is both grainy and lacking in color.

history.review_title: In the mood for absolute silliness? This is the movie : )
history.text: If you're in the mood for absolute silliness, and the stupid kind at that, then this is the movie for you! There are so many laugh out loud moments like what amounts to a male model music video plus Orange Julius--trust me, you'll laugh your butt off, and this movie is crawling with really funny celebrity cameos too. A little David Bowie anyone? It is adult themed tho and I would not advise this a good movie for family movie night.

history.review_title: Amazon Original Bosch bogged down in soap opera morass
history.text: While my husband and I are big Michael Connelly, Harry Bosch fans and greatly enjoyed season 1 based heavily on a Harry Bosch novel/mystery, season 2 strayed from the books and began sliding into the soap opera morass. We did actually make it through season 2 and held out hope that season 3 would be more in line with season 1. It was not. Tonight, as a Father's Day treat, we began watching season 3. By episode 3 of season 3, we couldn't bear to watch anymore. The stories/mysteries are bogged down by time wasting and stretching politics not in the books and not to mine and my husband's liking. We want Bosch, not the soap opera garbage. No more Amazon Original Bosch for us. If I could have given this zero stars, I would have.

history.title: My Life in Ruins
history.review_title: Cute, romantic comedy with fantastic Greek settings!
history.text: Cute, romantic comedy filmed in Greece. Given locations, pretty danged awesome! Nia Vardalous, Richard Dreyfus and cast of comedic characters, endearing.

history.title: The Magnificent Seven [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: GREAT movie in the vein of original with awesome conclusion
history.text: GREAT movie! Much of it filmed in New Mexico (beautiful!), in the vein of the original movie. Terrific cast. Conclusion worth the wait! Especially enjoyed Denzel and Pratt.

history.title: King Kong Lives [DVD]
history.review_title: An absolute horror in every way!
history.text: When I first went to see the 1976 remake of the 1933 original I was sickened over what I saw as I am a fanatical fan of the original. I figured it couldn't get much worse. Well I was wrong. I actually spent money to see this trash with two friends and other than one other person, we were the only ones in the theater. This made me watch the original yet another time in order to cleanse myself of this crap. If I could give it a minus-1 star I would.

history.title: It Happens Every Spring
history.review_title: Great Family Movie With Plenty Of Laughs
history.text: Very entertaining movie with quite a few belly laughs to boot. The scene where the catcher has the wooden splint on his hand is a riot as every time he tries to pick up the ball it just proceeds to move away from him. The hair brush scene is priceless. Just a fun movie that the entire family can watch rather than the usual R-rated junk that's put out there today.

history.title: Daryl Hall & John Oates Live in Dublin
history.review_title: Great Concert - Video sound better than the CDs
history.text: This is a great concert to say the least. Daryl Hall sounds great considering his age. The DVD sounds great, but the CDs were recorded too loud, but that is nothing new since no one seems to care about good dynamic range anymore. A great jam on "I Can't Go For That" and a good mix of their hits. 4 stars only because the CDs are too loud.

history.title: Wages Of Spin
history.review_title: Dick Clark - Not who you thought he was
history.text: This Phila based documentary shows the business side of the record industry in the 1950's. Dick Clark was not the goody-2-shoes we all thought he was. He knew how to make money and he didn't care who he stepped on to get it. Just pay attention to what happened to Charlie Gracie.

history.title: Gracie, Charlie - Fabulous
history.review_title: Great Story of a Great Performer
history.text: Just saw Charlie Gracie perform at a local pub and he was fantastic - or should I say "Fabulous". At 79 years old he plays the guitar like a youngster. His story is fascinating to say the least as he never got the fame he deserved. Glad to see that over the years great performers like Paul McCartney and Van Morrison and Graham Nash have given him his just due. Get the DVD "Wages Of Spin" to get a further insight into what happened to Charlie back in the 1950's. If you live in the Philadelphia area you have to go see him today to believe how good he still is. He has a website that lists his play dates in the area. You won't be disappointed.

history.title: Rust Never Sleeps
history.text: Purchased this hoping that the sound was going to be better than my old lp record of this concert. I was not disappointed as this was a great performance with great sound. The stage antics of the urchins running around was so typical of Neil as he was never a conformist and does what he wants to do. This was not a distraction. Video was very good. I always want to hear "Cowgirl In The Sand" and "Down By The River" but I guess he was tired of playing them so many times prior. All in all Neil fans will not be disappointed - great concert !

history.review_title: Not Even Close To Being Funny
history.text: Zero stars is what this deserves. Not even close to being funny. It is 100% crude and unlike the original series of movies it's rated R so you can't bring a 10 year old to see this movie. If you do you you'll find out why it's rated R. This also had to be made by some very liberal people who made sure that got every progressive message out there. A true embarrassment.

history.title: Motown 25: Yesterday Today Forever
history.review_title: The Motown Family at their best
history.text: Although this is a 3 disk set you only need to watch the one disk of the actual show. It's unbelievable to see the talent pool that Motown was. There is nothing today that compares to this music and the presentations. Someone like Beyoncé, who is a talent, doesn't come close to these performances. Back then you didn't come on the stage via a trapeze or a rocket ship or some sort of distraction. You also didn't come out half naked which is also a distraction from the actual talent of the performers. You heard the Motown sound without any amped up productions. The music itself was great and still trumps most anything today when it comes to some sort of soulful music. The bonus material is plentiful and enjoyable to watch. You will not be disappointed with this package.

history.title: The Strawberry Blonde
history.text: Set at a time around the turn of the 20th century this is an entertaining movie topped off by the great acting of Olivia Dehavilland and James Cagney. Of course today this movie comes across at times as a little corny, but on the other hand it represents a time when you didn't need to have filthy language and sex scenes. Multiple stories wrapped into one overall plot that gets a good message across - be certain of what you want before you get it. Along the way there are many laughs that make this a completely enjoyable movie.

It just brings back memories of the 1960's when there were a multitude of great groups and performers. This was raw talent at it's best that didn't require stage antics like today's so-called singers and groups. Joan Baez's version of "You've Lost That Lovin' Feeling" was actually pretty good. The Byrds and Lovin' Spoonful came in strong as well.

history.text: Artwork is good. Story isn't really there though. It really comes down to it's too much for a movie. Mystery stranger possibly from another world, don't have time to flesh that out so he will just wander in and out mysteriously. Beautiful woman running darkside of Tokyo, no time for that she will just claim to run everything while not accomplishing anything. Evil organization trying to control the world (why? that's just what they do) and kill everybody(why? again, just what they do), is sending deadly assassins to kill a rebel. The assassins come with extreme abilities some are enhanced humans(not explained) and others have psycic or magical powers(again not explained). Lone surviving rebel of a group that tried to take down this evil corp.,his group is unexplained, reasons untold, he is there to bring the characters together for a common goal, and we've run out of time ending the struggle continues. Feel satisfied? I don't.

history.text: I love these and I'll keep my eye out for more every year. Past editions are great as well. So many great speakers and leaders and teaching to help people develop greater influence for greater purposes. I'm thankful they keep putting these on DVD so I and others who could not make it to the Summit can benefit from that gathering. I'm one who mostly waits until people sell their used one so I can get it more affordably but the wait is worth it if you have to go that route as well.

history.text: Wow! I just watched it last night and I was surprised at how this movie held my attention. There are incredible people doing incredible things led by the Spirit of God. A wonderful film.

history.title: Dear Frankie
history.text: It's been a while since I have seen this movie but I remember being impressed by the heartfelt story. Dear Frankie is one of those when you finish it you say to yourself, "That was a find!" This is not a flashy film but a more subdued life telling. Treat yourself and watch it.

history.text: So slow and boring. Great director and this won awards for wardrobe and background stuff, but it showcased a movie to miss. This was rated pretty high by many and I was led to believe this would be worth my time and it isn't. Try something else.

history.title: Taking Chance
history.text: This movie has stayed with me. The word that comes to mind most strongly is Honor. It is rare how full of honor throughout we are given privy to. Kevin Bacon gives what I feel is his best performance. The scenes as his character makes the journey across America are memorable and moving. I'm glad I got the opportunity to watch this and you will too.

history.title: Shanghai Calling
history.review_title: Good fish out of water story
history.text: I love this kind of story. It's a fish out of water concept with the main character moving to China for work as he tries to climb the ladder of success. Along the way he encounters interesting people and situations that causes him to rethink his life, solve main problems and end up a changed person. I love that it involves some of the slice of life of expats working and living in such a big and beautiful up and coming city. They make light of how it is always under construction. There are the scenes you assume will come with the usual misunderstandings and stepping on toes of misunderstood cultural cues. Daniel Henney was a good lead, it was great to see Eliza Coupe in her role and Bill Paxton was a bonus.

history.title: MacArthur
history.text: This movie production was terrible! It feels as if it were shot by a high school student film class. The people were always underexposed so they were always acting in shadows. The background was always overexposed (so you couldn't see people's faces). There was always an annoying glow around the actor's faces when they were standing in front of a window or doorway. The camera crew didn't know the first thing about cinematography or composition! This movie was too painful to watch. All Gregory Peck did was walk around here & there trying to emote. Patton with George C. Scott was so much better! I wish they would get better directors & producers for films military biography films. They destroyed the life & image of the greatest American General in history!

history.review_title: Good history until 1944, good quality for the set
history.text: The first three (of five) disks of this set are very good, although I find the bells that probably sounded for commercial breaks get pretty annoying. Bert Lancaster is a good narrator/host, and for the first time in some time I saw films of the Russian Front I haven't already seen a dozen times. But disk four and beyond, which deals with the "liberation" of Poland and other eastern European states through the defeat of Germany, are so heavy with Soviet propaganda (they insisted on reviewing and probably rewriting every aspect of the series) that, considering what hell they brought to those "liberated" territories, are too much to swallow. DVD quality and sound are good and as I said, there's a lot here that you won't see on other disks even 40 years after their release, so I do recommend them.

history.title: Ultimate Civil War Series
history.review_title: A worthwhile video set at a very reasonable price
history.text: This is one of the better CW sets using reenactors and historical photos. The narrative and use of exerpts is good; the narrator and readers have pleasant voices without the hokey Southern and hick Northern accents common in these sets. The information is good; I've found a few things I disagree with factually but nothing glaring such as Grant participating at Perrysville in 1862 that's in one of my dvd sets. The reenactments are satisfactory although the scenery is the typical generic background of most reenactments; I would have liked to have seen a little more use of maps and photos though. I tell you one thing I absolutely love about this set is the intro segment. I have no idea if the music is original or taking from somewhere else, but I absolutely love it. It has a lovely brass heroic-tragic sound with various reenactment shots in the background. Note the drum-cannon segue into 1863-beautifully coordinated.

history.title: The Unknown Civil War Series: Gettysburg
history.review_title: and thought I'd love to see this done for the American Civil War
history.text: I recently purchased the "Battlefield" WWII series and admired its in-depth analysis of various battles, and thought I'd love to see this done for the American Civil War. This isn't quite it, but it's close enough to satisfy me. This 3-disk set covers each of the 3 days of battle, as well as some of the people, both military and civilian who fought or were affected by this huge and complex battle. I've studied the Civil War for decades and was aware of Jenny Wade, the only civilian death, and of Tillie Pierce, a Gettysburg resident whose writings have been featured on several books and disks about Gettysburg, including Ken Burns' honored series, but I never knew anything about her or of her amazing (and horrifying) experiences. My wife, who isn't exactly a history buff, was mesmerized with this series as we marathoned the entire series. Including closed captioning, my only beef with the disks is that it doesn't have a play all feature, which isn't much of a beef for an 11+ hours series. I highly recommend it.

history.title: Greatest Battles of the Civil War
history.review_title: Greatest Battles of the Civil War: Here's what you get.
history.text: Something that bothers me with buying videos online (and sometimes in the store) is wondering what's in the package. So, if you purchase this video, this is what you get: 8 episodes on two disks: Disc One: Antietam, Appomattox campaign, Gettysburg, Chancellorsville. Disc Two: Chickamauga, Shiloh, Petersburg Campaign, Vicksburg. "Unknown Civil War" does a pretty good and fair job of covering the people and places involved in these battles. I have the 3-DVD "UCW" on the Battle of Gettysburg and am well pleased with all of them. I do wonder why they call their series "The Unknown Civil War" though; I did learn a few new things but almost everything they cover can be found in almost any book on the particular battle or in general histories like Stephen Sears, Shelby Foote or James McPherson. I have an obscure set of disks called "America: Stories of War" that gives excellent coverage of Wilson's Creek and Perryville. Battles like these are the "unknown" war to most casual readers/viewers IMO. Each episode is approximate 50 minutes; all are narrated by Stephen Lang (Gettysburg, Gods & Generals) My only complaints are why it's called "The Unknown Civil War." With the exception of the Appomattox and Petersburg campaigns, I've seen numerous discs on the other battles. I was hoping for information on some of the more obscure and "unknown Civil War" battles likes Mill Springs, Perryville, Springfield MO, Corinth etc. But I do enjoy the treatment of the battles provided. Second, no subtitles although these are taken from the UCW series on the History Channel, and third no "play all." I take away a star for the last two factors.

history.title: Feud Season 1
history.review_title: Feuds are never about hate. Feuds are about pain.
history.text: The feud between Bette Davis and Joan Crawford was an unusually memorable one, particularly since both actresses were sharp-tongued, strong-willed and superstars. So it isn't surprising that "Feud Season 1: Bette and Joan" has plenty of material to chew on, as it explores the movie they made together, the Oscar competition that followed, and the final years of Joan Crawford's life. But it does more than give us a juicy campy mess -- this is ultimately a rather sad, tragic tale about the way older women are treated in Hollywood, and the loneliness that came with it. In the early sixties, Joan Crawford (Jessica Lange) is in dire financial straits, but also disgusted by the kinds of roles she's being offered. So she pitches a movie adaptation of the book "Whatever Happened To Baby Jane?" to director Robert Aldrich (Alfred Molina), and recommends Bette Davis (Susan Sarandon) as her costar -- despite the fact that they have hated each other for years. Aldrich manages to convince the embittered studio head Jack Warner (Stanley Tucci) to let him make the movie. The sharp-tongued Bette and proud Joan immediately rub each other the wrong way, but they join forces to keep the movie on track... or at least, they do until Warner orders Aldrich to keep them at each other's throats. The feud blossoms into all-out war as the women fight using sex, power and on-set tricks. But things become even worse after the movie becomes a surprise hit, and Bette is nominated for an Oscar -- and the industry approval -- that Joan craves, sending Joan into a desperate spiral. And with no good cinematic roles coming in (think "Strait-Jacket," "Trog" and a bunch of TV roles), the two are cast opposite each other in another "hagsploitation" film -- only to clash even more violently, in a way that could derail the entire film. "Feud: Bette and Joan" is an interesting experience. It starts off deliciously snipey and campy -- Hedda Hopper and her faaaaaaabulous hats swan through periodically, sniping breezily; Bette and Joan insult each other constantly, and Tucci's Warner chews the scenery with aplomb. It just wallows in the glamorous surroundings and barbed dialogue for the first few episodes, occasionally pausing for a glimpse of the troubles of the women's lives. And creator/partial-director Ryan Murphy plays this up even further -- he embraces the cheesy, horroresque camera angles and cuts, such as zooming in on Bette's angry, rigid face. And the steel-corded tension between the actresses keeps you on the edge of your seat as they both walk a tightrope of mutual dislike and respect. You never know what will set them off. But as the story unfolds, it begins to lose that campy flavor, and becomes something else. It becomes a rather tragic tale of loneliness, aging, mortality, rejection and the hollowness of fame -- these talented women struggle to experience love from both audiences and their own children, and are treated viciously even when they prove themselves profitable. This is especially true of Crawford, whom we see being bitterly lonely away from the mainstream Hollywood limelight, always craving love and acceptance from those around her, but never able to fully enjoy it. And Jessica Lange does an absolutely stellar job as Crawford -- despite the woman's narcissism and often-selfish actions, you can't help but feel sorry for her because she seems so unhappy, and because she craves approval. Sarandon doesn't look much like Davis, but she has the vicious barbs and pursed lips down to an art form, and on the rare moments when Davis is caught off guard, you see glimpses of a similarly unhappy woman under her thick armor. The supporting cast is almost uniformly awesome as well -- Jackie Hoffman as Crawford's stoic, brutally-honest sidekick, Judy Davis as Hedda Hopper, Tucci as the cruelly enthusiastic and misogynistic studio head, Molina as a harried director with his own set of insecurities, and Alison Wright as his long-suffering assistant who dreams of directing her own movie. Oh, and Catherine Zeta-Jones and Kathy Bates have fun recurring cameos as two other golden-age actresses who offer their own opinions and experiences. "Feud Season 1: Bette and Joan" is more than a guilty pleasure -- it's both a juicy exploration of a feud, and a tragic look at what women still struggle against today. Fun, sad, wild and insane.

history.title: The Mummy (2017) [DVD]
history.text: Since every movie franchise now has to be a cinematic universe, Universal decided to dig up up all their old movie monsters and fling them into new, flashier films. And their most recent dead-on-arrival attempt to revive their shared universe was “The Mummy,” a remake/reboot-but-not-really of previous films about an undead horror rising from the tomb… except they pretty much abandoned any actual material from those movies except “there’s a mummy, and a giant screamy face.” Instead, they present a mass of action cliches without a hint of irony, dressing it up with a “sexy” mummy and a crammed-in starting point for the Dark Universe. During an airstrike, soldier-of-fortune/looter Nick Morton (Tom Cruise) accidentally uncovers an Egyptian tomb buried under a town… in Iraq. Even the movie is aware of how strange that is. They just happen to have an archaeologist (Annabelle Wallis) on hand, who discovers this was the tomb of Ahmonet, an Egyptian princess whose lust for power caused her to sell her soul to Set, murder her family, and be mummified alive for her crimes. Never mind that the process of mummification would kill you. But things immediately start going wrong — the plane carrying her sarcophagus crashes, Nick temporarily dies, and then he is haunted by visions of a bandaged woman stalking him through the mist. He’s been cursed by her, and she wants to use him as the vessel for Set. And even when Ahmonet is captured by a Super-Sekrit Organization (like S.H.I.E.L.D., but less competent), Nick finds that he may have no hope of escaping her grasp. “The Mummy” is very much a MOAR action movie. Moar mummies. Moar crashes. Moar fistfights. Moar ‘splosions. Moar attractive women. Moar boogity-boo scares. Moar moar moar. This movie feels almost like a parody of a Hollywood action-horror movie, ticking off all the cliches and never bothering to do anything that we haven’t seen before… but without a sense of humor or self-awareness that everything in its story has been done before. Instead, we’re pelted with so many cliches that it feels like the studio raided TV Tropes. And as a result, its massive, bombastic nature seems like a storm conjured up to try to hide the fact that the plot is as thin as papyrus — and it’s definitely not scary, or as funny as it thinks it is (haha, Nick is naked!). There are a few spooky moments here and there, mostly when we see Ahmanet scuttling around in her undead state, looking like an arthritic Gollum. But more often we just careen from place to place, following Nick and Boring Blonde as they lurch from one crisis to another, building up zero momentum as they go. And as if to show the lack of care that went into it, there are also blatant fails at Egyptian mythology (Set as the god of death), ancient Egyptian culture, etymology (Jekyll claims “Satan” is an alternate name for Set) and history (what would the Crusaders have been doing in what is now Iraq? Being horribly lost?). Tom Cruise is… Tom Cruise. Despite playing a looter, liar and thief, we’re clearly meant to be charmed by his roguish one-liners and occasional moments of not-totally-self-centered-ness. But when you boil him down, there isn’t really anything about the character to like or be interested in, which makes Wallis’ Boring Blonde’s transition from contempt to love seem even more ridiculously artificial. And Russell Crowe plays a woefully unimposing Dr. Jekyll, who predictably transitions into a ludicrously unscary, scenery-chewing Mr. Hyde. Sofia Boutella does an excellent job with what little material she has; she seems to have been hired mostly because she can scuttle, scamper and bend a lot. Unfortunately, she’s simply not frightening here — her version of a mummy is too wriggly, weak and ALIVE to ever be a properly undead fright. She looks and acts more like a gymnast in a mummy-themed unitard. “The Mummy” has a few good spots that haven’t been totally dried out, but the withered hulk is just a standard Hollywood blockbuster — lots of sound and fury, signifying that the Dark Universe was dead on arrival.

Since every movie franchise now has to be a cinematic universe, Universal is digging up all their old movie monsters and flinging them into new, flashier films. And the first of those is "The Mummy," a remake/reboot-but-not-really of the previous films about an undead horror rising from the tomb... except they pretty much abandon any actual material from those movies except "there's a mummy, and a giant screamy face." Instead, they present a mass of cinematic and/or mummy cliches without a hint of irony, dressing it up with a "sexy" mummy and a crammed-in starting point for the Dark Universe. During an airstrike, soldier-of-fortune/looter Nick Morton (Tom Cruise) accidentally uncovers an Egyptian tomb buried under a town... in Iraq. Even the movie is aware of how strange that is. They just happen to have an archaeologist (Annabelle Wallis) on hand, who discovers this was the tomb of Ahmanet, an Egyptian princess whose lust for power caused her to sell her soul to Set, murder her family, and be mummified alive for her crimes. Never mind that the process of mummification would kill you. But things immediately start going wrong -- the plane carrying her sarcophagus crashes, Nick temporarily dies, and then he is haunted by visions of a bandaged woman stalking him through the mist. He's been cursed by her, and she wants to use him as the vessel for Set. And even when Ahmonet is captured by a Super-Sekrit Organization (like S.H.I.E.L.D. but less competent), Nick finds that he may have no hope of escaping her grasp. "The Mummy" is very much a MOAR action movie. Moar mummies. Moar crashes. Moar fistfights. Moar 'splosions. Moar attractive women. Moar boogity-boo scares. Moar moar moar. This movie feels almost like a parody of a Hollywood action-horror movie, ticking off all the cliches and never bothering to do anything that we haven't seen before... but without a sense of humor or self-awareness that everything in its story has been done before. Instead, we're pelted with so many cliches that it feels like the studio raided TV Tropes. And as a result, its massive, bombastic nature seems like a storm conjured up to try to hide the fact that the plot is as thin as papyrus -- and it's definitely not scary, or as funny as it thinks it is (haha, Nick is naked!). There are a few spooky moments here and there, mostly when we see Ahmanet scuttling around in her undead state, looking like an arthritic Gollum. But more often we just careen from place to place, following Nick and Boring Blonde as they lurch from one crisis to another, building up zero momentum as they go. And as if to show the lack of care that went into it, there are also blatant fails at Egyptian mythology (Set as the god of death), ancient Egyptian culture, etymology (Jekyll claims "Satan" is an alternate name for Set) and history (what would the Crusaders have been doing in what is now Iraq? Being horribly lost?). Tom Cruise is... Tom Cruise. Despite playing a looter, liar and thief, we're clearly meant to be charmed by his roguish one-liners and occasional moments of not-totally-self-centered-ness. But when you boil him down, there isn't really anything about the character to like or be interested in, which makes Wallis' Boring Blonde's transition from contempt to love seem even more ridiculously artificial.
