history.title: Hot Tub Time Machine
history.review_title: Not recommended for Noel Coward fans or those with a more refined sense of humor
history.text: 2.5 stars for this sophmoric tale of 3 schlubs (and a nephew) who were buds in the 80's but now have drifted apart leading miserable lives. An event triggers a reunion back at a ski lodge where they used to party back in the day. Alas, the resort has fallen on hard times and isn't the happening place they remember. The crew indulges in a wild night of drinking in their condo's hot tub and a spilled beverage shorts out the tub controls resulting in time traveling back to the 80's. Vulgar zaniness ensues. Call me a tradionalist but to me time traveling conveyances should be something more like H.G. Wells imagined, or at the very least a DeLorean but a hot tub seems to push the limits of belief. I have fond memories of the 80's and picked this up in a bargain bin for $5.00 though not sure why it was ever released in Blu-ray, it's no cinematic masterpiece. So, I'm no stranger to low brow humor and thought "Animal House", "National Lampoon's Vacation", and "Blazing Saddles" were all quite funny and cleverly written. They say humor is generational and to me at least contemporary films like this or "The Hangover" and it's ilk and other raunchy comedies prove the point. I just don't get the appeal of these flicks. It's unclear how John Cusack wound up in this farce lampooning all things 80's when he is something of an icon of the decade playing Lloyd Dobler in "Say Anything". The rest of the cast is largely forgettable. There are a few chuckle provoking moments but most of it's just profanity and vulgarity with some scatological and homophobic humor thrown in. It's amazing this mess garnered so many 5-star reviews on Amazon and that it even spawned a sequel in 2015. Oh well, to each his own and if this your kind of thing then dive on into the tub but if your tastes are a bit more mainstream than "Hot Tub Time Machine" is not recommended.

history.title: Bewitched: The Complete Series
history.review_title: Delightful trip down memory lane with Samantha and 'Derwood'
history.text: If you’re a heterosexual male of a certain age then there’s a very strong likelihood that your personal preferences in women were in part shaped by two TV shows; ‘Bewitched’ and ‘I Dream of Jeanie’. ‘Bewitched’ premiered to strong ratings on ABC in 1964 running for eight seasons and starred Elizabeth Montgomery as Samantha Stephens, a witch married to a hapless mortal and the challenges which follow. Darrin, her spouse is an advertising exec for a New York firm called McMahon & Tate and bears the brunt of trying to have a normal life while his wife and her meddling relatives magical powers wreak havoc on his existence- comedy mayhem ensues in every episode. The series was so successful the following year NBC decided they needed their own ‘magic blonde’ so Sidney Sheldon cooked up ‘I Dream of Jeanie’ about a gorgeous genie in a bottle discovered by an astronaut after landing on a remote island. The cast is superb starting with Montgomery; stunningly beautiful and incredibly charismatic you can’t take your eyes off of her. Two actors played her husband Darrin, Dick York and later Dick Sergeant who replaced York in Season 6 as a severe back injury forced York to quit the show. Agnes Moorehead is marvelous as Samantha’s mother Endora who is not thrilled with her daughter’s choice in spouses and David White as Darrin’s boss Larry Tate is a dependable straight man for all the antics. Of the recurring players Paul Lynde stands out as Samantha’s snarky warlock Uncle Arthur and can always be counted on for plenty of laughs. The show ran for 8 seasons and ratings began to decline in 1970 and frankly the cast looks pretty fatigued with it all at this point. All said and done ‘Bewitched’ holds up 45 years later although the plots become quite repetitive after awhile. Supposedly set in commuter town Westport, CT (a place I know very well) it looks nothing like Westport. Also, somewhat surprising for the period Samantha and Darrin are shown frequently occupying the same bed which network censors of the day might have been expected to balk at. Given it’s the ‘Mad Men’ era cocktails are constantly being imbibed, Don Draper would have been right at home. Also, it seemed strange to me that for a family show aimed at kids the final season Ms. Montgomery is clearly braless for virtually every episode…but it was the 70’s I guess. The show ends without fanfare or any closure for its audience and there are no special features of any kind with this box set. You'll be enchanted by ‘Bewitched’ even after all these years.

history.review_title: 'Tin Star' is an unsatisfying, bloody mess
history.text: "Tin Star" is an Amazon series that’s desperately trying to be a little bit ‘Twin Peaks’, a little bit ‘Fargo’, and a little bit ‘True Detective’ and failing at all three. Starring British actor Tim Roth whom I’ve never heard of before (but apparently has a fan base from the film ‘Reservoir Dogs’ which I’ve never seen) as London police officer Jack Worth who takes a job as police chief in a remote Canadian village called Little Big Bear along with his wife and two children. He’s got lots of baggage and struggles with alcohol dependency. This is a show where most all the central characters all make astonishingly poor decisions and exercise appallingly bad judgment straining the viewer’s credulity. None worse than Chief Worth (Roth) who falls off the wagon in spectacular fashion, gets in drunken brawls, has sex with strippers two at a time, taunts a biker bang and is savagely beaten by them, alienates himself from his family and subordinates, oh, and commits murder among other things. It was impossible for me to muster up any sympathy for this loser. How this guy doesn’t get fired or locked up or both is beyond belief. The supporting cast is largely an ensemble of unknowns with two exceptions. Christopher Heyerdahl who’s best known from his role as the murdering sociopath “The Swede” on ‘Hell on Wheels’ essentially plays a 21st century version of the same character here. Christina Hendricks of ‘Mad Men’ fame is totally wasted as a big oil company PR hack and is given little to do but slog around in unfashionable clothing until the last few episodes. Everyone else is largely forgettable. The plot gets darker and darker and Chief Worth's behavior completely goes off the reservation (no pun intended- the village has a local First Nations reservation nearby) and it all ends in a bloody mess that provides little satisfaction for the viewer. "Tin Star" is billed as "Season 1" but given how things conclude it's hard to see how a second season would really be possible or why anyone would care enough to watch. Personally I'm done with it and can't recommend you waste any of your viewing time when there are so many other options available.

history.title: Wonder Woman [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: You don't need 2 X-chromosomes to enjoy 'Wonder Woman' (contains few SPOILERS)
history.text: Like many the Lynda Carter portrayal of DC Comics superhero Wonder Woman is the one that I most identify with. When this current film version was announced and it was revealed that relative unknown Gal Gadot was cast in the lead I had my doubts about the Israeli fashion model’s ability to convincingly fill those red boots. Gadot’s quite pretty and charismatic but on the face of it seemed to lack the physicality to convincingly play the part compared to the statuesque Ms. Carter but honestly she pulled it off. Clearly for director Patty Jenkins as evidenced in the over two hours of bonus features this film was a labor of love and she had a specific vision. Incredible amounts of planning went into making this feature and it shows in the extraordinary level of detail; a simple daguerreotype photo seen for seconds in the beginning was made using the actual old time process to produce the image as an example. ‘Wonder Woman’ was more coherent than some of the big blockbuster Marvel outings where there’s just so many characters and so much going on that you can hardly keep track of what you’re watching. Not so in this case, all the central roles are well drawn and defined but most except Diana Prince lack much if any back story. It hardly matters as she’s the star of the show and it’s all about her. The pace was brisk, there are a few humorous moments such as when they take Diana shopping for street clothes at Selfridge’s department store in London but for the most part things are all business. It was fun to see Robin Wright take a break from the rigors of “House of Cards” and play something different in the part of Diana’s warror Aunt Antiope, too bad she didn’t get more screen time. The climactic big battle in the end goes on and on and is an orgy of CGI effects but delivers a satisfying conclusion. Less crowd-pleasing is the fate of Chris Pine’s Captain Steve Trevor who undertakes a suicide mission and flies off with a plane load of chemical bombs and proceeds to blow himself up. Given this film’s box office success it was surprising to see so many 1 and 2-star reviews here though many of those relate to grievances about the digital copy included with the Blu-ray packaging and not the movie itself. Some viewers complained ‘Wonder Woman’ was too “cheesy” which is comical if you go back and watch the old TV series and compare the two. Other unhappy reviewers didn’t like the abundance of CGI effects which for this genre are pretty much inescapable; heck they even had CGI in the latest rendition of “The Great Gatsby” and I don’t recall him being in the Justice League. And then some negative comments were focused on Ms. Gadot’s perceived inadequacies as an actress or felt she was too slight for the role. What can I say, to me she was convincing and I found her charming overall. Others took issue with Wonder Woman’s abilities to leap tall buildings and dodge bullets and other superhuman feats, they must have missed the part that she’s an immortal demi-goddess so none of those things would be outside her skill set. Also among the haters were a number of Greek mythology enthusiasts who took umbrage with apparent inaccuracies in the script. I would ask those folks to consider the source material was a comic book not a scholarly text so lighten up. In summary, ‘Wonder Woman’ was a pleasant surprise brightening the otherwise dark DC Comics universe. The trailer for the upcoming ‘Justice League’ looks pretty impressive so we can look forward to seeing more of her.

history.title: Major Crimes: The Complete Fifth Season S5 (DVD)
history.review_title: Season 5 of 'Major Crimes' does not disappoint
history.text: As I’m writing this the internet has just announced that ‘Major Crimes’ will be ending after it’s sixth season which is currently in production and due to air this month. It’s a befuddling decision by TNT given ‘Major Crimes’ still was the network’s highest rated show and the cast, and creator James Duff seem dedicated to continuing the series. Season 6 then will be the last and it’s been chopped from the usual 21 episodes to a mere 13 with which Duff & Co. will attempt to wrap things up for fans. Season 5 is solid and it’s hard to see any reason for the cancellation decision. Yes, there’s still too much Rusty and his tiresome relationship with Gus. How this young man regardless of who his adopted mother is manages the access to sensitive information inside the LAPD is beyond belief. Also this season the increasingly cloying romance between Capt Raydor and Lt Andy Flynn is taken to the next level- no chemistry between these two. Sharon remains a cold fish and seems like she might have more emotional investment in the copier than Flynn. These complaints aside the crimes are still cleverly conceived (for the most part) and watching the team go through their paces in solving them makes for enjoyable viewing. A major character is killed off this season that’s quite a shock if you didn’t read about it first on the internet. There’s a department shake up and a long overdue promotion for the finale that will satisfy long term fans. When “Major Crimes” sticks with its strength (which is dealing with ‘major crimes’) this series is one of TV’s best procedurals. The personal lives of the characters for me make less compelling viewing but that aside I’m disappointed the show is ending and like many hope for an eleventh hour reprieve from another network or alternate content provider.

history.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
history.review_title: A lighthearted take on the Spiderman saga that may annoy purists
history.text: After a dismal summer at the box office Hollywood’s few bright spots came from Marvel and DC (“Wonder Woman”). Spiderman’s long been a fan favorite in the world of superheroes and thanks to advances in film making we’ve been treated to some spectacular versions of Spidey’s story over the past 15 years. Starting with the Toby Maguire version directed by Sam Rami in 2002 which captured the origin story perfectly the series lost steam when the fairly abysmal Spiderman 3 ended things before Maguire started looking he was eligible for AARP. Then the “Amazing Spiderman” reboot starring Andrew Garfield as the webslinger debuted 2012. Not surprisingly most viewers found it to be mediocre by comparison to the Rami productions and this edition ended after a fairly incoherent sequel. Naturally news that once again Spiderman was hitting the big screen so soon after the last film was met with skepticism. The preview of the new Spidey in “The Avengers- Civil War” assuaged much of the concern and “Spiderman- Homecoming” is one of the best superhero films ever decisively ending any doubt. Tom Holland is well cast as Peter Parker and captures the right feel of the character as a very young, still immature teen. Director Jon Watts wisely skips the origin story that’s already been told in the last two generations of the franchise so we pick up shortly after “Civil War”. Bringing in Tony Stark (always terrific Robert Downey Jr.) as Parker’s mentor was a great addition to the tale and their interactions are very entertaining. I do agree with some viewers who felt Peter was too reliant on Stark Industries tech and lacked the skill and abilities he's had since day one in the comics. There are plenty of laughs as Peter’s very nerdy friend Ned discovers his powers and they try to leverage his secret identity to help in their popularity at their STEM high school. It goes without saying that we get tons of action and watching Spiderman try and perfect his skills and master the augmented suit given him by Tony Stark (including the AI assistant, a female Jarvis) is realistic and fun. Noteworthy supporting cast includes Michael Keaton as our villain and Marissa Tomei as Aunt May. I’m not sure why but since the appearance of the age appropriate Rosemary Harris as May in the 2002 film this character keeps getting younger; Sally Field played her in “The Amazing Spiderman” and now we have Ms. Tomei. Normally I’m not a fan of this sort of revisionist casting but it works here and Tomei is always a treat to watch. Sadly missing from the mix was M.J. Watson, Peter’s love interest and instead he’s pining for an African American young woman in a casting move that seems a contrived deviation from the source material. In summary, “Spiderman Homecoming” is a solid hit and the inevitable sequel will likely be eagerly anticipated by fans everywhere.

history.title: Supergirl: Season 1 [DVD]
history.text: This Supergirl update has much to recommend it to superhero fans. This reboot is clearly aimed at a youthful audience featuring primarily very attractive young people in tight clothing. The show nicely pays tribute to the past featuring Dean (‘Lois & Clark: The New Adventures of Superman’) Cain and Helen (‘Supergirl’ the movie) Slater as Kara Zor-El’s adoptive parents. Blake Neely’s triumphant theme music brilliantly captures the same spirit of John Williams’ iconic “Superman, The Movie” score that fits the positive mood of this new series. Melissa Benoist strikes the right vibe as Kara/Supergirl, cute and spunky with an unlimited sense of optimism. Just like her famous cousin Superman her disguise is a pair of glasses which wouldn’t seem likely to fool anyone. Her boss is media mogul played by talking stick figure Calista Flockhart as Cat Grant. Cat suspects that Kara (or ‘Keira’ as she calls her) is really Supergirl (maybe if Kara didn’t wear the same earrings when she’s in her cape?) but is eventually dissuaded though she doesn’t seem that gullible. Supergirl has help saving the world; fellow Catco employee “Winn” Schott who’s an IT wiz, her adopted sister Alex (beautiful Chyler Leigh) who works for a secret government agency (the DEO) that hunts alien bad guys, and Hank Henshaw (David Harewood) DEO chief who ironically happens to be a super powered shape shifting Martian . Like other reboots of the superhero genre “Supergirl” indulges in some revisionist casting. The most obvious is Jimmy Olson who has always been a geeky, bow tie wearing, freckle faced, red-haired white guy. In this new version Jimmy is now “James” and is a tall, strapping, bald headed African American model and Supergirl is smitten with him. Purists will find this change hard to swallow and though Mehcad Brooks is a likeable actor and tries his best he and Kara don't have much chemistry. A minor complaint on wardrobe, there are a number of military characters in “Supergirl” and for the most part the uniforms all look correct with one exception. Lucy Lane (yes, Lois’ sister) is an Army JAG major and when she’s in dress blues her service cap is for a company grade officer not a field grade officer and the eagle device is for an enlisted person not an officer. Also, she keeps her headgear on indoors although she’s not carrying a weapon, I know, nit-picking. My problem with the show is that it’s incredibly sappy constantly dwelling on themes of love, family, and inclusiveness ad nauseum. Considering the target demographic it’s hard for me to imagine jaded millennials not rolling their eyes as the super friends wallow in sentimentality. I got pretty bored with it all by the time the season ended. That said, I smiled at the end when Cat Grant promotes her long-suffering assistant and finally calls her ‘Kara’. Considering that “Supergirl” has three seasons under its belt my concerns clearly aren’t shared by the audience at large. If your looking for female empowerment I suggest the latest "Wonder Woman" film that came out earlier in the year. One and done for me.

Season 2 of this splendid PBS Masterpiece series based on Winston Graham’s novels does not disappoint. “Poldark” is an engaging period drama set on the coast of Cornwall and chronicles the frequently calamitous life of Captain Ross Poldark (Aidan Turner). In the first season Captain Ross a veteran of the war in the colonies returns to his home to find his girlfriend Elizabeth (Heida Reed) engaged to his cousin and his business affairs in shambles. He marries his scullery maid Demelza (Elizabeth Tomlinson) and makes various attempts to resurrect two copper mines that he owns that have fallen into decline. All the while he maintains a feud with the nefarious George Warleggan (Jack Farthing) a wealthy self-made man with a chip on his shoulder and a great dislike for Poldark. If this show is an 18th century version of “Dallas” then think of George as J.R. Season 2 picks up where things left off and provides plenty of twists and turns with the scenic Cornish coast providing a beautiful backdrop to the often soapy action. Fans of Jane Austen and “Downton Abbey” will likely find much to enjoy with this show with its lavish sets and costumes. A notable addition to the cast for this season is the love interest for Poldark’s friend Dr. Dwight Enys (Luke Norris). Heiress Caroline Penvenen (the stunning Gabriella Wilde) meets the good doctor while visiting her uncle and the two begin secretly meeting because her uncle doesn’t think Dwight’s good enough for her. Ms. Wilde in one scene enters a tavern and literally brings all activity to a standstill; wearing an ice-blue gown and long blonde curls she looks like Queen Elsa from Disney’s “Frozen”, she is a sight to behold. Highly recommended.

history.title: Elementary: The Fifth Season
history.text: Season 5 of “Elementary” returns to its roots with each episode’s primary focus being on Holmes and Watson solving specific crimes as consultants for the NYPD. Personally I found the past few seasons sub plots with Holmes’ brother Mycroft, father Morland, and protégé Kitty Winter (Ophelia Lovibond) all to be more of a distraction than anything else (lamentably Kitty makes a return visit for two episodes, I for one wasn’t missing her). This season introduces Shinwell Johnson (the late Nathan Ellis) a former gang member whom was saved after a shooting by Joan when she was still a practicing surgeon. This ongoing Shinwell storyline is interesting and occasionally takes center stage in some episodes but does not degrade the overall viewing experience. Johnny Lee Miller and Lucy Liu continue to have strong chemistry and watching them work as the modern day Holmes and Watson remains enjoyable. The supporting cast of Aidan Quinn as Capt. Gregson and Jon Michael Hill as Detective Bell are quite good and are a pleasure to watch. The mysteries are quite creative and clever keeping viewers guessing most of the time. Sometimes things don’t make much sense such as Holmes and Shinwell boxing in an NYPD gym. Shinwell is supposedly acting as a CI for the police and has integrated back into his old gang so why would he risk being seen at a cop gymnasium? In another episode Joan is awakened by gun shots in the brownstone; her reaction is to hop out of bed and run downstairs unarmed potentially facing death (it was Holmes playing a recording loudly), she seems smarter than that. Also notice that the detectives and CSI folks never wear shoe covers at the various crime scenes, the writers should watch a few episodes of “Major Crimes”. More unlikely is how much leeway Sherlock and Joan have with the NYPD, being permitted to lead interrogations in particular. I don’t know how ‘consultants’ work with law enforcement in reality and I realize they are the stars of the show after all but these two seem to get away with quite a lot. Hard to believe Captain Gregson and Det. Bell would be so passive and let civilians usurp their authority. Sadly it appears that “Elementary” is on borrowed time, initially CBS only renewed the series for a short 13 episode run and scheduled it as a mid-season replacement instead of a fall release…not a good sign. Just recently it was announced that the network expanded their series order for another 8 episodes bringing the total closer to the usual number. Despite this news the internet has many rumors that the sixth season will be the last and it won’t be aired until spring of 2018. I for one hope the rumors are wrong, this is a quality program and they haven’t ‘jumped the shark’ yet.

history.title: Simon & Simon: Season One
history.text: It’s been almost 38 years since “Simon & Simon” debuted and despite the long time since this series hit the small screen it holds up well. Rick (Gerald McRaney) and his younger brother A.J. (Jameson Parker) are struggling P.I.’s in San Diego who seem to spend entirely too much time with their mother. They have an office across the way from a competing mega Peerless Detective Agency headed by Myron Fowler (who looks like a used car salesman) and his very attractive daughter Janet Fowler (former "Miss Texas" Jeannie Wilson). The Simon’s are kind of like Oscar and Felix from the “Odd Couple” and the contrast between the two is a constant source of amusement. They poach clients from Myron on occasion while enlisting Janet’s assistance on more than one occasion. Cases feature many special guest stars from the era who are fun to see again. The boys spend a lot of time in Mexico which is depicted as a relatively carefree place whereas today their beheaded corpses would be found in a shallow grave first time they go south of the border. It’s all pretty light stuff and fun and still enjoyable entertainment. The first season theme music is not the one most viewers will recall, and in fact there are cringe-worthy lyrics they play during the closing credits. Thankfully, they got a new tune starting in season 2. It’s odd that the series isn’t available in a box set and you have to purchase each season individually. Also, the prices are what you’d expect to pay for the last season of a contemporary hit show and not one that’s almost 40 years old! I’m on board for more of “Simon & Simon”.

history.text: This is one of the worst movies I have ever seen and I am truly flabbergasted by all the good reviews...reading through the five star ones I think many are the same person. This movie has blood as thick as honey barely oozing from a cut to the jugular and that's good effects? The husband supposedly pieced back together a completely shattered mirror in a matter of hours? The last piece of mirror stays stuck on the bottom of a child's shoe for days? A girl doesn't report an attempted murder? What about the mother? What was Willie's punishment in the beginning? How was she just 23 but married to a much older guy and with a six or seven year old and why were they still living with the aunt? I'm sorry, but I love a good B horror flick as much as anyone but this one was horrible. And why was John Carradine given top biling when he was in the movie all of five minutes? And Amazon...why do you have this listed as being a 2013 movie?

I always try very hard, especially with indie films with small budgets, to be as kind as possible while giving my honest review. I also make it a point to actually give a true review meaning I cite reasons for my rating. This one is a hard one. I really wanted to like this movie. I went into it knowing it wasn't going to be the greatest because of it's limitations but this movie's downfalls are not due to low budget hindrances but rather to just bad decisions. Found footage films are pretty much all the same format and that's what's to be expected but there are issues with this one that have nothing to do with financial or even crew limitations. First of all, the camera work is actually fairly good and no where near as nauseating tilt-a-whirl like until the places it should be. And the acting is pretty good as well. I can see any of these actors doing well in the future. The interspersed interviews with the locals are wonderful and much better than most found-footage films...I wish there had been more of those. That's pretty much the only positive things I can say. The biggest fault of this film, and what ultimately kills it for me, is the horrible dialogue. Scenes that beg, beg, beg for more have the characters just simply walking away and not for any benefit to the plot. Scenes where Mike should be talking have him just turning and leaving. Without giving too much away, I can only say, if you choose to watch this, you will see what I mean. This may have been a choice to try and make the story even more mysterious but the decision to have the character simply not talk at all was a poor one that left me throwing my hands in the air in frustration. The last few minutes of the movie lacked realism in the choice of props...for example, a mattress supposedly abandoned for a long time has a new brand corner strip still attached?? Also, the decision to use badly done cgi was unfortunate. It would have been much better to have let the sounds finish the story instead of presenting a really hokey finally seen antagonist. This film could have been really great, better than Blair even, if it had only been executed the right way. Double entendre not intended.

history.title: Dirty Dancing
history.review_title: Classic Must See Dance Movie for the Ages
history.text: My regular edition VHS finally gave up the ghost so I ordered the cheapest DVD I could and I'm really surprised at how much better the widescreen in. My 17 year old daughter completely understands now why I cried when Patrick Swayze died. Now she is going to watch RoadHouse for the first time...I pass the torch with tears in my eyes. For the content, if you really don't know, short summary: girl (Baby) goes to Poconos with family, girl meets underground dance crew, girl joins, girl falls for the hottie (Johnny), he falls for her, "No One Puts Baby in the Corner." Just watch it if you haven't. Notable appearances: Jerry Orbach, Law & Order fame, as the dad; Cynthia Rhodes as Penny.

history.title: Clockwork Orange, A / 2001: A Space Odyssey (DVD) (DBFE)
history.text: Not my cup of tea but my hubby loves "Orange" so I got this. It's a genuine 2 pack, not all on one disc so that's a plus. My version was anyway. Good quality with no playback issues for either disc. As for the movies, I'll leave that up to you to go and read about them. I find Clockwork rather disturbing but that's my opinion. Graphic violence in it including a brutal rape and beating.

history.title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut (DVD)
history.review_title: Classic Movie at a Great Price
history.text: This movie has gotten harder and harder to find. I grabbed it here at a price I would normally only hope to find at Walmart on Black Friday. This will hopefully become more available with the new Star Wars movie but you never know. This movie blew my mind when it first came out when I was really young and it still stands the test of time. Yeah, new graphics are great, but it's movies like this one that paved the way for the kids who ended up making the new ones. Still a classic and boy does Harrison look fine in this one...now my 17 year old daughter understands why he is my favorite actor of all time. As for the actual DVD...it's a cheap one, to be expected, but pretty much the same as any DVD nowadays. The case is fine. Just treat it right and it will do the same for you!

history.title: Howl's Moving Castle
history.review_title: Wonderful, Timeless movie for All Ages!
history.text: This is one of the best animated movies my family and I have ever seen. The story is so original and captivating and the characters are as complex as any drama you'll find. We saw this movie a few years ago and have never forgotten it so I was very happy to find it at such a terrific price. It was on a waitlist for a short while so my husband received it a little late for Father's Day but he didn't mind one bit and he's watched it twice already in just the couple of weeks he's had it. Even if you aren't into the Asian anime movies, you should really give this one a chance since I don't know anyone who has seen it who hasn't raved about it as I do. It's simply a wonderful movie with a story you won't forget.

history.title: PIG HUNT PIG HUNT
history.review_title: Pig Hunt is rip-roaring scary fun!
history.text: Fangoria Fright Fest delivers yet again. Pig Hunt is a wildly entertaining movie, part horror, part comedy. When veteran John (Travis Aaron Wade) brings his girlfriend Brooks and his best buddies to his dead uncle's cabin to hunt for wild hogs, it seems like your normal weekend in the woods, but as they delve into the forest, they learn the awful truth about just how his uncle died and the local legend of the "Ripper". Mix in some crazy drug fueled cultish hippies and some of John's own backwoods kin, and the basis of a wicked little film is born. While some characters may be over the top, the dialogue is well written and believable. The monster is a true life nightmare one could actually imagine rather than a faceless, nameless wraith. The soundtrack is full of Les Claypool's work while he also lends his acting talent to the role of "Preacher". A couple of the movie tracks are the kind you find yourself remembering and perhaps even singing days after hearing them, especially Claypool's hillbilly rap, "Boonville Stomp" and "He Was a Good Man (Now He's Gone)". The protagonists are ones you honestly want to root for and to see conquer the evil wreaking havoc. Newcomer, Travis Aaron Wade, is a charismatic leading man and his girlfriend, played by Tina Huang, is recognizable from her "Rizzoli & Isles" character as Dr. Maura Isles assistant. The only downfall for this film is the characters of the drug crazed cult but fortunately, the rest of the story is engaging enough to forgive this. If "Jaws" and "Deliverance" had a baby, "Pig Hunt" would be it.

It's pretty funny to read reviews on here saying it was too long since it was just over 3 minutes...but that's actually the reason I'm giving it four instead of five stars. Some of the scenes could go a little faster to give a little more attention to the ending...especially since it was the "punchline/surprise" and best part. SPOILER ALERT: My only other criticism is the thing itself. (Even though I gave a spoiler alert I'm still strying to be discreet for the benefit of wandering eyes, lol.) I wish it had been more obvious what it was. I kept having to rewind and pause to figure out what it wasl Can you just imagine basically being told your spouse loves a sex doll more?

history.title: Home for the Holidays, Cover may vary
history.text: As for the movie, it's one of my all-time favorite comedies, hands down! The reason for a less than perfect rating is for the actual physical DVD and case. As soon as I pulled it from the package I heard the familiar rattle of a loose DVD and sure enough, the holding spindle was broken and the disc was free. Usually that's not a big deal but this time it caused a rather deep scratch on the disc. Luckily, I have one of those waxy DVD/CD repair sticks that worked because otherwise I would have had to return it. I know this is a common issue but I was rather surprised that Amazon sent it anyway as anyone handling this would have heard the loose DVD.

history.title: The Adventures Of The Wilderness Family Trilogy [DVD]
history.text: What's to say...the beloved trilogy all on one very inexpensive dvd. You can't even rent one movie for the price of this set. Good quality and came well packaged with no issues. Plays great. Robert Logan is still the hunkiest dad!

history.title: Vikings Season 4 [DVD]
history.review_title: The ruination of a once-great series.
history.text: *** SPOILERS AHEAD... SPOILERS AHEAD... DON'T SAY YOU WEREN'T WARNED *** Well, I loved the original cast, the sets, the costumes, the acting, etc. It has been consistently very good throughout the series. But now, in Season 4 the whole story line begins to become completely implausible. So, Ragnar wants to go back to Paris instead of back to England where he has a much better chance of getting a conquest? So after Rollo completely stuffs Ragnar's attempt to go sailing up the Seine River to assault Paris, Ragnar has the bright idea to haul all the Viking ships up over a cliff into the hills, drag them along for miles, and put them back into the river? What good did that do? Even if Rollo hadn't been waiting in the river for him (AGAIN), the Vikings still would have faced the same Paris with the same high walls, etc., etc. Militarily it made absolutely no sense at all. Sure enough, Ragnar is defeated, again, and this time his people go back to Kattegat, completely empty-handed, and what does Ragnar do? He goes wandering off in the wilds for a few years. Again, this is completely implausible. The series closes with a glimpse of Ragnar's latest crop of adult sons, all of whom seem to be a bunch of self-serving, cowardly jerks. Needless to say, I'm disappointed in this season,and if I buy the Season 4 DVD's it won't be for a long, long time when they are very heavily discounted. On the bright side, at least King Ecbert, the rotten but brilliant monarch of Wessex in England, gives uniformly brilliant performances, but in truth, all of the sequences dealing with England are very much better in a number of different ways from the silly, unlikely series of messes the show got into in France. If they decide to have a Season 5 I hope it's a hell of a lot better than this Season 4 was. *** UPDATE January 23, 2017 *** SPOILERS AHEAD, SPOILERS AHEAD *** The newest season has continued to big downhill slide of this series. Now Ragnar decided to go to England with his crippled son and a Viking contingent. He kills ALL of his own fellow Vikings after arriving in England, then he seeks out and surrenders to King Ecbert so that he can be transported to another king and executed. He does all of this on PURPOSE, so that his crippled son will get the other moron sons to go back to England and get "revenge". Again, nothing about any of this nonsense is plausible or entertaining at ALL. I watched one more episode where some of the other Vikings go back to Paris and talk Rollo into going down south toward the Mediterranean Sea for some more adventure. At that point I simply stopped watching. This series is RUINED, and that is a great shame. I am a verified purchaser of the first three years' worth of this series -- and that is the END of that....

history.title: NCIS: Season 13
history.review_title: Unfortunate settling of the whole series into a kind of ...
history.text: Unfortunate settling of the whole series into a kind of predictable mediocrity. Instead of developing engaging, complex plots as NCIS often used to do, now nearly all episodes are one-off, choppy, "cute" little stories. It's not "bad", per se... it's just no longer really "good"! Really, in my opinion, the whole series has gradually downhill after the "Eleanor Bishop" character came onboard, with the unfortunate departure of the "Ziva David" character. Season 13? No hurry. I'll wait to add it to my complete NCIS collection (so far) until this latest season hits the throw-out bins and becomes heavily discounted.

history.title: Sherlock: Season Four [DVD]
history.review_title: From a formerly VERY enthusiastic fan, this Season 4 was a profound disappointment
history.text: What a stunning disappointment. Each of the three episodes in this series was worse than the preceding one, until the great, wearisome agony of the "The Final Problem" at the end of it. No spoilers from me. The cast was still uniformly excellent, and all the movie-making craft was expertly employed. But the stories grew further and further distant from anything even remotely resembling Conan Doyle (to say the least), and in so doing, became completely detached from anything that I really found interesting at all. The last episode was pure torture; such a head-shaking waste of so much talent, and such a crash-landing for a multi-year series of programs that I had loved so much -- until this Season 4. Will there be a Season 5? Will it return to something that even vaguely resembles 'Sherlock Holmes' as we had come to love it with Cumberbatch and Martin...? We can hope, but I'm not overly optimistic. These developments tend to go from bad to worse.

history.title: The Statement
history.review_title: Bad, old Nazi collaborators in Vichy France, reviled decades later in a politically-correct film mediocrity. Ho-hum....
history.text: Rather tedious, formulaic, and, well, boring. I can easily see how this could have been edited down considerably and made into a better movie. Caine's performance was oddly uneven, but that's probably more the fault of the rather wooden, predictable techniques used by the director than anything else. The supporting cast was mediocre. And maybe that's the best way to describe this rather unremarkable story -- mediocre. What sort of characters would you expect among Nazi collaborators in a place like Vichy France during World War II? They weren't angels, but many years later they are supposed to be rounded up and treated like unreasoning monsters? The plot-dynamic is really based on revisionist, politically-correct nonsense. War is hell, and it will never be anything else....

history.title: Allied [BD/Digital HD Combo] [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: THIS is the movie that should have won "Best Picture" for 2016, but it wasn't even nominated for it!
history.text: THIS is the movie that should have won "Best Picture" for 2016, but, of course, it wasn't even nominated. Pitt was flawless, and this was definitely Marion Cotillard's best performance in a movie. There were so many areas where this movie excelled in every way, including absolute, spot-on accuracy in uniforms, architecture, sets, music, vehicles, airplanes, civilian clothing, and on and on. Rarely have I seen a WWII movie with such fidelity to details! At least it was nominated for Best Costume Design. The directing, cinematography, and editing deliberately lulled the viewer into thinking one set of things, and then another, and then another... a convoluted story that wrapped around itself in very interesting ways. And, no, it's not "Casablanca"... I find such commentaries to be both shallow and amusing. This is an entirely different kind of story, and almost as compelling. I rented this from Redbox, but I already plan to buy it, from Amazon, of course!

history.title: Dresden
history.review_title: It has gotten to be pricey in 2018, because the movie is no longer being produced.
history.text: It's a fairly-well done production although the "love affair" sub-plot is a bit implausible. Nothing is developed in the plot at all about how Churchill had reportedly demanded the complete annihilation of Dresden during WWII in retaliation for the bombing of Coventry several years earlier by the German Air Force (bombed by mistake, but, bombed all the same). The subtitles are not user-friendly at all for English-speakers. You cannot get any English subtitles when English is being spoken in the movie. You do get English subtitles when the dialog is in German, but the subtitles themselves are too big. At least you can turn all subtitles completely off! It has gotten to be pricey in 2018, because the movie is no longer being produced.

history.title: Where Eagles Dare [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Want to see this movie with a GERMAN vocal track, plus other languages, in a beautiful new released version? Wait no longer!
history.text: This review is for "Where Eagles Dare" in Blu-Ray, Region-Free -- with GERMAN as a spoken language, including English and several other Western European spoken languages, too. Also, subtitles in foreign languages, also. This version of the movie was released just a few weeks ago, but I have waited for this for decades! I have hoped that somehow, someone would finally release this movie with a GERMAN vocal track, and that is exactly what this Blu-ray version does. Not only that, but the video transfer is excellent and does not suffer at all from some of the strange "darkening" of scenes that are often noted in some older Blu-ray video transfers. The images are clean and rich, and the soundtrack is excellent also. That one scene in the castle where the two SS officers (one is "Major" von Hapen, and the other is "Colonel" Kramer) go at each other because of the growing intrigue surrounding the capture and upcoming interrogation of U. S. General Carnaby is absolutely PRICELESS in the German language (which I understand and speak). I hope you enjoy it, too. I only waited over 40 years for this film to be released in the U. S. with foreign languages, and now it's here! If this is what you want, be certain that you get this one version -- do not confuse it with others or you'll be disappointed....

history.title: The Last Kingdom: Season Two
history.review_title: Much more engrossing and well-made than Season One. Bravo! Can't wait for Season Three!
history.text: I honestly did not have particularly high hopes for this 'Season Two'. Season One was fairly well-done, I thought, and I did enjoy it, but, WOW, it was far outshone by Season Two in every way. I've read all of Cornwell's "Uhtred" books, and I've loved them all. That said, my sympathies go out to anyone who would try to put all of that into any kind of TV "series". To say the least, it is an immense story! But in Season Two, even with some necessary 'compressions' and a few omissions, the integrity of the overall story is rock-solid, believable, and thoroughly enjoyable. I was very surprised, and thoroughly delighted! Now, I despair at the thought that we may have to wait two long, dreadful years before there's a Season Three, but I certainly do hope there is one -- now, more than ever. I'll be eagerly awaiting it!

history.title: Speed 2 - Cruise Control
history.review_title: The reason sequels aren't taken seriously....
history.text: ....with a handful of notable exceptions, sequels don't have a good rap. This is a classic example, and when nearly everyone is saying the same thing ("it rots") there must be something to it. And so it is with "Speed 2:Cruise Control"--it's a nifty title, but the positives pretty much end there. Everyone loved the original "Speed", but this soggy sequel-of-sorts is capsized by a lame plot and ridiculous dialogue. Even worse, Sandra Bullock's spunky Annie-- who was nice-girl sexy, smart and likable in the bus thriller ---is cut down to a dumb, one-dimensional second banana on the cruise ship. Many films have been illuminated by Bullock's star-power, but S2CC's scribes have doused that light for fair. Thus, Jason Patric's character (also one-dimensional) is pretty much left to save the day single-handedly, over and over again. Just one act of heroism involving extreme athletics is enough to wind most guys, but poor Jason is sent to save fellow passengers from certain death, have shootouts with a cartoon villain (a cruelly cast Willem Dafoe), dive under the ship to keep it from ramming a tanker, steal a speedboat, chase an airplane on water (and actually catch up to it)....one brave feat after another without missing a beat.....well, that's how I spend a Saturday afternoon, don't you? Escapist fun is one thing, but this goes from inane to boring to completely unbelievable. The climax comes too late to save this doomed feature.....just watch the original "Speed" again instead. It's much more worth your time.

history.title: Project: ALF [DVD]
history.text: ....this movie is not a satisfying conclusion to the ALF story. The whole point of the show was his interaction with the Tanners, and whether or not he would rejoin his friends in space if the chance came up again. Indeed, the chemistry between the Furry One and the talented Max Wright made the show---the writers knew that, and they're really one of television's great, undersung comedy teams. "Project ALF" loses all that, and this just becomes a pale conclusion to what had been a lighthearted and warm family series. The only reason it gets more than one star from us is that, at least, some kind of effort was made for the loyal fans who made the series such a hit for all those years.

history.title: Madame X VHS
history.review_title: Of all the "Madame X"'s.......this is the one to see.
history.text: Of the many screen versions of this story, most viewers are probably familiar with the glossy Lana Turner soaper from the '60's. While Turner's performance as Madame X was admirable, the one to beat is this spellbinding turn by Gladys George. This version,in writing and acting styles, is of course more dated---it was released in 1937. (Today, a woman like Madame X would be a media darling, and probably have her own talk show.) Like the original play, this story is set in France----and we have to buy the main characters as being French, even though they speak with distinctly American accents, unlike the supporting cast around them. All of that is made believable, however, by the fine performances---with Miss George outdoing them all as the tragic fallen woman who sacrifices herself for her son. The ending is a killer, in every respect. This is an "old movie", to be sure,and Gladys George didn't make a lot of big ones....but she single-handedly makes this one a true classic.

history.review_title: Peck and Bacall still have it.

The storyline is something relatable, that could happen in any family, but in this case it's played out by two strong forces from the golden age of filmmaking. Fortunately, the script enables them to display the appeal, talent and humor that made them audience favorites. Park yourself by the tv with a bowl of chips and enjoy two pro's showing us how it's done.

history.title: Hush...Hush, Sweet Charlotte
history.review_title: Unsolved Murder + Spooky Old Mansion+ Resident Crazy Lady = Camp Fun
history.text: I want to add this to my collection--it's a Camp-Meets-Grand-Guignol classic. Some reviewers compare it unfavorably to the Aldrich/Davis collaboration "Baby Jane", but it's a completely separate story. While the plot is admittedly a bit of a stretch, it's highly watchable and the cast is obviously having a whale of a time chewing the scenery. Davis' rattled Charlotte may be unhinged but--unlike Baby Jane Hudson--you can sympathize with her. De Havilland, adept at portraying genteel ladies, just oozes insincerity as the opportunistic Miriam, and Joseph Cotten---every bit as effective, as the lecherous bayou MD---drawls one of my favorite movie quotes; "now, there's nothin' wrong with basket-weavin'.....'course, it never cured anybody, but it's most therapeutic." This doesn't show up on the Critics' top ten lists, but it did garner several award nominations after its release, including one for Agnes Moorehead's scene-stealing housekeeper. Pop some corn, sit back, and enjoy.

history.title: THE SCARLET PIMPERNEL
history.review_title: Undoubtedly one of the best made-for-TV classics
history.text: No need to rehash the plot---but is this a good watch? Most definitely, yes! For a TV incarnation, which necessarily condenses the story a bit as opposed to the book, it's beautifully put together....highly entertaining and it holds your interest. The cast is well chosen: the talented Anthony Andrews is completely convincing--both as the priveleged fool, Sir Percy, and as the cunning, dashing Pimpernel. Indeed, he brings not only buckle and swash to the role, but an infectious humor as well---especially in his scenes with the increasingly edgy Chauvelin. Ian McKellen is just plain wonderful as that villain, and he nearly gets our sympathy: he truly pines for his lost love Marguerite, but that isn't enough to make us forget what an evil wretch he is. Jane Seymour gives her best performance since 'East of Eden' and is stunningly beautiful as Marguerite---but more importantly, her carefully controlled intensity is just the right fit for the part. She and Andrews are well matched. The final scene is not to be missed. The witty dialogue and sword fight are every bit as good as in any Errol Flynn/Basil Rathbone classic---and, thanks to Andrews' amused taunting of the hapless Chauvelin, pretty darn funny, too. Do give this a watch, old chaps---you won't be sorry.

history.title: Borgia: Season Two: Rules of Love, Rules of War
history.review_title: Not your average folks next door.
history.text: For fans of the Borgia period in history (mature fans, that is; this is most definitely not family-friendly), you might consider this DVD set----bearing in mind that the 'good guys' are frequently bestial and the fast-moving plot may spin your head if you don't pay attention. Unlike the sumptuous and equally-addictive Showtime series--whose tale unfortunately came to an abrupt halt when it was canceled---this one from Canal ties up the story at the end of the third season, and even includes a satisfying recap delivered by the lead actors. As noted in the other reviews, a few liberties are taken with the script, but it generally follows a historical basis--gaining Ultimate Power came (and still does, to this day) at a heavy price. For the Church, at the expense of simple Scriptural teachings: its interweaving of politics and pagan traditions, persecution of "non-believers", and moral corruption infest it still. For the Borgias themselves, it was at the expense of family peace and harmony: they loved and hated passionately, gaining immense influence while losing each other to Ambition. A powerful addition to any historical DVD collection.

history.review_title: Best experienced by means of a superb AV system.
history.text: This is a five-star review mainly because of technical issues. I have watched this movie on my rather powerful home-theater system and was impressed with the sound quality and the remarkable video trickery. In addition to a group of satellite speakers made by me, my rig has two, five-toot-tall cylinder-tower subwoofers of my own design (with 12-inch Dayton Reference drivers and 700 watts of input power) that are tuned to 22 Hz, and which can reach down solidly to even 20 Hz. However, a month earlier I watched the movie at a friend's house and, in addition to top-line Paradigm satellites and two 600-watt McIntosh amps powering the left and right main systems, he has TWO huge Paradigm subwoofers, with each containing six powerful woofers and about 4000 watts of power. That's 4000 watts EACH and 12 drivers, in enclosures that weight 230 pounds each. On his system I could feel bass pressure waves at times that were almost lethal. I think the listening couch moved up and down, and perhaps even backward an inch or so with every "whump!" This is one heck of a demo disc for subwoofer fanatics. It has taken me two tries to decipher the plot of this movie, and once I had that done its story line actually began to make sense. (Reading the plot line on Wikipedia did not hurt, either.) Some reviewers have criticized the fragmentary nature of the movie, but that fragmentation is part and parcel of the design. Few movies are as plot integral with the technology as this one, and while one may tend to write it off as a cult presentation, it is actually quite a breakthrough item. I do not think it will start a trend, and if it did that tend would get tiring pretty fast. But as it stands it is a technical (and certainly a sonic) tour de force - provided of course that one has the audio system and big-screen TV monitor to do it justice. Howard Ferstler

history.title: Gettysburg
history.review_title: Superb presentation of a superb movie
history.text: I have owned and watched FOUR different video versions of Gettysburg. The first was the 12-inch laserdisc version that was surprisingly well made. It was the theater-length release, at 254 minutes, and for me, a Civil War buff, watching it was almost like a religious experience. (I had a similar epiphany when I watched the Ken Burns Civil War documentary some time before, now available as a DVD.) The second was the “director’s cut” boxed-set laserdisc, that came with a nice book about the movie and about the battle itself. This second version, 17 minutes longer than the previous release, extended some scenes and added a few new ones, at least one of which added some dramatic depth to the movie. While I believe that the early disc was audio encoded in basic Dolby Surround (I am stretching my memory here), the second was done in DTS, which is also how the original was presented in movie theaters. The problem with this 271-minute boxed set was that the video and audio (the DTS audio technology notwithstanding) were both inferior to that of the earlier disc. The video was excessively dark and off color in some scenes and, worse, the audio lost much of its impact, particularly the sections that involved canon and musket salvos. The canon salvos lacked the low-end reach and even the sequences with musket fire seemed to be dynamically compressed. The team responsible for the reissue may have assumed that the sonic impact of the canons and muskets we had with the earlier disc would be too much for most TV speaker systems, or even outboard audio systems that had anemic subwoofers. They did not want set owners to rage about destroyed speakers. The third release was a DVD, and it improved somewhat on the second laserdisc. However, even it seemed to lack the impact of the first disc. Worse, the length was dialed back to 254 minutes - an artistic blunder. The disc, being an early DVD, also had the program split between two sides, and in spite of the extra surface space the disc seemed to have some tracking problems with some players (both of mine, for example). I have read elsewhere that this was not unusual, and so I ended up ordering a fourth version from Amazon. This one was a blu-ray item - and included a second disc that included three featurettes on the making of the movie, plus a booklet built into the disc holder that offered up some historical information, as well as information about the main actors. The movie disc itself has running commentary options by historians James McPherson and Craig Symonds. A nice, tidy item, this set. Best of all, this fourth version combined the best technical aspects of the previous ones into a terrific visual and DTS-audio package. Indeed, the canon and musket cacophonies were now more emphatic than ever. I have watched a lot of action movies over the years, and while the individual canon thuds were no more powerful than many other explosions I have experienced with various dynamic action movies on my AV system, the combined impact of dozens of thuds piled on in close succession was in a class by itself. I am convinced that many subwoofer systems (or woofers on AV rigs that do not use subwoofers) would be damaged beyond practical use if the volume were played loud enough for the dialog throughout the rest of the movie to be properly audible. Technically, this is a stupendous, demo-grade blu-ray disc that demands a “serious” audio playback rig. It is also a stupendous story. The actors were very well chosen for their roles, with all of the principles doing standout work. There have been criticisms of Sheen as general Lee, but I do not agree. Perhaps someone like Jason Robards might have been better (Robards looked more like Lee than Sheen, which is what my southern-born wife thinks), but Robards was 70 at the time the movie was made and Lee was in his middle fifties, the same age as Sheen was when he played the part. Anyway, Sheen played Lee the way I see Lee. Some (major fans of Lee, we can be sure) have criticized how Sheen made Lee seem almost deluded when rationalizing the potential effectiveness of the charge on the third day. However, to my way of thinking Lee almost had to be deluded and over-optimistic about what his army could do. He had to be so to think that Pickett’s 15,000 men could traverse a mile of open space while under fire from every gun on the Union line within range. General Longstreet, as played by Tom Berenger, was the only fully rational and aware Confederate with authority involved during the battle. Longstreet wanted to have the army shift position to better ground and fight a defensive battle, but unfortunately he could not get Lee, who was looking for a fight, to make that move and did not have enough authority to veto the charge. Regarding that charge, the movie was done before the kind of CGI abilities we have these days, so the men involved with the movie version were real men - Civil War re-enactors who had the chance of a lifetime to do a large scale presentation. There were not as many as in the original charge (perhaps only a third as many), but judicious and skillful camera usage allowed for a scene that is unforgettable. Incidentally, Ted Turner, who helped finance the movie, had a small and brief part in the move that those with sharp eyes will spot pretty quickly. Documentarian Ken Burns also had a small, and equally brief part. Anyway, the movie is terrific. It probably would be a good idea for those not apprised of just what transpired during those three days to read an internet summary or two (or maybe even a book about the war in general) in order to get an idea of what was going on. The movie covers only parts of the overall encounter (even though those parts presented were manifestly important), and a bit of background should make the viewing more meaningful than ever. I also suggest that a viewing of the Ken Burns documentary on the whole war would be a rewarding experience.

history.title: Serenity [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: This Sci-Fi lover was not impressed
history.text: I appreciate Joss Whedon very much...this was the exception. I am a die hard sci-fi/horror movie addict, even the bad ones I enjoy watching. After painfully sitting through this movie I now understand why Firefly was such a disaster. Besides a very convoluted story and pieces of the film and plot which did not mesh well together it finally ended and I could not have been happier. The only other thing I was happier about is that I paid only $5.96 for the Steelbook blu ray version. The positive note was the cinematography..I will not even state the effects were excellent the the visuals were outstanding. Also for a casts of B actors they handled the script as well as the script allowed, so some kudos does go to them. Perhaps if I ever watched Firefly I might feel differently; or perhaps by watching this I have no desire to see Firefly...either way this was a disappointment. Sorry to all the thousands who gave this 4 or 5 stars, I just fail to see the reason.

I am a bit confused as to all the great reviews as well as the terrible reviews. I guess I would have to say I feel neutral about this movie in terms of "horror." The story line and acting are intensely believable and the musical score sets the absolutely perfect tone for the film. Cinematography is well handled and even the direction has its merit. It is a wonderful "prepubescent" Twilight movie minus the sparkly vampires. A vampire movie however is a stretch as there was no real "jump out of your seat moments." It is basically a story of two social outcast who find comfort and solace in each other...and that is fine. That story line could have survived on its own sans the vampire theme. The story is a sweet one of longing, acceptance and loyalty again vampires did not need to be added into the mix. While this came out during the Twilight craze I can understand why it was necessary to add the dimension to the film. Seriously, this is Twilight for the tween set, minus Kristen Stewart's dreadful acting.

history.title: Boyhood [Blu-ray]
history.text: I am still absolutely puzzled how BOYHOOD won all these awards last night at The Golden Globes. This was one of the films sent to me for Oscar voting (we get films either just out or currently playing not released on DVD/Blu-Ray for screening to vote). I finally watched it yesterday afternoon. It is three hours long...let me repeat three hours and it is like watching someone's home made 8mm of their kids growing up. There is absolutely NO plot...I was waiting for something to happen anything and it didn't. Seriously it is like a day in the life of a kid..who grows up. I love Ethan Hawke but he couldn't save this at all. As for Patricia winning an award...WTF? This is and I am serious watching old movies your parents made of you when you played football, graduated school, went swimming. The last three seconds is suppose to be the moment it all pulls together...you could see that coming for the first frame. I WANT MY THREE HOURS BACK. I just read that this was actually shot over a thirteen year period...pity the poor cast and no wonder it seems like someone's home movie...BECAUSE IT IS.

history.title: Mulholland Dr. (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Well at least it plays. Given the recent issues with Criterion blu rays I had my doubts about this playing when placed into my OPPO blu ray player...surprisingly it did. No need to speak about the film as it is a masterpiece, so this will speak only about this long anticipated blu ray release. I must say that the actual picture (not audio) shows no difference in blu ray vs. the regular DVD and that was a huge disappointment. I switched the two disc between my OPPO and I could not tell a difference. I even played the blu ray on the OPPO and the DVD on my Sony blu ray layer in the bedroom and saw no visible difference to the actual film. I was so hoping the film in blu ray would jump off the screen...it did not. Parts of the film actually looks distorted by comparison with the DVD. Huge let down. The positive side is the audio--a remarkable upgrade. I thought the sound quality in the DVD was fairly ballsy but the blu ray sound leaps out of the speakers. There are nuisances I never heard before watching the DVD played from my OPPO through my Bose speakers. I would venture to say this alone would be worth purchasing the blu ray but I am not sure. If you own the DVD and you don't care about the extras on the blu ray then don't bother. If you want a greater sound clarity then by all means go for it immediately. If you are looking for a stunning picture upgraded you will be highly disappointed.

history.title: Jurassic World [Blu-ray]
history.text: It's been almost twenty years since Jurassic Park and now we have a new park. Let's start with the fact that in order to enjoy this movie you need to suspend all reality. It is science fiction after all so for all those who comment that it is not factual and this could never happen...of course not-that is why it is called science fiction, for now.The musical score is breathtaking, far better than the first. There is also a far more human element especially when the brontosaurus dies...I must admit I cried and now I have to skip that scene. The four key principles do a stellar job in their portrayal of each character (Pratt, Bryce-Howard, Robinson and Simpkins). Pratt is exceptional in his portrayal to play it almost borderline "cartoonish" but stops just short that he is a "bad ass" as Zach (Robinson) describes him. Visuals are astounding and the action is fairly non stop. There is one issue that I really have an issue with and I am going to contradict myself about suspending reality. I watched Jurassic Park after watching (again) Jurassic World. In JP, the Velociraptors are seen as the primary enemy--they are, according to history, one of the more aggressive and fearsome of all dinosaurs. In JW, the Velociraptors are treated like a trained pack of dogs---a "family" pet as if they wish to snuggle with you on the couch. These creatures have gone from one of the most harmful to being domesticated. No sense of disbelief can make that believable in any way-and in my opinion, and again it is MY OPINION, that is what makes the movie falter. I am willing to buy into all other suspension of belief but that one, at least to me, is over the top and made me far more critical of the film.

history.title: Christmas Horror Story, A [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Christmas and Horror all in one
history.text: I have to admit I knew nothing about this film other than what I read from all the reviews so I thought, why not! I love horror movies, I love Christmas and Christmas movies and I love Shatner's overacting--it seemed like the perfect trifecta. Since I received my blu ray on Friday, I have not stopped watching this movie...far more than what I expected. Let's start with Shatner--he is excellent in the role and he does not, let me repeat does not over emote. He plays the part of the DJ perfectly, not corny or campy but as you actually might expect a DJ in a similar situation to respond. I was beyond surprised and disappointed---I so wanted the over acting Captain Kirk. The movie is four distinct stories, but unlike many have stated only one of the stories interconnects with itself---it is the surprising ending (and it is a surprise). The other three stories really are stories in themselves and in no way has to do with the one other story. Try and guess when watching as which one will surprise you in the end. That is the part of the movie which I loved. I read as most said there is a surprise ending,but I never expected what happened. The writing and direction are surprisingly well done and the cast works well in each of their respective venues. I would not say it is as much in the way of horror as I would have prefered but you can only go so far with Christmas without crossing a fine line. The cliches are kept to a minimum, the dialogue is not sappy and the effects are well done but do not take away from the stories--meaning the stories could stand alone without any special effects. I am extremely glad I purchased this and added it to both my horror and Christmas movies---it sits right next to A CHRISTMAS STORY, with Ralphie Parker---WOW, imagine that movie in horror form. HO-HO

history.title: 4th Man Out - Special Edition [Blu-ray]
history.text: I just ordered my blu ray of this today as I have been watching it on Netflix for one entire week. This may be one of the best gay themed movies ever. I read some reviews from gay critics who all panned the film as not being diverse, too corny, not realistic, etc, etc. What do those drama queens know. This movie has heart and is far far more realistic than any other gay movie ever produced (besides Shelter). Gay themed movies are always so stereotypical in type--this is not. First, our gay guy is working middle class high school educated, no college for him or his bros. The fact that there are more likely gays that fall into that category than what is always almost portrayed makes it entertaining. Unlike some who have stated it does have some stereotypical moments, I would not so much agree. Our hero is a mechanic---not a fashion designer, IT nerd, or some such "high powered" typical queen---he is an average everyday Joe. The writing is clever and witty without being over the top. The acting and the on screen chemistry between all four leads is evident and very plausible. The only downside is that Chord Overstreet grew facial hair for the role. The secondary characters, for the most part, are also authentic--with the exception of his neighbor lady. This movie holds a dear place in my heart for a major reason--it is me growing up. My closest friends to this day (and I am in my early 60s) are still all my straight buddies from high school (most went to college). There are five of us and I feel more comfortable with them than anyone else (even my other half of 35 years). They have been through all the drama and turmoil as well as all the great times and we are all still close. The fact that the lead character cares about his straight bros and that one is the "extra special" one parallel's my life entirely. For this reason, and not to mention it is a good flick, I can relate and understand so well. If you wish to see a truly heart warming, funny and touching gay-themed movie that avoids most of the stereotype, this is it. It is a human story and that is what makes it tug at your heart.

history.title: The Twilight Zone: The Complete Series Blu-ray
history.text: Here is some clarification based on all the previous reviews. Looking at the box set which is pictured, while it may say Paramount/CBS this is actually the Imagine Entertainment set, not some new set by Paramount/CBS. It includes all the extras on that set. The extras are on the last set of each season's disc. Also, the fact that it start off credits say Imagine Entertainment might be a real teller. Despite what others have stated, the discs are not that difficult to remove. If you hold down the center spool and press the disc can easily be removed. Clearly with 24 discs you want some security to ensure the discs do not move. All the episodes do have sub-titles, none of the extras have sub-titles. Needless to say, the blu ray discs are crisp and clean and the remastered sound is crisp and clear...has less hiss than the original audio source, but it is nice to have the option. All episodes, including the fourth season one hour episodes are included, which is great because they are so rarely shown. Please be aware that Amazon changes the price on this set daily. I ordered it on December 31, 2016 for $149 and the next day January 1, 2017 it was $71. I cancelled the one and reordered. You should pay no more than $75 for this set in blu ray. I felt I needed to clarify what other's have said about this set, especially being a new set by Paramount as indicated--it is not. It is the Imagine Entertainment set with a Paramount box...so, if you own the Imagine Entertainment set, no need to purchase this as nothing is new. ENJOY

history.title: Twilight Time Steel Magnolias Blu-ray edition (1989)
history.text: This review is NOT about the movie as it is five plus stars. It is about the blu ray from Twilight Time. I have the DVD and just received the blu ray. For some unknown reason Columbia Pictures never issued this as a blu ray, so Twilight Time did. Normally I have been pleased with Twilight Time releases (HINT: all their releases are far far cheaper on their website, as I just found) as well as Criterion Collection releases. Honestly, Criterion is the best of all of them...Criterion, Twilight, Shout!Factory and Scream!Factory. This is FAR FAR from a blu ray. I still own the DVD release and will continue to do so. There is absolutely NO difference between the blu ray and the Columbia DVD both in video and audio. I mean NONE. In fact, the blu ray is darker in tone then is the DVD. The darker tone does not account for a richer deeper picture, it is just dark. The DVD has a much brighter picture and the color at times appears sharper. Perhaps there is a reason why Columbia never issued this as a blu ray. If their reason was because the negative would not transfer well, I certainly understand--as it clearly does not.
