history.title: Reach For The Sky - Building a Skyscraper
history.text: I have just ordered this DVD from Amazon, and although I have not yet viewed it, I have watched this entire series online. It is a very well done presentation of the entire process of the construction of a skyscraper from the purchase and clearing of the site (in New York city) to the very end with a celebratory party for the main people evolved. I have watched this entire series at least twice now, and it is still so absorbing and fascinating. I had no idea of the efforts needed to make such a thing happen. So many people, from engineers, electricians, carpenters, so many different craftsmen and construction specialists are utilized to accomplish this task, This is also a very human look at this feat. Time is everything to making a skyscraper; schedules must be met, everything must coordinate to bring the project in on time and within budget. It is very much a human drama, one that will engulf you and let you see what goes on in those ivory towers where the decisions and agreements are made to achieve the goal. There is so much give and take between each team; it's almost like an opera of intrigue and uncertainty. Certainly, not everything goes as planned. How the people deal with that (and especially each other) is human drama at its finest. I am so happy this is out on DVD, as the story is so compelling, so REAL, that it still enthralls me after two complete viewings. The series is over three hours in length, but keeps my attention nonetheless. If you have any interest in engineering or construction, or are just curious about how the making of a skyscraper happens, this is the best show in town. Keep in mind that this was made prior to cell phones and many of the digital tools we take for granted today. No computers (of the desktop variety) are seen. Diagrams, blueprints, etc. are all handmade. Meetings are face to face; no email. Just about all communication is face to face. This is the way it was done at this point in time, and you may come away with a much greater appreciation of the many talents brought to the table for the completion of the project. I know my understanding has been greatly enhanced after watching this. I think yours will be as well; it is just that good. Addendum: I have finished (again) watching the entire series, and it is as "riveting" as I remembered it. Seeing it on DVD is much clearer than the original means I had (downloaded from ??) plus you have chapter markings to go by. However, this is a burnt to disk product, and lacks any extras. I don't think there probably were any to begin with, and I did not really miss them. i would be curious to see where the main characters are now, as it was easy to develop a kinship with some of them. Another aspect which I mentioned above was how this is a journey back in time to an era before cellphones, desktop computers, etc. It lends a much more human feel to this documentary. The people involved in this project were much more hands on, face-to-face with their points of view and their dealings with the many issues that came up. This lent the documentary a feeling of drama and reality. It really makes me wonder, still, how projects like this ever manage to get done. I know it is mostly about the money, but the human element is out in the open as well. I have gone on far too long about this series, but I hope some of you out there who enjoy seeing how things get done will give it a shot.

history.title: Death to Smoochy (2002)
history.review_title: Flat, Mean-Spirited and Humorless - Almost as Bad as Watching Barney Reruns Without Alcohol
history.text: War of the kid's show mascots, as a shameless Barney stand-in steals the national adoration (and television slot) of a down-on-his-luck Captain Kangaroo stand-in. With an invested Ed Norton as the former and a cackling, chaotic Robin Williams as the latter, the right pieces might appear to be in-place for some fireworks, but the film never gets there. Hopelessly predictable and cut-rate, it's a watery humorless mess. The cast seems to know they're in a stinker, too, with a steaming mound of half-assed performances and a full gallery of awful, borderline-offensive caricatures. Norton is really the only one who seems like he's into it, throwing his all into the part of a hopelessly naive nice guy who falls in bed with a den of vipers, though Williams admittedly doesn't get much substance to work with. Jon Stewart is particularly atrocious in his supporting role as a weak-willed executive with bad hair who constantly, pointlessly lingers around the fringe like a wet fart. Riddled with holes and desperately short on laughs, Smoochy's questionable morals seem to hint that the key to success in show business involves choosing the nicer of two warring mob factions. Bizarre, boring fodder without a purpose, this one was a real chore to finish.

history.review_title: More of a Self-Congratulating Lecture Than a Valid Cautionary Tale
history.text: Emma Watson plays Mae, a twenty-something who lands her dream job at "The Circle," your not-so-subtle Apple/Google/Facebook knockoff with sinister ulterior motives. Something feels wrong about the corporate campus from the very moment she arrives, but that doesn't stop Mae from mindlessly embracing the new gig and, quickly, ascending to lofty status as a global mouthpiece for the CEO (Tom Hanks in a Steve Jobs Halloween costume) and his underhanded cronies' narrow agenda. As a protagonist, Mae is infuriatingly naive and compliant. She's the proverbial horse-led-to-water, shown the dark side of the company's aspirations and then, against all sense of reason, doubling down on her support for the new evil empire. With a little nuance and a better understanding of metaphor, this could've served as a halfway decent Twilight Zone wannabe. Instead it's heavy-handed and preachy, forced and unfocused, with a blunt approach to morality that's more after-school special than Rod Sterling hypothetical. Flat, inept and simple-minded, it trips over its own feet in a feeble attempt to hit its misguided talking points. When it was all said and done, I felt like I'd been lectured by a loud, uninformed aunt on social media. I want to pat these filmmakers on the head and then back away

history.title: Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets
history.review_title: Stylish and Flashy, Valerian is a Conceptual Showpiece... but Not a Plot-Rich One
history.text: Luc Besson delivers a spiritual successor to The Fifth Element that's equally colorful if not half as deep. Visually rich and mesmerizing on the surface, it easily outreaches Avatar as a sci-fi fan's wet dream; a slick, breathing conceptual powerhouse to rival the cover artwork on so many pulpy, classic paperbacks. The art direction is a smooth continuation of Besson's earlier work, drawing heavily from European design and comic book artwork to set a scene that feels at once futuristically familiar and unsettlingly exotic. Designs for the various species of alien life are similarly remarkable and unrestrained, as are the wildly different habitats that have developed to house them aboard one massive, utilitarian space station. The opening scene, set inside a cross-dimensional bazaar, is a wonderful mishmash of creative world building and original twists on action movie tropes. But then it gets to the meat of the plot and... suddenly we're dealing with just another dopey laserbeam run-n-gun with a heavy, heavy emphasis on stale human characters and an over-reliance on CG. Forgive the constant comparisons, but it becomes The Fifth Element without Bruce Willis, Chris Tucker, Milla Jovovich, Gary Oldman or the blue girl singing opera to connect with the audience. Dane DeHaan and Cara Delevingne, wooden and flat with next to no chemistry between them, simply don't compare and the picture flails aimlessly without a firm leading presence. It's got humor in small doses and artistic vision in large ones, but without an equal narrative jab to match its creative haymakers, it falls quite short.

history.title: Despicable Me 3 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Silly, Light Fun with Gru's Old Crew, Plus a Few New Faces
history.text: Gru, his family and the minions are back to make a new friend and confront a new foil. This time, the opposition is former child star Balthazar Bratt, stranded deep in the 1980s, who takes out frustrations about an ancient sitcom cancellation on jewel owners and Hollywood big-spenders alike. Played with energy by Trey Parker and swathed in a dense cloak of pop culture references, Bratt brings a fresh new dynamic to the franchise that gives this third installment just enough of a boost to feel necessary. Most of those cultural winks were completely lost on my kids, of course, but they still appreciated his silly wardrobe, fly dance-fighting moves and crafty arsenal of unlikely weapons. There's a side story with Gru's forgotten twin brother Dru (both played by Steve Carell, of course), and a sweet arc that finds Kristin Wiig's special agent Lucy seeking a relationship with the reformed villain's three girls, but those feel like slight retreads and don't have the new criminal's panache. Clearly, Illumination was having a good time with Bratt, while the other plot threads were more like obligations. It's fun, with some great bits of physical comedy and a necessary return to the heartstring-plucking of the first film, though overall it lands in somewhat shallow waters. An improvement over the underachieving Despicable Me 2, if not quite up to the original's snuff.

history.review_title: A Riotous Buddy Comedy in Space, Spiritual Sibling to Marvel's Guardians
history.text: I had concerns after Ragnarok's trailers. Not because they were weak, but more the opposite: I worried that the finished product couldn't live up to the steep expectations they'd set. That, and I had anxiety that the out-of-nowhere neon '80s theme would be a thin, superficial gimmick, slapped on to ride a trend and nothing more. In both respects, I couldn't have been more wrong. The trailer's just the tip of the iceberg for this epic, sprawling, colorful, unabashedly hilarious joyride of an adventure. It does the big blockbuster moments well, with power and meaning and a shiver-inducing use of Led Zeppelin's "Immigrant Song" in two key spots. The dialog is right on-point for the duration, looser and more conversational than any of the previous Marvel films. Credit director Taika Waititi for that, allowing the cast to ad-lib freely in nearly every scene. Sakaar, a new planet that doubles as hub for all the universe's discarded crap, is a day-glow fantasy that would've been right at home in one of the Guardians of the Galaxy movies. In that setting, the retro graphics and glitchy synth score (a wonderful contribution from Devo frontman Mark Mothersbaugh) feel natural, and we're able to enjoy a fresh perspective on the Avengers' resident lightning-slinger. It does attempt to do an awful lot - I haven't even mentioned Cate Blanchett's sinister turn as this week's dark flavor - and that gives the first hour a rather scattered, random personality. Everything comes together nicely in time for the grand climax, though, and I left the theater with a huge grin and a new favorite of the MCU. It's everything I wanted, and a few things I didn't know I needed.

history.title: Lego Batman Movie, The (Blu-ray) (BD)
history.review_title: Biting and Satirical, Overstuffed and Scatterbrained
history.text: A sort of remix/spinoff of the formula that worked so well in 2014's surprising Lego Movie. Lego Batman hits a number of the same beats, from the abundance of stand-up comics in the cast to the quirky visual stylings and snappy musical numbers, but it also carves out plenty of time to make its own mark. Which, in this case, translates to a whole lot of nudge-grin-wink references to the caped crusader's long cinematic ancestry and some good-natured roasts regarding his cagier moments in other media. Batman as a pop culture icon is ripe for this kind of deconstruction, and the film is often quite ruthless about it, which feels refreshing and leads to some genuinely inspired takes on the character. Occasionally it can get a bit too cute and overreach, but that goes with the territory. Not every shot is going to find its mark. The exceptionally quick tempo can feel overwhelming at times, though, especially when we're jamming a dozen punchlines into the same spot that's been reserved for an important plot point. It functions for a greater purpose in the end, keeping the younger audience entertained with bright flashies while half the jokes sail over their heads, but at some points it felt like I'd just downed a dozen cans of Mountain Dew and my eyeballs were doing cartwheels. Entertaining but a touch on the shallow side, it frequently toes the line between overstuffed fun and downright sensory overload.

history.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Loose, Free-Spirited Fun: This is the Spidey I Know and Love
history.text: Considering how often Spider-Man has been filmed over the past fifteen years, the character really needs no further introduction. Marvel seems to agree, as they've completely omitted the standard origin story for the latest reboot (and merely glossed over it during his preceding appearance in Captain America: Civil War) to the benefit of everyone. Skipping the establishing shots and heading straight to the heart of the character - a high school kid, already in way over his head, who wants to fly with the Avengers - feels liberating and exciting, opening the door to all the good stuff that most other franchises would need an entire film's worth of development to earn. It's completely tangled up in the preceding MCU films, perhaps more than any of the other properties, which not only works to validate some out-there story decisions but makes the whole family seem even more interconnected and relevant than it already was. The shockwaves of the Avengers' first brawl in downtown New York, for instance, are still being felt; in this case, they're indirectly responsible for embittering (and arming) a man who would use that scorn to become The Vulture. But despite the wide connections and thematic similarities, Homecoming is very much its own thing. The phrase "street level" tends to be overused, but I can't think of a better way to describe Spider-Man's role in things. Where Captain America worries over government corruption or Thor throws down with gods and dark elves, Peter Parker is giving directions to old ladies and doing backflips on rooftops to amuse hot dog vendors. That makes him more down-to-earth and light-hearted, which are both keys to what makes the character tick. New York lives and breathes in this film, dirty and foul-mouthed but endearing all the same, and that plucky give-no-craps attitude comes alive in its home-grown hero. Peter also looks, thinks and acts like someone who hasn't quite figured out who he is yet, balancing his urge to be a teen and do teen things with his sense of responsibility and excitement over his evolving set of powers. Well-written, well-cast, well-acted and well-scored (seriously can't get much more spontaneously appropriate than the Ramones), Marvel's shown once again that nobody knows their characters better than they do. Tom Holland's Parker is appealing, witty, mistake-prone and worth rooting for. His supporting cast feels like a bunch of teenagers, not role-playing adults, and bring brilliant splashes of color to the film. Michael Keaton makes an excellent foil, sinister but not irredeemable. And the whole thing wraps up with one of the best parting shots in recent memory. It's not completely perfect, but in a way, that's almost fitting.

history.review_title: Dark and Daring, The Last Jedi is a Busy, Unpredictable Step Forward for the Franchise
history.text: Luke Skywalker takes center stage, returning to the screen (and the rebellion) after what seems like a lengthy hibernation in his family saga's long-awaited eighth episode. Of course, it's a creative wonderland, as all Star Wars movies are. Loaded with brilliant new settings, refreshing spins on old ones, wild unseen alien races and explosive action scenes, it retains its roots in an artistic sense. One particular scene, a lightsaber melee in Snoke's deep crimson throne room, sticks with me as one of the best-directed fights in the series. But there's much more to this picture than mere aesthetics. The Last Jedi constantly defies expectation, seemingly delighting in the chance to throw passionate fans off the scent. From character actions to fake-out non-revelations to the plot's relatively small scale, none of it is quite what I expected. More than once, I caught myself holding my breath, ready to be let down by a decision that seemed inevitable, and each time the film bucked me in a direction I hadn't considered. Sometimes that works to its benefit and sometimes it doesn't. It's a slower, more contemplative take on the franchise, particularly in the first act, which leads to a longer running time (longest of the entire series) without feeling too strung out or overly indulgent. Unlike The Force Awakens, Episode VIII uses its front-and-center returning cast to enrich and enhance the newer faces. Where Han Solo thoroughly dominated the screen, Luke and Leia use two very different methods to help Rey and Poe grow into heroes worthy of taking the spotlight. That's of crucial importance, and that it's missing from Finn's stalled character arc is a problem. Kylo Ren sees significant growth, too, successfully navigating a very delicate balancing act as his interactions with Rey, his light-side counterpart, gradually unfold. Not every gamble pays off, and it's hardly a film without faults, but I appreciate how often it was able to surprise me and its ability to wrangle so many threads together into a cohesive narrative. My first impressions have it a hair above the preceding episode, and on equal footing with Return of the Jedi.

history.review_title: Dumbo Has All the Ingredients for a Disney Classic, But it's so Short...
history.text: One of Disney's classics, though after seventy-five years its reputation may have outpaced the film itself. After the financial disappointments of Pinocchio and Fantasia a year earlier, the studio tightened its belt on Dumbo in an attempt to make up for the losses. It worked in one sense, giving Disney the box office victory it needed, but that penny-pinching and corner-cutting hurt the finished product. It's astonishingly short, barely weighing in at an hour including credits, which forces a sudden, jarring climax. The story's pace is quite smooth until then, taking its time to build characters and back-story, so by contrast the immediate rush to wrap everything up in a frenzied flash is disruptive. While it's cruising along in the first half, though, things are good enough. Speckled with colorful characters and a fresh circus setting, it bottles that classic, emotive Disney magic while still taking a few risks. The infamous pink elephant scene, in particular, is an unexpectedly surreal animator's playground that's several decades ahead of the curve. I was shocked to find offbeat similarities Danny Elfman's work in the film's score, too, which may suggest an even broader influence. Playful and heartfelt, though deeply under-cooked, Dumbo feels like a breezy short story when compared to the richer, more complete films elsewhere in the studio's early catalog.

history.title: Falling Down
history.review_title: Douglas is a Man Out of Time, Not to Mention Patience, in This Simmering Revenge Fantasy
history.text: Michael Douglas plays a working-class man, pushed over the edge by the stress of modern life, family problems, work difficulties and a whole slew of mental issues. He's basically on the warpath from the beginning, storming away from a traffic standstill to find (or instigate) a frothy, furious conflict with every step. Douglas's unnamed vigilante might play as somewhat sympathetic at first, or perhaps that was the intention, but as the climax approaches and more details are filled in, he's among the last to realize that he isn't this story's hero. Robert Duvall works a parallel route as the desk-bound former police detective, trying to get through his last day, who almost unconsciously cracks the case and throws himself into harm's way. There's a lot of subtlety and context here, which seems lost in Joel Schumacher's hammy, literal direction. Duvall's coworkers tease him relentlessly about dying before retirement, an obvious crack at the well-worn cinematic trope, but it plays as dumb and blunt rather than witty and clever. The rampaging madman is treated with strange admiration, marching through a hail of bullets like a superhero where he should have seemed detached and unhinged. I don't think Schumacher completely understood the story he was telling. With an excellent leading performance from Douglas and a sharp, surprisingly relevant script, it's a shame this didn't turn out better than it did.

Seems like so much more an innocent time. There is also --for me, coming of age in the sixites-- one scene of the two women preparing to go out clubbing, in all their sixties girl glory; big hair, cat makeup, girdles with lace panties and thigh high stockings that is much more erotic by comparison than the occasional nipple flash. history.title: Adam - Giselle / Carla Fracci, Erik Bruhn, John Lanchbery, American Ballet Theatre
history.review_title: Awful camerawork mars what could have been a perfect Fracci and Bruhn performance
history.text: I saw the name "Carla Fracci" and snapped like a salmon at this video. Now that I've watched it, I feel profoundly ripped off. Fracci's Giselle is legendary, and I was so looking forward to seeing her. But whoever shot and edited the film SHOULD have been shot. A dancer's body - ALL PARTS OF HER BODY - should be in the shot when she's dancing, and the shot should be at straight-on level, not overhead (or under-the-tutu, as it was for an unfortunate instant near the end of the second act). I know this ballet fairly well, and there is a part that I love in the second act, when Giselle does that series of small jumps that make her look weightless, then stays in place to do a series of little jumps-with-beats (I don't remember the terms). Fracci was doing that wonderfully well, when suddenly, in the middle of her footwork, the camera cuts to a FULL SCREEN OF JUST HER FEET DOING THE BEATS. That is a pet peeve of mine. Sorry. Then there were all the blurry bits, and the Wili-dancing we see only reflected in a pool of water (my theory is that they filmed a few steps, with one camera focused on the dancers and another on their reflection, so that later they could string the two bits together to make it look like one long dance sequence). And then in the first act, there were several inexplicable cuts to a barely-discernible face of someone of indeterminate sex, staring out at us with a coldly hostile expression on his/her face. It was like something out of "The Ring." I expected to get a phone call saying I had a week to live. My guess now was that it was the Queen of the Wilis, but it could have been someone who had wandered onto the set, for all I know. Oh, and I forgot to mention the horseback scene (as you may already have guessed, this movie was not a straight video recording of a ballet performance; someone tried to make a "movie" out of it, the way Baryshnikov did (successfully) with his production of "The Nutcracker".) All of Albrecht's entourage are riding horseback through the woods. We get an extended horse's behind view of them as they trot along. Unfortunately, the cameraman was apparently ALSO on horseback behind them with his camera, and the shot goes up and down and up and down with the motion of the horses until I actually started to feel motion sickness. But Fracci and Bruhn were so good. Lanchberry used to be the ABT orchestra's conductor back in the day, so it's not as if he didn't know that a ballet performance looks like. Maybe he spent so much time in the pit he figured that if he didn't need to see the dancers, nobody else did. So I'll be looking for more Fracci, but the pickings appear to be slim. But she's the Giselle they say she is, and more.

history.title: My Bodyguard (Widescreen Edition)
history.text: This film isn't aired enough. Chris Makepeace plays the new kid at a Chicago high school, who is bullied by a boy named Moody (Matt Dillon). He enlists the "bodyguard" services of the one kid everyone seems to be afraid of, a hulking truant named Ricky Linderman (played by Firefly's ADAM Baldwin, not Alec Baldwin as indicated in some other reviews here.) The arrangement doesn't last long, but both boys develop a friendship while each learns to confront their individual fears. Well worth watching.

history.title: Kripalu Yoga Gentle
history.text: I used to do Kripalu yoga on the weekends at a studio in New York. It was the best yoga class I ever had, taught by a wise woman who had done yoga all her life. When we moved, I really missed those classes. The local "gym yoga" classes here seemed so soulless. This video recreates my old studio experience in my home. Sudha is a wonderful teacher with a calm, respectful manner. I love this video. It's worth every cent I paid for it. I can't recommend it highly enough.

history.title: Total Stretch VHS
history.text: This review is for the DVD. I am in my 60s with chronic low back pain but I had no trouble doing this workout. But bendy people won't be challenged by it. A little too much choreography for me (I am really uncoordinated!) but for general flexibility, this might be a good choice for older beginners. Leritz has a likable manner and his directions are clear as far as they go. I would have liked to know more about proper form, and what I should be feeling where. I felt the hamstring stretch in my back until I tweaked my position on my own.

history.title: All in the Family: The Complete Series [DVD]
history.text: This is one of the best sitcoms of all time. Archie Bunker could easily have been played as a one-dimensional bigot in a forgettable show, but Carroll O'Connor gives him a humanity that makes us want to see him do better as he becomes wiser with experience. Jean Stapleton is equally fine as Archie's naive, good-hearted wife Edith. The comedy pokes gentle fun not only at the prejudices of Archie, but the moral vanity of his freeloading liberal daughter Gloria and her grad student husband Mike, who are forgettably played by Sally Struthers and Rob Reiner.

history.title: Beauty and the Beast (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Cocteau's "La Belle et la Bête" is unparalleled.
history.text: A classic Cocteau film which is pretty nicely done considering that it was apparently put together from several film elements available and directed by three separate people. The story is magical in the way it was filmed and the acting was very well done, particularly the one-dimensional character, Avenant, as portrayed by Jean Marais while he, at the same time, gives depth and emotion to the part of the beast. A special film which was a beautiful artistic creation in spite of severe financial constraints & limited resources in post-WW2 France. A story to own for anyone interested in classic film though I wonder if the cost of it being purchased on Blu-ray is worth the expense for the product does not seem to render a higher-definition video compared to DVD.

history.text: The Trip? Steely Dan may have said it best: "Show biz kids making movies of themselves an they don't give a....funk(?) about nobody else?" I cant remember. And I couldn't remember much about "The Trip". I saw it at the drive inn when it came out. I was 16 and smoking pot like it was going out of style! So that must be why I can't remember, right? There must have been some pretty cool stuff to "trip on"....right? Well, other than the house with the upstairs indoor/outdoor swimming pool, there's not much artistic value, special effects or soundtrack worth remembering. But the house, it's self had extreme historical value. At the time, it was home of the band "LOVE." As in "7&7 is - Love" (that's how it looked on my KRLA Top Forty Playlist.) It's a shame they weren't asked to participate in this movie. Because they were, as far as I know, the first commercially successful inter-racial rock band. I LOVE came together in L.A. late 1965' when composer, guitarist and lead vocalist Arthur Lee asked another brother, and 3 of his lighter skinned friends, 2 white, 1 Latino, to join musical forces. They had the perfect hippie name and attitude, more than a year before a hint of a "Peace, Love" hippie. A real cutting edge band, they combined rock, blues, jazz and Latin influences. They beat Lou Reed and The Stones to the future with the first heroine/suicide blues ballad: "SIGNED D.C." inspired by the suicide note left by their first drummer. Talk about street cred and cult status! A band full of outrageous musical mood swings. They were the perfect hippie rock band, which also, ironically recorded the perfect blue print for a punk anthem in "7&7 is," later to be recorded by The Ramons, and others, but none could match the rage of the original black vocalists! But this film wasn't as ground breaking. And the music sucks! It seems the so-called writers just guessed at what a "trip" might be. There's no real special effects. More like they just threw together random film clips, mixed with Fonda's home movies of Malibu. And why the dixieland jazz when Fonda realizes he's gonna get laid? Seriously? How lame is that? Would've been a good time for some LOVE from the house band! Hey Peter! Dennis! Bruce! You guys really blew it! Such a shame. Bet ya LOVE could've gotten this film into the Rock& Roll Hall of Fame. So far as show biz kids go, The Monkees were way more cool, and way more, in the words of Mickey Dolenz:"Psychedelic!" Now I guess I'll have to buy their trip movie, "HEAD."

history.title: Backfire
history.text: There appear to be several different versions (or packagers) of this fine little film. Mine is the Platinum Disc one, which is 90 minutes, full-frame, and uncensored. The timing and A.R. are not those given for the original production, but, if anything is missing, I didn't notice (relative to the version that shows on HD cable channels). The image is rather soft in places, like a 480i picture, but not in every scene; most of the movie (and, yes, the fleshy bits) look like a 480p DVD. I think the bit rate got up to 7.5 Mb/s in places, which is excellent detail for a DVD. Go figure. Being a rather intimate mystery story, the reduction to full-frame doesn't really hurt so much. Worth watching.

history.title: Big Bad Mama [Blu-ray]
history.text: The Blu-ray is a definite upgrade from the DVD, although not as much as one might expect. Still, it's the best version I've seen since the theatrical release. What I didn't recall was how unusual Wm. Shatner's performance was; note the economy of gesture when he lets Joan Prather escape. A fun film.

history.title: Little Fauss & Big Halsy [Blu-ray]
history.text: The film is entertaining enough, but nothing special. However, Redford gives the most clinically exact portrayal of a full-bore psychopath (not a slasher film serial killer) you'll probably ever see unless you actually meet one. I think it takes him about 10 minutes of screen time to wangle food, shelter, sex and money, starting with nothing but his shirtless body. He uses people relentlessly (like an untalented version of Rip Torn's character in Payday). It's interesting that Fauss's mother distrusts him from the time they meet; most people don't know they've been with a true psychopath until he's gone (and taken what he wants).

history.title: Now You See Me 2 [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD]
history.text: Magic, seen live, is awesome but, since the movies are themselves a type of magic in which literally anything can be faked, a movie showing magic acts begins with a handicap. The first in this series got by with a clever story, but this one seems forced and less convincing. It's still entertaining enough to watch, but that's not why I gave it one star. The problem is that the blu-ray is Atmos encoded and, like other Atmos disks I've played, will not produce the "standard" 5.1 channel sound. The audio track repeatedly cuts out, and you have to listen in flat 2-channel stereo. I don't think millions should be forced to settle for inadequate sound so that a few hundred (or thousand) people with 10 or more speakers in their room can be wowed. The disk producers should (1) warn customers that the disk doesn't support 5.1, or (2) include 5.1 channel sound on the disk (there are 5 soundtracks, none of them 5.1), or (3) put out multiple disks so we can vote with our dollars as to which we prefer.

history.title: How to Plan an Orgy in a Small Town [Blu-ray]
history.text: Back in the 50's, the British made a number of modest, charming and gentle comedies (often with Peter Sellers) that weren't LOL funny but kept a smile on your face throughout. Later, Bill Forsyth (Local Hero) managed the same effect. Delightfully humane comedies, with a tinge of weirdness. Now the Canadians have produced several more, e.g. A Dog's Breakfast, and Y.P.F. (which this very much resembles). And , for trivia buffs, the latter all have major links to Stargate: Atlantis. This is, in part, a modest ribbing of small-town life, but is more about relationships (with no treacle). The simulated sex is played for humor, and the nudity is contextual and limited (and if that's a body double in Jewel's big nude scene, I don't want to know that. Ever). Like the other films mentioned, it is pleasantly satisfying If you have been deterred by Amazon's BD-R warning, in case BD-Rs are as inferior to BDs as DVD-Rs are to DVDs, don't be. I haven't seen a BD-R before, and this one has a dark label side which makes it hard to see the data side, but the latter does appear much darker than a standard Blu-ray. There is no indication on the box or disk that this is anything but a Blu-ray, and my Oppo reads it as a standard Blu-ray. The bit rate is between 20 and 30 Mb/sec, like an ordinary BD. The picture is crisp and detailed (and the film has high production values for a small, indie film), and looks beautiful on a big screen. Indeed, if this really is a BD-R, I see why they blocked them from the North American market; you could record far better ones off satellite than you could buy from the studios (with all that annoying garbage like forced previews and time bars, which this disk doesn't have). I don't buy DVD-Rs because they are standard def visual hash, but I won't hesitate to buy BD-Rs if they all look as good as this one.

history.title: Deepwater Horizon [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD]
history.text: This is the third Blu-ray I've gotten from Amazon that had a Dolby Atmos soundtrack, and none of them will play 5.1 channel sound (it cuts out every few minutes). There is no encoded 5.1 soundtrack, so the only option is to listen in degraded 2.0 stereo sound. As always, it could be some specific combination of components that causes this to happen, which could be avoided by not buying movies with Atmos soundtracks except that Amazon doesn't warn you that the disk doesn't have 5.1 channel tracks (the standard for almost all non-Atmos disks). They tell you a lot of other stuff, but not that. Interestingly, the Atmos demo at the start of each disk plays perfectly in 5.1, but never the film soundtrack. Amazon, if you read this, PLEASE WARN us about Atmos-encoded disks.

history.title: Apocalypse
history.text: This is essentially a German retelling of Cormac McCarthy's The Road. It is obviously dubbed, competently in places and hilariously inept in others (esp. the crowd scenes). The acting is quite good, and the scenic design very good. Since it all takes place in a post-apocalyptic 2016, its time has come and gone. It's very depressing, of course, and functions more as a horror movie than anything else, but you can sit through it. It was produced by Roland Emmerich, but it's more intelligent than that would suggest.

history.title: 3 Bad Men (1926)
history.text: This film is the culmination of John Ford's considerable silent film period (something like four dozen westerns alone). It's an excellent and entertaining movie, tremendously augmented by a newly composed, folksy music track. The Blu-ray version has quite good image quality, given the age of the film. The acting, and script, are more subtle than I expected (referring to the matrimonial potential of an obviously gay character, one of the trio says that if his heart's in the right place, it doesn't matter what sex he is). The action sequences are sometimes compelling; although mostly shot with a static camera, there is a pan across the wagons lined up for a land rush that is staggering (that shot alone reveals why the film lost money). The ending was touching, but I thought it could have been much more so with a bit more character development; apparently, that's what the studio excised, against Ford's wishes. The film teeters on the edge of being a masterpiece but falls short, and the hammy acting of the main villain made that inevitable. None-the-less, this is one of the most enjoyable silent films I've seen in years.

history.title: Bobby Deerfield
history.review_title: It is a good movie... but at the end of it all it is completely pointless!
history.text: This is a weird movie by director Sidney Pollack, featuring Al Pacino. (SPOILERS BELOW). The racing scenes are reasonably good. There are two Grand Prix featured: France and Jarama (Spain). The car used by Pacino character is a Brabham-Alfa Romeo, driven by the late Brazilian driver Carlos Pace. There are two main plots: in one of them, Pacino is trying to figure aout, together with the team's engineers, what mechanical shaninigans may have caused the fatal accident of his team mate, The other plot is the most important. Pacino goes to clinic in Germany to interview a survivor of the above mentioned crash, looking for clues. There, he find a mysterious and highly uptight woman. She asks him for a ride out of the clinic, and their relationship blossoms, with Pacino cheating on his girlfriend/wife whatever. But the woman is terminally ill. The movie portrays Bobby Deerfield as egocentric jerk without heart, and being in love with such a terminally ill lady makes him open up a little and be less self-centered. But the woman dies soon after, and Pacino ends the movie alone, withou any inch that he has changes or not. (and after crashing his own race car in Jaram, also without any clues about what caused the accident). Weird movie, great photography.

In her a phone call to the ICC could have made things amusing.. it didn't even occur. He has a 0 experience dolt of a new attorney help run his new big case. I think we have seen this dead horse beaten enough. He has a substance abuse problem (this one pretty much falls out of the cliche' bag if bad writers look the bag and wonder "how can I add depth to my character?"). In the end it is just a big bile of rehashed cliche's and terrible writing mechanics, slapped together into another bad legal movie. On the positive side 1. Billy Bob Thornton 2. If you have a lawyer (say in GITMO) and you need to get information out of them, then forcing them to watch this will make them talk in a hurry. On the negative side. 1. sometime the stupid is so strong that it can cause you physical pain.

As a scifi fan I have to say this was a terrible piece of garbage. The idea is that Earth is in trouble and there is a new colony out in space that has just been founded. Knowing that water is incredibly important to humans they set it up on a desert world that in plausibly only has water below the surface. No, it is not a cold world where the water is frozen. Once on the planet people hallucinate and go to their deaths and yet they do not pick another planet. Yep, super dumb. Then there are the colonists. If the colony has to survive and you have billions and billions to choose from.. Well in this case they pick colonists from other scifi they have seen. The drug dealer, the bad cop who plays by her own rules, the gruff obese driller, the obese botanist, any cliche characters that you can take form other series and movies. It is like they do not understand that it takes money to haul weight into space and so we will not be seeing fat astronauts, not to mention all the other bad hires who fit a cliche but not common sense. The newest member is the last person you would send, a priest. A priest who smokes like all the other cool priests you have seen in the last 20 years. Why a priest? Well they are hamhandedly trying to make it look like the colony founder has found god on the possibly living planet. Yep.. So you can guess that in the future this will be the Faith and Spirituality scifi series that makes Star Trek 5 look good. I would love a new scifi show, just not this show. If Amazon plans one, please go with the stereo type that nerds love scifi and that nerds are smart. With that in mind, hire smart writers instead of morons who just want to rip off everything they have seen, than fill the rest of the show with drama bombs based on idiocy.

This is the opposite of Better Off Ted. I watched the whole thing, towards the end I was just hoping for a smirk by the end. No dice. Do you remember that kid in Jr High who though he was funny because his mom once told him he was? Do you remember how everyone else told him to shut up and that he was not funny? Do you remember how after everyone laughed at one of the funny kids, how unfunny kid would try to step in and be funny? Do you remember how he wouldn't shut up and you began to hope he would actually die? At least he finally got that mentally disabled kid to laugh at his jokes, so the 2 hung out alone and didn't feel such a need to bother the rest of humanity. Yeah, this show seems to have been written by that kid. It is like someone with no comprehension of humor tried watching shows they were told were funny and then tried to copy them. So this show tries to copy other stuff you have seen but fails to copy it in a funny way. In the end I was angry and wanted those 30 minutes of my life back. We need a term for comedies that offer up 0 laughs, or grins or even a smirk. I'd suggest "Cancer" but getting cancer was WAY funnier than this show.

history.title: Passengers [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Stupidity for drama's sake. Please keep your brain locked in the off position.
history.text: So glad I borrowed the Blu Ray rather than buying. WARNING: Some light spoilers here that may have been in the trailer. This is just a "trapped on a desert island" set in space with painful acting, stacked on top of writing that would shame a mediocre writer, and horrify anyone who passed Junior High science. This is the story of people going from Earth to a new Colony world on a ship with no redundant systems or backup plans to deal with malfunctions. So this is completely unbelievable and should be to anyone who has ever heard the word "parachute". This story also depends heavily on the deplorably stupid idea that by the time we can travel between the stars, that the human life span has not been extended at all from the modern day, even with the magic medical technology that the ship has. This amazing medical tech is a single machine for ~5,200 people and can only be used by approved crew members, so if you find someone who needs real medical help like defibrillation (like those machines on the walls at your work, next to the band aid box) and you are not a high level crew member, that person is dead. Yep, the medical tech is magic amazing but too dumb to do medical on its own, that defib at your work will pretty much handle itself after you slap the pads on someone and hit a button. Space ships will use all available space because to have more internal space means having to build more surface area. Yes, we get a pretty ship but it is an insanely stupidly designed ship. Also when it comes to surviving a malfunction caused by damage, planting trees in decks and such just dooms the ship/passengers. Now for the "romance". In this movie a really good looking man revives a good looking woman to keep him sane as he travels awake to a colony world where he will be about retirement age when he arrives. So for no good reason they talk about dying of old age before getting there (they are traveling at half of C). She complains about how he murdered her.... and then they live happily ever after. Now to get an honest idea as to what really happened imagine the guy was hideous because in the future they cannot extend human life, so maybe they can't make you better looking. If the guy was gross, this would be a horror film but it is a romance because he is good looking. Yes, his needing to wake her up also depends on less entertainment technology than we have today. We already have people who live out their lives on line and in games, with future AI I would doubt that players know who is human and who is not. There is also the assumption that he cannot "Netflix and booze" his way all the way to the destination, while viewing hundreds of years of the best entertainment humanity has produced.

history.title: Arrival
history.review_title: Five stars for what looked like a one star movie.
history.text: I borrowed the Blu Ray and I'm glad I didn't buy this as it is a single viewing movie. Any additional times you view it will be to show it to friends. The movie starts and in the first seconds you are saying "Please do not use this cliche again" with in the next minute or few you are saying "I wish you didn't do that but I knew you were going to". From there the movie trots out piles of dead horses to beat. It is a painful trudge through dumb moments and bits that have been recycled more times than you can count. They were stupid the first time they got written and every time after that that they got stolen and reused... But then they throw in a clue or two here in there that make you ask "Hmm, what's up with that?" the end reveal is too slow in coming so it loses "The Usual Suspects" impact. Like "The Usual Suspects" this is a single viewing movie. This is a three to four star movie but earns its last star(s) for the bravado of the writer/director making a film to directly ridicule the audience's stupidity. Embarrassing and making fun of your customers, few have the guts to do that. For those who do not understand how the writer/director is making fun of the audience, I will hide the spoiler as best I can by putting it in comments. This is your end twist, so if you have not seen the movie and plan to please do not look in comments.

history.title: Ghost in the Shell (2017)
history.review_title: Worst movie of the last few years.
history.text: I'm so glad I rented this rather than buying. If you are unfamiliar with the Ghost in the Shell anime or anime in general then this is just a bad movie. If on the other hand you are a fan of the Ghost in The Shell anime or manga then this movie is an abomination. This starts with with casting a movie star who is best known for having her derriere in the center of the frame when the director can justify it and not for her acting ability, in the lead roll. White washing is not the issue, anime hit it huge in the US because most of the people thought everyone in anime was white despite their Japanese names. People really have a hard time believing that characters like Sailor Moon are actually Japanese and not Norwegian or Icelandic. So white washing is not the problem. The problem is that when people complain that their are no strong female character in film, often characters in anime are held up as a contradiction to the statement, among these Motoko Kusanagi is front and center. Not in this movie however. After it gets Americanized: Motoko Kusanagi's genius gets stupidity washed. It is like the writer heard the complaints about the original movie's English dub being dumbed down and said "hold my beer". Motoko Kusanagi's strength gets weakness washed. Motoko Kusanagi's top level hacking ability gets "How do I start emails?" washed. Motoko Kusanagi's confidence gets insecurity washed. Motoko Kusanagi's presence gets cringing emo washed. Systematically the writers attack and destroy everything that makes Motoko Kusanagi, Motoko Kusanagi. If Deadpool was an anime, these writers would have his character being a mute, vegan, pacifist by the time they were done making the live action movie. Once they have done that they just tack in some iconic scenes from the original movie and call it a day. With the exception of Takeshi Kitano the rest of the casting was bad but lets face it, you could cast Takeshi Kitano as the lead in Heidi and it would still seem like a good casting choice. I have no idea what they were thinking when they cast Batou. Fans will also notice other terrible writing choices like swapping out Togusa's iconic Mateba for a new Chiapa. Not that the Major's team gets much screen time to begin with. Well until Hollywood decides to make a live action Akira or Cowboy Bebop movie, this piece of garbage reigns supreme as worst film adaptation of an anime or manga... but lets look to the future and imagine Michael Cera playing Spike in Bebop or Shia Labeouf as Kaneda in Akira!.. Wait, lets not look to the future, I have changed my mind about that.

history.title: Wind River [DVD]
history.text: I do understand that the writer/director wanted to make a point about the fact that Native America women's missing person status is not quantified by the federal government. However, I am absolutely sick & disgusted with so many films that include non-stop shootouts with blood & gore all over the place. Shooting the wolf was bad enough but I do understand about sheep herders/cattle owners wanting predators killed (my mother grew up on a ranch in Wyoming). But the rape/murder scene was too horrific & went on Far too long. I sped through it, hoping to see that all the evil men (also predators) would be devoured by mountain lions. The repeated reference to a mother mountain lion & her kits made me Hope that the evil men (or at least one of them) would be eaten by lions. It would have been a pure Chekovian moment. I won't do a spoiler but this didn't happen. It was all too severely depressing. I am starting to realize that Sundance movies are Not for me. It's important to know facts like how bad it is on reservations & how Native womens' disappearances are not noted. But TOO MUCH VIOLENCE.

Way too much violence. I am so sick of shoot outs with blood & guts flying. Horrifying. I realize the writer/director was trying to make a point Native women disappearing & no one investigating the disappearances. However, why show so much horrific violence. The wolf being shot, the woman being raped, sodomized, her boyfriend being murdered (I sped through all that). Just horrible. Done for shock value, like Peckinpaugh. The acting is very good but the violence is over the top.

Moody atmosphere. Sad time period, the fall of The South. A group of women in a Young Ladies' School are trying to survive this harsh time in the south. A badly injured soldier is found by a little girl picking mushrooms. I immediately thought "Chekov! Mushrooms on the mantlepiece!" It was quite dark in most scenes. But I do understand the director was setting the film in a time when there was no outside lighting, everything was candles or the muted sunlight coming through huge oak trees covered in Spanish moss. I did have to put captions on, as some actors mumbled. This is a problem with films nowadays. The women take care of this soldier & complications ensue. Everyone does a great job of acting. Colin Farrell as the soldier is brooding, tempting, furiously damaged. Nicole Kidman is erect, noble, competent & brave. Kirsten Dunst is lovely, vulnerable, intelligent. Elle Fanning is a cat-eyed hussy, fun to watch her. The younger girls are all talented. Especially Addison Reike as Marie.

history.title: Tutankhamun [DVD] [2016]
history.text: I absolutely loved this mini-series. All the acting was brilliant. It followed the lives of archaeologist Howard Carter, his benefactor Lord Carnarvon, Carnarvon's daughter (the first woman to enter the tomb of King Tut, Carter's competitor & eventual friend (Herbert Winlock), a woman archaeologist (Maggie Lewis) and many others. The setting is gorgeous. The excavations are believable. The anticipation & excitement as first the steps are found (by an Arab boy) & then the chamber, still sealed. I well remember reading about all this when I was 10 years old. To this day, archaeology excites me. My husband & I have done expoloring (not excavating, though) at many neolithic sites all over Europe. It was fascinating to follow this story of the most amazing archaeological find in history.
Depressing, dark, endless torture. Hellish. I usually enjoy Scorcese films but this was warped.

My husband & I had watched "How to Be a Latin Lover" starring Eugenio Derbez and Loved it. Hilarious all the way through. This film is more serious but also has a lot of hilarious scenes. This film shows how a Latin Lover becomes a single Dad. He is such a loving father. Then the mother (who deserted her daughter as an infant) comes back, demanding custody. Complications ensue. It is a beautifully realized story with Excellent acting by all. The little girl is phenomenal. The ending is sad but strangely uplifting (I do believe in Heaven so this is the hopeful part). Throughout, Eugenio Derbez directs with care and love. The colors are absolutely beautiful: tangerines, golds, bright reds, verdant greens.

history.review_title: Confusing: no real sense of a satisfying ending
history.text: My husband's mother is British. We love British/Irish/Scottish movies & tv shows. I adore Jim Broadbent & my husband is a huge fan of Michelle Dockery. So we were drawn to this film. We do not require car chase/shoot 'em out movies whatsoever. But this film was too long & drawn out with no real "sense of an ending." First of all, why are all the young men (Broadbent's youthful friends & himself) sandy-haired fellows? It was difficult to keep them apart. My husband kept thinking the young man playing the young Broadbent character (Tony) was Adrian Finn (his best friend) in the flashback scenes. The music really brought us back to the 60s (Psychotic Reaction in the scene where Tony meets Veronica, with her Leica camera). All the scenes in the 60s were so spot on. The cinematography was wonderful throughout the film. Every actor in this movie did a wonderful job, young & older. But the film was based on an extremely enigmatic book. There really is NEVER a sense of an ending. No information is given to explain why Veronica burned the diary her mother had bequeathed to Tony. Or who the father of Veronica's "half brother" might be. Is it Tony? Did Tony sleep with Veronica's mother? If I rated this Only based on the acting skills, it would get 6 stars. But based on the fact that we are left mightily confused, it gets 3.

ZERO stars. I think highly of Nicole Kidman & Colin Farrell as actors. But this writer/director must have some form of serious mental illness. He has now made 2 films which are horrifically sadistic, monotone, meaningless & cruel. Actors think they are doing something highly unusual/artistic. Sorry, it's just balderdash.

history.title: Dear Zindagi
history.text: The only reason why I wanted to see this movie was because SRK was in it. I think this is the first time I saw this actress and didn't know that she was more famous than SRK. I'm assuming this because the biggest part in the movie was given to the main actress. The story is all about a woman's life and SRK doesn't show up until half the movie is over. It was a little boring until he did show up. Getting to the reason of why she was emotionally broken, was interesting and heartbreaking. I kept expecting these two characters to get married. I like SRK in these serious roles and in the roles he plays when he got older. All of that singing and dancing that doesn't make sense in the story, doesn't appeal to me and it usually runs on to the point of boredom. I've seen many of his films and too many have poor acting, silly behavior or too much of the same singing and choreography. The two I've seen so far, where the acting was well done, and I liked a lot, were Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi, and Chak De! India. When he plays a humble guy and not a conceited guy, I think his acting is much better. As he got older, his acting also improved and the more famous he became, he started playing in movies where they could afford to hire better actors. At first his acting in "Dear Zindagi", didn't seem natural, but he got better as the story progressed. It was a good story, but it's not a movie I want to see again or own.

history.title: Jab Tak Hai Jaan (2012) 3 Disc Set- (Hindi Movie / Bollywood Film / Indian Cinema DVD)
history.text: Everyone who had anything to do with this production, did a wonderful job. The scenery in the first part of the movie was gorgeous. Wherever it is, I want to go there. There was one scene where Katrina Kaif's acting wasn't that great, but she was pretty good in the rest of the movie and she danced and sang well, if that was her voice. I liked her character's faith in Jesus. Her character's relationship with Jesus was more give and take than what I'm used to seeing. I enjoyed watching SRK while he portrayed this honorable character. His character's personality was similar to the altar ego in Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi. The best acting I've seen him do was in RNBDJ. I think it was the first Indian movie I saw him in that got my attention. Though there was a lot of scenes with their religion in that one, it was still an enjoyable movie. In Jab Tak Hai Jaan, the story was also good and it was fun to watch. I recognized many of the dances in this one that were in RNBDJ, but it was still entertaining the second time around. I love all the music in Jab Tak Hai Jaan. The later song and dance scenes that the reporter was doing, ran on longer than I liked, but she also sang and danced well and the music was good for dancing. (She was also the main actress in RNBDJ.) I could have seen more of the street dancing, in JTHJ, because it was cool and was refreshing that strangers would have this camaraderie and skillfully danced with strangers. The dances were interesting and music was a good blend. It was disappointing that the reporter was an atheist in the story, but she was very likable, cute and very charming. I liked her energy, courage and boldness. She was also funny and joyful. I liked her better, and thought she and SRK's character made a perfect pair. The first time I saw this movie was on Netflix and liked it so well, that I bought it. It's also tempting to buy the soundtrack.

history.title: Vice [DVD + Digital]
history.text: My friend picked out this movie to watch. This is pure fiction and pure filth. It's a story about evolving artificial intelligence who were given a sensitive heart, and it's about an immoral human being who got rich from letting other rich immoral people commit all kinds of crimes and abuse against them and get away with it. I'm exceedingly grateful I didn't spend a cent on this video. If I had, I would have used a sledge hammer on it and thrown it in the trash. Many scenes were highly offensive and I got up and left the room many times. There were scenes involving lesbians, a guy raping a woman and beating her up, and a lot of shooting, killing, bad language and using God's name in vain. I never understood the urge people feel to use his name in vain when some of them don't even believe in him. Why not use Buddha as a cuss-word or Muhammad? The actor on the right of the cover, played a hero police detective. And there were a few other decent people in the story. I became interested in the last thirty or forty minutes. The plot got interesting for me, when a mistreated female android, escaped the laboratory from a sadistic scientist. The chase scenes were too long and I lost my interest again.

history.title: Hwarang : The Poet Warrior Youth (K-Drama w. English Sub)
history.text: I love how this story plays out in the first five and last episodes. Although, it kept my interest throughout the entire drama. It was fun watching the confident skilled fighter who was carefree, funny, a little oblivious, yet protective and clever. And he was also nice to look at. This part was played by Park Seo Joon. He looked so different, that I thought this was a new face I hadn't seen before. As the story progressed, he lost his magnetic carefree manner. Though the PSJ character didn't stop being attractive, in the early scenes of the story, there was a suspenseful energy (like how you feel watching a leopard getting ready to attack) that got lost as more things happened to him. That was too bad because he was more appealing that way. Actress Go ah ra's role was lovable and funny too. Her expressions and manner were delightful. She was forthright, and was no respecter of persons, unless they were her dad, the king and queen. It was so funny how she sometimes spoke to the lords and those in authority. Her skills were medical and storytelling. And it was appealing to watch both sides in action. I missed watching her amusing energy while telling a story. PSJ's character was amusing in how he didn't always do what was expected. And she was like that, too. Her manner was appealing, sometimes even when she was crying. I'm glad I hung onto the end. While my mood was being affected by the story, I was asking myself why I was watching another period piece and ready to give up on it until I realized I was on the 19th episode. But the last episode had such a satisfying ending. All the actors were believable and sometimes funny, especially the lead trainer. The twists in the story were interesting. There were many good looking men in the drama. The queen was the prettiest female. Overall though, the men were better looking than the women. It was an entertaining twenty episodes and the time went by fast. I would love to own this video and watch it whenever I wanted, as I've already watched the drama three times.
