history.title: Game of Thrones: S7 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: as they stopped lifting entire lines straight from the book like they did in seasons 1-2 (not a bad thing
history.text: boi the quality of the show's writing completely came off the rails and completely collapsed for season 7. the quality of the dialogue had been noticeably decaying very slowly starting around season 3-4, as they stopped lifting entire lines straight from the book like they did in seasons 1-2 (not a bad thing; the dialogue in the books is clearly superior most of the time). Season 6 was a vast improvement over the boring mess of season 5, but it seems as though all the writers retired after that season and a new flock of fanfic-writers were hired on for season 7. the dialogue sounds clodding and tedious, less like the style of the previous seasons and more like that written by kids trying to imitate the speaking style of the show without having understood anything being said without someone else helping explain it to them. With all the "adult" characters in the series either dead or displaced (or killed off this season), the younger characters are put more and more in the spotlight, and the writing still treats them as the "younger" characters despite countless years having passed and several of them very noticeably grown up now. Arya still behaves in a boorish, piggish manner of an 11 year old that, despite being a homeless vagabond for 6-7 years, a young adult would've grown out of or at least learned how to behave reasonably. Bran seems to have completely forgotten basic human interactions, and goes around claiming he's no longer Bran but the Three Eyed Raven, then goes on to say he doesn't know what that means but that he's also still himself. There's an entire subplot involving him receiving the dagger initially used to try to kill him that goes nowhere and makes no sense at all. He supposedly has the full Greenseer sight like the old Three Eyed Raven had, but he barely ever uses it until it becomes necessary to propel the plot. Any and all substance in the character interaction and dialogue between fan favorites like Jaime and Bronn or Tyrion and Varus has been completely drained and squeezed dry, leaving almost all their interactions as empty snarking banter that serves only to fill up time with snark-riddled exposition. It gets to a point where you're sick of hearing these people talk and you start identifying more and more with Sandor Clegane in how much he hates hearing snarky people snarking all the time at each other, nonstop with the snark. Scenes between Cersei and Jaime are nearly impossible to remember, they all blend and merge together with the same empty exposition-talk. Daenerys is still, sadly, bereft of any real substance. She appears to have learned absolutely nothing from her experiences in Meereen, and basically has nothing to do other than to be the avatar of Liberty come to Westeros. Book Daenerys feels much the same, but at the very least she suffered from not learning from her bad decisions, or was frustrated by her inability to resolve a situation in a satisfactory fashion, with no backup plan available. She was much like Walter White in the last season of Breaking Bad, having "conquered" all his great enemies and overcome immense odds, but still at heart the same hesitant, meek man he was at the very start, not an unstoppable force of nature. TV Daenerys is an unstoppable force of nature. Never does she seem to be in any danger, no matter if she's riding a dragon into battle against worn out troops with a host of Dothraki cavalry to support her, nor when she's riding in the freezing cold with hardly any support against literal ice demon things and their relentless zombies, wearing the same leather outfit as she did on a hot flaming battlefield without a hair out of place or a bead of sweat. Even when Viseryon is killed, it's telegraphed so hard that you'd be shocked if it didn't happen. That would appear to be a problem in terms of the season overall; ever since the show creators got to reach the Red Wedding (which they themselves admitted was the very event that inspired them to make the series and that they would be happy that, if the show got cancelled or otherwise suspended for some reason, they at least got to depict the Red Wedding), it seems as though they've gradually lost interest in the plot, and are steadily rushing along the plot. It's become a running joke now that characters seem to Fast Travel wherever they're needed, with little to no realistic passage of time. As well, no consideration seems to be taken for the characters. Some of them just appear and re-appear just for the sake of the actor mugging it for the camera. The appearance of Beric Dondarrion and Thoros of Myr last season was a big disappointment in finally putting an end to any speculation that Catelyn Stark would be resurrected, but with them marching north with Sandor Clegane, there was hope that they would find some other interesting use in service of the overall story. Instead, their role ends this season with them just tagging along with the main character's stupid mission, then dying off. The fighting with the Wights has also been so badly watered down that they're no longer the horrifying tanks like they seemed to be in Season 1, where cutting off large pieces of them did nothing to stop them. Now, we see people stabbing the Wights through the "heart" and the Wights going down. Our heroes are able to fight off hundreds of them with disgusting ease like it was Lord of the Rings or a video game, Wights being easily dispatched with things that would dispatch a human, not a frenzied living corpse which can still fight even when literally cut in half in either direction. The writing has also fallen apart to such a degree that gaping plotholes are emerging now, this late in the series. Suddenly Beric Dondarrion suggests that the Night King, a guy who has only existed for a few hundred years, is the key to defeating all the White Walkers, who have existed for at least 10,000 years. Making the Night King the worldly avatar for the Great Other (who has been referenced before in the show, though not named the "Great Other") makes sense, but acting as though killing the Night King would somehow cause ALL the White Walkers and Wights to die off like it was Skynet is some incredibly shoddy storytelling and a cheap copout to ending the series without requiring much in the way of titanic battles and heroic sacrifices. Another plothole involves Dorne and even the Reach. Dorne was sabotaged from Season 5, turned into a nonsense story (with nothing in common to the books) that they gave up on, dropped a bridge on, then scrounged up to support Daenerys, then given up on again. The Sand Snakes and Ellaria Sand are dispatched and what few ships they have serving Daenerys are destroyed or captured and so... Dorne is suddenly somehow out of the war. The same with the Reach, as House Tyrell loses its ships, and then loses Highgarden, and... they're suddenly out of the war. This was literally the biggest plot point for seasons 1-3, that Robb Stark would win major victories, beating the Lannisters in every battle, and yet still losing the entire war because he could not make any serious gains and the Lannisters could replace their losses quickly. This is all completely thrown out in a single episode's single 10-minute naval battle that somehow completely knocks 2 entire major factions out of the war completely. And they can't even use the excuse of being war weary, as Dorne was not fighting for the entire series, and the Reach had only begun fighting AFTER Stannis was destroyed and the Riverlands besieged by exclusively Lannister/Frey forces. They try to use the copout that the Tyrell armies are suddenly not good fighters, and that this explains them being completely destroyed in a single battle against a tiny Lannister force. A lot of this season feels this way, as though the writing staff were populated by fans of the series, not interested in losing any of their favorite characters or seeing them suffer any serious defeat or setback, and not interested in any sort of event to upset the status quo as established at the end of season 6. No one in charge of writing seems to care anymore. Plotholes are gaped and exploited just to get the series going to the next series of events, and everyone is just moving along to get to the end. The only people who seem to be putting in any effort anymore are the people in charge of the visuals, sets, and costumes

history.title: The Witch
history.text: I went into this overly hyped by all the gushing praise it received, as well as being genuinely scary or something. the intro to the movie had a silent, naturalistic aura that was highly reminiscent to me of "There Will Be Blood", and the film's overall style and tone was absolutely perfect. there was tension to be had with the young twins and the accusations tossed about at thomasin, as you're caught between wondering whether parental wisdom or puritan stupidity will prevail during these tense fights. The dialogue is all done in a 17th century Puritan style for added authenticity and the acting is all around solid, but ultimately the story goes nowhere. There's supposedly the insinuation by the director that the events that unfolded may have been the result of hallucinogenic fungi from the dead crops, but absolutely nothing in the movie itself suggests this even remotely. Due to the highly naturalistic tone of the film, there's no real room to have anything done in a surreal or unreliable fashion, or have a heavy soundtrack pounding during certain scenes, so it's likely not possible to play with this level of uncertainty in reality. But there's also no attempt made in it, either. Everything is presented straightforward, with no real surprises or twists or even shocks. Things happen, other things happen, things happen after that, then suddenly we're naked in the woods and the movie's over. The tone allows for a general unease and creepiness to pervade, but something about the film or possibly my own tastes prevented me from feeling uneasy or creeped out by it. I was more frustrated by the puritan stupidity by which the family was so ready to basically abandon thomasin and eject her from their family based on literally nothing, escalating when something actually does start to happen to her brother. the style in which the film was shot, along with the carefully researched dialogue and set makes it feel more as if this was a proof of concept film, showing that a realistic Puritanic-Witch-era film with that sort of dialogue and no flashy supernatural effects or dopey witch costumes or shrill old male judges shrieking in wooden courthouses at women could work as a good and profitable film. It works as a proof of concept, but it doesn't actually do anything beyond that.

history.title: Automata (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: the story of the man who did nothing
history.text: this began with a simple and intriguing enough concept of a post-apocalyptic future in which robots were built to help fix earth damaged from some manner of abnormal solar radiation which has wiped out the vast majority of humanity. when it becomes clear the projects assigned to the robots aren't actually working, people start to turn on the robots, directing irrational hatred and frustration towards them that the planet is essentially doomed. All of that is covered in an introductory expo-dump with title cards and still images. the movie begins with the idea that these robots are bound by two protocols; never to hurt humans and never to touch themselves (for repair or alteration) and at the start of the film, a randomly drugged up guy finds a robot repairing itself and shoots it in the head. then we get to Antonio banderas as Jacq Vaucan, who works for the company that makes the robots, has a pregnant wife who does nothing in the film and serves no purpose, and is tasked with figuring out who is responsible for altering the robot that was caught repairing itself. this somehow leads him and the drugged up cop to Cleo, a robot that has apparently been altered and works as a prostitute. the drugged up cop played by Dylan McDermott for absolutely no reason at all goes berserk, shoots off Cleo's leg, and says he will slit Jacq's throat next time they meet. Jacq then encounters the person responsible for altering Cleo, Dr Dupre, and they have an incoherent, tedious philosophical discussion involving evolution and sentience with the clumsy phrase "Come down from the tree". Then, somehow, the movie completely goes off the rails. It genuinely feels to me that a significant portion of the plot got excised at this point, because out of nowhere the company Jacq works for somehow thinks Jacq is the one responsible for altering the robots and has somehow betrayed his entire species. They also inexplicably have footage of a robot altering another robot, footage which never appeared at any point earlier in the film, nor do we ever see or later find out where this footage was acquired. So now the company sends some random hobo children to murder Dr Dupre and Jacq, but Jacq escapes with Cleo. He then gets knocked out in a car crash and Cleo and a bunch of other robots are now dragging him through the desert, called the "Sandbox". There's a whole lot of time with Jacq whining to the robots and conversing with them. We also go back to one of the company men, Robert, who hires the drugged up cop to go find and rescue Jacq and bring him back alive, while the company is trying to kill him for no real reason. The drugged up cop finds Jacq and immediately tries to kill him for absolutely no reason, and Jacq kills him with a flare gun. The drugged up cop's partner escapes and tells the company that Jacq was in the desert with some robots he says were "alive" for no real reason. The robots did not in any way act differently from regular robots, nor display any sign of disobeying the two protocols at all. Something went seriously wrong in the writing or editing in this part of the movie. eventually they take Jacq to a place at the end of the desert where they meet the person responsible for first altering robots... and it's a robot as well. this one is apparently conscious and self-aware and sentient and has free will and is building a new robot. All Jacq wants to do is go home. The company, at this point somehow convinced that Jacq is responsible for altering ALL the robots and trying to escape from them and has some secret heinous plan of some sort which is never explained or even fully described. The best we get is a backstory expo dump with one of the company executives describing how they made a fully conscious sentient AI that learned everything from humans in 8 days, then became smarter than humans, so they made it develop the Two Protocols for future robots, then deactivated it. Aside from making for a very interesting backstory, this is in no way relevant to the movie at all, and is never brought up ever again. So now the company has kidnapped Jacq and Robert's wives and Jacq's newborn daughter for absolutely no reason. They then send some of their people out to the desert to get Jacq, and then for no reason at all start threatening and intimidating Robert and saying "You don't have a home anymore" when Robert panics and says he just wants to go home. So naturally Robert shoots at the guy who threatened him, then gets shot in turn, having only grazed him. At absolutely no point is this random betrayal explained in any way. In fact, when Jacq shows up and finds Robert dying, Robert accuses Jacq of betraying all of mankind, while Jacq literally says that he hasn't even done anything and is just trying to get home. Robert then tells him they have his wife, and Jacq runs off somewhere. The robots are now trying to use a ferry to cross over a dry river to get to a radioactive area where they can go on and live free from humans. The company people then arrive and start killing the robots, apparently thinking they are hiding Jacq or that Jacq is trying to escape with them or something. Then Jacq appears in a car and runs down most of the company men, then gets into a brief shootout with the head guy. The head guy then accuses Jacq of betraying mankind and his species and such. To re-iterate, Jacq has done LITERALLY NOTHING since running from Dr Dupre's hideout. He hasn't disobeyed company orders (or hasn't been given enough time yet to do so), he hasn't stolen anything, he hasn't been caught doing anything, and yet they've somehow pinned a broad-ranging incoherent conspiracy to him while he was literally being dragged half-dead through the desert. For no reason, Jacq only seems to implicate himself, by saying that humans are not his people anymore, which leads me to believe that a massive amount of the movie ended up getting cut. One of the robots, built like a cockroach of some sort, goes and kills the company guy and saves Jacq. Cleo and the cockroach then go off into the desert and Jacq and his wife go home. So ultimately, this movie spent about 50 minutes playing out with a moody, noirish vibe somewhat reminiscent of "Blade Runner" with hints of I, Robot (the short stories novel), after which literally half-way through it combusts into an incoherent mess of ill-defined accusations, nonexistent conspiracies, and several thoroughly boring sets of scenes in the desert culminating in a curiously tension-free action sequence. And it bears repeating yet again that Jacq Vaucan has not done a single thing for the entire second half of the movie, yet if you hadn't watched his scenes at all you'd think he was Jason Bourne kicking ass all over the city in a fight to clear his name.

Only 18 years of his life have been *settled* - now about to be unsettled by his sons interest in professional sports and a bigger issue (see the movie). He is obsessed about past and present fences - those he cleared w a ball and bat and the one he builds around his house . Who knows why? Some great writing here but 95% is philosophical , reflective ...and "Preachy". No spoiler intended but don't wait for Denzel to say "where's my coffee?" Picture runs too long and is quite convoluted . Worth seeing, in bits and pieces, especially if you enjoy anything with Denzel .

history.review_title: Great bits And pieces and occasionally brilliant script - but inconsistent and flawed . DeVito fans go for it.
history.text: Deck The Halls ? Not much going on I dude the house st Christmas time here, it’s all about the antagonist (why ? Who offended him?) Danny DeVito , a blue collar guy with a few bucks and plenty of debt , who moves into a very quaint Massachusetts town to settle down - but first he must “out -Christmas “ Matthew Broderick , the neighbor next door . Why ? The movie doesn’t explain the “challenge “. The premise is really cool . Danny DeVito is excellent . He’s not as engaged as he could be but he acts very well. A lot of Louie DePalma going on which is just fine with him. His straight man, if you will , is Matthew Broderick , and he plays it too straight . This dude can act if he wants to but the script too often gives him fluff to sort out - or maybe the director is at fault for not putting more nuance in the character . The frantic DeVito and the milquetoast Broderick . Good casting . But I think the latters best work was decades behind him - to wit, the naive college kid in The freshman (1980). I think Tom Hanks would have been a better choice than MB. I think back to the great The In Laws w Peter falk and Alan Arkin, the fbi guy and his brother in law , the mild mannered account (as I recall). There was rhyhme and reason to all the shenanigans . I want to say this movie would have been very good if the powers that be shaved off about 12 minutes and capitalized on three or four great set ups for hilarity which fizzle . One glaring : at the winter fest the two rivals take a breather from all the contests and sit down to watch three hot dancers in short skirts do naughty holiday numbers . Turns out that two are DeVito’s tall sensuous daughters and the dancer in the Middle is Broderick’s rebellious teen . I guess her new friends got her out of her shell ? The script doesn’t support that. Anyway , it was a good chance for another DeVito prank on his competitor , get him to call out lecherously to his own kid ....but no, both daddies are schocked sbdcrun to church to wash their faces in absolution water . This picture is very reminiscent of the 1980 “neighbors “, w ackroyd and belushi . This 2006 flick is funnier . But to think what a first Class comedy director could have wrought with *those* two .

history.review_title: Season 6 starts out great. The burglar episode where the guys each have ...
history.text: Season 6 starts out great. The burglar episode where the guys each have a different story as to how the crook was knocked out. The episodes with Mr. T and Mrs. Z were pretty cool. BUT....once you hear the name, "Maggie McKinney," RUN! To me, Maggie and her son Sam ruined the show. Mr. Drummond getting married again should have been reserved for a series finale, rather than midway through season 6. With the addition of Sam, it took away the brotherly bond that Arnold and Willis had, and makes the show's opening theme song useless. "....a man is born, he's a man of means. Then along come two, they got nothing but their jeans, but they got, Diff'rent Strokes...." I also thought the scene where the boy is found hanged was done poorly. A guy hangs from your ceiling, you scream all of two seconds, and afterwards, it's like they forgot he was there. history.title: Brigadoon [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A great movie with a nicely done blu ray version.
history.text: My wife and I love this movie and have multiple versions on DVD. I have a hard time believing that this movie was done entirely on a soundstage. Even with the clearer images of the blu ray remastering and a 53 in high quality screen I cannot tell the forestage from the painted backgrounds. The blu ray version looks and sounds great. I compared it briefly to a standard dvd version copyright in 1997. The image on the standard DVD is much softer than the blu ray with less detail. The sound is fine on both but a bit crisper on the blu ray. Of interest is the differences in image framing between the two programs. The blu ray has a bit of the side edges cut off which allows a larger overall image however for those interested in seeing how the cinemascope image actually looked my earlier DVD copy seems better as it shows the entire image at the expense of large bars on all four sides of the image. If you don't own a copy of this movie I would suggest the blu ray for the clearer image and better sound. If you already own a copy and are not enamored with the film, like my wife and I are, I am not sure its worth the cost of the blu ray disk. There are a few deleted scenes but no other extras on the blu ray.

history.title: Sommernachtskonzert 2017 / Summer Night Concert 2017
history.text: What a great concert! Even though outdoors the sound was excellent and the video had great color saturation and clarity. To hear John Williams' Hedwig's theme from Harry Potter played by the amazing Vienna Philharmonic conducted by a great conductor grounded in the German Classic repertory was revelatory; it did not sound this good when I heard it in the movie theater. history.review_title: Great movie now on blu ray
history.text: Topper is one of my favorite movies. When one considers when it was filmed, the special effects are amazing. I compared this blu ray version to the 2003 Artisan standard DVD. The blu ray has sharper background and more detail but the sound is similar and the imaging of the key figures is fine. I am not convinced the blu ray adds that much compared to the earlier DVD but if you don't own this movie I would suggest getting the blu ray for the better image quality. If you love his movie then definitely get the blu ray. The blu ray gives a choice of black and white or colorized -- please, please watch it in black and white as the director intended it to be watched.

history.title: Holiday Inn [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: a great film, even greater in glu ray
history.text: This is one of our favorite movies. My wife and I watch it at least once a year. The single disk blu ray edition is a visual and audio improvement over the standard DVDs that we own. The original black and white in blu ray sparkles and has impressive detail. The colorized version is also included on this disk. We watched that version also. Though I am not a fan of colorization, this colorization actually added to our appreciation of the film. For example the back curtain on the fourth of July sequence really stands out in the colorized version (red, white and blue stripes) while it is so-so, hardly noticeable in the black and white version. The extras can only be accessed from the colorized version and include a number of very interesting shorts and interviews. The commentary track on the colorized version by Ken Barnes is very interesting. If you want a DVD of this movie, I would suggest this blu ray version.

history.title: Berliner Philharmoniker - Waldbhne 2015 from Berlin - Simon Rattle - Camera, Lights, Action!
history.review_title: Away from the classical but not a "pop" orchestra
history.text: This is a review of the blu ray version of this concert which, at this writing, is not listed on the Amazon website. As with all previous Waldbuhne concerts the disk is technically excellent. The sound is vivid with a large dynamic range and there is minimal to no outside noise. The color is lovely particularly the transition from daylight to darkness. I was not thrilled by the music selections, but other reviewers were more enthusiastic. It think it is hard to make a coherent piece from the fragments of sound required of a movie soundtrack. In a few cases composers have gone back and created suites based on a soundtrack they have written -- I have heard some beautiful works by John Williams. However for this concert I felt that the very large, usually excellent Berliner Philharmoniker was not nimble enough to pull this off.

history.text: I watched this film on DVD -- contained in a horror collection of 10 films. This film is the worst of them all. It commits the sins of being totally boring, certainly not frightening, no character development, no explanation of what is going on, long scenes that go absolutely nowhere, editing and cinematography that is quite inept. I had to fast forward through some of it, because I'm thinking "this is a really boring film that is going nowhere. Should I keep watching? Maybe it will go somewhere. ... let's skip forward and see if anything happens." As it turns out, not much happens, and you can skip through most of this film or watch it straight through-- you still won't be interested, and there will be no explanation. So, my best advice: skip this film. The only reason I am reviewing it is because I looked it up to verify that my opinion matched with others'. Yes, it does.

history.title: The Shadows
history.review_title: Poorly executed. Should have been a 30 minute short
history.text: This film was in a collection of horror films that I have. It is not a good film. But, it is not the worst film ever made (which is the best I can say about it, and why I don't give it a 1-star rating. I've seen worse.) An indie film with low budget, bad script, very bad acting, borrowing from many other horror films, and some really bad acting. Friends are holed up in an old lighthouse, after apparently being shipwrecked/crashing into another ship (this part is not shown in the film). For some reason, love triangles a la Melrose Place are inserted into the script. Doors open (even though locked)and slam shut, and become locked or stuck. This happens many times. Girls run out of the safety of the lighthouse, into the storm, for no apparent reason. This happens many times.The "pirates" or shadow creatures keep trying to get into the many doors and windows that are barely boarded up. Not sure why they can't just get in, but that does take up a lot of time. Very dark photography, so we can't see what is going on. This should have been pared down to a workable 30 minutes, instead of the 90 minutes running time. Obviously, this is some sort of first attempt at making a film, maybe a student film. It has some good elements buried inside its way-too-long running time. With better actors, and a tight script, the director could re-make this as a successful short film, since she obviously has some talent. But, here she has bitten off more than she can handle.

history.title: The Babadook
history.review_title: Not a typical horror film: complex psychological horror is depicted
history.text: 4.5 Stars. "The Babadook" is not a typical horror film. It is unusual in that it tells a serious story, and can be interpreted as depicting mental breakdown in progress, with all "paranormal" goings-on reflecting the inner turmoil of the protagonist. The mother-son relationship is the core of the film, along with the mother's inability to accept the car-accident death of her husband, 7 years ago. We actually have two mentally handicapped individuals depicted: the son has some serious issues, and the mother is still in morning after her loss 7 years ago. Both individuals feed upon the other, causing the Babadook's importance to increase in power and take over both of their lives. The kid's rather normal fear of monsters is taken up and amplified by the mother in her own mental breakdown. No outsiders actually are witness to the "monster" or out-of-the-ordinary happenings. All these "happenings" seem to occur only from the mother's point of view. Her little boy does not actually claim to see anything, though his imagination successfully terrorizes him. This is a bit "scary", but it is not just a horror story intended to scare you. So, those looking for simple, scary monsters may be disappointed.It is not "The Candyman", in other words. It is an intelligent film -- regardless of genre-- and can be compared somewhat to the surrealist horror film "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari", from the 1930s (I think). Or, there are other psychological horror films that are comparable. The internal turmoil of the characters are depicted, along with the interface with the external world. That's not easy to do successfully. The acting, cinematography, script, sets, etc. are all extremely professional. There is no feeling of "low-budget" amateurism. To the contrary, this film was done on the highest level of film-making. Surprising, since this is the first film made by this director. The "extras" on the dvd are minimal. But, the interviews with cast and crew was very informative. Highly recommend watching the interviews, as the themes and context of the film are well-explained in detail.You will get a lot out of it.

history.title: Sabotage
history.text: I am not a fan of this film. It seems to be very highly over-rated by critics and others. I do love Hitchcock films in general, but this is a very "clunky" film that is well-below normal Hitchcock standards. The characters throughout the film behave in a most-unrealistic manner. That's the thing that really detracts. For example, when Mrs. Verloc (the wife) and Mr. Verloc (her husband, and sabateur) find out that Mrs. Verloc's kid brother has been blown up in the bombing incident, they really do not react in a any fashion that we would consider "normal" today. Their behaviors are so abnormal as to make me wonder why no critics are pointing this out. It's amateur hour in depicting "grief" -- if that's what you want to call it. Mrs. Verloc does not even appear very upset when her husband confirms that,yes, it was he who gave to bomb to the boy to carry. [ Yes, I know she's thinking maybe she should stab him. That scene, again, was very amateurish. And, she successfully stabs him -- and he dies immediately.] There are many instances of "what the?..." regarding human behaviors depicted in this film. I won't belabor the point, though. [Does anyone notice that there was absolutely no sense of chemistry or love or affection between husband and wife? I didn't even realize they were supposed to be a married couple at first. I thought he may have been her long lost uncle. So, any resemblance to real people is strictly coincidental in this film.] Sorry-- it really "bugs" me that so many consider this a great film, when it clearly is not. The cinematography is good, though. Typical Hitchcock, with unusual angles, etc. The characters behave in a nonsensical manner. The plot is OK, but the idea that Mr. Verloc is under suspicion because he claimed to be sleeping when the the electricity failed by sabotage -- but several people said , no, he was "out". That is ridiculous. That's your basis for questioning whether somebody is a terrorist? [Compare this to today's world: Say, you don't know anything about the "school bombing" because you were sleeping, and somebody says-- no," He wasn't sleeping!" "Arrest that man! He must've done the bombing!" Ridiculous. But, that is what happens in this film, essentially. Overall, this is a bad film. But, for it to be a Hitchcock film, that makes it very disappointing.

history.title: The Hellstrom Chronicle
history.review_title: Great documentary disguised as "science fiction" horror film
history.text: I purchased the Blu Ray version on Amazon about a year ago. But, I see that the Blu Ray version is not currently offered. I think that Blu Ray was the only version offered when I purchased it. I saw the film in 1971 in the theater, and I remember it being billed as a horror film. I used to go every Saturday to see horror film matinees. This is a thing of the past. But, I remember being confused about Dr. Hellstrom. Was he real? The note at the end seemed to say he was not real. I remember thinking: we are doomed. Insects will take over the world. I never saw the film since 1971, but I had often thought about it. I looked online over the years -- but never found it until about a year ago. So, I was excited to see it again. This film is definitely a documentary, disguised a bit, to scare the viewer into thinking about the bigger picture. Everything in it is as true today as it was back in 1971. And, the photography is incredible, standing up to anything you've ever seen before on any Nature doc or Science Channel doc. That's why I was pleased to have the Blu Ray version. But, it is not widescreen, and there are no extras. Just the film. The film depicts a wide array of "monsterous" insects in their natural habitat, gorging on plants or one another or on animals. Also shown is a variety of reproduction methods used by assorted insects. All filming is ultr-close-up. Dr. Hellstrom is the narrator who explains what is going on, and who's thesis is that insects will always be here, no matter what man or nature does to destroy the earth. They simply multiply so fast that any obstacle can be solved rapidly by simply evolving to confront the obstacle. Humans, on the other hand, cannot evolve so rapidly. This is basically true. But, Dr. Hellstrom does not delve into the beneficial aspects of insects -- except briefly for bees. He presents the viewer with an endless variety of terrifyingly-efficient killer insects and relentless eaters.So, while everything he says is true, there are other reasons that we do want insects-- at least, some insects. The insect is not properly placed within the context of nature as a whole. Still, it is scary. This is an excellent film to show to high school students. It can generate a lot of thought about the place of Man in the universe, evolution, the rapidity of evolution (which is now seen by science as occurring more rapidly than previously thought), ecology, etc. The only thing fake about this film is the fictional Dr. Hellstrom.

history.title: KONG: SKULL ISLAND: SE
history.review_title: Great special effects, but is just a bad fantasy about killing creatures that man has never seen before. Disappointing.
history.text: Amazing special effects -yes. Story- basically a re-imagining of the original, with action that nods to the original (fighting with flying helicopters, picking up and saving the beautiful girl) Predictable -- yes Character development -- none, really Humor -- Yes, too much for a horror/thriller film. But OK for a childish fantasy, which this is. Funniest lines-- John C. Reilley, who plays a very odd character Big disappointment-- the film displays (and seems to teach) that it is perfectly normal and OK to kill a newly-discovered species "just because". The original encounter with Kong (by the helicoptering mission) goes right into attack mode! A more nornmal reaction would be amazement, followed by, hey, we have to study this thing. But, no, in this film, the reaction is: kill this giant ape! It's really big, and might be dangerous! Must be killed!. So, this sort of attitude is 1) not really what we would expect and 2) not a good idea to be passing along as "normal". So, because of this ridiculous plot, I am not a fan. Set up for sequels-- you bet. They set up a never-discovered island where giant creatures exist both on the surface and underground. No explanation for this, but it means that they will go back again -- and definitely kill some more.

I don't understand her motivation in this film (I won't elaborate, but you won't understand it either). The bat-guy (again, I won't elaborate) really does make this a "must-see" movie, though.

history.title: Tai Chi Zero
history.review_title: Odd combination of good story and questionable production
history.text: The story is interestingly good but it is inconsistent. You have a character that acquires super powers but is plagued from a side effect of that power. He then goes to seek a cure of sorts for his skills problem. When he gets to this place of masters he suddenly becomes a weakling idiot and his skills are diminished for no apparent reason. Then the story starts to jump between making sense and suddenly glorifying the characters of the story with increased abilities. Basically the flow of the story is not balanced and some of the parts are over dramatized with bad acting in those situations.

history.text: This movie has some great realistic fight scenes (No wire work), a better than good story line and very good acting. Some of the fight moves were so fast it was hard to follow the strikes and how did they keep from really hitting each other? It was strange seeing Keanu Reeves being a bad guy but it was a nice change for him. I felt like the ending was to quick and seemed to be missing something but I just can't figure out what it is. Maybe a kiss on the mountain top, but then again I'm somewhat of a romantic. I say See it.

history.title: Falling Skies: Season 2
history.text: The series captured my interest from day one. It has many intertwining stories weaved into every episode that connect well to the next one without dragging the story line out into endless dialog that babbles on-and on-and-on. It also does not dwell on melodrama for very long which is refreshing. Although the series is based on a fictitious apocalyptic event with scfi space invaders it was made with realistic believable human reactions and awesome alien creatures and effects (Finally). The acting was above standard and the characters were very interesting. I thought the contrast between the non-aggressive and aggressive posture of some of the characters were to separated. I believe most people would have a have a mix balance with some extreme moments. Usually people with extreme attitude are not well accepted and are cast out quickly. It always amazes me how lax security is when unknown elements are present. The stupid things always make for problems and I find myself thinking that I would never do what the characters are doing in the story and It drives me nuts. Its great fun to watch.

history.title: Tank Girl
history.review_title: Tank Girl a wacky retro movie
history.text: I love this retro movie with its silly punky cartoon style. It does have some sexually suggestive moments that young teens often flirt around. The plot is centered around a futuristic post apocalyptic style society in which the powers that be control the population by hording all the resources. Of course there is an under ground resistance and a rebellion but it is as wacky as Lori Petty can make it. I gave it 3 stars because of the naive way the theme develops and its implications of a casual 60's style, lack of a healthy moral code of conduct.

history.title: Cowboys & Aliens
history.review_title: A fun SciFi Western that challenges the norm
history.text: I kinda liked this out of the ordinary SciFi Western that the critics panned. It is great to see something a little different than the same OLD THEMES re-made over and over again. Doesn't Hollywood have any kind of creative imagination any more? There are tons of SciFi books that have been out there and loved by the readers for years, yet all we get are the same old stories that are maybe altered just enough to be a little interesting. OR maybe it is the limited scope of the movie going public that can't seem to grasp new concepts that lie just outside of their commercialized comfort zones. How shallow it that?

history.title: Breaking Bad - Season 03 (4 discs)
history.review_title: the Breaking Bad series, it's edgy, sinister and sucks you into the story
history.text: Who doesn't like the Breaking Bad series, it's edgy, sinister and sucks you into the story. But remember you need to start form the beginning of this story to get the true feeling of what happens and why. Having lived through the 60's I have seen people that easily fit into the characters of this story. It is scary that such people exist but life is full of viciousness and men that don't care about anything but their own version of how to live and treat other people. This is a story about people who teeter on the edge of both worlds and how they manage to slip off one side or the other and back again. You learn to hate them and to have sympathy for them but then realize it was their choice that lead them down the rabbit hole. Like dominoes, one thing leads to another and before you know it you are plugging yourself into the story line, good luck with your out come.

history.title: The Shadow of the Tower
history.review_title: A series that reflects the coldness of this king.
history.text: Though well acted, I found this series as cold and dreary as its' protagonist. While Henry VII was an efficient king, he was not a pleasant one, and unfortunately neither is the series. Henry VIII may have been a monster, but at least he was a colorful, flamboyant one, unlike his father. The series is of interest from an historical perspective, but NOT from an entertainment one. A documentary would have served the same purpose. It is not that I want historical dramas to be so embroidered that they devolve into colorful fantasy. I don't. In fact I have been known to criticize historical inaccuracies, but this series just doesn't cut it. It is a totally colorless "sister" to "The Six Wives of Henry VIII" and "Elizabeth R."

history.title: The Jewel in the Crown (25th Anniversary Edition)
history.text: I must be crazy, and am certainly a minority of one. Others have complained about the picture and sound quality, but while at least somewhat valid, these factors are not the issue for me. I remember starting to watch this much-touted series when it first aired some thirty years ago, and quickly growing bored with it, and I was hardly a kid even back then. It had all the elements that I should have loved...an exotic setting, visual and historic accuracy and a superb cast, and yet it somehow left me cold. Now, all these years later, I figured it must have been me, I must have missed something, so I decided to take the plunge and try again. Lo and behold, I still found it dreary and boring. I tried to persevere, and slogged through about half of the series before giving up in utter frustration. For one thing, I did not find any of the characters in the least bit appealing or sympathetic, even those who were not nasty or bigoted where hopelessly naïve or shallow. I have read several of the other reviews and find myself wondering if I had watched the same show they had. Oh well, to each his or her own!

history.title: Fall of Eagles
history.text: An excellent series. I watched it, enthralled, when it was originally broadcast, and was delighted when it was issued on DVD. It is sumptuous, as historically accurate as any such series is likely to be and the acting is generally superb. My reasons for withholding the fifth star are two. First, in typical Hollywood fashion, the cover touts John Rhys-Davies as one of the stars, no doubt because his name is somewhat more familiar to American audiences than many others. However, he only appears VERY briefly, perhaps five or ten minutes, out of a series that runs almost eleven hours! I readily acknowledge that this is a minor complaint. My second is a bit more substantive. While, as previously noted, the acting is almost uniformly high quality, I found Charles Kay's performance as Tsar Nicholas II a bit problematic. Though an inept and clueless monarch, Nicholas had two redeeming qualities from everything I have ever read: he was a devoted family man, and he was consistently gracious and considerate of even the lowest servant with whom he came in contact. Mr. Kay portrays him as utterly humorless, acerbic and even waspish. I would attribute this to the writing and direction were it not for the fact that I have seen other performances by him, and this persona seems rather consistent. Michael Jayston's portrayal in "Nicholas and Alexandra" seems more accurate. Nevertheless, a wonderful series.

history.title: Almost Human: The Complete Series [DVD]
history.text: Yet one more example of the often bizarre and frequently incomprehensible programming practices that permeate today's tv. If a program isn't INSTANTLY watched by every human (and android?) on the planet, yank it and replace with yet another inane sitcom! This was a really great show: thought provoking concept, wonderful casting and acting. great writing, superb production values and emotionally charged interactions between the leads as well as the secondary characters, spiced with droll humor, leavened with poignancy. In short, a masterpiece in every way. I thank the powers-that-be for releasing it on DVD. Merci, even if the show was shown no MERCY!

history.title: Masterpiece: Wolf Hall
history.text: I attempted to read the book(s), but did not care for the writing style, in spite of the historical period depicted, which has always been a favorite of mine. Nevertheless, I decided to watch the series. I was rather bored with the first episode, but chose to watch ensuing episodes. I found Mr. Raylance's portrayal of Cromwell growing on me, and, indeed, so too the series as a whole. I must say, though, that I continue to find Damian Lewis' portrayal of Henry VIII rather low key for such a notoriously flamboyant character. Whether this is a product of the writing, directing or acting...or a combination, is a matter of conjecture, but it is a bit strange. I would remind other viewers to keep in mind that the oft, formerly seen obese, near-cartoon-like portrayal of Henry is very misleading. Holbein's portrait, which would seem to be the basis for such portrayals, was painted rather late in Henry's life. In his youth, he was slender, athletic and handsome, and didn't become heavy until his late forties. At the time of his marriage to Anne Boleyn (1533), he was still, at 42, in relatively decent physical condition. All in all, a thoughtful, serious attempt to portray an historical period accurately, albeit from a rather different perspective.

history.title: The Lost Prince
history.text: I clearly remember, when Queen Mary died in 1953, my own mother commenting that SHE had been the true embodiment of a queen. Well, if by that she meant a cold, rigid, humorless woman, more concerned with public perception than she was about her own children, then I would have to agree. This movie, wonderfully produced and acted, does not help Mary's reputation, or that of her equally cold and indifferent royal husband, George V. If we are expected to believe their attitudes were a product of their time, we need look no further than the current queen's reaction....or lack thereof, in the wake of the death of Princess Diana in 1997, more than 80 years after the events depicted in this movie. It is, however, a wonderful insight into the inner workings of the world's most famous royal family, and a very poignant exploration of the tragic life of an obscure member of that family.

history.title: Druids [DVD]
history.text: I have always been fascinated by the story of Vercingetorix, since reading the Classics Illustrated version of Caesar's Gallic Wars as a teenager. However, while the story in this film is therefore of interest, I believe Christopher Lambert was a poor choice to play the noble Gaul. Not only is he a barely mediocre actor, the very timbre of his voice is off-putting. Then ad the thoroughly Germanic Klaus Maria Brandauer as Caesar and you have a less-than dynamic duo in the lead roles. I have given this production three stars for the effort it makes to tell the story of Vercingetorix, despite the quality of the actors.

history.title: Daniel Deronda
history.text: While I find George Eliot's writing ponderous and difficult, the story of Daniel Deronda is, in itself, very interesting and moving. This dramatization is extremely well done. Furthermore, despite my opinion of George Eliot's writing style, I must commend her courage in exploring the Jewish aspect of the story. Hers was an era of rampant and blatant anti-Semitism, when virtually all Europeans imbibed Jew-hatred with their mother's milk. It took an extraordinary person to overcome this overwhelmingly prevalent attitude. It is a story both gripping and poignant. Highly recommended.

This is a beautiful movie, visually exquisite. Furthermore, it is well written and, for the most part historically accurate. All of that would hardly matter if the performances weren't of equal quality, which they, undoubtedly are. Even the smaller roles are cast from strength, most notably Jim Broadbent as King William IV. My one, slight caveat about the casting, which has been noted by another reviewer, is Paul Bettany as Lord Melbourne. His acting is fine, but he definitely is too young for the part, as Melbourne would have been about fifty-eight at the time of Victoria's accession. I would also like to suggest that those who enjoy this movie should watch the BBC series "Edward the King' which traces the career of Prince Bertie, the future Edward VII. The portrayal of Queen Victoria in that series is far less flattering than in "The Young Victoria." Though she was unquestionably a great queen, she was, unfortunately, a considerably less wonderful parent. She treated her nine children like servants, and made it quite clear she had little but disdain for Bertie, whom she blamed for Prince Albert's early death. That, however, is another story, and that reality does nothing to diminish our pleasure in this portrayal of the young queen.

history.review_title: A supreme work of the dramatic arts!
history.text: Why, oh why, can't I give this incredible series 10 or even 15 stars? It would deserve every one. The basic story, the writing, the acting, the sets and costume....all simply, and utterly glorious. So engrossing that you barely notice how few scenes take place outdoors, one would assume in an effort to trim the budget a bit. Those scenes that are "outdoors" are filmed from a relatively close vantage point, so you can't tell if they were actually filmed outdoors or on a sound stage. And guess what? It doesn't matter one iota! As an historical costume buff, I would like to take note that this was probably the first drama taking place in ancient Rome that didn't use the typical generic costumes. Covering a time span of almost a hundred years, the costumes actually changed as one would expect in such a time frame. But the writing and the acting, are, of course King....and WHAT a king...or, in this case, emperor! Another reviewer has commented on Sian Phillips portrayal of Livia. A true tour de force if ever there was one. In one scene , as she appears to be nursing one of her victims, said victim, unaware of what she has done to him, tells her how kind he is. In one of the greatest lines in the series....or ANY dramatic work, she responds with supreme, bloodless unctuousness: "Kindness has nothing to do with it." The writer should have gotten an award for that line alone, and Ms. Phillips an award for delivering it! I could go on and on. Suffice to say that if you have any interest in historical drama, this is one to savor, over and over again.

history.title: The Mothership Connection Live 1976
history.review_title: Only took 40 years for me to see what I've always imagined ...
history.text: Wow! I don't know what to say... I didn't know this existed. It's everything I imagined was going on (and more) when I was a kid in the 70's listening (in particular) to Mothership Connection, Dr. Funkenstein and Motor Booty Affair, just how I pictured the live show, but it took 40 years for this "youth" to actually see it. If you are a fan of that period or this band, you will not be disappointed. Yes the sound is very good and the video is somewhat limited by a "network TV" look, but not distracting or too dark for me. Blu-ray probably wouldn't have made much difference, the DVD is great quality and there's a nice 3-page synopsis inside the case. "You won't believe how they party"!: There are a lot of people on stage - all amazing, apparently even some of Sly and TFS and Bootsy's Rubber Band members joined them for this and future shows on this tour (Sly bowed out after a couple more dates.). Everyone sings. And well. Everyone. I didn't know Mr. Clinton used three very gifted guitarists on this tour, including one who is also my favorite band vocalist Glenn Goins - hard to believe he was only 22 years old here and would pass away just two short years later of Hodgkin's lymphoma. Sad, but I am grateful to have this audible and visual memory of him and the whole P-Funk 1976 experience.

As to the facts portrayed in the film and true story, both are beyond incredible. If you look up the historical/true facts, where Pvt. Doss kicked away the grenade saving many lives, was in a fox hole and he was wounded with 17 pieces of sharpnel. Then he was later wounded in his arm, breaking bone, and making one arm all but useless, he the crawled over 300 yards to safety! Not carried and lowered down as in the film. BECAUSE the producers felt would be too much for viewers to actually believe!!! We are not talking crawling on flat football lawn 300 yards. Bomb craters, battle metal everywhere, bodies, and who knows what kind of debris...... Beyond an amazing story about a man who was above and beyond. Surrounded by USA marines, and army soldiers, who they themselves heroes. As every medal winning hero seems to say: The True Hero we buried..... I salute our WWII vets, all vets.... Liked the movie. history.title: Anastasia
history.review_title: Exciting animated musical that stands the test of time
history.text: Pros: A great Disney-like animated musical. If you didn’t know better you would think they created it. Fantastically fleshed-out story, with a street-wise and beautiful heroine, cocky yet loveable love interest, fantastic bad guy, and amazing side characters. The musical numbers are catchy and performed brilliantly by professional singers whose voices match our leads. Our side characters actually do their own singing. The animation is way better looking than the artwork for the DVD cover, which is horrendous by the way. The voice acting is stellar! It’s a film geared toward the entire family, but will most likely appeal to girls (young and old). Its one of those films you can watch over and over again. It is featured both in widescreen or Pan-scan setting. You must watch it in widescreen. The animation is so brilliantly drawn in exquisite details from that era. Cons: Wished it was longer, it was sooo good.

history.title: Strange Magic
history.review_title: A gem of a movie I never heard of until recently
history.text: This movie was based upon a story written by George Lucas and created by Lucasfilm. I absolutely loved it. I got to say I never understood the incredible amounts of vitriol against Lucas and his movies, when he the man who truly changed fantasy/sci-go Cinema features forever with Star Wars A New Hope (having wrote and produced it) along with developing one of the worlds best creative effects company ever. It’s sad that so many people find it acceptable to be mean and petty for anything and everything. And with the internet when a few people attack on a personal level the mob forms and makes it so much worse. And that’s exactly what seemed to happen to Lucas. It’s okay to express what you do or do not like in a movie )or other things) as long as it is done in a respectful way, but unfortunately that is not how society chooses to act these days. With that said, i will end my preach here, and discuss the movie. Pros: 1). A Very entertaining, enjoyable, rockin’ animation that takes place in a fantasy world full of fairy’s and dark creatures. This is a humorous romance that is wrapped up in a beautifully crafted story with moral lessons to be learned. 2). This is a true musical. 95% songs. 5% speaking. Hence, the story is told through the songs - popular songs from the last few decades, some reworded a bit to fit the story. I would think that people who enjoy live musical theatre will enjoy this. Or, if you like Grease, a psychedelic version, you might like this. 3). Made for young and older audiences. 4). CGI and the color palette is amazing. The design of creatures was top notch. 5). The music was catchy and fun. The musical cd will be put on my Christmas list. 6). The voice actors all have incredibly good singing voices that really showcased their abilities as well as conveyed what their character was feeling in the moment. 6). Contains extras on the making of. Very cool stuff. Cons: 1). Only offered in DVD. It would be neat to see how even more stunning it would be in that format. 2). This movie would be incredible if it were converted to 3D.

history.title: Public Enemies
history.text: I was very upset that this movie was rated R. I really think that it sunk the film. There was a total of three swear words (if that), the violence was almost cartoonish (Dick Tracy with Warren Beatty was much more violent)and there was certainly no sexual content. But the hand held camera action was kind of unusual even though I know that Michael Mann was going for a natural look and I think they achieved that. Being the huge Johnny Depp fan that I am, it made me sick that while the filming of this movie was going on 11 miles down the road from where I live, I couldn't go meet him but I think he made an awesome Dillinger. He was definitely much more interesting than the real guy. The real Dillinger looked like a scum-bag. Depp gave him some class. I didn't really believe the character of his girlfriend though. The way he treated her, she had no reason to fall for the guy or put her life on the line the way they did. Even their one love scene was so lame, it was difficult to believe in their romance. The character of Billie had was about as charming and believable as a rock-nuthin! Christian Bale, on the other hand, as Melvin Purvis, scared the daylights out of me. He was determined to get Dillinger and I'm sure that is what drove him to madness, Purvis I mean. I also did not like the the beginning of the movie, where he shot down Pretty Boy Floyd like he was a deer. Not cool. All in all, I was O.K. with the film but I'm not so sure that I want to own it. If I want to look at Depp I can always watch one of the three Pirates movies that I own, or Benny and Joon (young Depp) or Sleepy Hollow (again much scarier than this film). I just wish this film had been a little bit better and maybe Oscar worthy. Now, I don't think so. Too bad.

history.title: The Imaginarium of Doctor Parnassus [Blu-ray]
history.text: I tried to watch this film, I really did. If for no other reason but to see Heath Ledger's last performance. Well, what a waste of time and effort. What a mess of confusion, violence, and depressing images. I couldn't figure out what was going on, no matter where I picked up the film, at different scenes when it was of cable. It just never went anywhere, unless you count all of over the place, going somewhere. It was really a waste of time, also for the great actor Christopher Plummer. I can't figure out why any of the fine actors in this film signed on-especially the ones who filled in for Ledger after his death. And why three of them? To make the storyline, whatever it was, seem more confusing, weird, creepy and depressing? Well, mission accomplished then. If there are people out there, who justify this film with the prhase, 'this is my kind of weird', then that is what they are signing on for by watching this film. Some kind of weird-the worst kind!

history.title: Nuns on the Run
history.review_title: Will watch it over and over..........
history.text: This movie never loses it's timeless comedy style. Robbie Coltrane and Eric Idle will always be two of my favorites just because of this movie. It's just so silly, yet the serious side of what they are involved in, is hardly skipped over. After one of their 'partners in crime', a poor hapless little fellow named Norm, is eliminated by their horrible mob-boss, Casey, basically to teach Charlie (Coltrane) and Brian (Idle) a very hard lesson, the two very unhappy criminals set out to 'go straight'! Obviously, after that, hilarity ensues! After they end up in the convent, dressed as nuns, (which wouldn't fool anyone, I'm sure), Brian yells at Charlie-'You call this, going straight?' Anyway, great film, lots of fun and the good guys come out OK in the end. The quality of the film is top-notch, brand new, as promised and I was very happy to finally have a perfect copy of this awesome film. Thank you for very good service and a perfect product. I am 100% satisfied.

history.title: Feasting on Asphalt - The Complete Second Season: The River Run
history.text: This series is the perfect confluence of Alton Brown's engaging foodie personality, motorcycling, and the open road. It's a smooth continuation of Season 1 and that's a good thing. history.title: Gulliver's Travels (Widescreen Special Edition)
history.review_title: Frame Content Deleted to Make an Artificial "Widescreen" Version
history.text: I should have read the reviews before I purchased this "Widescreen Special Edition". I incorrectly assumed that the movie was originally filmed in genuine widescreen and that the version I happened to see on TV years ago was cropped down to full screen 4:3. I thought I'd get the genuine widescreen version by purchasing this disk. In actuality, the movie was originally filmed in full screen 4:3 and to make this "Special Widescreen Edition", the remastering company cropped out--deleted--a portion of the frame to give the appearance of widescreen. Even this new "widescreen" version isn't a genuine widescreen but rather an odd letterboxed frame. On modern TVs, it'll likely project on the screen surrounded by black bars on all 4 sides rather than using up the available screen real estate (perhaps an aspect ratio flag isn't set properly on the DVD?). On my LG TV, I had to use the TV's "zoom" function to fill up the available screen area with the image. The actual frame size, once I took out the letterboxing, is 720x388 or 16:10...a weird aspect ratio somewhere between 4:3 full screen and modern 16:9 HDTV widescreen. In the attached frame captures, the picture on the left shows the original 4:3 frame content. The frame on the right shows the new "widescreen" frame content. You can see that a significant portion of the bottom of the frame is cropped out. In my opinion, rather than enhancing the film, removing frame content actually detracts from the film...literally. I recommend purchasing the original 4:3 version.

There was enough gore and violence to make this an R-rated movie. Special effects were really good. The PG-13 rating was handily secured by the anachronistic and completely useless F-bomb about three-quarters of the way through the movie. history.title: X-Files: The Complete Season 1 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Now Available in Widescreen. Amazing Quality Increase
history.text: Purchasing The X-Files on blu-ray is a no brainer. The quality increase is amazing and further lends to the motion picture feel of this weekly drama. Pros: - Amazing quality increase and much less judder over the DVD version. I'd estimate the increased resolution is 90% of that observed in modern 1080p video. That's pretty amazing considering it was shot 20 years ago. Additionally, the increased bitrate really smooths out motion and reduces motion blur. - Early seasons are now available in anamorphic widescreen. It's a genuine widescreen as well since the original was shot in widescreen and cropped down to full screen. What a difference over the old full screen version. Cons: - The blu-ray menus aren't as user friendly as I'd prefer. The two main menu colors--black and dark gray--make it difficult to determine what menu option is selected. MediaInfo reports the following video and audio specs. Average episode size: 10-12 GB Average overall bitrate: 34 Mbps Video: 1920x1080 progressive scan, 24 fps, 16x9 aspect ratio Best audio: DTS MA/Core, 5.1 channel surround, 48.0 KHz Watching the The X-Files on blu-ray is a completely new viewing experience for this series.

history.title: X-Files: The Complete Season 8 [Blu-ray]
history.text: This review is specifically about the "Black Crush" encoding problem in X Files Season 8 early production batches, and excellent Fox Customer care. It explains how early productions batches of Season 8 have an encoding problem that results in very dark "black crush" portions of the video. It offers comparison screen captures and a way to contact Fox Customer Care for replacement. I received replacement disks free of charge (including shipping both ways) in about 10 days and the new disks do not have the encoding problem. Kudos to Fox Customer Care for quick service. The disks are presented in the same amazing increased resolution and bitrate of previous seasons.

history.title: My Big Fat Greek Wedding 2 [DVD]
history.review_title: Not As Good As The First One. Odd Dialog Pace.
history.text: The movie had some funny parts, but I don't think it was on par with the original. - Plenty of jokes and funny parts. The writers tried to hearken back to key lines from the first movie (like "Why you want to leave me?") but some of the lines are delivered in an odd, unfunny manner. - Pretty much all the same cast. That was a nice carryover that welded the two movies together. - In a serious moment, one of the brothers--Angelo--comes out as homosexual. His family embraces his gay lover and welcomes him into the family. It was weirdly out of place and seemed to be a scene shoe-horned in to support the homosexual acceptance movement. - Dialog delivery timing was just...off...in many places. The pace of the dialog was just a bit weird which left the movie feeling choppy, and the choppiness interfered with the effectiveness of the movie's humor/jokes. - As in the first movie, this movie adheres to the "smart wife, stupid husband" storyline between Gus and Maria. - Part 2 is pretty much a smooth continuation of the first movie. The theme is largely the same, so the viewer isn't forced to adapt to a new world. That's a good thing. It's worth watching once, I suppose, but I don't think it has the attractiveness to garner repeat viewings like the first movie has.

history.title: Alone
history.review_title: A Couple Dozen F-Bombs Per Episode
history.text: I didn't like this season as much as previous seasons. It doesn't cover as much ground as previous seasons so it feels rushed and incomplete. There are no doctor visits (for regular on-camera health checkups) in this season, which added a lot of depth because we were able to see the medical side of survival. Also, participants don't develop their camps or survival methods as well as previous participants and the editing focuses more on the fighting and drama between participants rather than on development of survival techniques. Some of the participants have some pretty serious potty mouths with upwards of a couple dozen F-bombs per episode--"f***ing", "motherf***ing", "f*** me", "f***"...pretty much any way they can invent to use it. That gets old after awhile.

All reality TV shows suffer from a little bit of fake scripting. This one seems to have a little bit more than most. It's entertaining, but take the drama with a grain of salt. Pros: - Great scenery. - Likable characters who display a wide range of interests and skills. - There's a good variety of activities--hunting, fishing, repairing equipment, building, personal issues. - Gives some reasonable idea of what subsistence living is like in an isolated Alaskan town. Cons: - Nonstop, bleeped out profanity. - Fake sound effects. - Lots of high tempo drama music. - Some believability or credibility problems. For example, when Charlie complains about an intruder setting a trap right next to his line, the intruder's trap appears to have a lot of old wire wrapped around the trap and the bait, and the set pole end is cut but appears to be well weathered...conditions not likely on a "new" set. A lot of injected drama like "I'll fight to the death for my trapline." Really? You're going to commit murder for a trapline? In another incident, Courtney supposedly blows an ATV tire (complete with fake sound effects) 20 miles from home and says she would normally walk home but for her daughter. They supposedly spend the night in a little pine bough shelter, in the middle of winter, with a foot of snow on the ground. Twenty miles at approximately 2.5 miles per hour (the average pace of a healthy adult) over flat ground translates to 8 hours of walking. Seems questionable they would put themselves in such a dangerous situation without proper survival gear or tire repair kit. Plus, Courtney's husband conveniently shows up the next morning just as they decide to start walking the 20 miles home. What husband would just wait around the house while his wife and daughter were out in the middle of winter overnight in a known location?? It's just not believable. - The amount of pain inflicted on trapped animals should be unacceptable in this day and age, but all characters justify the pain as "a way of life" and "we respect the animal". None of them would consider purposely inflicting 12 to 24 hours of pain and suffering--and often freezing to death while hanging from a leg--on other animals like caribou or moose but don't think twice about doing it to trapped wolves, foxes, wolverines, martin, etc. Do a Google image search for "leg trap" if someone tries to claim it's "painless" or "comfortable." - The new couple, Chris and Jessi, are terrible actors. They don't behave or respond naturally in front of the camera, which is a telltale sign of scripted drama. In one incident, their sled dog races off and dumps a log out of the sled (on camera) she was pulling. Chris and Jessi go looking for her while lamenting how she'll die in the snow if they don't find her. Then they find the sled with the dog harness attached, upright, with a log in it. Manufactured fakery. - This season really plays up "the road" and "the intruders from the road". Despite the fact that the characters are all doing their resource gathering on public land--land that all U.S. citizens pay for and have a legal right to access--they feel entitled to it and they feel entitled to keep other U.S. citizens off of that public land. They even imply a willingness to use violence to protect "their" land. I get it. They've had near monopolistic use of public land and now they're upset that others are accessing it, too. That's understandable, but the implication that it's *their* land and that they'll use violence to protect it is immoral. It's entertaining, but I think the scripted drama is a little too much. When I watch it, I just keep in mind that it's "reality TV" and not a documentary.
