history.title: Chick Corea: Now He Sings, Now He Sobs [DVD]
history.text: Every now and then I wind up with a performance video like this where the director thinks he's clever with camera angles and editing and the results are completely distracting and truly annoying. Now, the music on this disc is great, just like you'd expect it to be with three virtuosi like this. The set list is mostly standards, only one tune from the original "Sings/Sobs" album so it's not as adventurous but it's all tastefully done and well played. But I wish I could just pop this in to the CD player to get the audio because the camera work is so gimmicky and useless. Unless, of course, you think that extremely tight close-ups of Miroslav's right hand and the back of Roy's head are helpful. I got the feeling that the director was inspired by Sergio Leone because of all the tight close-ups of the musicians' faces. And the hand-held camera guy standing behind Roy appears to have had a few too many at the bar before the set started because he zooms in and out and wobbles significantly. Oh, I guess that's "artistic". So is all the jumpy editing--no shot lasts more than 5 seconds. You can have a variety of camera angles without getting so gimmicky about it, you can back off enough so the musicians playing actually look like musicians playing instead of a lot of anonymous hands and feet flailing around. I base that on the dozens of other "in concert" videos I have where the director saw his/her job as communicating the experience of the concert rather than using the concert as raw material for a lot of self-indulgent second-rate cinematography.

history.title: Ulysses' Gaze [DVD]
history.review_title: It has its pleasures but ultimately...
history.text: I thoroughly enjoyed the cinematography and the director's pace, using long shots--many of which required some intricate choreography on the part of the cast. But I can't say I have the slightest idea what the film's about. Harvey Keitel doesn't really have dialogue, he has stylized recitations which make him appear to be mostly a mouthpiece for the director: almost like a single-actor chorus. He encounters women who instantly fall in love with him, but they're all played by the same actress so she's serving as some kind of archetype, I guess. I never figured out why the three reels of undeveloped film were significant enough to risk a journey into a war zone, or how they were to be interpreted in the context of war in general. I thought that at the end, when Keitel delivers a soliloquy, things might get tied together, but it left me more perplexed than before. Maybe I'll give the film another try at a later date, but I think I'll try a different Angelopouos film first.

history.title: Davis, Miles - Round About Midnight
history.review_title: Messy product that might have some value for diehard fans only
history.text: This disc is amateurishly presented and sloppily packaged (i.e. bootleg). It looks like it might have been taken from some Italian TV show; it's in black and white, though the picture quality isn't bad. There's a title block in the upper right-hand corner of the screen that remains through the entire disc that says "Miles Davis", just in case you forget for a moment who you're watching, I guess. There's no song selection menu and no chapter divisions, so you just have to play it straight through and fast forward it if there's a particular part you want to see. The song listing on the cover has no relation to what's on the disc and it has nothing to do with the album Round About Midnight. The song listing is: 1. Honky Tonk 2. What I Say 3. Sanctuary 4. It's About That Time 5. Funky Tonk 6. One Phone Call 7. Human Nature 8. Someting on Your Mind 9. Time After Time NONE of these songs are on the disc, except for Sanctuary. The disc is actually footage of the "Lost Quintet", i.e. Miles, Chick Corea, Wayne Shorter, Dave Holland, Jack DeJohnette, circa 1969. That is the only reason I'm not sending this disc back for a refund: I'm keen on getting any video of that group and the sound and cinematography on this disc aren't bad. But the idiotic editing is: the disc starts with what was probably the group's last song of the set (because it ends with "The Theme"), there's a fade-out, it resumes with another song, then another fade-out, then the group plays, as the last song on the disc, the song which would have been the opening song of the show (Directions). It's clear that the entire performance isn't captured here. There are some good shots of the interaction between the players and the director did a good job on setting up the camera angles. But it's a mess of a disc and you'd have to be obsessed with the Lost Quintet (as I am) to enjoy it. For anyone else, it will be a big disappointment.

history.title: Miles Ahead
history.review_title: Miles makes a wrong turn and somehow ends up in an action movie
history.text: Cheadle deserves praise for his attention to detail in portraying Miles--the vocal inflections, the facial expressions, even the fact that his fingering on the trumpet tracks the music. And there are a lot of small details that he gets right as well, including the fact that a lot of Miles' dialogue in the film consists of actual quotes. But then you have the action movie/buddy movie/blaxploitation part of the film that looks like a concession to the Hollywood money men. The sleazy promoter character who steals the tape was laughably cliche, the chase scenes and the final recovery of the tape were utterly standard and predictable and I found myself getting pretty bored about midway through the film. I have no problem with Cheadle not attempting a rigidly historical portrayal of Miles along the lines of "Ray" or "Get On Up". I've seen his approach described as "impressionistic". That's fine, I'm not a purist who's going to pick at the film's every little departure from "fact", but I don't spend money on action buddy films, either. It's a shame that Cheadle spent so much time and effort studying Miles only to weirdly use his life as a take-off point for an empty genre like this.

history.title: New Orleans Drumming (DVD)
history.review_title: The Heart of New Orleans Drumming
history.text: I bought this set back in the '90s on VHS tapes. I re-watched them recently because there appears to be a lot of interest in New Orleans drumming, including street beats. That means there are a lot of people giving instruction (like on YouTube) on New Orleans street beats, a lot of it inaccurate. This set will give you the real deal--a lot of history and tradition--and it will show how the New Orleans parade rhythms were adapted into other settings (like Ahmad Jamal, Dr. John, the Meters, even Patti LaBelle). All of the drummers here talk about (and demonstrate) specific examples, but also show what is the general the New Orleans "feel"; this can go a long way toward allowing you to adapt this feel into your own playing and not just limit it to a bit of Mardi Gras genre color. The drummers here all explain themselves very well and give good examples of what they're talking about. This set's been out for a while but it still holds up. It looks like Alfred Publishing has discontinued it but there are still copies floating around in VHS format or DVD on other web sites (like Musician's Friend). Highly recommended.

history.title: Knight of Cups [Blu-ray]
history.text: I've watched Tree of LIfe and To the Wonder as well as Knight of Cups. I found Tree of LIfe to be a great film but Knight of Cups less so. It's in the same style as Tree of LIfe but it seemed repetitive--here's yet another scene of the protagonist wandering through life with that lost look on his face, here's yet another scene of him romping on the beach with his latest girlfriend, etc. The voiceovers in Tree of Life were spare and, while a bit oblique, seemed like appropriate poetic commentaries on the characters' experience; here, the voiceovers are wordier, carrying too much of the narrative, even to the point of sometimes functioning as dialogue. And they're delivered in that solemn half-whisper that Malick seems to require, which here often seems a bit overdramatic for the content of the words. This film is more verbal than Tree of LIfe, which means it's a bit easier (not easy) to "get" the film's themes than it is with Tree of Life, but the visual and cinematic aspects of the film feel less remarkable (though they are nevertheless quite fine). Sometimes the whole thing starts to feel ponderous, which is something I haven't experienced in a Malick film before. I could watch Tree of Life any number of times to peel away its layers of meaning, but I don't think I could return to Knight of Cups. It's a decent Malick film, which means it's better than 90% of what's out there, but not up to his other films.

history.title: Don't Come Knocking
history.text: I loved "Wings of Desire" and "The American Friend", and after watching "Paris, Texas" I got interested in Wenders' take on the American West. I checked out his book of photography of the West and read his comments about the West in films. But this film has none of the meditative quality of other Wenders films and his take on the West is jam-packed with cliches. It might be that Wenders is playing with the cliches, a comment on old Hollywood Westerns, or maybe the cliches came from Shepard, but I find that kind of hip "meta" stuff to be pretty tiresome. The cinematography felt pretty jumpy, with lots of cut shots and reaction shots, none of the long, extended shots that I enjoy so much in Wenders' other films. There are some shots of landscapes and buildings that are very fine but Wenders doesn't linger on them like he has in previous films. The acting is uninspiring except for maybe one scene with Lange and Shepard. The music soundtrack is way too busy, it seems to be there all the time, getting in the way of the film just like the music in the bar gets in the way of the dialogue between Shepard and Lange. The ending was pretty insipid, not quite "they all lived happily ever after" but close. Not at all what I expected from a Wenders film.

history.title: Classic Musicals - 50 Movie Pack: Royal Wedding - Second Chorus - Stage Door Canteen - Breakfast in Hollywood - Hi-De-Ho + 45 more!
history.review_title: Good for Jazz/Swing, Other Bits of Interest, Can't Go Wrong for the Price
history.text: I bought this for 9 bucks last year and it's definitely worth it for that price. I'm not particularly interested in musicals but I do like old jazz/swing, and there are plenty of films here featuring such greats as Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Nat King Cole, the Dorsey brothers, Louis Jordan, Cab Calloway, Lena Horne, the Andrews Sisters, Artie Shaw, Lionel Hampton, and Sara Vaughn. The video quality on some of them is mediocre at best but it's a chance to see footage that doesn't get a lot of play otherwise. On the musicals side, there are a couple of Fred Astaire films and one with Judy Garland and Frank Sinatra. Admittedly there are some real dog movies in here, like "The Great Gabbo", "Sing, Cowboy, Sing", and "Minstrel Man", but some of them are so goofy and of their era that they're kind of entertaining. There are two to three movies crammed onto each side of each disc so don't expect convenient labelling, but there is an accompanying booklet that gives a decent amount of info on each of the films.

history.title: Whiplash [Blu-ray]
history.text: If you think it's realistic for a guy, just broadsided in a nasty car wreck, to pull his battered and bleeding self out of the mangled wreckage, stagger off to his gig and show his dedication by getting on stage to play with the band, then you'll find the rest of this movie plausibe. But it's full of caricatures, not characters, it's melodramatic, and underneath the melodrama there's a cliched success story with an ending that's telegraphed from the opening minutes of the film. For the most part the guy acting the part of the drummer isn't doing the actual drumming, which is fine--he's an actor not a musician and it's possible to do quick cut shots of him "playing" while the soundtrack has someone else doing the actual playing. (They could have at least mention the actual drummer in the credits, at least I didn't see any credit given.) In the scenes where the actor's actually playing--when he's supposedly practicing uptempo stuff--he's actually just banging around at random. I took this to mean that director doesn't acknowledge any difference between skilled musicianship and random noise, at least when it comes to drums. The "play till your hands bleed" stuff is just silly, and if the guy, out of frustration, tried to punch a hole through a real snare drum head, he'd probably break his hand before he'd have any success. But these are, I guess, the kind of minor details that might be labelled "jazz purism". So ignore the fact the movie's about jazz; this melodrama's still flawed in more fundamental ways.

history.title: The Trial
history.text: The visuals in this film are fantastic--the extravagant sets, the lighting, the camera angles--and make the film worth watching. Welles does a good job of creating a claustrophobic atmosphere as the film progresses. The acting--well, Anthony Perkins has some good moments and some other moments in which he seems kind of wooden, Welles isn't particularly into his part but he's always interesting to watch, Romy Schneider and Jeanne Moreau do the best they can with what are fairly strange roles, and Akim Tamiroff reprises his quivering (and somewhat annoying) character from "Five Graves to Cairo". The one thing that really bothered me about the film was Welles' habit of post-production dubbing in of the dialogue. He did that on a number of other films, rather than record the dialogue on the set. Maybe it was because of budget. But it gives everything a hokey feel when the ambience (or lack of it) of actors' voices doesn't match the setting they're in. It's not as bad as many dubbed foreign films but it's noticeable and annoying nonetheless. I wonder if some of the weaker moments of Perkins' dialogue didn't come from bad dubbing. And, though not having read the book, I doubt that Kafka ended his story the way Welles ends this film. Anyway, it's a visual masterpiece. I'll watch it again, maybe with the sound turned off.

history.title: The Revenant
history.review_title: Like taking a time machine to the 1820's American wilderness!
history.text: This film transports you to the 1820's American wilderness where the mountain men carved out a living trapping for furs. This movie has captured that time and place like no other I've ever seen including the 70's classic "Jeremiah Johnson". You feel the fear as the arrows from Indians pierce men's heads and bodies and a bear attack leaves Hugh Glass for dead. Blizzards, avalanches, and storms are common place, and men have little time for anything but survival in this cold, brutal hell they have found themselves. The beauty of the untouched wilderness is breathtaking to behold and this film captures it like no other. The language is rough as are the men here but so is the life they are experiencing. Eating raw, and often rotten meat was commonplace for these men back then. It was just a game to stay alive...

history.title: An American Werewolf in London [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A Classic Film for Everyone, Not Just Horror Fans...
history.text: A film that never gets old is one that people want to see again and again. In spite of the fact that this odd little film from the early 80's was not taken seriously at first, it is now obvious that it will live on in film history as one of those rare projects where everything came together just right to evolve into a film that not only appeals to horror fans, but just about anyone-young or old. The story is tragic, but funny at the same time. It seems to remind us that life is short and unpredictable and that monsters can overcome us without warning anytime. David Naughton, who was known only for his Dr. Pepper commercials was perfectly cast as a young man who was loved by many, but turned into a bloodthirsty monster by the full moon. One feels sorry for him as he has no control over his curse, just like real life -we all deal with pain and death sooner or later regardless of our position in this life.

I really liked this movie for a number of reasons. First, the father and son interaction reminded me of my close relationship with my own father. We spent a lot of time together and often worked side by side. Emjay Anthony, who plays the son is an incredible actor in that he was on camera for long periods of time and had some complicated fast paced scenes. Second, it was as if Jon Favreau told his actor buddies that he was writing, staring in and directing a movie and they all asked to be in it. Actors who usually are stars and carry movies seemed happy to take bit parts and not overact. Scarlett Johansson kept her attractiveness under wraps. Sofía Vergara as hard as it is to believe gave an understated performance. Still latin. Still hot, but more mother and supportive cheerleader than an object of men's desire. John Leguizamo was the friend everyone wishes they had. Funny at times, reflective at others but always on your side. Finally there is the food, music and scenes from Miami, New Orleans and Austin. Also thought that social media was used as a vehicle to convey a message and not, as it often has become, a story-line crutch. However, with that all said, if strong language, especially when spoken by a preteen bothers you, be aware that this movie has its moments. The young man is often treated like an adult so the language is not out of character for the roles. But, it still might be a bit strong for some people's liking.

For these kind of revenge films to work you have to hate the bad guys and care about the good guys. The Hunter's Prayer tries to mix it up a bit with a bad guy (assassin, junkie) who is trying to be a good guy. The other good person, a young woman is cute but not all that loveable. The real bad guy is bad enough, he feeds a no-one-will-miss-villager to his specially trained to kill dog, but we don't get to know him well enough to really hate him or his henchwoman and henchman who looks too much like our maybe not such a bad guy assassin. In the shadows, it often is difficult to tell them apart. The reason I did not give one star has nothing to do with the story or acting but special effects. Without giving too much away, there is one scene where a bad guy gets run over by a car (in reverse) that comes out of nowhere. You are going to want to watch this scene over and over again and in slow motion if you can. Oh, and there is a chase scene where the chased car strikes another car in just the right place to spin it around to hit the chaser vehicle. Pretty clever. I like a good revenge movie. Bad guys getting their due and good guys coming out on top. I like the predictability. Here, the sappy ending is too little and far too late. You feel like you got to the bottom the Cracker Jacks and instead of a surprise you found a coupon for a free prune juice.

Other than number of viewers, there are two strong indicators whether a show is successful. Are those viewers anxious to see what is next and do they talk about the show with others? Designated Survivor has two actors who starred in their own shows and is smart enough to give them about equal screen time doing what they do best. Then you have a strong supporting cast who get enough screen time that we have gotten to know them. It also is good to see a chief executive portrayed as other than a self-important arrogant jerk. Sincerely hope that Designated Survivor becomes one of the most successful series ever. Maybe then the content providers will take note that this is the quality of programming that viewers want and will pay to watch.

This review is about the Salvation TV series and not about how Amazon did not initially make all episodes available for free. Santiago Cabrera, as the billionaire, Darius, is incredible. His looks, his movements, the delivery of his lines are flawless. He is believable in the role. And, there lies the problem. All the other actors don't even come close. Jennifer Finnigan, was barely tolerable in Tyrant but is downright annoying here. Ian Anthony Dale is not as macho or attractive as he thinks he is. Again, annoying. Tess, the omnipotent virtual assistant, probably gives the second best performance. Erica Luttrell who plays the president's advisor is not listed in the main cast but should be. Beautiful, bright, sexy and devious. She hits the mark with all of them. The storyline is a simple one -- asteroid is on its way to destroy earth and must be stopped. How that should be accomplished and by whom is a source of friction between the various factions. Without a scorecard it is hard to tell the good guys from the bad guys at any given moment, especially because it seems the good guys may have been bad guys in the past. The visual effects and cinematography are fine. Get rid of a few annoying actors and this show could be watchable instead of cringe worthy.

history.review_title: An absolutely wonderful and entertaining production
history.text: Jenna Coleman, who plays Victoria, starts out as an exceptionally cute young girl and blossoms into an exceptionally beautiful young woman. Her interactions with and affection for her older advisor Lord Melbourne, Rufus Sewell, feel incredibly real and genuine. Acting at its best. The costumes, sets and cinematography are exquisite. The supporting cast also is outstanding in bringing even the most insignificant character to life. Overall, just an absolutely wonderful and entertaining production.

history.review_title: Too Much Like that Annoying Dr. Phil
history.text: Dr. Phil's overblown ego strikes again. The first season was only watchable because of the actors and newness. The second season has Bull turning into that megalomaniac Dr. Phil who thinks the world revolves around him and hangs on his every world. I am going to miss Chunk.

Don't make my mistake. I remember when this first was available on Prime. I watched the trailer and maybe part of one episode and proclaimed this a Porky's remake and didn't watch beyond that point. Started watching again the other day with the same opinion but once I got past the first few episodes my opinion started to change and I really enjoyed the rest of the series. After the first couple episodes the gratuitous nudity is gone and so is most of the foul language. In its place are deep friendships, loyalty, empathy and compassion even when romantic relationships end. In that sense, it brought back fond memories of my youth. And, that seems to be what Red Oaks is all about. Each episode is only about 25 minutes, so take a couple of hours and give it a chance. Although there are main characters, one thing I really liked was how the supporting cast were all given their fair share of screen time and all pulled their weight. Ennis Esmer as Nash, the club tennis pro, was hilarious. Characters who were meant to be annoying were appropriately so.

history.review_title: Not the Best, Nor the Worst
history.text: If you are someone who enjoyed Strike Back, you will like this show. It is not as tight as The Unit, but it is definitely watchable. My hope is that enough people will tune it so the series has the opportunity to get better. Mike Vogel, who plays the lead, has improved since his Bates Motel and Under the Dome days. For those complaining about the politically correctness, all I can say is get out a little more. In the first few episodes, the woman who is the sniper also went into a beauty salon and a woman's only bath house. She also was shown to have a crush on her leader. They are not just depicting her as a woman with a gun. As for Anne Heche as the Deputy Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency, what about her job would require it to be done by a man? Sofia Pernas and Tate Ellington portray analysts who work for the Deputy Director and support field operations. Two fine actors who, again, it would be nice to see have a series last long enough for them to show what they can do.

Modern Family was a great show when it first started. Now, it is barely watchable. The actors seem tired and bored. The writers are struggling and the kids have grown up not so cute. Time for some of the actors to move on.

history.title: Bridget Jones - The Edge of Reason (Widescreen Edition)
history.review_title: Loved the first one...hated this one!
history.text: Loved the first film and have watched it more than 100 times over the years. This 'sequel' was horrible. The acting was forced, Renee Zellweger looked odd. In the original film she was chubby, in this one the weight gain looks unnatural and again, she looks odd. The story line was downright silly, and not funny. Very disappointed-

history.title: PROCOL HARUM:LIVE PROCOL HARUM:LIVE
history.text: A must for any fan, and not just die-hard fans. Over two hours of live music filmed during their Denmark Concert in 2001. I could listen to 'A Whiter Shade of Pale' all day long!

history.title: The Elia Kazan Collection
history.review_title: Nice Thoughtout Set - But Every DVD Damaged
history.text: I paid $50 for this set and received it this weekend. I opened it immediately and looked carefully at each DVD. What is going on??? Each and every DVD is scratched. Some more than others, but still scratched. I didn't expect to have them in this condition with a brand new set! I will attempt to view each movie to see if they all play - if not the set goes back. Very disappointed as this could have been a really great classic set, but the damage to the discs take away from the entire set.

history.title: Danielle Steel's: Crossings ( TV Mini-Series)
history.text: I have waited years for this to come out on DVD! I have all the other Danielle Steel TV movies/miniseries and this was the only one not released here in the United States until now.(it was available in the U.K. for a long time) It was even better than I remember. The storyline is set at the beginning of WWII and includes many historical events and figures. The entire cast is wonderful, headed by Cheryl Ladd and Lee Horsley. Christopher Plummer and Jane Seymour only add to this lavish miniseries. There is romance, intrigue,and suspense. The picture quality is great, no complaints here, but don't expect HD remastering. With almost 5 hours of viewing, you really get your money's worth! This is a must for anyone who loves Danielle Steel, or if you are a fan of the great TV miniseries that were once a mainstay from the 70s - 90s. Enjoy this fabulous miniseries once again, or maybe for the first time, you won't be sorry.

history.title: A Charlie Brown Valentine
history.review_title: Charlie and the Gang Bring Back Memories!
history.text: Charlie Brown and the gang celebrate Valentine's Day in their own unique way...need I say more!!!!! The 'Peanuts' gang have a universal appeal, and never seem to go out of style. I still laugh when I watch now, as I did as a child. Just love watching with the kids!

history.title: Agatha Christie's Murder on the Orient Express [DVD]
history.text: What a bore! Nothing compared to the 1974 film which also had an all-star cast. This adaptation is set in the present day and looses something of the effect that the book had. While the original film uses a storyline that has hints of 'the Lindburgh' kidnapping, this one falls flat. It took a lot of energy just to sit through it (I was hoping it would get better....) I would not recommend this to Agatha Christie fans.

history.title: Jackie (BD+DVD+DHD) [Blu-ray]
history.text: What a bore! Natalie Portman's impersonation of Jackie Kennedy was awful, and her voice drove me to distraction. Everytime she attempted to talk like Jackie, I felt like fingernails on a blackboard! I tried three times to get through this film and couldn't, it was just terrible. I am still trying to figure out why Natalie Portman was nominated for a Best Actress Oscar for this film, but then again she got the Oscar for 'Black Swan' another horrible film. Save your time and don't bother with this one.

history.title: The Jane Austen Book Club
history.text: I was pleasantly surprised by this movie. I took the DVD out from the library and after one viewing, I immediately ordered my own copy from Amazon. The story of these people, all brought together by the forming of a book club that only reads the works of Jane Austen is so charming, funny and even heartbreaking. I love this movie! I have watched it several times and enjoy it just as much each time. Great cast! Take a chance, you might just love it too!

history.title: Strange Relations
history.text: I came upon this movie on one of the cable channels years ago, and since then I think I have seen it at least 100 times. A sweet and charming story of an adopted man, who due to medical need must locate his birth mother. To his surprise his 'mother' lives in England, so off he goes to find her. This is when the fun begins! Julie Walters is perfection as the now grown woman who as an unwed teen gave up her baby for adoption. Paul Reiser was just a delight as the son, who is a 'fish out of water' with his new family. I don't want to give away too much of the story, but what I will say is the rest of the cast is just fabulous, including Olympia Dukakis as his adoptive mother. Give it a try, you will be pleasantly surprised!

history.title: A Star For Christmas
history.review_title: Worst Christmas Themed Movie I Have Ever Watched!
history.text: This movie has the worst acting, most idiotic storyline, and just plain stupid dialogue! Can't believe I bought this DVD! What a waste of money as I will never watch it again!

targets.title: Signed, Sealed, Delivered: The Complete Series (Hallmark)

history.title: Torchwood - Miracle Day (Series 4) [DVD]
history.review_title: TORCHWOOD in American hands is hideous.
history.text: The final Russell T. Davies story from TORCHWOOD should not have been made. It's terrible from begining to end. It is an awful story which was dragged on for ten days. It could have been told in one or two. Boring American characters dominate the ten days of this story while TORCHWOOD, or what's left of it, takes a poor back seat. Most of the music, if you can call it that, is annoying. The ethos of TORCHWOOD was utterly destroyed by R.T. Davies in Children of Earth in which he destroyed what remained of TORCHWOOD following the second series in which he senselessly killed off two popular characters. Removing TORCHWOOD from Cardiff ruined the show for me. But, I wanted to see what happened so I purchased the DVD set. I wish I had not spent the money. My comments do not reflect the respect I have for the dealer who sold the set to me.

history.title: In The Year 2889: Classic Science Fiction Horror
history.review_title: Please, do NOT BUY THIS MOVIE!
history.text: Please, do not waste your money on this awful film! The package is "nice", almost no information on the back though. The film itself is trash. Very, very old, poor condition, horrible acting, no plot, color fades in and out, lots of scratches and dust spots. Worst purchase I've made on Amazon.

history.title: Torchwood: Children of Earth (DVD)
history.text: Russell T. Davies seems determined to kill off his TORCHWOOD creation. This mini series is good but the story ends badly.

history.title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
history.review_title: Excellent addition to Star Wars universe.
history.text: Great new installment in the Star Wars universe. A bit confusing because so much is new and unexplained. Well worth the price.

history.title: Boston Legal Season 1-5 Complete Collection
history.review_title: I loved the series when it was broadcast and I'm enjoying ...
history.text: I loved the series when it was broadcast and I'm enjoying it all over again now with these nicely priced DVD's.

history.title: Legend - The Complete Series
history.review_title: FINALLY available on DVD! Great fun!
history.text: I loved this quirky show during its brief run on the short lived "UPN" network. Great work by John DeLancie and Richard Dean Anderson. For years I looked for this on DVD and now it's here! If you are a fan of either actor or if you simply want great entertainment, purchase this set.

history.title: Farscape The Peacekeeper Wars [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Great final chapter to a much loved TV series.
history.text: I have been a fan of Farscape for many years. I purchased this blu-ray version of Peacekeeper Wars after I lost my original DVD version.

history.title: The Last Ship: The Complete Second Season [Blu-ray + Digital HD]
history.review_title: Great value for an exciting show.
history.text: I only recently discovered this series. The Blu-Ray edition is great.

history.title: The Last Ship: Season 1 (Blu-ray+ UltraViolet)
history.text: I only recently discovered this series. Glad I bought the Blu-Ray edition. Great value.

history.title: The Untouchables/The Complete Collection//includes all 42 episodes [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Finally, a show I love is available on DVD or Blu-ray.
history.text: I've waited for YEARS for this great show to finally be released on DVD (or Blu-ray). I have only watched a little so far but I'm delighted with what I have. I could probably get all technical and find something to complain about as others have but I'd rather simply give thanks for a project long overdue on my DVD shelves. The cast was perfect and the music is incredible. It has one of the best musical intros I've seen on television.

targets.title: The Man Who Would Be King
Marco Polo (473 Minutes. 3-DVD Box & Ken Marshall, Denholm Elliott, Anne Bancroft, Burt Lancaster) (1982)

history.title: Time Machine, The (BD) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Dated as the special effects may be, I truly love almost everything about this classic sci-fi gem. None before or since Rod Taylor could surpass him as the awestruck and noble hearted time traveler. George Pal's distinctive artistry depicting the scenes of the future ages on earth as they wiz past Taylor's machine and the barren yet beautiful open landscapes of where he finally arrives really draws you into everything. Yes, the whole Morlok "bad guys vs. good guy" thing was clunky and wasted alot of time; but that's Hollywood. And I must say that it was actually Russell Garcia's score that truly made the entire movie so captivating and unforgettable. Finally, thanks to Warners for their superb Blu-Ray version-and for the many great vintage titles they've been steadily releasing at Warner Archives.

history.title: Peter Gunn: The Complete Series
history.text: This is what you need to get-to date, at least-if you want the complete series. Timeless Media assured me that these DVDs were made from the best film or digital transfer they could get. Picture quality is >90% three stars or better. Unfortunately, sound quality varies quite a bit, on average three stars, sometimes worse. Still, the audio is just good enough to appreciate most of the really superb jazz cues and entire live (?) performances. Craig Stevens was Peter Gunn alright, but take away that music and its just another private eye TV show. One other thing, besides the so-so audio quality, what's sadly missing are the VERY cool animated intermission cues. Lucky me, I've got them in my A & E DVD set released circa 2003.

history.title: Vertigo [Blu-ray]
history.text: Another superb Warners BD transfer! Picture AND Bernard Hermann's score (!!) are stunning.

history.title: The Flight of the Phoenix
history.text: Some of the direction and/or acting were a bit overbearing, but still one of the best "survival" flicks ever. Sadly, as others have noted, the let down here was that the sound quality should have been a lot better. Whether it be on location or on a sound stage, 35, if not, 16mm Westrex mag film recorders were the norm among major film studios like Fox throughout the 50s and into the 70s. And the mags were most likely stored as properly as were the photo negatives. This unhappy DVD release-which took years to finally happen-reminds me of another Fox DVD screw up, "Goodbye Charlie". Here a pan & scan was used rather than the original 2.35:1 theatre release.

history.title: AGENCY with Robert Mitchum, Valerie Perrine, Lee Majors
history.text: Good story. Though produced on a low budget for limited distribution and with actors approaching the end of their careers, credit is due them and the story writers for handling what even today is controversial subject matter. That elections are won and products and ideas accepted via powerfully seductive and subliminal media technology is not something you're lucky to see portrayed on TV, except perhaps when all good politicians and corporate execs are asleep and dreaming. If you like "Agency", check out John Carpenter's "They Live". And don't forget: " "OBEY", "CONFORM", "MARRY AND REPRODUCE", "CONSUME", "WATCH TELEVISION" and "SLEEP".

history.title: A New Leaf
history.text: "Gracious.... Heavens", if only I could solve my problems as Henry Graham solved his, though (happily) not quite as he had planned. I loved the deadpan Matthau in nearly everything he did. The supporting cast here, perhaps chosen by director May, are all fine, with several standouts, including the late George Rose. BIG thumbs up to Olive Films for restoring key parts of the original music that Paramount swapped out with some kind of junk for the VHS release (e.g. When it dawns on Henry that he's practically penniless), as per my timely pleas for them to do so. Still, I was hoping that for the BD version director May's alternate version would have been included, which ran an additional 78 minutes-with subplots and an ending quite unlike that which producers Evans and Koch forced May to go with. So we'll probably never get to see what May really had in mind and why, even if Matthau himself was happy with the issued release.

history.title: Spirits Of The Dead 1968
history.text: I have Arrow Film's superb BD version, but I also wanted a DVD copy. Sadly, unlike the BD version, this DVD has no English dubbed soundtrack. Sent it back.

history.title: Perry Mason: Season 3, Vol. 2
history.text: “Crying Cherubs” was good. That tough and sexy Liza kind of stole the show, though it’s always a pleasure listening to Abraham Sofaer. “Irate Inventor” was my favorite from that season. Anything to do with technology, including stolen, in this case, often makes for a very interesting story. Speaking of which, I was sorry to learn of the passing of “Big Dave” Brockman. I never had the pleasure of meeting Dave, but he was clearly a brilliant electrical engineer, computer scientist, animal rescuer, nature photographer, Perry Mason fan and more. His site helped me connect with my favorite episodes. Truly, a fine man.

history.title: Perry Mason: Season 5, Vol. 2
history.text: My two favorites from this season: “Mystified Miner” and “Angry Astronaut”. Both typified the early 60s, when the American economy and the industrial and tech sectors in their prime and there were unmistakably WAY LESS PEOPLE. Indeed, much that was in view was just cleaner, quieter, less costly, more plentiful and unspoiled-and way less “improved”. Where did we go wrong?

history.title: Alfred Hitchcock Presents - Season Seven (5 disc box set) [DVD]
history.text: It's been over 3 years since Season 6 and still no Season 7 DVD set released from Universal. Pressed DVDs still offer better longevity, but isn't it time that Amazon step's up and issues Season 7 and the rest of the series on DVD-R? And it's not like there's no demand for it-the numerous customer reviews of DVD sets for Seasons 1 thru 6 prove that.

targets.title: I Married a Monster From Outer Space
Law & Order Criminal Intent - The Third Year
Tony Hillerman DVD Collection (Skinwalkers, Coyote Waits, A Thief of Time)
The Addams Family - The Complete Series

history.review_title: An 8 minute short that's perfect for your digital stocking!
history.text: The tale of Rudolph is well known by everyone, but this particular cartoon seems a bit obscure. I've certainly never seen it before today. The animation is okay, but the audio is quite terrible. It sounds like the voice actors were delivering their lines inside a cramped and tiny closet. Beware: One glance at Rudolph's mom might convert you to furry fandom!

This is a VERY low budget film. It's practically a "home movie." There's not too much violence and just a tiny bit of nudity. This could play on the Lifetime network (IF they were airing 5 dollar bargain bin flicks). Joe Estevez is sometimes really fun to watch in corny B-movies, but unfortunately he isn't given much to do here. Fans of his who are looking for another Werewolf (1995) or Soultaker (1990) should look elsewhere. The crazy mother character is legit bonkers from the get-go. There's zero subtlety in her behavior. That can be mildly amusing at times, but not quite enough to call this a "so bad it's good" type of outing.

history.title: Trailer Trauma 3: 80s Horror-Thon [Blu-ray]
history.text: This is a great collection of trailers, from well-known classics to completely obscure oddities. Definitely fun to watch and an awesome resource of information. 5 stars.

history.title: Crystal Lake Memories: Complete History of Friday the 13th [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Buy, Buy, Buy, Now, Now, Now
history.text: This is a fantastic documentary. Even casual fans of the Friday films will probably enjoy this presentation. It's fast paced, but thorough. Hell, at one point they even highlight the Friday the 13th TV series (which had nothing to do with Jason or Camp Crystal Lake). Almost everyone from the films participates, and Corey Feldman narrates the entire feature. Very informative and fun, definitely made by people who deeply love the franchise. 5 stars!

history.review_title: Splatter University... somehow less exciting than ACTUAL school
history.text: This is an incredibly rotten film. If you're looking for the typical staples of a slasher flick (nudity and gore) you'd better search elsewhere. Majority of the time this movie focuses on a cast of truly unlikable characters. It's like watching an unfunny high-school comedy, or a lame teenage soap opera. When the killer does make his (brief) appearances, he barely delivers any screen presence, and his kills are extremely bland. I can't think of a single redeeming thing to say about Splatter University. Avoid!

history.review_title: Big Like Me comes up short
history.text: I watched this whole documentary, so I can't say I wasn't entertained on some level. However, I didn't really like it. The main star (Greg Bergman) has extremely low self esteem due to his "insufficient" penis size. He pursues multiple avenues to try and rectify the issue, and as one might expect, most options are a complete waste of time and money. Throughout the film we're subjected to Greg's stand-up comedy act, and unfortunately I didn't find any of it to be funny. It's more angry rantings than jokes. I won't spoil the ending, but I didn't like the overall message of the documentary. It was also painful to sit through the Online dating portions of the film (where Greg's sole source of conversations with women consist entirely about penis size... obviously not good first date subject matter, unless you're TRYING to look like a creep). This doc may appeal to some, but it was a complete miss for me.

history.review_title: Firehead... an inaccurate title for a horrible film
history.text: If you like really bland and forgettable action flicks, then this is the movie for you! Firehead is the story of a man who can shoot blue laser beams out of his eyes. He can also create a personal deflector shield of some sort with his mind... but these super powers are rarely ever used (for budgetary reasons I assume). Most of the time the action is limited to boring gunfights. Christopher Plummer makes a sad appearance in this rubbish, along with Martin Landau. Both actors are far too good for this movie. Chris Lemmon (Jack Lemmon's son) is right were he belongs however, in all his cheesy b-movie glory. He'd go on to co-star in Thunder in Paradise a few years later (playing second banana to Hulk Hogan). The Rifftrax crew makes this trash fun to watch, just be ready to crank down the volume when the LOUDEST, most obnoxious child actor hits the screen. Her piercing shrieks might blow apart your speakers! Thankfully she's only on screen for short periods of time.

history.review_title: Not enough focus on Lenny Bruce
history.text: This is an interesting documentary, but it feels like a very brief introduction to Lenny Bruce himself. Majority of the time is focused on the evolution of show business AFTER Lenny's untimely death. I wanted to see more on Lenny's life, and hear about his various legal battles in greater detail. Instead disgraced entertainers like Michael Richards and Don Imus stole a lot of the spotlight. I didn't feel like I wasted my time watching this documentary... but now I'm in the mood to watch a substantial doc on Lenny's history. Unfortunately, I'm not sure if one of those exists at the moment.

history.review_title: Susan. Susan. Susan! SUSAN!!! Susan! Susan??? Susan! ...Susan? SUSAN!!!
history.text: A young girl who's totally obsessed with spiders grows up to become a crazy social outcast. Big surprise! Around her late teens or early twenties she starts using spiders like deadly weapons, sending them out to attack anyone she deems an "enemy." It's not long before her law enforcement uncle uncovers this madness... and promises to keep it a secret, IF she'll become his lover! It's a deadly web of spiders and incest, accompanied by a killer Rifftrax commentary. What more could you possibly need?

This movie has one incredibly misleading title. There's no actual "puppet people" and they never mount an "attack" of any kind. Still, it's quite entertaining in its own special way. A mad scientist /slash/ doll maker shrinks real-life people into personal doll-sized minions. The minions are forced to sing and dance at the scientist's request... or face punishment! The minions attempt to escape multiple times, and strangely there's no real resolution. The movie closes with a weird open-ending, as if the filmmakers simply ran out of time (or money) to finish the story. The special effects are great (in a super cheesy way)... NOTHING is set to scale. Also, there are plotholes a'plenty! For example, the minions are too small to be heard by anyone... yet they regularly converse with the full-sized mad scientist without any difficulty whatsoever. It's a mess of a movie, but fun to watch, and the Rifftrax commentary makes it twice as entertaining.

targets.title: Caligula 2: The Untold Story – Digitally Remastered

history.title: Gran Torino
history.text: I thoroughly enjoyed this movie. Eastwood starts out as an old crusty bigoted, anti-Asian person. But he gradually becomes transformed by his Asian neighbors' kind, affectionate treatment into an understanding, appreciative, caring member of their family. A fascinating relationship develops between him and the neighbor teenagers--a young man and a young woman. Of all the roles I've seen Eastwood in, this by far is the best--his facial expressions say more than any words he says. His directing is simple, impactive, and straightforward--no hi-tech frills and stunts--and it serves the story quite well. The script also works well, and the ending offers a heartrending surprise, definitely against the grain for Eastwood, but thoroughly believable and exemplary. It exalts rather than degrades him, and enables him to obtain the justice required without sacrificing moral principles. Highly reccomended!!!

history.title: The Young Stranger [VHS]
history.text: This is a nice family drama that explores a son's conflicted relationship with his father. It shows the sad consequences that result when father's spend much time trying to become rich and famous and calously neglect to care for and love their sons.

history.title: Padre Pio Miracle Man
history.review_title: Greatest Spiritual Bio Movie Ever Made!
history.text: This is one of the greatest religious films about a saint that I've ever seen. The acting, directing, writing, settings, cinematography and music are all perfect, and the story is told in a most believable, inspiring and moving way. It also conforms closely to the saint's biography. Worth seeing many, many times. Truly inspiring to one religiously dedicated. Deeply heart-wrenching, faith-building, and conscience raising. Amazing!

history.title: Apostle Peter and the Last Supper (DVD)
history.text: I did not find this movie either exciting, moving, or compelling. This was chiefly because the actor playing the part of Peter emoted his memories of Jesus in an almost monotonic tone throughout. Since the subject itself was so awesome and electrifying, I expected Peter to show a more feelingful or emotional level of recollection of his Master than the ho-hum manner in which he spoke his lines. I was not convinced of the conversion that occurs near the end--it happens so abruptly and quickly that I couldn't help feeling that it was forced to give the story a positive ending, without providing a gradual build-up to the point of conversion that would make it inescapably logical. I felt that the actor who played the part of Jesus did not have the spiritual understanding needed to make me believe that he truly believed in what he was saying. To me he sounded like a very worldly person trying to act very spiritual. In other words, his performance was unconvincing to me. For example,I think the actor in the TV miniseries JESUS OF NAZARRETH did a far superior job and did convince me.

history.title: St. Peter
history.text: With the exception of Omar Sharif, I found the acting bad, the dubbing-sync terrible, the story not credible, and thus I turned off the movie after thirty minutes. I can't help but agree with most of the points of the other negative reviews. I was not religiously inspired in the least by this film as I have been by other Biblical presentations such as Jesus of Nazareth, Joseph, Abraham, Moses, etc.

history.title: The Passion of Bernadette

history.title: Star Wars-Clone Wars: Season 1-5
history.text: Let me start off with the most important part: IT DOES NOT WORK. I have region-free UK releases of Game of Thrones and Battlestar Galactica that work perfectly on every blu-ray reading device I own including an Xbox One and PS4. THIS ONE DOES NOT WORK. Now, for the exponentially less important things. As most will know, this is not the complete series. It doesn't include the theatrical film, nor Season 6 ("The Lost Missions") or the 2003-2005 Cartoon Network miniseries (which canonically meshes with this series and introduces two critical characters not introduced in this 2008 series). At roughly 40% of the price of buying each season separately or the US Blu-Ray collection, you'll get the cheapest blu-ray cases that, with two or three discs each, take up as much space as some 6-disc cases I have, and does not include the mini art books and inserts that came with the initial releases of seasons 1 and 2, but that may still be worth it to you if your player can read Region B discs. Episode guides are on the flip side of the cover insert, but at least Season 2 has episodes listed on two separate discs while omitting others. In short, unreliable, which is bothersome considering how messed up the chronology of the first three seasons was (In usual Star Wars fashion). However, the series is entertaining for kids and adults and the dark themes of Revenge of the Sith begin to show themselves halfway through the series, with several multi-episode arcs that are like watching an entire Star Wars movie. This is the easiest and by far cheapest way to get the "whole" series (To date, no set contains the movie and season 6 and they must be purchased separately) and is worth it if you're willing to deal with numerous superficial inconveniences and if your set happens to work in the US. Pick up the movie, Season 6, and the original 2003 series (in two volumes) and find an episode guide to get the correct order of episodes. Force knows you'll need it.

history.title: Logan
history.review_title: While a fully canon entry in the X-men series, ...
history.text: While a fully canon entry in the X-men series, I'm hesitant to call Logan a Superhero film. It tosses out all cliches and doesn't lean on past movies to tell a story that is, at its core, about family. Equal parts Superhero, western, and road trip movie, the film brings back Hugh Jackman and Sir Patrick Stewart for their final outings as Wolverine and Professor X, though as indicated by the title, these aliases rarely come into play in the deeply human narrative. They're joined by Dafne Keen as Laura, or X-23, a mysterious 11-year-old with a connection to Logan that both try to deny. Keen's performance is stunning. Not just as a first-time child actor, her talent blows other industry veterans out of the water. in the 90-minute documentary (broken into digestible featurettes) on the making of the film, it's noted that Keen understood her character so well, she was improvising with Jackman DURING HER AUDITION, and holds her ground throughout the film, never overshadowed even by a Knighted actor. The only negative thing about the film is that, while it concludes the Wolverine trilogy and even the majority of X-men films to date, it's come out before the series is completely finished, with the preboot saga and several subseries continuing. That being said, it does NOT depend on the other films to be a compelling story of what is essentially a family. With plenty of action and a bit of gore.

history.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past (The Rogue Cut)
history.review_title: Rogue Cut: Best of the prequels
history.text: As a relatively new fan of the X-men series, I've been a bit bored with the prequel series. However, Days of Future Past is a pivotal film in the series and brings things back to form, with the return of Director Brian Singer. After The Last Stand and Origins: Wolverine's questionable quality and First Class and The Wolverine's changes of form, it was nice to see the series return to its roots as well as prep itself for more films to come and in a way erase the unanimously worst two films of the series. That being said, as long as you've seen the first two films, you will know what's going on, though seeing all of them (In release order is best) certainly helps. Now, The Rogue Cut obviously brings the titular character back, and offers more of a sequel to the first three films, including a redemption arc for Magneto in its additional 15+ minutes. That being said, it doesn't drag on like some Extended Editions do. This is the definitive version of the film, and even if you own the original cut, I'd say it's worth throwing out in favor of this cut. If you end up hating the added scenes, the original version is included as well, on the same disc in the blu-ray version.

history.title: 4 Kid Favorites Cartoon Network Hall of Fame Number 2 (DVD)
history.review_title: Need an episode list? Here you go.
history.text: If for some reason you've never seen these shows, here's a quick rundown. These are all from the first seasons of classic shows from the late '90s/early 2000s but they're suitable for kids of all ages, though Courage can get very eerie. The basic premise is evident in their titles, but here's a quick rundown anyway: SAMURAI JACK: A samurai is flung into the distant future by a shapeshifting wizard who rules the world. Jack has to return to his own time and stop the wizard from ever taking over. Light action sequences. COURAGE THE COWARDLY DOG: Courage lives with an old couple in the middle of Nowhere, where eerie visitors come to visit, with sinister plans for the couple. It's up to Courage to save them. Very eerie. Definitely not for kids under 8 years old. CODENAME: KIDS NEXT DOOR: A group of kids part of a global network of secret operatives save their neighborhood from rival factions with childish goals (Stealing candy, spreading lice). Suitable for all ages. (Obnoxious to me as an adult) FOSTER'S HOME FOR IMAGINARY FRIENDS: 8-year-old Mac has outgrown his imaginary friend, Bloo, and brings him to live at the titular organization. Mac must visit Bloo every day or he will get adopted out. They're joined in their hijinks by Madame Foster, her imaginary friend Mr. Harriman, her granddaughter Frankie, the lanky and friendly Wilt, the cuddly Eduardo, and bird-like Coco. (I disliked this show as a kid but love it as an adult. It teaches valuable life lessons and stuff) EPISODES: Samurai Jack: -The Premiere Movie (3 episodes) -Jack, the Woolies, and the Chritchellites -Jack in Space -Jack and the Warrior Woman -Jack and the Three Blind Archers Courage: -Queen of The Black Puddle -Everyone Wants to Direct -The Snowman Cometh -The Previous, wonderful, adorable, Lovable Duckling -Heads of Beef -Klub Katz -The Revenge of the Chicken from Outer Space -Journey to the Center of Nowhere -Little Muriel -The Great Fusilli Codename: -I.S.C.R.E.A.M. -P.I.R.A.T.E -L.I.C.E. -L.I.Z.Z.I.E. -T.H.E.-F.L.Y -C.A.T.S. -S.P.A.N.K. -S.U.P.P.O.R.T. -G.R.O.W.-U.P." Foster's: -The Trouble with Scribbles -Seeing Red -Phone Home -World Wide Wabbit -Berry Scary -Who Let the Dogs In? Actual review: I wanted something Halloween-themed for my classmates to watch in the background in animation class, but wasn't ready to commit to a full season of "Courage." Having watched Foster's as a kid and meaning to watch Samurai Jack for years, this seemed like a great opportunity. The good: -First 7 episodes of Samurai Jack, arguably CN's most serialized show ever -Buy the first two volumes of this collection and you get the complete first season of Courage -Foster's turned out not to be nearly as trashy as I thought it was as a kid. It was very enjoyable. The cons (Very small nitpicks) -Disc 2 of Foster's. You'll have to pay another $12 for the whole first season to get the other disc. -Disc 2 of Courage. Not a problem if you intend to buy Volume 1 of this collection. -Samurai Jack froze during episode 3 on my computer, despite being spotless. Played fine on my PS4 -DVD case just stacks all discs on top of each other like an early-2000s multi-CD PC game (Luckily I have some 4-disc cases laying around) -Honestly... Kids Next Door wasn't great. While it was a great hit of nostalgia, it just left me wanting to spend money on more Courage and Foster's (And I already planned to buy the Samurai Jack blu-ray collection). Not necessarily a bad thing. And a warning: DO NOT BUY VOLUME 3 OF THIS COLLECTION (Dexter's Lab/Kids Next Door)

history.title: Manor House
history.text: Were it not for Lady Anna, Sir John, the cook and Edgar the Butler, this series may have flopped. Each of those four characters, though hated for it, adhered to Edwardian rules of the era. They demanded the same from all house staff, much to the staff's displeasure. What I found most interesting was the joy and laughter the overworked and penniless house staff attained during their hardship. The rich master and lady rarely smiled as they fulfilled their stuffy roles as a filthy rich Edwardian couple. All-consumed with putting forth the proper image to friends and associates, the parents had no time for Guy, their youngest son. Guy found love, happiness and comradeship in the basement with the "lowly" house staff who, no matter how burdened they were with work, always had time for the boy. We enjoyed this series very much. It's a DVD we'll watch over and over.

The actors do little more than sit or stand in one place and deliver their lines. The movie actually put me to sleep a couple of times. It's an OK film, but I'll never watch this DVD again.

history.title: Children Of Men
history.text: If there is a redeeming quality to this depressing mess, I missed it. I keep wondering why anyone in his right mind would write this, produce it or act in it. It's mankind's futuristic plunge into barbarism, violence, filth, misery, despair... and the only glimmer of hope for humanity is a newborn baby who won't stop its agonizing crying once it's born. The sudden cessation of war when soldiers stopped killing everybody long enough to bow down and permit the newborn miracle baby to safely pass was laughable at best. After wallowing through almost two hours of blood and guts, shattering gunfire, screams, blood gushing out of heads and chests, grimaces and a non-stop wailing newborn that I wanted to strangle into silence, the movie suddenly ends. It's one of the most depressing movies I've ever seen, and it had absolutely no point.

Since when is the life of our president, or anyone else for that matter, worth more than America itself? If the terrorists kill our president, we'll all boo-hoo the moment, then we'd go elect another. Big deal. In Olympus Has Fallen, Asian terrorists were unknowingly invited to the White House. When the attack began outside on the lawn, the American president and his secret service, against protocol, brought his guests into the president's underground safety bunker. That's exactly where the Asian terrorists wanted to be. Oh, brother! Our government, national security and military looked like a bunch of clueless buffoons who were outmaneuvered, outgunned and outwitted at every turn. The standing president (Freeman) is faced with obeying terrorist demands which will save the president's life, but sign America's death warrant. Pah-leeze! This movie rates a zero on the believable scale. I give it two-stars for the acting. If you love violence and high-tech weapons that rip people apart and splatter blood and gore all over the place, this movie is for you. It's all action, brutality and tension. Unfortunately the plot is as old as dust... so if you enjoy a plausible story line, as I do, avoid this movie. I give it two stars because of the decent acting.

history.title: The Homesman
history.text: This film is mostly a slow mover with too many rape/sex scenes. One-scene in particular is very disturbing due to the manner in which a newborn baby was murdered. You'll know the scene when you see it. You'll never forget it. Meryl Streep didn't appear until that tail end of this movie about three insane women being transported across the plains by "desperate-for-a-husband" Hillary Swank and grisly, loner Tommy Lee Jones. The duo encountered several obstacles along the way, but the encounters were boring and nothing we haven't seen. Towards the end something shocking happened that I hadn't expected or anticipated it. Suddenly Jones was thrust into the lead roll, and for me, the movie soared after that. I'm not sure why. Maybe it's because Swank was as dull as the desperate and plain Cuddy character she played. Maybe it's because Swank's character held Jones back. This certainly isn't a great flick, but it's worth a watch. I doubt I'll ever watch this again.

history.text: According to writer and producer David O. Russell, Three Kings is a true story. That seems far-fetched, but who am I to say it isn't. I enjoyed it whether it's fiction or fact. Three Kings is the perfect blend of drama, action and comedy. Clooney, Wahlberg and Ice Cube are in top form as gold hunters turned humanitarians.

history.title: Star Trek: The Original Series - The Complete Series
history.review_title: Impressive, but there's No English Subtitles for the Hearing Impaired.
history.text: This is the first time I’ve noticed the brilliance of colors on the control panels and walls of the Star Trek set. The picture is vivid, sharp and clear. Even when I increase the picture to “widescreen”, very little clarity is lost. It’s amazing what they've done to this old TV series. The audio is perfect. The discs are all silver and plain, but I’m sure that’s what helped keep the costs down. Each episode runs approximately 50 minutes, the standard time for an hour-long program in the 60s. Younger viewers will notice footage that’s never been shown in the television repeats today. Any Star Trek TV fan would be honored to own this set. So far I’ve only watched the first two episodes, but I’m thrilled beyond measure with this purchase. I bought my boxed set at Walmart. It's unfortunate that the producers chose to ignore America's hearing-impaired population. The subtitles are only in Spanish and French.

history.title: Stanley Kubrick: A Life in Pictures
history.review_title: A Must See Documentary of the 20th Century's Greatest Film Maker
history.text: This is a brilliant documentary of the greatest film director of the 20th Century. It is especially fresh, as it was made and released May 2nd, 2001; only 2 years after his death on March 7th, 1999. He had/has no equal. He never made a film of the same genre; please note "Paths of Glory" (1957) and "Full Metal Jacket" (1978) are both about war; the former is an anti-war film and the latter a truly brilliant war film. An IQ said to be well over 200, he took risks no one else would take and virtually all of his films from "Lolita" (1961) on were surrounded by controversy. Narrated by Tom Cruise, this takes you from his childhood throughout his life until his death in 1999. It has clips from every film he made, and interviews with actors from each film (whenever possible, as a couple have no living actors). The very revealing interviews are a who's who of directors, actors, cinematographers, writers, producers, etc., plus his family and childhood friends. To name a few, directors like Martin Scorsese, Sydney Pollack, Steven Spielberg, Woody Allen, actors like Nicholson, Malcolm McDowell (he had the role of a lifetime as the star of "A Clockwork Orange" (1971) numerous writers, cinematographers, and all the key people who worked for him on films. I believe the greatest of all ironies regarding The Academy Awards is the fact that Stanley Kubrick NEVER won an award for Best Director; whilst so many people who worked and acted in his films did win in their respective fields won Academy Awards. The only "Oscar" Kubrick ever won was for Best Visual Effects for "2001" (1968). However, he did win the highly coveted DGA Award (Director's Guild of America). He was not able to be present to receive the award, but sent a taped acceptance speech which was gracious and is also very "Kubrickian" (not an original term, but appropriate). I have seen it, but I forget where. I am sure it is on one of the Bluray copies of Kubrick's films. Another thing I like is delivered by Jack Nicholson, when asked about Kubrick. Nicholson replied (please excuse my paraphrasing) "Everyone acknowledges he (Kubrick) is the man, and that is really an understatement". It is chock full not only of scenes from all the films he made, but also includes scenes and information about films he didn't make. He always wanted to make a film about Napoleon. He had made extraordinary preparations for the film (for example, he had 10,000 uniforms made; half were made of paper for the troops very far away), but shelved it. The one film I truly wish he has made was to be called "The Aryan Papers" about a Jewish family hiding from the Nazis in WWII. As with Napoleon, he had gone to extreme lengths of preparation; however, once he heard Spielberg had begun shooting "Schindler's List", he shelved it as well. He knew both stories could not be told simultaneously. I even had a short-lived resentment against Spielberg. Take nothing away from "Schindler" and Spielberg, as it is a terrific film; probably the one he is most proud of. I truly believe Kubrick's film would have been better, but we will never know. Spielberg loved Kubrick and who knows (?), he may have had his own thoughts about this. I like what director and sometime actor Sydney Pollack mentions, the term "perfectionist is used often about some directors; it usually means someone is a pain in the ass". He does go on to say "Stanley (Kubrick) is the only true 1000% perfectionist". Whether you are a casual fan of Kubrick's films or an ultimate, almost obsessed fan (like me; I own all 13 feature length films he made, plus a couple of shorts), this is an absolute must see documentary. I will stop here, as I could go on indefinitely about my favorite director.
