history.review_title: Good Show, But Amazon Streaming Sucks.
history.text: I'm quickly finding that this show is quite interesting. However, due to Amazon's sub-standard streaming, I doubt I'll continue it -- at least for now. There's nothing more annoying than trying to watch a great show, which happens to pause and stutter every few minutes/seconds. This review may be helpful for those who are interested in doing what I did. It's for those who have heard great things about this show, and have decided to check it out with a free month of Amazon Prime. If this is you, then I want to manage your expectations. The show is great, and I'm very interested. I'm about half way through the fifth episode, and I'd love to watch more. But the fact that it's a good story, which demands your attention, makes it even more painful to watch with Amazon Prime's free-month of defective streaming. Amazon's streaming is nothing like that of Netflix. With Netflix, you can watch shows and movies without the problem of freezes and pauses. The picture quality may get worse, or better, but you can always continue watching without any loss of continuity. As long as you have stable internet access, you can watch a show. The same can't be said when streaming with Amazon -- at least not with the free trial. If you try watching an episode on Amazon, you may be able to get through short spurts of good streaming. But you can be sure that it's just a matter of time before it starts pausing and freezing when you're just starting to get into the story. If you truly want to watch this show, the way it's meant to be seen, then I suggest finding another way to watch it. From what I can tell, it'll be worth the wait. The story is decent, and the writing is solid. But if you're like me, and you want to be able to watch a good show with no distractions, then you should probably find a better way than a free month of Amazon Prime's streaming service. I'm sorry to make this review primarily based on Amazon's streaming. But I hope it'll help someone who's thinking of doing what I did. I don't recommend signing up for Amazon Prime in order to watch shows. If the show's good, you're likely to be frustrated and gain nothing but a ruined experience.

history.title: Passengers
history.review_title: Highly Enjoyable, If You Don't Know the Premise
history.text: I watched this movie in the theater, and was fairly impressed. Then again, I didn't watch any trailers and avoided knowing anything about it before watching it. That always helps a movie because, at the very least, you can be surprised concerning what you may see. This movie is easily one of those movies. The premise of the movie is thought-provoking. I won't spoil anything because, as I've stated, not knowing beforehand is what made me really enjoy this movie. Just know that if you like serious sci-fi, and you don't need an explosion every 5 minutes, then this may be something you'd like. "Ex Machina", "Cube", and "Sphere" are a few other movies that I can think of that are like this. After watching the movie, I decided to watch a few of the trailers. After doing so, I can see why some people may be disappointed if they watched the trailers before viewing the movie. This is primarily because the trailers steal the movie's intrigue. After watching them, there's not much more to anticipate when you watch the movie. Anyway, I did enjoy this movie. I'd recommend it to anyone who likes serious sci-fi, and doesn't need non-stop action, or continuous laughs, in order to appreciate a film.

I watched this movie because I'm a fan of Aaron Paul, from "Breaking Bad", and Mary Elizabeth Winstead, from "10 Cloverfield Lane". When I saw that they had made a movie together, I was curious to see it. They're both great actors, and I wanted to see them work together. I can understand why some would say that they don't like this movie. It's not because it's a bad movie (It isn't a bad movie), it's because some people just don't like dramas. So they watch the movie, and aren't impressed because they don't like dramas. I get that. What I don't understand is how someone could say that this movie has terrible performances. One review stated that, and I simply can't understand it. This is because the performances are very real -- especially Mary Elizabeth Winstead's. No fake tears, just extremely authentic acting. She does such a great job that you almost feel as if she really has her character's struggles. So I'm thoroughly impressed with the performances. When someone states that the acting is bad, I can only conclude that they must be a troll. If these performances are bad, then what's good? How could these performances have been improved? As for the story; it's about what you may expect. It's a drama that tackles a very real subject. If you're into that sort of thing, then I don't see why you wouldn't like this movie. As for me, I was entertained enough just to see Aaron Paul and Mary Elizabeth Winstead work together. It's not a movie I would choose to own (I borrowed it from my local library, and I'm more into serious sci-fi), but it was certainly worth my time for the performances alone.

The concept of this show gives it the potential to be as great as "Dexter", maybe even greater. I love the idea of an exceptional computer hacker with severe psychological problems. This basic premise, alone, is enough to make me curious. It also doesn't bother me that the writers chose to mix in that "Fight Club" vibe. All of that could work very well, if the story was written in such a way that the audience could easily follow exactly what's going on. For me, that's clearly the biggest flaw with this show. It's not hard to loosely follow the details. But I have to agree with many of the bad reviews when they say that the story can be a bit difficult to follow, at times. This is mostly due to poor writing, in terms of how the story is told. The writers want you to hate a company, but they don't do a good job of giving you real reason to hate it. When they do try to explain it, it's done in a minimal, simplistic way. That's only one example of how the writers tend to spend too little time on aspects that should be key in explaining what drives the character's motivations throughout the show. One show that has exceptional writing, with a fairly mediocre concept, is "Breaking Bad". That show is my favorite, and is an example of what great writing can do. If this show had those writers, it could be epic. This is because those writers take the time to clearly develop character motivation, and you're never lost when it comes to following all of the moving parts of the show. That's only because the writers take the time to unfold the story at a proper pace, and explain everything adequately. I also agree with some of the other bad reviews in terms of sexual, vulgar content in this show. It's never necessary for any show, but is completely unnecessary for this one. It really serves no purpose other than cheap, negative shock value. Such scenes are a great way to ruin a good show. One bad review pointed out that the show is also a bit racist; at least with one scene in the second season. Once again, this is a big turn-off, and the statements, in the scene, were completely unnecessary. Despite all of these significant flaws, I still like the concept of the show. And although it's a bit hard to follow, at times, the concept is strong enough to keep me watching; at least up to this point. I enjoy the main character's struggle for sanity. I like how his psychological problems haunt him, and shape his world. This aspect reminds me of "Dexter", as I've mentioned before, and is interesting enough to keep me entertained. However, if the incoherent writing begins to dominate to the point of me not being able to follow the story at all, I may have to stop watching. All of this is disappointing, since this show could have been epic. If you like the aspects that I like and have mentioned, then you may want to give "Dexter" a try, if you haven't seen it. Although it too has some unnecessary sex stuff, the writing is more solid. "Breaking Bad" is even better than "Dexter". It also has some of the unnecessary sex stuff; although it has a lot less than the other two shows. As for "Mr. Robot", it's an okay show. But it suffers from many of the flaws which I, and other reviewers, have pointed out.

Before watching this movie, I mostly viewed Edward Snowden as a traitor. After all, he stole and leaked classified information. In doing so, he violated his obligation to government secrecy. He knew he was going to be working in the intelligence community, and that he was obligated not to tell of what he knew. So, in that sense, he betrayed his government, and is, therefore, a traitor. However, this film at least explains his motivation for doing what he did. For Snowden, if this film is accurate, the good news is that he got what he wanted. He wanted people to know that the U.S. government spies on its citizens and allies. After learning that the government does this, do I believe that anything should change? For me, the answer is "no". Let me explain why. If everyone is cheating in a race, are you obligated to cheat if it's important to win? Is it considered cheating if everyone else is doing it? This is what every nation faces when it comes to upholding their standing in the world. The fight for superiority is the reason there was a space race, and a nuclear arms race. No one wants to use nuclear weapons. But it's just as dangerous to be the country that doesn't have them, as long as everyone else does. If all nations are in a knowledge race, then I would rather my nation know more secrets than the others. I agree with what Corbin O'Brien said in this movie. He basically said that the use of modern technologies, by a country's citizens, comes at a price. I'm okay with the government viewing my E-mails and internet activity, or even tapping my phones. I don't even care that there are cameras everywhere, nowadays, in public places. I say, let them watch, read and listen, as long as they don't bug my home. I'm okay with understanding that conversations made via electronic communication, is monitored, and that you're being watched by cameras when you're in public. But I also agree with what Edward Snowden said on the FAQ section of the DVD bonus section of this movie. He spoke about the importance of privacy, and that privacy gives a person the right to be ourselves without others judging us. So as long as I can have privacy in my own home (aka don't bug my house), then I can always have the private space that I need. I don't think it's realistic to believe that the United States can keep up in the world, if other nations aren't willing to play by America's rules. The U.S. Constitution may prohibit the government from listening to all phone conversations and reading citizens' E-mails. But if other countries do it, (or are willing to do it) and we don't, then we could be at a severe disadvantage. I've always suspected that the government (or anyone else) could be listening in on my phone conversations, reading my E-mails, or watching me in public. So I treat such forms of communication as public. Bugs are where I draw the line. Privacy should always be available in a person's home. Don't bug my house or any place that is supposed to be private. Beyond that, I feel that the government should have the freedom to do what is needed in order to compete with the rest of the world. I'm not sure something can be called cheating if everyone's doing it (or would do it, if given the chance). If all other nations are able to gather more intelligence by monitoring its citizens and increasing their surveillance capability, then that just puts the U.S. at a disadvantage if our government won't. As for the movie, I feel it was good in the sense that it made its point. Some reviews said that the movie is boring. I wouldn't call it boring as long as you know that it's not an action movie. However, if you watch the movie in order to learn more about Snowden, and the privacy controversy, then this is a good movie to watch. I haven't watched any Snowden documentaries, or interviews (except what's on the DVD), so I have nothing to compare this movie with. But it does inform the viewer of the story and subject material. As far as "bias" is concerned, I think most people are smart enough to make up their own minds about how to view Snowden. This film isn't likely to change any of that, nor should it.

I can't recommend this show to anyone. First of all, I had to will myself to finish the first season. I was about to call it quits by the fifth episode, but comments were telling people to "hang in there, because it gets better". So I completed the first season, and it didn't really get much better. It provided a mild climax for the finale, but it wasn't much of a payoff. I really could have stopped watching. The show is basically a soap opera about a cult, and nearly every other scene is a sex/nude scene, or a scenario of one character sleeping with another. Before choosing to continue watching beyond the fifth episode, I wanted to know more about the show's creator, and see if there was some purpose behind the show. It was then that I was able to see the one redeeming quality of this show. That quality is that it purposely speaks about religion. As a Christian, this show was a challenge to watch. Not only because of my previous reasons, but because it attempts to view a cult lifestyle, as a normal lifestyle. It feels like an atheist's perspective of how they may view any family who chooses to follow a religion. It always bothers me when "religion" is viewed as a lumped concept -- as if all religions are basically the same. It's the idea that all religions have a holy book, a leader, followers, and that the followers pray and think about an afterlife. As a Christian, it's true that I base my life on a holy book, and that I have chosen to worship, and follow, a person who died a long time ago. It's also true that I understand that there's an afterlife, and that I pray to God. But it's a huge mistake to lump Christianity into a group of religions, as if it's just another religion. Let me explain why. Christianity is based on the reality that a man, who lived over 2000 years ago, did something that no other human being has ever done. He performed all kinds of supernatural miracles, including rising from death. It's a reality that is based on factual evidence, which makes it different from any of the other religions, which are all fake. This evidence is shown by the fact that all humans reference all of time to Jesus' birth. I could go on and on about how significant this is, but it does make all of the difference in the world. If Christ didn't perform all of those miracles, and rise from death, then all Christians are just as foolish as any of the characters in this television show. But Christians don't fall into this category because our belief is based on reality; a reality that is easily backed by evidence that we see today. It's not based on a fairy tale that someone simply made up. So, as a Christian, it's annoying to watch a show that seems to correlate faith in the afterlife, with cult lunacy. It's only lunacy when it's not based on fact, or truth. But if a belief is based on truth, then it makes all the difference in the world. It becomes no more strange than believing that atoms exist. Anyway, I applaud the show's intention to bring up the concept of religion as a talking point. A wise person thinks about death because no matter how long we live, we'll be dead much longer. So religion is always worth talking about, and I give the creator of this show, credit for focusing on that topic. For me that's its redeeming quality. That's why it gets two stars, instead of one.

history.title: We Need to Talk About Kevin
history.text: This movie is a moderately thought-provoking piece about the potential difficulties and ramifications of raising a troubled child. I didn't know anything about this movie before watching it, and didn't realize that it was based on a book until after viewing it. As some reviews have stated, the movie tends to jump back and forth in time throughout the movie. Although I prefer a linear story, this perspective isn't completely bad since it doesn't prevent the movie from making its point. After watching it for a few minutes, I began to wonder if it was going to be one of those abstract movies which serves no real purpose. This movie certainly isn't that. It has a purpose, and it explores a topic which most drama fans may find interesting. If you enjoy drama, and are a patient audience member, then you'll likely find value in this movie. If you don't like spoilers, then this is where you should stop reading this review since the rest of it will focus on my frustrations with watching this movie. I can't talk about these frustrations without mentioning key moments in the movie. My take, after watching this movie, is that these parents may be partially responsible for what took place at the end of the movie. What frustrated me most is the fact that Kevin was never disciplined. He would talk back to his parents, and they merely accepted it. He would disrespect them, and they accepted it. He would manipulate them, and they accepted it. The only time his mother ever did anything in retaliation to his unacceptable behavior, is when she threw him across the room after he willfully crapped his pants. She shouldn't have thrown him across the room, but she was right to react. However, even after doing so, she apologized to the child, as if she's the only one who did anything wrong. I can't help but wonder if the whole tragedy could have been avoided by use of adequate discipline and the right spanking at the right time. The goal of this movie isn't to shed light on the importance of proper parenting. Rather, it seems to focus on the notion that some people are born psychopaths. However, I could have been more challenged, as a viewer, if these parents had at least simply spanked this kid when he needed it. I do like the fact that Kevin used a bow, in order to kill his victims, rather than a gun. It allows this movie to focus more on the attacker, rather than the means of attack. I believe this is where the focus, of such a topic, should remain. Ironically, earlier in the movie, Kevin reveals that some of his motivation is to gain attention. So that, too, is thought-provoking -- To seek a solution may be to perpetuate the cause of the problem.

After watching the first 46 minutes of this movie, I finally decided to turn it off. I then chose to look at some of the reviews here on Amazon, and agree with most of the negative reviews. There was a time when I would have willed myself to finish a movie like this. However, experience has taught me that some movies simply aren't worth finishing. In the past, forcing myself to finish bad movies has left me wondering why I chose to continue to waste my time and attention. For me, there are a few big problems with this movie. I was surprised to find that it was made in 2010. It feels as if it was made in the 1970s. This is likely intentional since it takes place in 1983. Either way, it's hard for me to get into a movie which feels overwhelmingly fake. If it were only the technology, that would be one thing. However, the characters are equally fake. As some have pointed out, many of the characters don't behave like people. Lines are spoken slowly with over-the-top, fake tones. There's no way for me to buy that there is anything real about this movie. Therefore, I can't be drawn into it, or appreciate it. It just comes off as boring and pointless. I've watched movies, which are much older than this one, but are great movies. "Close Encounters of the Third Kind" and "Alien" are two great examples. The technology is dated for those movies because they're old movies. However, the writing and acting allow you to get drawn into the story. Characters act like actual people, which enables you to identify with them and suspend your disbelief. You're able to trick yourself into believing that these extraordinary events are actually taking place, and can therefore, be drawn into the story. That doesn't happen with this movie. It's all just too fake for me to appreciate anything about it. I agree with one reviewer who said that if you like movies like "THX 1138", then you may find some value in this movie. I couldn't finish that one either, but at least it had the benefit of being made in 1971. Therefore, I could forgive the limited technology. That movie also made a greater attempt to create characters who act like people. I couldn't appreciate that movie either, but I had more respect for it. If you like movies like that, then there's a chance you may enjoy this movie. I now have a greater appreciation for good writing in old movies. "Alien", released in 1979, continues to be my favorite movie. It's a reminder that just because a movie was made decades ago, and there were more limits to special-effects technology, it was still possible to make an excellent movie. "Beyond the Black Rainbow", falls short of this tremendously. Some people have said that they appreciate the atmosphere and music of this movie. I'm a great fan of good atmosphere, and I understand the tremendous effect that atmosphere can have on a story. However, I wasn't impressed in terms of this aspect either. If you're looking for a good movie with a similar isolated atmosphere, I would highly recommend "Ex Machina". I love that movie, and, in my view, it only has one flaw. It has a few nude scenes. But when it comes to good music, atmosphere, a thought-provoking concept, and a well-told story; that's your movie. I just wish they had done away with the nudity in that movie. It's never needed, and always hurts a movie.

I'm glad I didn't pay to see this movie. I borrowed it from my local library. Even then, it wasn't worth my time. I knew nothing about this movie prior to watching it. As I was watching, I suspected it must be based on a game, book, or some other previous work. After reading other reviews, I quickly learned that this is the case. I can see how this movie is based on a game. The premise is extremely weak and is too much in the fantasy realm for my taste. As a game, I understand why it may be successful. This is basically because games generally boil down to players being able to participate in fighting and such things. But as far as a story is concerned, I couldn't appreciate this movie at all. In my view, this movie aspires to be as great as "The Matrix". However, unlike "The Matrix", the story uses a technology which is pretty hokey. How is a guy supposed to fight while tethered to a machine which is attached to his waist? Furthermore, the incentive for a story wreaks heavily of a complete fairytale. For me, it's not thought-provoking, but just plain silly. The thought that some assassin tendency is passed on via a person's heritage, and blood line, is ludicrous. Because of this, among other ridiculous notions, there's no way for me to appreciate the story. I also couldn't appreciate the motivation for anything which takes place throughout the movie. Earlier, I surmised that this movie is based on a video game. This is because it spends very little time explaining anything in any real detail. There's mention of what's going on, and why, so you're able to understand the premise. But it's done in such a superficial way that you don't care at all about any of the characters, or what they're trying to accomplish. I'm surprised that some of the positive reviews are comprised of those who aren't familiar with the game. I would have guessed that it would be the other way around. If you're familiar with the game, you would at least already have a context for what you're going to see, and would therefore, have a greater appreciation for the concept. But as far as a storyline is concerned, to me, this movie is a joke. The movie has good fight sequences and adequate special effects; as do most action movies these days. So if that's all you care about, then you may appreciate this movie. I also like the actors, who do as much as can be done with such a weak concept and script. But if you're into thought-provoking concepts, like that of "The Matrix" (I only truly appreciate the first Matrix film), then this movie will likely be a huge disappointment for you. In all honesty, I almost turned off this movie, and wasn't going to finish it. But often times, I like to finish what I start; unless I simply can't take it anymore. For me, this movie came extremely close to being unworthy of viewing completion.

history.title: Jekyll:S1 (DVD)
history.review_title: Easily the Best Rendition of Jekyll & Hyde that I've Ever Seen
history.text: The title of my review isn't an exaggeration. This show does as much as you can with the concept of Jekyll and Hyde. In fact, I'm not sure I could think of many ways to improve this production. I watched this show a few years ago. I happened to walk into the room, while a friend was just starting it. I fell in love with it right away. Recently, I wanted to show it to another friend. I remembered how great it was and decided to buy it. He took one look at the cover and started to judge it. I told him to trust me. After the first episode, he was hooked, just as I had been when I watched it. We blew through all six episodes over the course of a day, or two. Later, my friend told another person about it. The same thing happened. I let my friend borrow the DVD and the new guy was blown away. He had to leave, but was really torn about it. He really wanted to keep watching! I've seen enough reviews to know that nearly any show/movie, with lots of reviews, is going to have a few single-star reviews. Though something may be great, these reviews are going to come from people whose tastes I'll never understand. Everyone's entitled to their opinion, and the world is so big that we can be quite vast in our differences. How else can you explain someone giving "The Shawshank Redemption" one star? history.title: Arne Dahl
history.text: Each of the 5 disks contain a two part episode, and each part is 90 minutes long. For binge watchers, this doesn't represent any problems, but for me I only watch one part of an episode on one day, and the next part another time. While the team at first seemed disjointed, I quickly warmed up to the characters. It doesn't make sense to compare this series to The Killing or The Bridge; if that's what you're looking for, don't purchase these. However, if you want very well acted police procedurals and a diverse team of experts, then give this series a try. These dramas are not fast-moving, and while they are suspenseful, they won't keep you on the edge of your seat. Rather than focusing on one really strong character as The Killing or The Bridge, you get to know a team that has been pulled together by Commander Jenny Hultin, an older female officer. It takes time for the team to gel, but they do, and the rewards are great if you stay with them through five, two-part stories.

I expected Julianna Margulies to be good - I've always liked her - but she's far better than good; she's excellent. The really great thing about The Good Wife is that everyone else is good too, even Chris Noth. I have to admit, I'm not a big Chris Noth fan, but he's better in this series than I've ever seen him. I've only watched about half a dozen episodes so far, and I'm looking forward to many more to enjoy. If you've hesitated to try this series for any reason, give it about 50 minutes. history.review_title: Takes Kalinda's character down the wrong path
history.text: I commented on another reviewer's statements regarding the unfortunate decision to take Kalinda's character down the wrong path. The addition of an abusive husband who has some type of sick hold over an otherwise strong character did nothing to enhance the mystery of Kalinda. In fact, it diminished her character. I don't think the writers really understood the strength of the character they had created. Whatever they intended her to be, Archie Panjabi took her beyond that scope and created a truly unique and memorable woman. It's no wonder Panjabi left the series after Josh Charles, and now, Julianna Margulies appears to be leaving as well. Even the Kings are leaving. In my opinion, the problems start with not fully appreciating the complexity of Kalenda's character. The decision to portray her as just another of Peter's conquests to damage her friendship with Alicia was the first of several miscalculations in developing the character of Kalinda Sharma. The writers took the easy way out with Kalinda and focused on superficial sexual encounters rather than providing more substantive character development. There are still many fine episodes in The Good Wife. But the heart has gone out of it.

history.review_title: While season 5 is better than season 4
history.text: While season 5 is better than season 4, the show continues to trend downwards. I understand why Josh Charles wanted to leave the series - its decline is obvious - but why kill off his character? Let me say here, that I'm not a fan of killing off characters in a TV series. For me, it shows a lack of imagination. But seriously, having a client shoot Will in the court room by grabbing the gun of a careless guard was a real stretch, and it's been done before on TV. And now the series has to keep exploring Alicia's grief - not just in season 5 but beyond. Enough already. This truly is pure soap opera material, and when The Good Wife began, it was much better than a night time soap drama. Unfortunately, the soap opera aspect is taking over more and more of the show. I'll still watch for the few episodes that are actually good, but I can see why the show is coming to an end. And, for me, the beginning of the end started with the writers taking Kalinda's character in the wrong direction in season 4. It's all over but the shouting.

history.review_title: Very good look at real life in Israel
history.text: Very interesting, real-life documentary about an Ethiopian-Israeli policeman who is assigned to an Ethiopian neighborhood. He says "I thought I would be chasing criminals, but what I do most of the time is help these people adjust to life in Israel." The cultural difference is intense, best exemplified by an older woman who sat telling the cop that men have the right to beat women, and that women have the Evil Eye. The cop explains to her over and over that there are laws in Israel, and no man is permitted to beat his wife. The Ethiopian émigré doesn't agree, and apparently can't fathom such laws. Really a close, sympathetic look at the culture shock and problems of these emigres to Israel. A few amusing moments, like the family who called the cop to come fix their TV so they could get the Ethiopian channel. He did it, too!

This is an interesting documentary on the most austere yeshiva in Israel. The students single-mindedly study day and night. The world of the ultra-orthodox is mysterious to many, fascinating to some. Why do they do what they do? They are literal interpreters of the Torah, and they send their most intelligent sons to study for years-- often a lifetime. While this seems absurd and a waste of brainpower to probably more than a few onlookers, it is an ancient tradition in Judaism. One of the first things the Jews did when conquered by the Babylonians and the intelligentsia were forcibly removed to Babylon in the 5th century BCE, was to set up a school of learning, from which derived the Babylonian Talmud. This school was in continuing existence until the late 1950s, when a purge under Saddam Hussein resulted in its closure and the violent deaths of many Iraqi Jews. This particular yeshiva had been located, prior to the Hitler era, in Lithuania, but after the genocide it reopened in B'nei Brak, Israel. The ultra-orthodox, called "haredi" in Israel, live for the most part removed from the rest of society, in their own neighborhoods. They have come in for a great deal of criticism, because some of the haredi sects refuse to serve in the military among other things. However, there are in fact haredi units in the IDF. And, with typical Israeli inventiveness, the government has a program that uses some of the brilliant young yeshivabochers as software designers, since they are trained from early childhood to be sensitive to nuance and exploration of thought to the tiniest detail. All in all, this is as close a look as possible (obviously it doesn't show everything) of the lives of the young men who spend their young lives study in Ponevezh. Some leave to get married. Some want to get married but no match is found for them. Some prefer the austere, monastic rigor of the yeshiva, though marriage is encouraged, even mandated, for all in Judaism. This is a life far removed from the western secular world, and will no doubt be incomprehensible to most viewers. So, keep an open mind.

history.title: The Little Traitor ( Ha'boged Hakatan ) [ NON-USA FORMAT, PAL, Reg.2 Import - Denmark ]
history.review_title: A little gem of a film-- a must see
history.text: This film is taken from the novelette by the renowned writer Amos Oz called "The Panther in the Basement." The film is true to the story, which is partially autobiographical. It's a marvelous little gem, filmed in Jerusalem, set in 1947 when Israel was neither a state nor not-a-state. The British were in the last months of their Mandate and were particularly hard on the Jews, seeming to favor the Arabs. British patrols enforced daily curfews; Jews had to be in their houses by eight o'clock p.m. At this hour, the Irgun, the secret army, began its operations. Adults talked about this constantly, children listened, and three little boys formed an organization to fight the British: "FOD-- Freedom Or Death." The only problem was that one of these little boys happened to be caught by a British soldier when the child was running home after the curfew siren had sounded-- so he was stopped. And there began a friendship between the child and the British soldier, a decent, kindly man whose father and brother were vicars, and the soldier interested not in fighting but in languages. So he employed the boy to help him learn Hebrew, because the only Hebrew the soldier knew was straight from the Bible, antique and not at all modern Hebrew. And naturally, because the boy was going to see the soldier at British headquarters in Jerusalem, the child was noticed and trouble ensued. The acting in this film is marvelous. The tragi-comic life of a Jewish child in the final days of the mandate were actually lived by Amos Oz, who was born in 1939 as Amos Klausner in Israel to emigrant parents of a scholarly family. He is the grand-nephew of the renowned scholar and former activist Yosef Klausner of The Hebrew University. This film is historically accurate as well as highly entertaining.

history.title: Compliance
history.review_title: MY PICK FOR BEST FILM OF 2012
history.text: As a film historian, Compliance was indeed my pick for Best Film Of The Year for 2012. It was underseen and shunned by most major awards, though as you can see was quite critically acclaimed. Ann Dowd should've had an Oscar nomination; though all the performances were raw and intense. The film is very difficult to watch in subject matter, focusing highly on the sexual assault of a young woman. The tension and suspense are nail biting. That this film is based on a series of actual events makes it even more terrifying. From an historian's perspective, I find it sad that this film did not have a wider audience; most are not even aware of it. But absolutely, if you can stomach it - get the kids out of the room, and prepare not to breathe for the next ninety minutes. It is absolute perfection which will make you sick to your stomach and make you think twice about what may or may not be going on in your neighborhood burger joint.

history.text: This rates a solid 3 1/2 stars for me. I thought it was a unique story, but it fell a bit flat in the storytelling department. Actually the "telling" part is what kept it from being better. I felt I was being led by the nose when the story was good enough to just let me get there on my own. The love story dwarfed the aid story. Had they been more intertwined, I think that would have made it better as well.

history.title: Snow Flower and the Secret Fan
history.text: This is a story of the deep love between girls and women. I wanted to love this. I think there were some things that were too subtle while others hit you over the head unnecessarily. The movie jumped around a lot making it hard to stay connected as well. It jumped a lot between Chinese and English too. While I appreciated that it wasn't entirely subtitled, language makes a difference in feeling and so many other things that I don't think it was a great choice. Anyway, it was really different so I am glad I watched it. It left me with a lot of questions and thoughts. I like movies that do that.

history.title: The Crown: Season 1 [DVD]
history.text: The series is well done. The interesting part is that it's about real people. The dull part is that it's about really dull people who have absolutely nothing to do with the real life of 99.99999% of us. I mean the main character is a woman whose sister even says she has no character and she says she has the type of face that, if she's not smiling, she looks cross. It's like watching an automaton. Do you care what happens to an automaton? It's so unrelatable. It just feels like celebrity peeping or reality tv on a different social level. I was ready to turn it off before the series ended.

history.title: Line of Duty, Series 4
history.text: Brilliant writing. After 4 seasons I expect ideas to get stale, but this doesn't disappoint. It covers a wide range of humanity and gives lots of twists and turns. It stayed "edge-of-your-seat" fun until the end.

This is a light, modern look at the themes of Jane Austen. In the story, a present day woman in her 30s is infatuated with Austen romance. She uses her life savings to go to an emersion resort to live in the Austen days and be romanced by an actor. She gets the cheap package while two other guest have the Platinum experience. Our Jane gets to really experience the life of the Jane Austen characters who never had any money. It doesn't turn out to be all its cracked up to be, but the experience leaves her and the viewer completely enchanted. The writing does a good job of showing the Austen themes in modern romance. It also blends a bit of realism with a huge dose of comedy. The actors did a great job. I'm smitten!

It took me a while to join the GoT bandwagon. I found it hyper sexual, violent, and the characters weren't all that likable. Once I got past that, I loved all the twists and turns. There was so many surprises. The characters were deep, complex, and experienced growth. No one was safe from the ax. Season 7 is good, but it's definitely a kinder, gentler version. It feels really different. The others had a flow to them. You knew that episode 9 was going to have a big explosion and episode 10 would bring it all together, but also have a cliff hanger or teaser. There are only 7 episodes in this season, so that's the first shocker. Jon's a broken record. He bangs one drum, "The walk walkers are coming." He has always been a sort of one hit wonder dullard, so I suppose that's no surprise, but he has a lot of screen time in this one so it does get old. The surprise romance (I won't say between who) is not all that hot or sexy. No chemistry. It's predictable, but not an "ooohhhh! moment. A lot of banners change sides or are annihilated. Nothing all that dramatic there. Many characters meet their demise. There are no cross bow on the toilet "gotcha" moments. They are original but not the stuff you talk about the next day. Bran is now a dullard too. The Three Eyed raven has no personality. Bleh. This season is good, but it feels like it just tidied up a bit too quickly. It feels like a rush to the end of the series instead of simply telling the tale. It's like checking boxes: what happens to X, Y and Z. And it feels like most of the characters are war weary and old. They've lost a lot of zest. Where is the fire? Still good, just a kinder, gentler version.

This is a solid movie that suffers from a horrible title. I avoided this because the title seemed so "blah." The story is solid though. It's long, but you don't feel the time pass. You aren't sure what is going to happen, but it all seems plausible. The suspense is there right up until the end. It's well acted and well done. Bravo!

history.title: Victoria & Abdul [Blu-ray]
history.text: Great story. I found it interesting from a human interest perspective and also a historical perspective. I can't imagine what it must be like to have zero privacy and surrounded by haughty people you don't like. Abdul (like Mr. Brown before him) must have been a breath of fresh air. Good for Victoria for saying to h*ll with convention and letting herself enjoy life. The on screen chemistry between Dench and Ali was wonderful. You can so totally see how the queen could have been captivated by him.

history.title: Blow-Up (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.text: Wonderful Criterion release of Blow-Up. Love this film. Gives a small insight into 60’ English scene. Mod/rockers type of stuff. Plus a great mystery to boot.

history.title: Phantasm
history.text: Great job with the remastered. Looks great and still is a freaky movie after all these years....BOY!!!

history.title: Saturn 3 [Blu-ray/DVD Combo]
history.review_title: Fond Memories Of This Movie Squashed!
history.text: When I decided to order the Blu Ray of Saturn 3, I hadn’t seen it for probably 20-25 years. I had found memories of it growing up in the 80’s but after viewing it recently through mature adult eyes, it became crystal clear why this film flopped at the box office originally. Plot holes and bad dialog/acting fill this movie completely to the point of laughable. Watching Farrah Fawcett act is pretty painful as always though watching her strut around in revealing garb is nice. Kurt Douglass comes off as a creepy old man who seems to have FF on this base for nothing more then being a sex slave. One of the biggest problem is the plot and how the movie is set up in the beginning. They never answer the question on why Captain Benson kills Captain James to take his place in delivering and setting up this robot on Saturn 3. This is how the movie starts out and yet through the rest of the film, nothing comes of it as though it never happened. No one seems to notice that the original captain was murdered and this guy took his place for like weeks on Saturn 3. Really ridiculous. And lets talk about that robot. This thing is a hulking mass of metal and moves as slow as a sloth. It’s comedic to watch them run around in terror and fear when its painfully obvious there are many ways to run circles around it and disable it. Ohhhh, the wonders of watching films as a kid. Getting lost in the movie and not thinking of if a movie is good or bad, just enjoying it for what it is. I guess I should not have grown up. Or maybe just not have watched Saturn 3 again.

history.title: The Alligator People
history.text: A fun swamp horror film. The alligator people effects are bad but the movie is fun!

history.title: Freaked
history.text: A weird little comedy/horror film thats hit or miss on the jokes but interesting to see the kind of freaks they come up with.

history.title: I Bury the Living [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Bury The Plot And Enjoy The Film!
history.text: I love this film and consider it a underated classic of B cinema even though the plot really does not hold water when all said and done. It’s got a great atmosphere, mystery, and that old b/w horror charm.

history.review_title: Paulides Is Missing 411 From His Own Film.
history.text: I’d been waiting to see this for a long time and I have to say Im pretty disappointed in it. I haven’t read the books because when I found out about 411, they were already out of print. However, I have listen to David Paulides on Coast To Coast and all his podcast and videos and read snippets of his books on-line. He presents some interesting cases and facts that are just bizarre and strange for these kids disappearing in our national parks. You get a feel for his sincerity and passion to try and understand why this is happening. The problem with the documentary lies in a couple of areas. First, and probably the oddest, Paulides himself is a Missing 411 from the documentary. You hear him one or twice briefly on a radio and thats it! How odd that this is his project with all the investigation he has done, and he is not part of the film. I thought for sure he would be the host or voice over telling the stories but this is not the case. Second, the documentary really does nothing to convince us that the children featured in the film, and there are only about four maybe five, are nothing more then either kids that wondered off into the woods or abducted by a individual. In fact, the main case they focus on really seems to be a crime situation as the family is highly suspect in the child’s disappearance. The parents even hired a private investigator to help try and find their son and he ended up quitting because he felt they were involved in the childs disappearance. It’s examples like this that derails what the documentary is trying to accomplish. When you listen to Paulides and read about some of his cases he has investigated, he provides information that makes you stop and think. You understand that something is oddly off from a “normal” disappearance, but the documentary almost goes the other way in trying to show that the parents are guilty without coming out and saying it. As far as the other cases goes, there isn’t anything that would seem unnatural in the situations. If you want to say that some unnatural/supernatural event took these kids or extraterrestrials, which is what I believe Paulides has eluded to but not openly said, then you gotta eliminate all earthy possibilities. You have to be able to say that we have positive evidence that this child was not abducted by a psycho and killed. That this kid was not dragged off by a bear and mauled. If you can’t eliminate those things, then you can’t start reaching for the stars for a answer. Paulides himself does a good job getting that information through, but the film does not. Not sure why or what happened but my guess is Paulides had little to do with the documentary.

history.title: Night of the Living Dead - 50th Anniversary [Blu-ray]
history.text: I have to agree with the another reviewer on here that this is a horrible transfers. All they did was put the movie onto Blu Ray and I guarantee there was no restoration. It looks like all the standard DVD versions. We put one of our $4.99 DVD copies on after viewing the Blu Ray and everything was exactly the same. Same over bright areas, same scratches, same fuzzy scenes etc. I will never buy from Mill Creek again as they apparently like to be deceptive.

history.title: Rawhead Rex (Special Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.text: The remastered Blu Ray is fantastic looking. So glad this is finally available. I have not owned this since the VHS days.

history.title: The Last House on the Left (Unrated Collectors Edition) by 20th Century Fox
history.text: God, what a horrible film. This has to be the corniest horror film set to the worst mucis ever. How did Craven even get another job after this?!?

history.title: Desperate Housewives: Season 5
history.review_title: THE FIRST SLIP UP/THE FIRST BAD SEASON
history.text: Believe it or not, I'd never seen DH until earlier this year (maybe an episode here and there). At the suggestion of several friends and family members, I began watching season 1. I fell in love with the show and bought each following season. While I was watching these, I wasn't watching season 5, waiting to watch them all together. I am so disappointed with this season! Where do I begin? I hate that they jumped 5 years. But since they did, why on earth do they present plot lines through flash backs in almost every episode? Does anything good happen to these people this season? Carlos got his sight back, that's pretty much it. All the hard times on everyone proved for depressing viewing. I'm having hard times myself, I don't need to see it on Wisteria Lane. What happened to all the comedy? I can't believe they killed off Edie. Huge mistake. The show won't be the same without her. Edie was fun, and her quick wit and sharp tongue always cut to the truth of the matter. While I'm on the subject of Edie, does anyone believe for a minute that Edie would give Dave the time of day, let alone marry the guy? He is totally opposite the type of guy she likes. And as everyone points out, really stupid mystery. A child could figure it out right away. The gay couple which were introduced in season 4 are barely utilized in season 5. For the first few episodes, they're merely decoration. Marc Cherry, a gay man, should be ashamed of himself. He is really letting down a huge fanbase of the show. The men are all pretty useless this year, except for the "villian". Orsen becoming a clepto? Come on! Tom having ANOTHER mid-life crisis? Been there, done that. If only Gale Harold hadn't had his motorcycle accident, I wonder what they would've done with his character? Terri Hatcher was completely annoying this season, and she was always one of my favorite characters. They made Marcia Cross's Bree as cold as stone this season. We saw nothing beneath this woman's hard exterior. And what a pity about Dana Delany. This great actress had to make do in season 5 with whatever paltry tidbits they threw her, after giving her such a great storyline in season 4. So what, in my opinion, recommends this season at all? The Eli Scruggs episode--flashbacks, but really great sentimental writing. Outstanding performance by Beau Bridges. The episode where the girls scatter Edie's ashes--again with the flashbacks, but Nicolette Sheridan really shines before fading out. Also some of the loveliest writing of the season. These 2 episodes ALMOST re-deem the season. Eva Longoria's Gabrielle is finally humbled by poverty (enough with the head bands, though), but mid-way through gets back to her shallow self. They do a little more with the Karen McCluskey character, who is great fun. Maybe she'll fill Edie's shoes. The children of Gaby and Susan are adorable (but I miss Lynette's little ones). Anyway, if you purchase this season, it will be because, like myself, you've become attached to these characters, and want to follow them, even during the down seasons. And every great show has at least one of those. Let's hope they come back in Season 6.

history.title: Monte Carlo
history.text: There's probably a good reason MONTE CARLO didn't have the success of SINS--it's not as good. Joan Collins looks lovely and her wardrobe is beautiful, but i found this to be a very boring film. Olive Films has also released SINS on dvd. I highly recommend SINS--it's a delicious escape--much better plot, better acting, better fashion, better location, more Stars. I grew up in the 80s, and i loved watching mini-series, but i never saw MONTE CARLO till now. It almost put me to sleep--the boring pace, bad acting. I felt this could have been condensed into one 2-hour film. SINS, on the other hand, is one of my favorite 80s miniseries, and i'm so happy it's finally been released on dvd here in the States. This is just my opinion, but if you're wondering which is better, i recommend SINS--it's juicy fun!

history.title: Winter Meeting
history.text: As usual, Bette is the best thing about the picture. She carries it and her performance is top notch. It's not a bad film, just too long with lots of dialogue/exposition. And Jim Davis may have been miscast but it's not his acting that's the problem-- it's his accent and deadpan delivery, which he made famous years later on Tv's Dallas. Not one of Bette's best, but worth a look. Bette's greatest period was the late 1930s-late 1940s.

history.title: The Corn is Green (1945)
history.text: Bette's performance is flawless. But the film is too long and the outdoor scenes are obviously shot on a soundstage. And this was a distracting problem for me-- did EVERYONE in this Welsh mining town have a beautiful singing voice?! If so, why were they slaving away in mines? They could've made their living as a traveling choral group. It was almost laughable. Worth a look for Bette, but i enjoyed the late 1970s version with Katharine Hepburn better.

history.title: Female on the Beach
history.text: This film is slightly trashy but fun to watch. Joan gives her usual intense performance. Perhaps it would've been better if the beach comber/ hustler was younger and more attractive, like the one who came to replace him at the end of the picture. One of Joan's campiest pictures.

history.title: Beauty and the Beast: 25th Anniversary Edition - (BD+DVD+DIGITAL HD)
history.review_title: 25th Anniversary Blu-Ray is no better than the previous editions
history.text: As with past Blu-Ray editions of Beauty and the Beast, this new 25th anniversary Blu-Ray contains white shadows around the lines of the characters' faces. It is distracting to the point it gave me a headache. I have read other reviews from buyers who also have this problem. I was hoping the problem would be fixed with this new reissue. The DVD, however, looks fine so it's not a total loss. I was just hoping for a sharp hi-def Blu-Ray. I see no point in buying any reissues of this film years from now. (By the way, my copy included the digital code- but I bought mine at Target.) Blu-Ray: 1 Star. DVD: 4 Stars. Overall Rating: 3 Stars.

history.title: Planet Earth II
history.text: A glorious return to the beauty of this planet. It will humble you and fill you with wonder.

history.title: I Am Divine
history.review_title: A Fitting Tribute to a Legend
history.text: A fun and fitting tribute to Divine. I have watched this over and over. Fascinating and Marvelous!

history.title: The Fox
history.text: Performances are fine and it's very atmospheric, but it adheres to the rule of that time in films, which is- if you're gay you have to be punished, usually by death. I always think about the gay people who went to those films, wanting to see their lives represented. What message did that send them? I always wanted to see this. Im a fan of Sandy Dennis. But this isn't something to watch more than once. Worth watching for its historical context and that's all.

history.title: Strike a Pose
history.review_title: A Must See for Fans of Truth or Dare
history.text: If you are a fan of Madonna's 1990 Blond Ambition Tour and 1991 film Truth or Dare, this is a film you must see. If you were a gay man coming of age in the early '90s you know how major that tour and documentary was. Strike a Pose will take you back to those times. It will take you home, a reunion with old friends. A Powerful and Profound film.
